title: The dashboard HTML has no data; content waits for hydration and then for /api/runs
oneLine: The route has no loader: the server renders only "Checking access and loading runs…" and the client fetches /api/runs after hydration (dev: request starts at ~235 ms, content = hydration + API + ~30 ms).
verifierReason: Facts confirmed: apps/web/src/routes/index.tsx:39-44 has no loader, :161 starts in loading, :176-210 fetches in an effect. Re-run: server HTML is 27,700 bytes with the loading text one time and no run data; local order is paint 68-80 ms, /api/runs start 228-249 ms. Corrections: (1) the claim that runs.$runId.tsx has the same pattern is wrong about the mechanism; that route uses the router loader of contract decision P03 (runs.$runId.tsx:31-49), so the dashboard is the outlier; the pull route text is at :181, not :179. (2) The gain is overstated: in production (orchestrator record, not my measurement) the request starts at 0.24-0.36 s and then waits 0.9-2.0 s on the server; a server loader removes only the first part, and a blocking loader moves the wait before the first byte unless it streams. (3) The repository already calls server-rendered data a separate scope increase (docs/simplification-audit/evidence/feedback-performance.md:30). (4) Three items the recommendation must handle: forward sessionHeaders (api/index.ts:220-222), toLocaleString(undefined) dates cause hydration mismatch (index.tsx:156), and client caches must be bounded (feedback-quality.md:18).

title: Header navigation reloads the whole document, although both lists are already in memory
oneLine: app-shell.tsx:52-57 renders NavLink with a plain href, so queue/history/status clicks load a new document and refetch /api/runs; the in-page router Link to history makes no request.
verifierReason: app-shell.tsx:15-19, :29, :52-57 are plain anchors. Re-run in the opposite order: footer router Link gives 0 new documents and 0 new /api/runs; each header click gives 1 new document and new /api/runs requests. NavLink spreads props onto ak.Role.a (nav.ariakit.react.tsx:588-609), so render={<Link/>} is feasible. No test or contract rule needs a full reload; app-shell.tsx is new in f83fef6 with no stated reason. Production cost of one such load is about 1.2 s to content and 2.7 s to stable (orchestrator record). Addition: all three views share the document title 'Visonaut' (__root.tsx:10), so client navigation needs a per-view title.

title: "Refresh runs" blanks the page and three header items, and reloads the alerts
oneLine: refresh() sets state to loading (index.tsx:242-245): list, title, repository, bell, and account menu disappear, scroll and history filters reset, and /api/operations loads again (1 -> 2).
verifierReason: index.tsx:242-245 sets loading; :251, :254-257 gate the repository name, bell, and account menu. Re-run: during a refresh the header has no buttons and no repository, main is only the loading line, scrollY goes 600 to 0, page height 1,880 to 900, /api/operations loads 1 to 2, history query is lost. Addition: keyboard focus falls to <body> after a refresh (measured). Correction to the sketch: native disabled on the focused button can drop focus; use aria-busy or accessibleWhenDisabled.

title: /api/operations waits for /api/runs, and the service view loads runs that it does not use
oneLine: OperationsAttention mounts only in the ready state (index.tsx:254-256, 363-364): two authenticated requests in sequence, each with a session read and an account read (at least 6 D1 round trips per load).
verifierReason: index.tsx:254-256 and :356-364 confirmed; the bell and the service page mount only in the ready state. The serial order is measured in production by the orchestrator (not by me): /api/operations starts 66-250 ms after /api/runs ends in every sample. Correction: the count is too low. /api/operations is at least 6 sequential D1 round trips by code (assertConfiguredProject is skipped only for /api/runs at api/index.ts:123-126; session and account reads at authorization.ts:32-43; three queries at api/operations.ts:16-47), so one dashboard load is at least 9, not 6. Alternative 2 (/api/session) adds a third authenticated request and goes against the tested intent at route.browser.test.ts:88-103.

title: Pull request titles are erased when the webhook is processed, so the queue shows "Pull request" as the title
oneLine: dashboard.ts:57-62 reads the title from github_webhook_delivery.payload_json, but webhooks.ts:330-335 sets payload_json='{}' on every processed delivery; after that the lookup matches 0 rows (reproduced in sqlite, production not read).
verifierReason: dashboard.ts:57-62 and review.ts:288 read the title from payload_json; webhooks.ts:330-335 sets payload_json='{}' for every processed delivery; dashboard.test.ts:42-56 inserts a row that production cannot produce. SQL re-run: title before processing, 0 matching rows and NULL after. git log -S confirms 339926d (#129) then 5712036 (#155). Production is corroborated by the orchestrator record ('#7746 · Pull request'). The repo's own design record said it first: feedback-ui.md:134 'reading old webhook payloads is not a viable title source'. Corrections: the store is already selected there (nullable title on the run row, no PR table; feedback-ui.md:139), which is option C and rules out option B. Option A works in SQL but the documented backfill predicate payload_json != '{}' (compact-processed-webhooks.md:10-12, .sql:6) would match and erase the trimmed rows again, and three more clear sites and two tests need changes.

title: ak-ink-danger, ak-ink-warning, and ak-ink-success do not exist; errors and status icons have no color
oneLine: ak-ink-* accepts only numbers; six uses (index.tsx:271,331,531, user-menu.tsx:66, operations-attention 370,501) emit no CSS, so error text and icons render in the body color.
verifierReason: @ariakit/tailwind output.css:816-821 defines ak-ink-* for a number or an arbitrary value only. Re-run: 0 CSS rules for ak-ink-danger|warning|success, 2 for ak-ink-60; the sign-in alert and the forbidden icon have the body color in dark and in light. All six uses confirmed with rg. The correct form already exists in the repo (runs.$runId.tsx:232, review/item-list.tsx:272), so this is also an inconsistency between pages.

title: $layer="primary" is not a recipe color; the main buttons paint a fixed pale gray in both schemes
oneLine: COLOR_VALUES has no "primary"; the buttons get --layer-color: primary and compute to oklch(0.95 0 0) in dark and light, so the main action is a pale gray box in light mode (review workspace uses "brand").
verifierReason: utils/styles.ts:6-13 has no 'primary'; layer.ariakit.react.tsx:79-100 turns an unknown string into --layer-color. Re-run on the real preview server and the fixture: inline '--layer-color: primary', background oklch(0.949994 0.0000497986 23.7884) in both schemes, logo slot oklch(0.515341 0.1546 248.516); the light sign-in shield box is oklch(0.999994) on a card of oklch(1). Additions: ui.css:6 declares --color-primary: var(--color-brand) (the intent), but the token is not in the output CSS, so var(--color-primary) would not work either; $layer="brand" is the working value. Alternative 2 (type change) diverges from pinned upstream code where (string & {}) is deliberate; a lint rule is smaller.

title: Review cards are 240 px tall; a queue of 40 runs is 8.5 screens long

Correction: the 40-run queue is synthetic data. The production /api/runs answer was 2,285 bytes (orchestrator record), which is a few runs, so '8.5 screens' is a stress case and the impact depends on real queue size. title: The same facts are stated two to five times; most words on screen can go
oneLine: Queue with one run: 55 words, about 18 carry data; run count 3x, run state 3x per card, repository 2-3x, "nothing to do" 5x, history scope 3x; the report lists each removable text.
verifierReason: Word counts re-measured and equal: sign-in 34, empty queue 38, queue with one run 55 (same text word for word), queue with 8 runs 222, preview queue 59. All cited lines exist as quoted. Corrections: the third 'count' at index.tsx:471 is a heading without a number; the 'words that carry data' column is an estimate; the removal list is a design opinion.

title: Failed and stale runs are at the bottom, with a clock icon and no color
oneLine: "Needs attention" renders last (index.tsx:542-543) with the same Clock3Icon and gray text as "In progress"; with 40 runs it starts at about y=6,540 of 7,608.
verifierReason: index.tsx:542-543 puts both groups after the review cards; :580-582 uses the clock for every row; :588-590 has no commit, time, or color. Screens match. Corrections: 'Needs attention' starts at y=6,698 of 7,608 in the 40-run fixture (report: about 6,540). Moving it first changes contract decision U05 'List review work first' (current-contract.md:147). A run with state 'failed' never reaches the queue (dashboard.ts:71); 'Run failed' rows come only from dead comparison tasks.

title: Eight run states share four looks, and the same badge has two shapes
oneLine: needs-review, comparing, and incomplete are all yellow with a clock; failed, rejected, and needs-recompare are all red; the fixture state "reviewing" is gray; the badge is a pill in cards and has a 2 px radius in the table.
verifierReason: index.tsx:142-151 and :385-386 map 8 states to 4 looks; review-status.ts:50-58 has no 'reviewing'; preview-fixtures.ts:84 sends it. Re-run: badge radius 3.35544e+07px in a card and 2px in the table. Correction: the auditor did not find the cause. It is the documented concentric rule of $rounded (frame.ariakit.react.tsx:116-122; output.css:1062-1065): in the table the parent frame is the tr (radius 0, padding under 1rem), so the badge gets the 2 px floor; in the card the 21 px padding turns the rule off. The fix is the existing $forceRounded prop (frame.ariakit.react.tsx:127-130).

title: Only 1.7% of a review card is clickable; history rows link the text block only; link names repeat
oneLine: Card 1120x240 with one 142x33 link; history link covers 36% of the row; tab order reads "Review changes" x4 and "Open run" x4; time elements have no dateTime.

title: Runs without a title print the kind twice; the icon is always a pull request; nothing links to GitHub

title: Copy defects: wrong plural, wrong claim for a first-time visitor, lost server message, error far from its button
oneLine: "1 view await approval."; every 403 says "Your repository access changed"; non-OK answers drop the server message and reference; the sign-in error renders at x=160,y=69 while the button is at x=774,y=363.
verifierReason: Re-measured: '1 view await approval.' is in the DOM; a 503 with a reference and a 409 both show 'The run list is temporarily unavailable. Please retry.'; the sign-in alert is at x=160,y=69 and pushes the button from y=325 to y=363. The three 403 codes are at api/index.ts:111, authorization.ts:46, github.ts:227. route.browser.test.ts:75 confirms the review page shows the reference. Corrections: wrong_origin cannot reach a same-origin request unless the origin is misconfigured; the 409 needs a missing project row; naming the repository on 401/403 needs a server change (errorResponse has no repository).

title: The sign-in screen is a marketing page for one button
oneLine: 34 words, two headings, and two paragraphs around one action; the repository is not named; the header shows three links that a guest cannot open.
verifierReason: Design opinion. Facts under it are right: index.tsx:281-319, 34 words in main, the three navigation links render for a guest, the button is at y=325. Severity lowered: the session lasts 7 days and is extended on use (auth.ts:43-44), so a working maintainer sees the screen rarely. Alternative 2 (redirect without a click) is not small: signIn.social is a POST that sets state, and it needs the server-side check of DASH-01.

title: "Use another account" probably returns the same account
oneLine: The button only signs out of Visonaut and the GitHub provider sets no prompt (auth.ts:29-35), so GitHub most probably signs the same user in again; not tested against GitHub.
verifierReason: Code facts confirmed: index.tsx:344-351 only signs out; auth.ts:29-35 sets no prompt; the forbidden screen also shows the account menu (measured). The behavior was not observed by anyone. GitHub's documentation confirms prompt=select_account and adds that the picker also appears when several accounts are signed in, so the loop can affect only a browser with one GitHub account signed in. The fix is feasible per request with the installed better-auth 1.7.5: signIn.social accepts additionalParams (sign-in.mjs:110, :231; create-authorization-url.mjs:54-57).

Please retry.' (:130), has no actionError state, and uses a boolean action; after sign-out the run route calls window.location.assign('/') while the other two set the guest state. title: Small visual inconsistencies
oneLine: Button radius 6.5 px against 2 px on one page, error card width follows the message, five card paddings and two radii, a decorative icon box in every row, uneven section gaps, mixed heading punctuation.
verifierReason: Re-measured: 'Review changes' 6.5 px and 'Open run' 2 px; error cards 531 px and 433 px wide. Corrections: (1) the radius difference is the documented concentric rule of $rounded, the same cause as DASH-11 (row padding 14 px under 1rem with radius 10.5 px gives the 2 px floor; card padding 21 px turns the rule off); use $forceRounded. (2) The gaps are 56 px and 28 px, not about 64 and 36; the spacing unit is 0.25em = 3.5 px. (3) There are four card paddings (4, 6, 7, 8), not five. (4) Card width varies because the card is a grid item with mx-auto.

title: Difference mode shows the mask alone: no screenshot context and no image boundary
oneLine: The diff pane renders only the red-on-transparent mask (screenshot-viewer.tsx:242-261), so the reviewer sees red pixels on an empty checkerboard and cannot tell what they belong to.
verifierReason: Code: apps/web/src/components/screenshot-viewer.tsx:242-261 renders only `variant.diff` in the diff pane. Mask format checked in both engines: packages/cli/src/png-comparison.ts:67-75 (`diffMask: true`) and packages/compare/src/compare.ts:110-119 (`data[offset] = 255; data[offset + 3] = 255;`). Screens 03, 12, 17 and 42 show red pixels on the checkerboard, with no picture below and no image edge. The overlay recommendation is feasible: a mask always has the candidate size (apps/web/src/api/local-comparison.ts:584-591 rejects another size), and the contract rule "Pixel diff paints differences red" (docs/simplification-audit/contract-issue-1.md:264) stays true. No correction to the facts. Severity is my judgment: one key (S) gives the context back, so the cost is time, not wrong information. The auditor rated it high.

title: A small change is a few screen pixels, and nothing points to it
oneLine: A 120 px change is about 5 x 4 screen px in Compare and 56 reddish px in Difference at 1440 x 900; on a 640 x 3200 image it is 4 px; 200% opens at 0,0 with the change off screen; no boxes, no jump to change.
verifierReason: I ran the auditor's measure.mjs again. The output is byte-identical to measure-output.txt (`diff` printed IDENTICAL). M1: scale 0.4332 in Compare, so a 12 x 10 change is about 5 x 4 screen px. M2: 56 reddish px at 1280x720, 4 at 640x3200, 1 at 256x8192. Screens 02, 10 and 17 match the captions. Code: `mode` starts as "side" and `zoom` as "fit" (apps/web/src/review/review-workspace.tsx:197-198); the pan position starts at 0,0 (screenshot-viewer.tsx:35-48). Corrections: (1) Change regions computed in the browser need the mask before Difference is selected. That reverses decision P02 "Load diff when selected" (docs/current-contract.md:149), and review.browser.test.ts:1695-1717 pins it with `expect(requests).toBe(0)`. The report asks for a decision but does not name P02. (2) A canvas can read the images because the URL is same-origin (`/images/<id>`, apps/web/src/api/review.ts:423). The CORP header at apps/web/src/api/images.ts:55 is not the reason. Limit: the images are synthetic. Real capture sizes were not measured.

title: Panes do not share pan; zoom, mode, and variant changes lose the inspected place
oneLine: Each pane keeps its own scroll ref (screenshot-viewer.tsx:35-48): baseline [400,200] vs current [0,0]; 100% to 200% keeps raw offsets; Compare to Difference lands at [0,0]; next variant resets pan but keeps zoom.
verifierReason: M4 to M7 reproduce exactly: baseline [400,200] with current [0,0]; after 100% to 200% the centre point moves from [678,434] to [339,217]; Difference opens at [0,0]; the next variant resets to [0,0] and keeps 200%. Code: per-pane `position` ref (screenshot-viewer.tsx:35), raw offsets restored (:42-48), reset on identity (:39-41). Evidence that the report did not use: the binding contract says "Preserve zoom and image position when possible" (docs/simplification-audit/contract-issue-1.md:264). A zoom change keeps the scroll offsets, not the image point, and Difference opens at the corner, so the behavior is below that rule. Two tests pin the present behavior: per-pane position across modes (apps/web/src/review/__tests__/review.browser.test.ts:1367-1391) and the reset to `{ left: 0, top: 0 }` on a variant change (:1695-1760, "keeps pan until the variant changes"). A shared view or a kept place across variants must change the second test.

title: The image gets about a quarter of the window, and Fit does not fit the visible area
oneLine: The stage is a fixed h-[min(56vh,650px)] below seven rows of chrome: image starts at y 432 of 900, uses 26% of the window, and its bottom 59 px (138 px at 1280 x 720) sit under the sticky action bar.
verifierReason: The layout facts hold: `h-[min(56vh,650px)] min-h-80` (screenshot-viewer.tsx:134) and the sticky action bar (review-workspace.tsx:1017). But three numbers include the 24 px label that only the fixture page has. I removed the label and measured again (verify/extra4-output.txt, verify/extra5-output.txt). Current at Fit, 1440x900: picture 832x468 at y 408 to 876, 36 px under the action bar (the report says 59). 1280x720: 115 px, 31% of the picture (the report says 138 px, 38%). Compare at 1280x720: 15 px hidden in each pane. "The document still scrolls" at 2560x1440 is false on the real route: the scroll height is 1440 without the label (1464 was the label). Real overflow is 94 px at 1440x900, 15 px at 1920x1080, 0 at 2560x1440. The shares change little: Current 27.8% of the window, Compare 13.4% for each pane. On the real preview route (port 4310) the stage is 41 px lower because of the read-only banner (viewport top 431, verify/extra-output.txt E1). Also true and not stated: at 1440x900 the stage bottom (y 894) is under the sticky bar (top 841).

title: Comparison techniques that are missing
oneLine: No overlay or onion skin, swipe, blink, change boxes, synced pan, pixel inspector, device-pixel 1:1, auto zoom to change, free zoom, or drag to pan (model.ts:2-3; drag and Ctrl+wheel measured as no-ops).
verifierReason: Each row of the table is a fact that I checked. `ReviewMode = "side" | "diff" | "new" | "original"` and `ReviewZoom = "fit" | 1 | 2` (apps/web/src/review/model.ts:2-3). screenshot-viewer.tsx has only onScroll, onLoad, onError and the pan onClick handlers. M10 reproduces: drag leaves [0,0], Ctrl plus wheel keeps 200%, cursor is auto. Which techniques to add is a design opinion that cannot be refuted. Notes for the design phase: the contract fixes S/D/F and fit/100%/200% (docs/simplification-audit/contract-issue-1.md:264 and :276), so new modes and zoom levels change contract text and docs/review-guide.md. Decision P02 (docs/current-contract.md:149) limits each design that needs the mask at first paint.

title: Arrow keys never pan, there are no zoom keys, and the mouse cannot drag
oneLine: With the focusable pane focused at 200%, ArrowRight changes the variant and ArrowDown changes the item; +, -, 0 do nothing; pan needs four 25 px buttons per pane (10 tab stops in Compare).
verifierReason: Confirmed by a new run: with Shortcuts on, ArrowRight and ArrowDown on the focused pane change the variant and the item (M3); "+", "-", "0" do nothing; a drag does not pan; the viewer has 10 tab stops at 200% (verify/extra-output.txt E2); pan buttons are 25 x 25. Corrections: (1) This is decision U04 "Page-wide review arrows with pan buttons" (docs/current-contract.md:146). Its record says: "With global navigation enabled, arrows on the image change the selected comparison... This is the user's selected tradeoff. It must not be described as a new accessibility failure" (docs/simplification-audit/evidence/feedback-ui.md:115). The report does not cite it, and its recommendation reverses it. (2) "Arrow keys never pan" is false when the Shortcuts switch is off: ArrowRight moved the pane to [40,0] and ArrowDown to [40,40] (verify/extra3-output.txt G2; the handler returns at review-workspace.tsx:396). (3) PageDown, Space, Home and End scroll the focused pane (the auditor's own M3), so only horizontal moves need the buttons. (4) "No scrollbar is visible in the captures" is a capture artifact: headless Playwright adds `--hide-scrollbars` (node_modules/.pnpm/playwright-core@1.63.0/node_modules/playwright-core/lib/coreBundle.js:43338-43341). (5) Shift+ArrowRight also changes the variant (G1), so alternative (a) needs a handler change.

title: Difference says "within the comparison tolerance" for an image whose size changed
oneLine: Local comparison stores no mask on a size change (png-comparison.ts:64-66, maskExpected false), so screenshot-viewer.tsx:249-253 shows the tolerance sentence next to "100.00% changed · Needs review".
verifierReason: I traced the full chain. CLI: different sizes return `{ outcome: "changed", changedPixels: pixels, ratio: 1, sizeChanged: true }` and no mask (packages/cli/src/png-comparison.ts:64-66). Service: a mask together with `sizeChanged` is rejected (apps/web/src/api/local-comparison.ts:584-591). Store: `maskExpected: !!result.mask` (apps/web/src/api/workflow-materialize.ts:351). API: sends kind "changed", `diff: null`, `maskExpected: false` (apps/web/src/api/review.ts:487-515). Client: use-evidence.ts:98 needs no mask, so the status is ready, and screenshot-viewer.tsx:249-253 picks "Pixel changes are within the comparison tolerance." Screen 22 shows that sentence below "100.00% changed · 1,100,800 changed pixels". The case is stronger than the report says: on local-v1 runs the sentence can appear only in this wrong case. Rows with a changed profile and changed pixels get a mask (png-comparison.ts:82-104). Tolerated unchanged rows have no candidate image, so Difference is disabled (review.ts:450-454; verify/extra-output.txt E7). The valid case exists only for legacy-engine rows (apps/web/src/api/tolerated-mask.test.ts). The contract makes each size change a review row (docs/current-contract.md:124). Not checked against a production record, by the auditor or by me. The fix is feasible because the API sends both image sizes.

title: Images with different sizes get different scales in Compare, and nothing marks the size change
oneLine: Each pane fits its own image: 1280 x 720 renders at scale 0.433 next to 1280 x 1600 at 0.293; the only hint is 10 px caption text.
verifierReason: M12 reproduces: 1280x720 at scale 0.4332 and 1280x1600 at 0.2925. But the cited screen 20 (1280x720 to 1280x860) does not show the effect. Both pictures are 555 px wide there, so the scale is equal. The scales differ only when one picture reaches the height limit of the stage (468 px at 1440x900, so a picture taller than about 1.19:1 in a 555 px pane). The sentence "the same button is 43% of its size on the left and 29% on the right" is true for the M12 pair only. "Nothing marks the size change" is confirmed: the only signs are the two 10 px captions (screenshot-viewer.tsx:103-105) and the text "100.00% changed". No `sizeChanged` field reaches the client (apps/web/src/api/review.ts:487-530), so a badge must compare the two sizes. How often capture sizes change was not measured.

title: Added, removed, and locally matched variants keep the two-pane layout with an empty pane
oneLine: Pane visibility depends only on the mode (screenshot-viewer.tsx:221, 236): new, removed, and matched-locally variants show a half-empty or fully empty stage, and on a phone the empty pane comes first.
verifierReason: Screens 23, 25, 27, 36 and 37 and verify/extra-output.txt E7 confirm the empty pane and that Baseline and Current stay enabled. Corrections: (1) The empty pane is a binding rule, not an oversight: "For a removal, F shows “Removed, no new image”; S shows the old image and a labeled empty pane. D is unavailable when either paired image is absent; keep the current view and explain why" (docs/simplification-audit/contract-issue-1.md:265; design r9 D30 in docs/design-r9.html; test review.browser.test.ts:1155-1179). The report says "Maintainer decision needed: no". That is wrong, because a single-pane layout replaces this rule. (2) "Locally matched variants are the normal case for unchanged items" is not proved, and the code points the other way. `candidateOmitted` needs different digests (apps/web/src/api/review.ts:450-454). A byte-identical unchanged pair shows the same stored image in both panes (verify/extra2-output.txt F3). How often tolerated pairs occur was not measured. (3) I did not measure the phone distance claim again.

title: Status rows and pan buttons move the image by 9 to 54 px
oneLine: Stage top is 414 px when ready, 423 zoomed, 439 for added, 455 while loading, 468 on error, because status rows and pan buttons are inserted above the image.
verifierReason: M8 reproduces: stage top 414 ready, 423 zoomed, 455 loading, 468 load error, 439 added. These are fixture values; subtract 24 for the real route. Sources checked: review-workspace.tsx:924-930 and :940-991; screenshot-viewer.tsx:95 and :108-130. Screen 30 shows the loading text three times. The report understates one point: the jump is not limited to uncached images. With the stock data-URL images I sampled each frame during 4 variant changes. 10 of 93 frames had the loading row and the stage 41 px lower (verify/extra-output.txt E4), about 2 to 3 frames for each change. That row also has `role="status"` (review-workspace.tsx:941-943), so a screen reader gets "Loading this comparison’s images…" on each change.

title: No preload and no placeholder: each variant change shows an empty stage until two full images load and decode
oneLine: Zero requests for the next variant before selection; then 2 image requests (3 in Difference) while the stage is blank; the 256 px thumbnail and known dimensions are not used as a placeholder.
verifierReason: M13 reproduces: no request for the next variant, two requests after a selection, and the mask only on the first Difference. `key={identity}` and `invisible` until ready are at screenshot-viewer.tsx:148 and :162. Each first request is one D1 read and one R2 read (apps/web/src/api/images.ts:24-41). Corrections: (1) The lazy mask is decision P02 (docs/current-contract.md:149), not a defect. (2) Alternative (a), keep the old image until the new one is decoded, conflicts with the binding rule "On selection, clear or cover stale pixels immediately" (docs/simplification-audit/contract-issue-1.md:266). (3) The thumbnail claim is wrong for current runs. `thumbnail` comes only from `result.thumbnailImageId` (apps/web/src/api/review.ts:505-506). Only the retired legacy Worker wrote that field (apps/compare/src/process.ts:191, :206, :228). A local-v1 result has only outcome, counts, versions and mask fields (apps/web/src/api/workflow-materialize.ts:344-353). So alternative (b) and ideas C4 and R8 have no data; the preview route shows the placeholder tile (verify/extra-output.txt E1 `"thumbnails":["SPAN"]`). (4) Preload is feasible (`"Cache-Control": "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"`, images.ts:52). But each preload is a Worker call with D1 and R2 work, because the route does not use the Cache API (no `caches.` in apps/web/src; https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/reference/how-the-cache-works/). The number of preloaded neighbors must have a limit. No production latency was measured.

title: The image has no visible boundary, and the checkerboard does not mean transparency
oneLine: The checkerboard is the background of the whole scroll box and the img has no ring, so light captures merge with the light stage and dark captures with the dark stage.
verifierReason: Code: the checkerboard is on the scroll container and the `` has no border (screenshot-viewer.tsx:134 and :162). Screen 02 (light) and screen 41 (dark, real route) show the picture edge merge with the stage. The claim about the fixed pattern is correct: with the default `background-attachment: scroll` the background "does not scroll with its contents" (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/background-attachment). The claim about the element box is correct: a 640x3200 image at Fit has an element box of 555x468 and a drawn picture of 94x468 (verify/extra-output.txt E6), so a border on the `` would be wrong. The utility `ak-layer-darken-*` in the snippet exists (apps/web/node_modules/@ariakit/tailwind/src/output.css:237).

title: Four vocabularies for the same four views
oneLine: Buttons say Compare/Difference/Current/Baseline, alt text says Reference/New image/Pixel diff, help and docs say Side by side/New only/Original only, code says side/diff/new/original.
verifierReason: All strings exist at the cited places: toolbar labels (review-workspace.tsx:845, :860, :874, :888), captions (screenshot-viewer.tsx:37-38), names (:219, :229, :245), empty texts (:220, :231-233), help text (review-workspace.tsx:174-175), announcement (:378-380, :928). The guide table is at docs/review-guide.md:31-37 and :76-77 (the report says 29-37). The guide line "Fit: Image scaled to the available viewer width" (docs/review-guide.md:35) is wrong, as the report says.

title: Fit never enlarges small images and squeezes tall or wide images; zoom has three fixed levels
oneLine: A 32 x 32 capture stays 32 x 32 in a 591 x 504 pane; a 640 x 3200 capture becomes a 94 px strip; only Fit, 100%, 200% exist, with no fit-width and no device-pixel 1:1.
verifierReason: The facts hold: M11 (a 32x32 image stays 32x32 at Fit), E6 (a 640x3200 image becomes a 94 px strip), `ReviewZoom = "fit" | 1 | 2` (apps/web/src/review/model.ts:3). Correction: the three levels are the written contract, "Provide fit/100%/200% inspection without changing stored reference pixels" (docs/simplification-audit/contract-issue-1.md:264), and the guide lists them (docs/review-guide.md:35-36). So "three fixed levels" is the selected minimum, not a defect. More levels are a design choice. 100% and 200% give a way to read small and tall images today, so I rate this low. The sizes of real Ariakit captures were not measured by the auditor or by me.

title: Phone layout: the first image starts at 63% of the screen, and the two images are never visible together

verifierReason: M15 reproduces: the first picture starts at y 535 of 844, and the mode group is 401 px wide in 366 px. Correction 1: "never visible together" is too strong. After a page scroll of about 500 px both pictures are on screen at once: baseline at y 42 to 240, current at 564 to 762, below two sticky headers (to about y 95) and above the action bar (y 755). About 73% and 96% of them show (verify/extra-output.txt E3; verify/screens/e3-phone-scrolled-505-dark-390.png). They are never both complete and never side by side. Correction 2: the stacked layout is the contract: "Keep a usable narrow layout with the list above the viewer and stacked comparison images. This is not a promise of certified mobile workflows at launch" (docs/simplification-audit/contract-issue-1.md:267). The guide says mobile workflows "have separate validation scope" (docs/review-guide.md:94). The open question in the report has this documented answer.

title: The disabled Approve button looks enabled while images load or fail
oneLine: While evidence loads the brand button is disabled but keeps the same background and opacity 1; only the label drops to 73% alpha (cross-lane with the action bar).
verifierReason: M9 reproduces: the disabled Approve button keeps background oklch(0.515341 0.1546 248.516) and opacity 1; only the text alpha changes to 0.73. The result is the same for an unchanged variant, and `title` is empty (verify/extra-output.txt E8). Screens 30, 36 and 41 show it. Cause that the report does not give: this is the look of the design system. `ak-disabled` only lowers the contrast scales (apps/web/node_modules/@ariakit/tailwind/src/output.css:113-116), and the recipe removes border, shadow and gradient (apps/web/src/components/ariakit/styles/control.ts:69-77). The layer fill stays. So a recipe change belongs upstream. The app-level option is to drop `$layer="brand"` while disabled, as the report says.

title: Accessible names and roles in the viewer
oneLine: Focusable scroll region has aria-label but no role; mode names include the shortcut letter ("Compare S") with no aria-keyshortcuts; pan label and title differ; exclusive modes use aria-pressed toggles.
verifierReason: Confirmed: the label of the scroll container is not in the accessibility snapshot (verify/extra-output.txt E2 lists figure, text, group, buttons and img only). Mode buttons are named "Compare S" with no `aria-keyshortcuts` (M14). Exclusive modes use `aria-pressed`. The Current icon is green (screenshot-viewer.tsx:98). Wrong: "The Difference button uses aria-disabled and a click gives only a screen-reader message". The rendered button has the native `disabled` attribute (`"disabledAttribute":true,"matchesDisabled":true`), because Ariakit turns `aria-disabled` into disabled. A click does nothing and writes no message. Only the D key writes the hidden status text (verify/extra2-output.txt F1; test review.browser.test.ts:1163-1168). Added: at 200% the figure name becomes "Baseline 600 × 400 Pan Reference", because the pan group is inside the figcaption (F2). No screen reader test was done by the auditor or by me.

title: View state is not shareable and not remembered

verifierReason: `useState<ReviewMode>("side")` and `useState<ReviewZoom>("fit")` are at review-workspace.tsx:197-198. The route search has only `comparison`, `item` and `variant` (apps/web/src/routes/runs.$runId.tsx:24-29). The sidebar state is stored (review-workspace.tsx:226-233). Mode and zoom reset on a reload and on a new run (`key={props.model.run.id}`, review-workspace.tsx:192), not between variants. The contract line "Preserve zoom and image position when possible" (docs/simplification-audit/contract-issue-1.md:264) supports the direction of the recommendation. The finding is from code reading, as the report says.

title: The viewer goes around the primitives, and its class hooks have no styles

So new vendored primitives change a recorded choice and the NOTICE pin. Doc drift that the report did not list: docs/simplification-implementation.md:87 still says "remaining CSS controls image painting and pan geometry" and links review.css.

title: Small text and state defects around the viewer

The stale pan after Retry is now measured, not only derived: the reference pane is at [300,150] before Retry, [300,150] after it, and [0,0] after Current then Compare. The control run without Retry keeps [300,150] (verify/extra-output.txt E5 and E5b). Corrections: (1) The announcement mismatch exists only through the D key. A click on the disabled button does nothing (verify/extra2-output.txt F1). (2) "Difference stays enabled for an unchanged variant" is true only when both images exist: legacy runs, or byte-identical local pairs that show "No pixels changed." title: The review page gives the screenshots less than a third of the viewport

verifierReason: IMPORTANT FOR ALL IDS: /Users/diegohaz/.claude/jobs/f65a6229/tmp/audit/ui-benchmark/report.md does not exist (checked 16:59 and 17:10; rg for 'BENCH-' in the job directory finds nothing). Corrections: (1) the 1920x1080 numbers (0.247/0.231) are a fixture artifact, because the 600/640 px fixture images are not enlarged in Fit; with an injected 1280x720 capture the share is 0.267 at 1440x900, 0.275 at 1280x720, and 0.342 at 1920x1080 (more than a third). (2) In Compare mode the image is width-limited (pane 591 px, image 555 px), so less chrome above does not enlarge a landscape image. title: The viewer cannot overlay, swipe, or blink the two images
oneLine: ReviewMode is side | diff | new | original; GitHub, Playwright, reg-cli, Chromatic, Percy, and Argos all offer overlay, slider, or toggle modes, and the stored diff is already a transparent pixelmatch mask so these need no backend change.
verifierReason: Overlay and swipe: confirmed absent. model.ts:2 has only 'side' | 'diff' | 'new' | 'original'; measured toolbar is Compare/Difference/Current/Baseline plus Fit/100%/200%. 'Blink' is refuted: F and G show Current and Baseline in the identical rectangle (measured left 548, top 408, 600x400 in both), and both images stay mounted with the hidden attribute (screenshot-viewer.tsx:216-241), so alternating F/G is an aligned, instant manual blink, the same as the Argos 'Single view' with left/right. Missing is only a one-key toggle, an automatic blink, and any hint in the UI. Feasibility: a mask overlay is cheap (production mask is red on transparent, png-comparison.ts:74 diffMask: true; images are same-origin), but it must be a toggle to keep selected decision P02 'Load diff when selected' (current-contract.md:149) and must add 'diff' to the required evidence (use-evidence.ts:95-102).

title: Zoomed panes scroll separately, so a zoomed comparison shows two different regions
oneLine: After two pan clicks at 200% the baseline pane is at scrollLeft 296, scrollTop 252 and the current pane stays at 0,0; each pane owns its scroll state and there is no drag or wheel zoom, while Argos keeps zoom and pan in sync.
verifierReason: Code: each pane owns its viewport ref, position and pan (screenshot-viewer.tsx:34-35, 73-80, 138-144); nothing links the panes. Measured at 200%: scrollTo on Reference gives (300,200) while New image stays (0,0); 'Pan New image right' moves only that pane to (296,0); a wheel moves only the hovered pane. Screenshot verify/screens/v03-zoom-200-desynced-dark-1440.png shows two different regions. Contract U04 selects 'Page-wide review arrows with pan buttons' and tests each pan button on its named pane; it does not require independent panes, so a linked pan is compatible, but review.browser.test.ts:1367-1387 and 1695-1757 must be reviewed. Extra: 8 pan buttons appear at zoom, and a zoom change keeps scroll pixels, not the image point ((400,250) at 200% became (45,0) at 100%).

title: Nothing shows where the change is inside the image
oneLine: The page prints only a ratio and a pixel count (for example 0.05%, 120 pixels) and no code reads the mask; Percy, Argos, Chromatic, and reg-cli highlight changed regions and step through them.
verifierReason: 'Nothing' is too strong. Difference mode shows a mask of changed pixels at image coordinates (screenshot-viewer.tsx:242-262). In production that mask is red pixels on a transparent background (packages/cli/src/png-comparison.ts:67-75, pixelmatch diffMask: true; legacy compare.ts:109-119). True parts: Compare/Current/Baseline show no marker, the mask has no screenshot below it, there is no bounding box, jump-to-change or minimap, and a size-changed pair has no mask (png-comparison.ts:64-66). Evidence warning: the fixture diff is the whole screenshot with a red fill (fixture-model.ts:26), so no screenshot in the lane shows a production-like mask. Not measured by the auditor, which is correct. Client-side bounding boxes are feasible (same-origin images, api/images.ts:55) but need the mask loaded (P02).

title: The variant strip hides the verdict and holds three variants
oneLine: Three of seven variant pills fit at 1440 wide (content 2079 px in a 1120 px strip), approved pills look like pending pills because VariantSummary renders no status, and every pill repeats the shared axis text.

After I approved chip 1 and rejected chip 2, their computed color, background and border equal an unreviewed chip. 'Three variants' is a fixture number: the fixture label adds '1280 x 720' (fixture-model.ts:19). Production builds six parts including the raw key (api/review.ts:469-482); with labels of that shape chips are 384-413 px and only 2 fit at 1440x900 (3 at 1920x1080), versus 3 with the fixture. title: The queue uses a 240 px card for 22 words and states each count three times
oneLine: Queue cards are 240 px high with 21 to 24 words and start at y=361, so two fit at 1440x900, while the history table shows the same runs in 64 px rows; Argos and Graphite use dense rows in sections.
verifierReason: Card size reproduced with the same nine mocked runs: 240 px high (236 at 390 px wide), 21-24 words, first card top y=361, 2 cards fully visible at 1440x900. 'Each count three times' is not reproduced. Measured text: run count twice ('4 runs are ready for review', '4 Runs to review'; routes/index.tsx:436-437, 452) plus the implied list; pending and rejected totals once each in the tiles (index.tsx:453-454) and the per-run parts once on each card (index.tsx:502-503), which are different numbers unless the queue has one run. title: The dashboard has no keyboard flow
oneLine: No key handler exists in routes/index.tsx or the pull route, and the run page has no key to return to the queue or open the next run; Linear, GitHub, Graphite, and Chromatic connect list and detail with keys.
verifierReason: Fact confirmed: the only key handlers in app code are review-workspace.tsx:395-447, 730 and item-list.tsx:316; routes/index.tsx has none. Wording correction: the dashboard has a native keyboard flow, because all controls are links or buttons; 8 Tab stops reach the first 'Review changes' link. The claim should read 'no shortcut keys and no list navigation'. The contract asks for keyboard-only operation of the review UI and has no dashboard shortcut requirement, so the need is a judgment.

title: One decision stops at one item, and equal diffs are not grouped
oneLine: The widest decision scope is all changed variants of one item behind a confirmation dialog; Percy has snapshot, matching-diff group, and build scopes and Chromatic has accept all, with public demand and a documented risk on both sides.
verifierReason: Facts confirmed: the client builds a command for one variant or one whole item only (use-review-session.ts:408-436) and no grouping code exists. Two corrections. (1) The scope is a selected contract decision, not an omission: D02 'Current variant; separate whole-item actions' and D21 'Shift+A / Shift+X' (contract-issue-1.md:410, 429), and U02 says 'Preserve D02/D03/D21 verdict scope'. A run-wide action needs a contract decision. (2) The server already accepts targets from several items when wholeItemKey is absent (review-commands.ts:166-170 selects by comparison_id and id list; api/review.ts:847-851 caps at maximumCaptures = 40,000), so no API change is needed. Platform risk, not measured: each target adds 4 statements to one D1 batch (review-commands.ts:227-271) and D1 documents 1000 queries per Worker invocation on Workers Paid (https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/platform/limits/), so about 245 targets can reach it if each batch statement counts; chunks break the 'every target or none' rule (review-guide.md:49). Grouping by (reference digest, candidate digest) is feasible client-side (model.ts:10-16).

title: The item list cannot sort by change size or filter by kind or axis
oneLine: Items keep the declared order and the filter has four status values, although ratio and changedPixels are in the model; Argos shipped sort by change size after a 248-file build report and Percy sorts by diff percent.
verifierReason: Confirmed: no sort (order is attention then accepted in model order, navigation.ts:34-47, item-list.tsx:91-101) and the filter has four status options only (screenshot-filter.tsx:17-22; measured All, Needs review, Approved, Rejected), so no kind filter. Refuted part: an axis filter exists as text search. matchesFilter searches variant keys, labels and labelParts (item-list.tsx:45-64); measured: typing 'firefox' reduces 3 items to 1, 'menu-dark' to 1. Limits are real: it filters items, not the variant strip, and nothing shows that it is possible. A sort is client-only (changedPixels and ratio are in model.ts:37, 40) but must go through onOrderChange (item-list.tsx:102-104) because arrow keys use that order.

title: The run page states the review status four times
oneLine: Sidebar text, header text, identity row text, and a badge all say needs review, plus a dot and a progress bar; the page shows 97 words and 26 controls for a one-item run, where Argos uses one progress chip.
verifierReason: Measured on the real route at 1440x900: '2 of 2 need review' in the sidebar (item-list.tsx:256), '2 of 2 need review' in the header (review-workspace.tsx:596-598), 'Changes need review' in the intro strip (:620), and the 'Needs review' badge (:642). Four status texts, as claimed. Scope correction: they report three scopes (item, run, variant); the true repetition is the run scope (count, label, progress bar). With Details open two more appear (:463-467). Contract limit for a redesign: 'Show counts such as 2 of 6 need review ... Counts and text must accompany color' (contract-issue-1.md:261), so counts and text next to color must stay. Severity lowered: repetition, no functional effect.

title: Three vocabularies name the same four image modes, and the guide uses labels that the UI does not have
oneLine: Buttons say Compare, Difference, Current, Baseline; accessible names say Reference, New image, Pixel diff; the guide says Side by side, Pixel diff, New only, Original only, and All runs where the UI says Queue.
verifierReason: Toolbar: Compare, Difference, Current, Baseline (review-workspace.tsx:845, 860, 874, 888). Help dialog and code: 'Side by side, red pixel diff, new image only, or original only' (review-workspace.tsx:174-175) and 'side' | 'diff' | 'new' | 'original' (model.ts:2). Pane accessible names and status text: 'Reference', 'New image', 'Pixel diff · red pixels changed' (screenshot-viewer.tsx:218, 229, 245; review-workspace.tsx:379, 928). The guide uses 'Side by side', 'Pixel diff', 'New only', 'Original only' (review-guide.md:31-34) and also 'All runs' (:92; UI says 'Queue'), 'Approve'/'Reject' (UI: 'Approve & next', 'Reject view') and 'Retry' (UI: 'Retry images'); rg finds none of these labels in apps/web/src.

title: The ? key does not open the shortcut list, and its button is below the fold
oneLine: The Keyboard help button sits at y=985 to 996 in a 900 px viewport and the key handler has no ? branch; Argos opens the full shortcut list with ?.
verifierReason: The key handler has no branch for '?' (review-workspace.tsx:395-442). Measured: Shift+Slash opens 0 dialogs on the fixture and on the real route; a click on the button opens 'Review with the keyboard'. The button is in the footer (review-workspace.tsx:1172-1178) and is below the fold on every tested viewport: y=985 of 900 (fixture), y=1002 of 900 and y=901 of 720 (real route), y=1086 of 1080. Additions: the button is a 26x26 icon; shortcut hints are visible on buttons (S, D, F, G, X, A, 1-6), so discovery is not zero. The contract key table has no '?', so adding it does not conflict; it must keep the excludesShortcuts rules (:88-97).

title: A rejection has no reason, and there is no place for a note
oneLine: ReviewCommand carries a verdict and targets only; Percy writes a comment on a change request and Argos, Chromatic, and Vercel pin comments to the pixel, so the reason for a rejection must travel through another channel.
verifierReason: Facts confirmed: ReviewCommand has no text field (model.ts:109-120), the decision table has no note column (migrations/0001_service.sql:143; 0024_core_simplification.sql:47), and the UI has no input. But this is a recorded non-goal: 'No ... comment system at launch' (docs/simplification-audit/contract-issue-1.md:57, binding per current-contract.md:7). So the current behavior is deliberate and a recommendation asks the maintainer to reopen that scope. Related provable gap: the run page has no link to the pull request where a note can be written; only routes/pulls.$pullNumber.tsx:281 links to GitHub.

title: Noise has no verdict of its own
oneLine: The verdict type is approved or rejected only; Argos (ignore and auto-ignore), Chromatic (ignore, flake filter, quarantine), and Happo (report flake) all added a third channel for diffs that the change did not cause.
verifierReason: Facts confirmed: ReviewVerdict is 'approved' | 'rejected' (model.ts:1) and the database has CHECK (verdict IN ('approved', 'rejected')) (migrations/0001_service.sql:143). Context: the contract excludes 'automatic approval of visual flakiness' at launch (contract-issue-1.md:57) and handles noise before review with the comparison settings, threshold 0.2 and pixel caps (current-contract.md:109). A third verdict is not a UI change: it touches the DB constraint, the check result ('Rejected ... still fails the visual check', review-guide.md:47) and approval reuse by exact identity (current-contract.md:184). Prior art exists (Argos 'I: Ignore a flaky change'), so whether to add it is a product decision.

title: `$layer="primary"` is not a recipe color; six primary surfaces including both sign-in buttons render neutral gray
oneLine: routes/index.tsx:301,310,346,508 and routes/pulls.$pullNumber.tsx:194,226 pass "primary"; the recipe knows only canvas/brand/secondary/success/warning/danger, so it emits inline `--layer-color: primary` and the computed background is rgb(238,238,238) in both schemes instead of brand rgb(0,106,187). A third sign-in button (runs.$runId.tsx:236) has no layer at all.
verifierReason: Six `$layer="primary"` sites exist (routes/index.tsx:301,310,346,508; routes/pulls.$pullNumber.tsx:194,226). `primary` is not in COLOR_VALUES (utils/styles.ts:6-13) and falls through to `--layer-color: primary` (layer.ariakit.react.tsx:97-100). Re-measured: button background 238,238,238 in dark and light; swapping the class to `ak-layer-brand` in the page gives 0,106,187 with white text, so the fix works. Corrections: the icon tile is pure white 255,255,255 (not gray); brand also appears in the header logo slot (app-shell.tsx:30); the contract asks for "mostly flat neutral controls" (contract-issue-1.md:247), so the intended color is a maintainer decision. The value was introduced one commit ago (f83fef6).

title: Selection is hand-rolled with `$lighten`; the selected sidebar row and variant chip are not visible in the light scheme
oneLine: item-list.tsx:199-202 and review-workspace.tsx:719-739 set `$selectedPush={false}` plus `$lighten={2}`; measured selected rgb(254,255,255) on rgb(252,253,253) = 1.017:1 in light (1.258:1 in dark), and the selected chip has no ring while unselected chips have one. The top nav with recipe defaults is visible in both schemes.
verifierReason: Variant chip claim is correct: glider to canvas 1.017:1 in light, selected chip has ring spread 0px while unselected chips have a 1px ring. Sidebar claim is overstated: the row surface is 1.017:1, but the Nav draws a 2x44px selected bar (28,29,29 on 252,253,253 in light; item-list.tsx:307) and the label weight changes, so the row is marked. Recommendation is feasible but weak: emulated `$lightnessOffset={2}` gives 1.348:1 in light; the recipe default measured on the top navigation gives about 1.16:1. Both are far below 3:1, which supports a colored selection. Contract U03 requires link and tab semantics for any new picker.

title: Nested frames lose their radius: square buttons, tiles, badges, and cards in five places
oneLine: Computed border-radius is 2px for Approve/Reject (review-workspace.tsx:1062-1097), "Open run" and clock tiles (index.tsx:580-597), table status badges (index.tsx:725-727), and popover alert cards and guide button, while the same components measure 6.5px, 7px, 10.5px, or full pill elsewhere. verifierReason: Radii re-measured: Approve/Reject 2px, Details 6.5px, Open run 2px, group icon tile 2px vs 7px, table badge 2px vs pill, popover card and guide button 2px. Cause confirmed by readme lines 397 and 816; adding `ak-frame-force` in the page restores 6.5px on Approve and a pill on the table badge. Corrections: Undo and "All 7 changed views" are also 2px, so the decision buttons are not the only square ones; the direct parent is the ButtonGroup frame (control.ts:501-506) inside the square bar; the app already uses `rounded-full!` as a workaround (operations-attention/index.tsx:493); a third radius of 8px exists in the footer and top nav. Cosmetic only, so low.

title: Text is muted with `opacity-*` in 13 places; two measured cases fail WCAG AA in the light scheme
oneLine: `opacity-50` on the 10px run meta strip (review-workspace.tsx:610) and the 11px item count (:551) measures 3.96:1 in light; `ak-ink-40/50` text of the same size measures 4.59:1 because ink keeps the AA floor.
verifierReason: The 13 `opacity-*` sites exist. All six contrast values reproduced (light: 3.962, 3.962, 4.737, 5.710, 4.588, 4.588). I also measured the two cases the auditor left unmeasured: details-panel `dt` labels at 12px are 3.962:1 in light (a third AA failure); the batch dialog description is 5.710:1 and passes. Note: `ak-ink-danger` style color names are not valid ink utilities, so only numeric `ak-ink-*` is a correct replacement.

title: A disabled brand button keeps its full brand fill; "Approve & next" looks active on read-only runs

verifierReason: Measurement is correct: disabled Approve keeps 0,106,187 and the label drops to alpha 0.733 (3.73:1 on the fill). But this is documented upstream behavior, not a recipe defect: the upstream sandbox has an example "Disabled brand — The color stays and the text fades." (ariakit/app/src/sandbox/ariakit-ui-button/index.react.tsx:990-999), the readme says `ak-disabled` "changes contrast settings only" (line 609), and the contract says to preserve copied disabled-state handling (contract-issue-1.md:256). The alternative "report upstream and wait for a fix" does not apply. What remains is an app-level design choice.

oneLine: In-memory Tailwind compile: 371,158 bytes with all sources, 332,500 without tabs+kbd (−10.4%, −5,364 gzip). The app uses native details, hand-rolled scroll boxes, and plain-text key lists where the vendored primitives exist.
verifierReason: No importer of kbd or tabs in apps/web. My in-memory compile reproduces the numbers exactly (371158 / 336336 / 332500 bytes; gzip 47886 / 43213 / 42522). title: `ControlButton` is imported as `Button`, the real `Button` as `FlatButton`, and font size is overridden by class 18 times
oneLine: control-button.tsx:4-13 adds `$rounded="lg" $p={2.5} text-[13px] leading-5` (and restates the default `$kind="flat"`); five files alias it to `Button`; its defaults are copied by hand in three other components; `$size` is used once while `className="text-xs"` is used 15 times. verifierReason: Aliases and wrapper code are as quoted; three button heights confirmed (25, 26, 35px). Corrections: nine of the fifteen `className="text-xs"` overrides are on the ControlButton alias and have no effect, because `.text-xs` precedes `.text-[13px]` in the stylesheet (css-full.css lines 2289 and 2302); "Shortcuts on" and "Close help" measure 13px. So the minimal recommendation (`$size="xs"`) also fails on the wrapper, since it emits the same class. The font `$size` variant is used twice, not once (NavLink at review-workspace.tsx:737, then contradicted by `text-xs` at :746). The `recipe` prop exists only upstream after the pin (87749801f).

verifierReason: Measurements confirmed: 1120px strip, 2079px content, 3 of 7 chips fully visible; view switch 366 vs 401px at 390px. Corrections: the missing scrollbar is the macOS and mobile overlay scrollbar (computed `scrollbar-width: auto`), so classic-scrollbar platforms do show one; the 1-6 key limit is contract behavior (contract-issue-1.md:273) and arrows reach all variants; "six of seven chips share..." is synthetic fixture data (fixture-model.ts:19), production labels come from api/review.ts:469-481; the action bar "All 7 changed views" is a second count hint; the contract requires the "full variant label" to stay available.

title: The hand-rolled history search shows keyboard focus only as a text underline; the select draws its ring inside the field border
oneLine: routes/index.tsx:656-662 uses `outline-none focus-visible:underline` on a raw input inside a Frame label; measured outline none with only text-decoration underline on focus, wrapper unchanged. Three fields use three focus styles; upstream InputGroup handles the group ring.
verifierReason: Re-measured with Tab focus in both schemes: search input `outline: none`, `text-decoration: underline`, wrapper unchanged; select `outline: solid 2px` inside the field. `focusWithin` exists (styles/focus.ts:86), so the alternatives are feasible. Correction: this is not a WCAG 2.4.7 failure; the W3C text counts the text caret as a focus indicator ("a vertical bar is displayed in the field", https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-visible.html). The real problem is three focus styles for three fields.
