title: Count strings have grammar and placeholder defects
oneLine: "1 view await approval." (index.tsx:502), "All 1 changed views…" (review-workspace.tsx:1055), "— changed pixels" (:647), "Color threshold 0.2; " with a trailing separator (api/review.ts:525), and "Comparison N" that is the run revision (2 becomes 4 after one save).
verifierReason: Confirmed: `1 view await approval.` (measured), `All 1/0 changed views…`, trailing `; ` in the threshold (normal production output because Ariakit sets threshold 0.2 + maxDiffPixels 0, playwright.config.ts:54-55), and `Comparison {n}` = run revision (api/review.ts:602, review-commands.ts:225). Wrong assumption: additions do have a count. The CLI sends the full image area with ratio 1 (packages/cli/src/local-comparison.ts:245-252; server requires ratio 1 at api/local-comparison.ts:570), so an addition reads `100.00% changed · 240,000 changed pixels`. Only removals give `— changed pixels` (packages/service/src/local-comparison.ts:247 `resultJson: null`).

title: Empty image panes and the pixel-diff hint make false or unneeded statements
oneLine: The Baseline pane always says "New image, no reference" when the image is null, also beside the error "Required reference evidence is unavailable", and "Pixel diff requires both a reference and a new image." shows on every addition and removal.
verifierReason: Confirmed: screenshot-viewer.tsx:219 always uses `New image, no reference`; the hint at review-workspace.tsx:924-930 has no mode condition; screen 69 shows the contradiction. Corrections: the Current pane text does depend on `kind === "unchanged"`; screen 62 is a fixture-only state; both strings are contract text (contract-issue-1.md:265 names `Removed, no new image` and requires to distinguish an absent reference from a load error, so the defect is a contract deviation and the `Removed` rewrite needs approval). Alternative (b) removes the only visible explanation: on key D the reason goes to an sr-only element (review-workspace.tsx:377-381, :1202).

title: Three sign-in texts, three access-denied texts, three loading texts
oneLine: Each route has its own gate copy; the dashboard uses a five-block marketing hero, the run page names "Ariakit" and offers only Retry on HTTP 403, a first 403 says "Your repository access changed.", and loading text names the access check.
verifierReason: Every table cell matches the three route files. Measured: first-load HTTP 403 on /?view=history prints `Repository access required Your repository access changed. …`. The run page has no account control in the forbidden state (runs.$runId.tsx:58). Corrections: the proposed gate shows `ariakit/ariakit`, but 401/403 bodies carry no repository (api/index.ts:38-44); all 403 codes (not_maintainer, invalid_identity, wrong_origin, invalid_origin) map to the same sentence; a skeleton must keep a status for assistive technology.

title: Error prefixes mislabel server responses, and one user message never arrives
oneLine: The client marks every HTTP 409 as "Conflict." (client.ts:274-276) although the server uses 409 for expired sessions, closed history, and missing records; HTTP 401 on save renders "Not saved. Sign in with GitHub." with no sign-in control; review-queue.ts:37 throws a plain Error that becomes the generic 503 text.
verifierReason: Re-measured all three outputs plus `history_closed` (also prefixed `Conflict.`) and the predecessor error (arrives as `The service is temporarily unavailable. Reference: …`). Worse than reported: after `review_session_expired`, `Refresh current state` cannot recover because client.ts:293-303 keeps the session promise; measured `{"sessionRequests":1,"commandSessions":["session-1","session-1"]}`. Alternative (b) (new status codes) conflicts with current-contract.md:83. Code `conflict` also covers non-reviewer conflicts (review-queue.ts:30, :46).

title: Pipeline and storage words reach the reviewer
oneLine: Attempt, Baseline revision, Comparison N, sealed, trusted Submit, CI bundle, promoted history, image bytes, evidence (17 strings), and sha256 digests in the details panel are printed without translation to the review task.
verifierReason: All cited strings exist. Wrong detail: digests are 64 hex characters without a `sha256:` prefix (packages/protocol/src/hash.ts:46-49); the 71-character value is from the auditor fixture. The proposed details panel drops the engine row, but contract-issue-1.md:292 says `Show changed pixel count, ratio, dimensions, engine, and threshold`; attempt and commit are contract run identity (issue-1:260). Severity lowered: most strings are in a closed panel or rare states.

title: The service status copy has five names for the feature and operator runbook text in every alert
oneLine: Operations, Service status, Service attention, operation alerts, and service alerts name one feature; the surface holds 596 of 2,256 client words (26%), with 15 alert bodies of 12 to 33 words and five sentences about its own mechanics.
verifierReason: Texts, 9-of-12 titles, 15 bodies (12 to 33 words), and the `Active captures` label for runs are confirmed. The recommendation is not feasible as written: the linked guide (apps/web/src/operations/README.md, 92 lines, 5 headings) has no per-alert sections and 0 matches for webhook, redeliver, backup row, admission limit, shard, so the alert bodies are the only runbook text. docs/review-guide.md:7 requires a recovery action and first/last-seen times per alert. `Refresh rule three times` is overstated (one sentence, one time stamp, one button).

title: Accessible names differ from visible labels, and shortcut letters are part of button names
oneLine: Captions say Baseline/Current/Difference while alt text says Reference/New image/Pixel diff; a pan button has aria-label "Pan Reference left" and title "Pan baseline left"; button names are "Approve & nextA" and "Compare S"; the Screenshots sidebar is named "Review navigation" and "Review items".
verifierReason: Playwright accessibility snapshot confirms `Compare S`, `Difference D`, `Current F`, `Baseline G`, `Reject view X`, `Approve & next A`, and images `Reference` / `New image` under captions Baseline / Current. Not a WCAG 2.5.3 failure (the name contains the visible label), so severity is low. One announcement starts with `Service alert update` (index.tsx:259), not `Service attention:`. The fix is feasible; the repo already uses aria-keyshortcuts (review-workspace.tsx:574) and an aria-hidden hint (variant-summary.tsx:129). At least ten test locators depend on the current names.

title: Heading punctuation and capitalization are inconsistent
oneLine: 11 headings end with a period ("Your review queue.") and the others do not; labels mix "Retry Undo", "fresh Submit", and "Approve & next"; five different retry phrasings exist.
verifierReason: The 11 titles with a period and the cited titles without one all match the lines. The style rule is a judgment. Extra evidence for the brand question: the logo text is `visonaut.` with a period (app-shell.tsx:34).

title: The UI does not say who is signed in or which run a tab holds
oneLine: No caller passes login to UserMenu, so it always shows "Account" with "Manage your GitHub session."; the tab title is always "Visonaut"; conflict text prints the numeric GitHub user ID.
verifierReason: user-menu.tsx:24 never receives `login`; no client code calls /api/session; __root.tsx:10 is the only title; the reviewer value is the numeric GitHub user ID (api/review.ts:500, :857, :902; authorization.ts:48). Correction: the `head` sample does not type-check because `loaderData` is optional (router-core route.d.ts:307) and the run loader returns a union; the dashboard and pull routes have no loader.

title: The preview shows dates from 1969 and says "Preview fixtures" four times on one screen
oneLine: preview-fixtures.ts uses createdAt: 0 and checkedAt: 0, so the public preview renders "Dec 31, 1969, 9:00 PM", and the fixture label is used as repository name, eyebrow, notice, and account label.
verifierReason: Measured on port 4310: date `Dec 31, 1969, 9:00 PM` (machine is UTC-3; it is Jan 1, 1970 in UTC) and `Preview fixtures` count = 3, not 4; the fourth label is `Preview account`. preview-fixtures.ts:86 and :107 use 0. Two of the strings are asserted by tests (route.browser.test.ts:568, :583).

title: The review guide names controls that the UI does not have
oneLine: docs/review-guide.md uses "Side by side", "Pixel diff", "New only", "Original only", "All runs", "Retry", and "The Runs page", and says Recompare is retired, while the UI shows Compare, Difference, Current, Baseline, Queue, Retry images, and the Recompare button.
verifierReason: Guide lines 15, 31-34, 39, 76-77, 88, 92 and the button lines match. The `digests` item is weak: the panel does show policy and profile digests (review-workspace.tsx:510-517). Cause: PR #252 changed the UI without the guide. The guide uses the contract names, so reverting the buttons is also an option. More drift not listed: guide :45 `Approve`/`Reject` vs `Approve & next`/`Reject view`; no `[` row in the guide key table.

title: Twelve strings cannot be shown by the production code path
oneLine: The recompare flow messages, two client fallbacks that the server always overrides, the noop message (no code sets noop), "@{login}", and three server recompare errors are unreachable from the UI.
verifierReason: All twelve strings checked. `pendingComparison` is set only in `recompare()` (use-review-session.ts:532), which returns at :509. No code assigns `noop: true`; git shows the producer was removed in 5712036 (PR #155), and a stored result is replayed only for the same command ID and request JSON (review-commands.ts:98-101), which a new page cannot produce. Note: `This closed review is read-only. Capture a new complete run.` is still shown, from the server (api/review.ts:595); only the client copy is dead.

title: Header links, the brand link, and the "Queue" button reload the whole document
oneLine: app-shell.tsx:16-18,29,53-58 and review-workspace.tsx:580 use plain <a href>; each header click loads a new document and refetches /api/runs, while the in-page <Link> to history costs zero requests.
verifierReason: Quotes match app-shell.tsx:15-19,29,53-58 and review-workspace.tsx:474-479,580. Re-measured on port 4310 with a window marker: header links, brand link and workspace "Queue" replace the document (document + /api/runs again); in-page "View history" and queue card links do not. No test or contract rule requires plain anchors. NavLink render={<Link/>} is feasible (same pattern at review-workspace.tsx:748-759). Minor wording fix: StrictMode is in the production entry too; only the double effect is dev-only.

title: No page ships data from the server, and each mount starts again with "Checking access…"
oneLine: Server HTML holds only loading text (index.tsx:161,176-184; runs.$runId.tsx:31-36 ssr:false, gcTime:0); the API call starts after hydration, Back remounts and refetches, scroll goes from 250 to 0, and no link preloads.
verifierReason: Finding confirmed: server HTML has only the loading text for /, /runs/<id> (ssr:!1) and /pulls/N; Back shows "Checking access…" at scrollY 0 and refetches /api/runs; no preload option exists. Contract supports it (current-contract.md:150, P03 "Use the existing router loaders"; only the run route has one). Corrections: the sample index loader has no ssr option, so it would run in the Worker where a relative fetch has no base URL or cookies (needs ssr:false or a server function); the alternative "remove gcTime: 0" with staleTime: Infinity shows a model that never refreshes and loses session decisions.

title: The alerts request waits for the run list, and the Service status page waits for a run list that it does not use
oneLine: OperationsAttention mounts only when the run list is ready (index.tsx:254-256,356-364); measured /api/operations starts after /api/runs ends on both / and /?view=service.
verifierReason: index.tsx:254-256,356,363-364 as quoted. Re-measured with 400 ms API delay: /api/runs 162->563 then /api/operations 594; service view 190->591 then 607; history view has the same serial order. Addition: the permission cache stores only resolved results (authorization.ts:60-82), so starting both requests together on a cold isolate causes two GitHub permission calls; the alert-count-in-/api/runs alternative avoids that.

title: After a click on a run, the old page stays for up to 1 second with no feedback, then the page goes blank
oneLine: runs.$runId.tsx sets pendingMinMs:0 but no pendingMs, so the 1000 ms router default applies: queue still shown at 152, 501, 902 ms after the click, then a one-line pending page without account menu.
verifierReason: Behavior confirmed: router default is defaultPendingMs 1000 (router-core router.js:626-627 and TanStack docs); with a 3 s API delay the queue stays until 951 ms, the pending text shows at 1151 ms with 4 header controls, the workspace at 3601 ms; with 600 ms no pending state shows. Correction: the installed @tanstack/react-router 1.170.38 Link exposes only { isActive } (link.d.ts:38-42), no transition state and no data-transitioning; use useRouterState status === 'pending' instead.

title: The dev stylesheet contains Tailwind and ui.css two times for the root, and four times on the run route
oneLine: styles.css imports review.css, which imports tailwindcss and ui.css again; dev root CSS is 883,047 B with 2 copies and the run route 1,625,503 B with 4 copies (production build not measured).
verifierReason: Dev measurement reproduces (883,047 B with 2 copies; 1,625,503 B with 4). But the quoted styles.css:1-3 does not exist: the file is one line, @import "./review.css". The real cause is the dev stylesheet endpoint adding CSS dependency modules separately. The existing production build has one stylesheet (464,666 B, 60,125 gzip) with one copy, so there is no production impact. The recommendation as written (delete review.css and its @import) would leave styles.css empty and remove all styles; the two imports must move into styles.css first.

title: The review workspace uses 408 px of a 900 px viewport before the first image pixel
oneLine: App header 48, main header 48, identity strip 26, heading, variant chips, view controls, and captions stack above the image; the image band is 48% of a 1440x900 viewport and 28% of a 390x844 one, with three links to "/".
verifierReason: Band geometry re-measured and equal: headers 0-48, 48-96, strip 96-122, heading 154, chips 233, controls 286, first image pixel 408 at 1440x900 (518 at 390x844); three links to / in the top 96 px; repeated facts at the cited lines. Added contract fact the auditor missed: U02 "Use one review shell" (current-contract.md:143) already selects one compact header and moving run facts to Details, and its 'before' number was y385, so the selected decision is not delivered. The choice of redesign is judgment.

title: Each page has the document title "Visonaut"
oneLine: __root.tsx:10 sets the only title; /, history, service, a run, a pull page, and /nope all report "Visonaut".
verifierReason: __root.tsx:10 is the only title; no other head option or document.title in apps/web/src. Re-measured: all six URLs return the title "Visonaut". Correction to the sample: the loader can return { status: 'guest' }, so loaderData?.model.run.title throws; it needs loaderData?.model?.run.title. Queue and pull pages have no loader, so they need an effect until loaders exist.

title: URL model: pages are a search parameter, a pull request link works only with a check ID, and view state is not in the URL
oneLine: /?view= selects three pages in one 752-line route; /pulls/N without check always 404s (api/review.ts:739-741) and then redirects to a run UUID; the run model has the PR number only inside its title string; mode and zoom are local state.
verifierReason: All quotes verified: index.tsx:40-42 (752-line file), api/review.ts:739 check regex then 404, pulls route 70-72/82/216-223, review.ts:561 title string, local mode/zoom state. Measured /pulls/4817 without check: "Review unavailable" with only Retry and no GitHub link. Addition: /pulls/N?check= and /runs/<id> are stored as GitHub check details_url and compared in pre-run-checks.ts:261,328,369,508-511, so both shapes must keep working; the proposed table keeps them. The preferred URL model itself is judgment.

title: Item and variant links add history entries and scroll the page to the top; keyboard selection replaces the entry
oneLine: Links in item-list.tsx:205 and review-workspace.tsx:750 push (history 8 to 9 to 10) while navigate uses replace (10 to 10); both reset scrollY from 200 to 0, against 200 to 149 without the router.
verifierReason: Link clicks push and reset scroll (history 2->3, scrollY 200->0): confirmed. "Keyboard selection replaces the entry" is only true with focus outside the chip row (2->2). After a mouse click focus stays on the chip, and each arrow key then pushes (3->4->5) because followVariantLink (review-workspace.tsx:99-121) calls click() on a Link without replace. replace and resetScroll exist in the installed types, and adding them to the Link fixes this path too.

title: An unknown URL shows the bare text "Not Found", a missing run offers only "Retry", and the root has no error component
oneLine:
No notFoundComponent or errorComponent on the root or router; GET /nope returns

Not Found

with no shell, and RunError shows Retry for 404 and 403.
verifierReason:
GET /nope returns 404 with body

Not Found

, 0 links, and the router console warning about a missing notFoundComponent. Run 403 and 404 states offer only a 724 px wide Retry. No errorComponent on index or pulls routes. Production path confirmed: assets config has no not_found_handling. Addition: the root component renders , so a root errorComponent must render the document or use shellComponent.

title: With a root font size above 16 px, the item list and the details panel cannot be opened between 1024 px and 64rem
oneLine: JS uses matchMedia(max-width: 1023px) (review-workspace.tsx:211-213) while CSS uses the 64rem container query ($show="5xl"); at a 20 px root and 1100 px width there is no sidebar, no toggle, no dialog button, and 0 item links.
verifierReason: Confirmed and measured for both the item list and the details panel: at a 20 px root and 1100 or 1279 px width there is no sidebar, no toggle, no dialog button, and Details opens nothing. The scope is wider than reported: with the default 16 px root and a scrollbar that takes 15 px, windows 1024-1038 px wide have the same dead zone (shell 1009-1023 px, matchMedia false). The recommended rem media query does not fix that case; only the CSS-decides-both-sides alternative does. Scrollbar case simulated with ::-webkit-scrollbar, not tested on Windows.

title: The first Tab stop on a run page is the whole page, and there is no skip link
oneLine: Shell has tabIndex={0} and aria-label on a div without role (review-workspace.tsx:528-534); first Tab focuses a 1440x994 div with a 1 px edge outline, and nine stops come before main.
verifierReason: First Tab stop is div.shell (role null, aria-label, 1440x994, outline auto 1px); nine stops before main on a run, six on the dashboard; no skip link. tabIndex -1 is feasible because the key handler is on the document (contract U04). Correction: the label is used by tests in four files (route, pulls, scale, review browser tests), not only at the two cited lines.

title: Small muted text has a 3.96:1 contrast in the light scheme, uses pixel sizes that do not follow the user font size, and is muted in six different ways
oneLine: text-[10px] opacity-50 on the run identity strip gives 3.96:1 in light (5.34:1 dark); six mute mechanisms (ak-ink-60 x45, opacity-60 x9, opacity-50 x4, ...) and 13 font sizes, 4 of them in px.
verifierReason: Re-measured contrast: strip and sidebar count 3.96:1 in light (5.34 dark), changed-pixels line 4.74, sidebar title 5.71. Counts reproduce exactly (ak-ink-60 45, opacity-60 9, opacity-50 4, opacity-55 1, ak-ink-50 1, ak-ink-40 1; 13 font sizes). The ink floor claim is true: ak-ink-50 and ak-ink-40 both compute to alpha 0.5418 in light, and ak-ink-60 gives 5.71:1, so the minimal alternative passes AA.

title: Sign-in, sign-out, and access errors exist three times, with different layout, copy, and recovery actions
oneLine: index, runs, and pulls each implement createAuthClient calls (6 sites), a different sign-in card, and different 403 actions; the run 403 state has only Retry and no account menu, and sign-out behaves differently per route.
verifierReason: All cited ranges match. Measured each gate: queue guest button 369x33 primary, run guest 724x33 flat, pull guest 161x33 primary; 403 actions differ (Retry + Use another account / Retry only / Use another account only); account menu only on the queue 403. Sign-out differs at index.tsx:234, runs route 193, pulls route 142; createAuthClient at six places. Screenshots show three different designs.

title: The account menu never shows the signed-in user; the login prop and two identity endpoints have no caller
oneLine: UserMenu accepts login but no caller passes it, so the label is always "Account"; /api/me (server.ts:88-104) and /api/session (api/review.ts:713-721) have no client call in the repository.
verifierReason: UI part confirmed: no caller passes login, the menu shows "Account", and context.identity.login has one use. /api/session has no reference anywhere in the repository. /api/me has no client caller, but docs/operations/retire-preview-auth-at-cutover.md:59 names it as a manual probe and evidence files record it, so a removal must update that runbook. docs/review-evidence-plan.md:62 still claims routes call /api/me first.

title: There is no layout route; four call sites build their own shell and header, and the header differs between pages
oneLine: index, pulls, runs, and review-workspace each render Shell plus AppHeader with a repeated --shell-header-step hack; text-sm on one shell shifts the header by 1.5 px, and controls go from 4 to 6 between loading and ready.
verifierReason: Four call sites verified, each repeating the header-step class; only the dashboard has text-sm. Re-measured header: 14 px shell font, padding 10.5 px, nav 527.6/384.8/31.6 on the dashboard against 16 px, 12 px, 526.4/387.3/32.5 on run and pull pages; aria-current only in the index HTML. A pathless layout route and nested shells are supported.

title: Keyboard help sits in a page footer below the fold, next to a "Recompare stored run" button that can never be enabled
oneLine: ShellFooter (review-workspace.tsx:1172-1205) starts at 954 px on a 900 px viewport; the server always sends recompareAllowed:false (api/review.ts:592) and the endpoint always throws, and the guide says the control is retired.
verifierReason: recompareAllowed: false is the only server value (review.ts:592) and the endpoint always throws (950-986), so the control is dead; no help trigger exists outside the footer and '?' opens nothing. Corrections: the footer is below the fold at 1440x900 and 1440x1100 but visible at 1920x1200 and 2560x1440; the auditor's footer screenshot shows an enabled button because the mock omits recompareAllowed, while the production shape shows a disabled button plus a 16 px sentence. Removing the endpoint changes 409 behavior asserted by three API test files; removing only the UI has no contract risk.

title: One object has several names in the navigation, and the review guide names controls that do not exist
oneLine: Item is also screenshot and review item, variant is also view and capture, alerts have five names; docs/review-guide.md names a "Runs page" and an "All runs" control that are not in the UI.
verifierReason: Every cited string is at the cited line in review-workspace.tsx, item-list.tsx, index.tsx, app-shell.tsx and operations-attention/index.tsx. review-guide.md:15, 31-34 and 92 name a "Runs page", four view names and "All runs" that the UI does not have; the viewer mixes Baseline/Current captions with Reference/New image labels. Also the guide says Approve/Reject while buttons say "Approve & next" and "Reject view".

title: Shell parts are overridden with ! classes, controls are hand-built where primitives exist, and two vendored components have no user
oneLine: Four !important overrides on shell parts, native progress, manual separator, four ak.Dialog with manual backdrops, title= tooltips; the vendored copy has 13 components against 27 upstream, and kbd and tabs are unused.
verifierReason: Overrides, hand-built controls and the four ak.Dialog uses are at the cited lines; 13 vendored against 27 upstream components; kbd and tabs have no user. Contract notes the auditor missed: D10 (current-contract.md:54) says keep the component set with no pruning or replacement, so the unused components are deliberate and an upstream update needs a decision; U03 (line 144) selects variant tabs, but the code uses Nav links and Tabs is unused, which is contract drift.

title: Visual details in the shell chrome
oneLine: Details panel header misaligned by 22 px with the strip, "Accepted" at 16 px beside 12 px rows, 724 px wide flat buttons that look like text, loading text not centered, 1.8 px bold shift on the selected nav link, favicon differs from the header mark.
verifierReason: All eight items re-measured or seen on screen: details header 96-144 against strip 96-122; Accepted toggle 16 px against 12 px rows; loading text at (336,60) on the run page and (160,69) on the queue; 724x33 and 592x33 flat buttons; current link 131.8 px against 130.0 px; pill plus underline on the current link; favicon V against the aperture mark; account popover over "Refresh runs". The weight of the list is judgment.

title: Header controls are smaller than 24 px at a 390 px width, and shortcut letters show on touch layouts
oneLine: At 390 px the brand link is 19x23 px, the account button 29x29, and the workspace "Queue" link 68x23; key letters show on touch; the guide puts phones outside the launch scope.
verifierReason: At 390x844: brand 19x23, nav links 33x33, account 29x29, Queue 68x23, previous and next 29x29; shortcut letters show on view and action buttons. WCAG 2.5.8 text and its spacing exception are stated correctly; the guide puts mobile outside launch scope. Addition: the view-mode group is cut at the right edge with no scroll hint.

title: The sidebar preference script runs in the head of each page, but only a client-only route reads it
oneLine: __root.tsx:21-26 adds an inline script and suppressHydrationWarning for a value that only the ssr:false workspace reads in a state initializer; no CSS reads the attribute.
verifierReason: The head script is in every document, including the 404 page. The only reader is review-workspace.tsx:202-206, the route has ssr: false, and no CSS or test reads the attribute, so the initializer can read localStorage directly and the typeof document branch cannot run.

title: Shortcuts stop after a mouse click on a variant pill
oneLine: `.review-variants` is in the shortcut exclusion selector (review-workspace.tsx:94-96), so after a click on a pill A/X/S/D/F/G, arrows and 1-6 do nothing (measured: calls 0, mode stays side, in fixture and routed app).
verifierReason: Re-measured on the fixture and on the routed app: after a click on a variant pill, focus is on the link inside `.review-variants` (review-workspace.tsx:94-96, 729) and `A`, `D`, `ArrowDown`, `3` do nothing (calls 0, mode stays `side`). The keyboard path (ArrowRight inside the strip, then `A`) fails too. Correction: the fix can be the removal of `.review-variants` from the selector, because `followVariantLink` already calls `preventDefault()` (line 115) and the page handler returns on `defaultPrevented` (line 396). Alternative (a) with `stopPropagation()` is not needed and does not stop a second listener on `document` in the routed app.

title: Focus jumps to the page root after each decision and after Undo
oneLine: `onFocus()` (use-review-session.ts:317, 470) focuses the role-less root `div` (tabIndex 0, aria-label); next Tab goes to the brand link and Approve is 30 Tab presses away; the root is also the first tab stop.
verifierReason: Behavior confirmed: after Enter on Approve or Undo, focus is on the role-less root `div` (use-review-session.ts:313-317, 470; review-workspace.tsx:248, 528-534); root is tab stop 1 on the routed page; 30 Tab presses back to Approve. Correction: the recommended fix (remove `onFocus()`) does not keep focus on the button. Approve and Reject are `disabled` while the next images load (lines 1064-1070, 1082-1088); measured 2 frames disabled, then `document.activeElement` is BODY. The fix also needs `accessibleWhenDisabled` or no disabling during load. `docs/current-contract.md:196, 198` list focus as behavior to preserve. The claim that assistive technology gets no name is not tested. Shortcut users are not affected, so medium.

title: Item list unreachable when the px media query and the rem container query disagree
oneLine: `narrow` uses `(max-width: 1023px)` but the sidebar uses `@5xl/shell` (64rem); with a 20px default font at 1200px, or a 15px scrollbar at 1024-1038px, sidebar, toggle and the Screenshots button are all hidden (0 rows visible).
verifierReason: Re-measured: default font 20px at 1200px gives no sidebar, no toggle, no Screenshots button, 0 of 3 rows visible; emulated 15px scrollbar gives the same at 1024 to 1038 and the sidebar returns at 1039. Limit: with native macOS overlay scrollbars at 1030 the sidebar is visible, so the scrollbar case needs space-taking scrollbars. Alternative (b) `(width < 64rem)` verified for the font case. Large effect, small trigger population, so low.

title: Shift+A and Shift+X skip the confirmation that the button path requires
oneLine: `Shift+A` saved 7 targets at once with no dialog (review-workspace.tsx:426-429), while the button "All N changed views…" opens a confirmation dialog first (1042-1059, 1242-1296).

title: Ideas that widen the scope of a decision need rules that do not exist
oneLine: Contact sheet multi-select, a feed with an implicit target, group approval, and a buffered key press are not covered by the evidence-ready, frozen-target, and one-command rules.
verifierReason: The server accepts targets of more than one item when wholeItemKey is absent (review-commands.ts:166-170) and adds four statements for each target; only the client enforces 'evidence currently displayed'. It is a design limit; nothing shipped is wrong. D1 documents 1000 queries per invocation; how a batch counts is not stated.

title: Shortcuts compare event.key: letters fail on non-Latin layouts, and unshifted digits fail on AZERTY
oneLine: Synthetic events: a Cyrillic key on KeyA saves nothing and an unshifted AZERTY digit selects no variant; a key-then-code fallback fixes both.
verifierReason: Synthetic events confirm the facts (Cyrillic key: 0 calls; AZERTY digit: no selection; Caps Lock A: one target). The recommended snippet also fires for key 'Process' and 'Dead' and breaks the '[' compare; it needs an isComposing guard and a one-character check. No real layout was tested.

title: No request reaches POST /validate, but the contract says the Worker validates uploads
oneLine: uploadStagedImage calls the comparator only for non-local capabilities (workflow-owned.ts:1066), which the service no longer issues; local uploads are stored after a size and SHA-256 check only, so validation adds zero ingest latency and the Worker does no work.
verifierReason: I could not refute it. Every citation is correct. `apps/web/src/api/workflow-owned.ts:1066-1067` is the only `comparator.fetch` call (rg over apps/web/src and packages, tests excluded). `:182-187` throws HTTP 409 for a reservation without `local-v1`. Both capability issuers set local mode (`workflow-owned.ts:383`; `apps/web/src/api/local-comparison.ts:297` and `:444-447`). A capability lives 15 minutes at most (`packages/security/src/capabilities.ts:98`, `:123`). The repository's own test asserts the behavior: `workflow-owned.test.ts:1740-1750` has `expect(compare).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`. For a local upload the service checks only size and SHA-256 (`workflow-owned.ts:1042`), and `apps/web/migrations/0001_service.sql:73` forces `validated = 1` for every row. The documents disagree: `docs/current-contract.md:32` and `:188`, `README.md:5`. Corrections: (1) Severity is medium, not high. There is no runtime harm today, and the public image route sends `nosniff` and a sandbox CSP (`apps/web/src/api/images.ts:51-54`). The defect is a contract mismatch plus an idle Worker. (2) Removal touches more places than the two snippets: `apps/web/src/runtime.ts:45`, `:49`, `:263`; `apps/web/src/api/context.ts:78`; `apps/web/wrangler.jsonc:85-90`; `.github/workflows/deploy.yml:130-131` and the assertion at `:352-354`; `deploy-web-target.test.mjs:119`; and test fixtures that mint a capability without the mode (`workflow-owned.test.ts:393-404`, `api.test.ts:343`). (3) The sentence 'Cloudflare refuses to delete a Worker while a service binding points to it' is not in the official page. The page says only that the target Worker must be deployed first (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/bindings/service-bindings/). The order advice is still correct. (4) New measurement from the saved deploy log of run 37357689984 (2026-10-05): the comparator deploy step takes 6.96 s on each push to main (18:47:08.25 to 18:47:15.21). (5) Production request counts were not read by the auditor or by me. 'No request' is a source proof, not a traffic measurement.
secondLensReason: The facts are correct: the only comparator call is workflow-owned.ts:1066-1067 behind comparisonMode !== local; both issuers always set local (workflow-owned.ts:383, local-comparison.ts:440), other modes are rejected (workflow-owned.ts:182-187), and a capability lives at most 15 minutes (capabilities.ts:98, :123). So a production upload does size and SHA-256 (1038-1044), a signed-receipt check (1090-1101), then writes straight to the IMAGES bucket (1103-1106) that the public route serves. The contract text is wrong in four places (current-contract.md:24, :32, :48 D03, :59 D16; retire-server-comparison.md:39). I lower severity from high to medium: latency is zero, run cost is zero requests, and I found no exploit path because images.ts:48-57 sends nosniff, a sandbox CSP and same-origin CORP, and the trusted Submit job decodes every capture (cli png-comparison.ts:15,25; local-comparison.ts:239). Production request count of visonaut-compare was not verified (needs Cloudflare analytics). Fix feasibility: removal is possible but runtime.ts:48-54 (requireBackendBindings), deploy.yml:352-354 and :130-131, and deploy-infrastructure.mjs:32-40 must change in the same build or every backend request returns 503 or the deploy fails; D03 is an explicit keep rule, so removal needs an approved contract change; delete the Worker only after the rollback window. Inline validateImage has a memory risk the report omits: inflateBounded is async (binary.ts:40-67) and the CLI sends 5 parallel PUTs (engine.ts:33), about 85 MB at the pixel bound against the 128 MB isolate limit (calculation, not measured). Calling /validate for local uploads meets the one-image-per-isolate gate and causes 503 retries. Counter-argument: nothing is broken at runtime, the service already trusts the Submit job for the receipt, and a documentation correction is the cheap accurate action.

title: The production comparator binds D1, R2, and the operations queue, but its code uses none of them
oneLine: apps/compare/wrangler.jsonc:38-59 gives the fetch-only image parser write access to the production database, image bucket, and operations queue; index.ts takes no env.
verifierReason: Citations are correct. `apps/compare/wrangler.jsonc:38-59` binds DB, IMAGES, and OPERATIONS. `apps/compare/src/index.ts:5` is `async fetch(request: Request)` with no `env` parameter. `rg 'env\.' apps/compare/src` finds only `probe.ts:26` (PROBE_TOKEN), which is a different Worker. New live proof that the auditor did not have: the deploy log of run 37357689984 (2026-10-05) prints for visonaut-compare `env.OPERATIONS (inherited)`, `env.DB (visonaut)`, `env.IMAGES (visonaut-images)`, and `Producer for visonaut-production-operations`. The retention is deliberate but has no stated reason (`apps/compare/README.md:18`). No contract line requires these bindings on this Worker; the runbook protects the resources, not the bindings (`docs/operations/retire-server-comparison.md:47-49`). The recommendation is feasible: bindings are not inherited between environments and are declared per environment (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/configuration/). Severity is low, not medium: the Worker has `workers_dev: false`, no route, and no caller (CMP-01), so the extra privilege is not reachable today.

title: Two guards for a completed retirement still gate each production deploy
oneLine: deploy.yml:117-124 reads two idle comparison queues by hard-coded ID and a Container binding on every deploy; deleting the queues would fail all later deploys.
verifierReason: Citations are correct: `.github/workflows/deploy.yml:117-124`; `deploy-comparison-retirement.mjs:5-9`, `:32`, `:38-42`; `deploy-infrastructure.mjs:7-8`, `:11`. No Wrangler file defines `VISONAUT_CODEC_BACKEND`. New measured proof from the saved deploy log of run 37357689984: the Container guard step took 0.41 s and the queue guard step took 0.34 s. The log also shows that the repository variable `VISONAUT_CONTAINER_RETIREMENT_VERIFIED` is still set, with `observedAt` 1790888614976 = 2026-10-01T21:03Z. That receipt was four days old. The guard requires a receipt younger than one hour when the binding exists (`deploy-infrastructure.mjs:21-26`). The step passed, so the live `CODEC_CONTAINER` binding is absent and the guard is a no-op. The queue-deletion hazard is real: `assert(response.ok, ...)` fails on HTTP 404. Removal is feasible: no workflow test asserts that the two steps exist (`deploy-migrations.test.mjs` checks other text). Corrections: the two test files have 103 lines (70 + 33), not 97. Severity is low: the cost is 0.75 s and three API reads for each deploy, and a failure needs a future queue deletion or an API error.

title: The legacy comparison engine and its helpers have no production caller
oneLine: process.ts, the RGBA engine, jSquash encode, the capacity wait branch, both probes, and the Container (about 2,100 lines) are reached only by tests, scripts, and manual diagnostics.
verifierReason: Citations are correct. `processComparisonTask` has these importers only: `apps/compare/test/process.test.ts:6` and `apps/web/src/api/tolerated-mask.test.ts:11`; `apps/compare/container/transport.ts:3` takes two symbols from the same file. `compareImages`, `createThumbnail`, `validatePolicy`, and `selectedComparisonPolicy` have importers only in probes, tests, scripts, and tooling. The production entry `apps/compare/src/index.ts:1-2` imports only `codecs.ts` and `validate.ts`. `validate.ts:22` passes no wait time, so the wait code at `capacity.ts:17-30` is dead. `probe.ts:37-46` compares an image with itself, so the mask branch cannot run. Line counts match (container 573, tests 682, probes 102, scripts 518, lock file 651). The contract keeps diagnostics (`docs/current-contract.md:188`; `docs/operations/retire-server-comparison.md:39`), and the report says so and splits the steps correctly. Correction for step 3: more files depend on the engine and on `jsquash.ts` than the report lists: `packages/service/src/service.test.ts:17`, `apps/web/src/api/api.test.ts:8-9`, `apps/web/src/api/workflow-owned.test.ts:3678`, `packages/compare/test/codecs.ts`, and `tooling/evidence/e01-clients/run.mjs:10`. These tests need another codec helper before the deletion.

title: validateImage spends about half of its time in a bitwise CRC-32 and keeps two copies of the inflated image
oneLine: Measured locally: CRC-32 is 2.18 ms of 4.52 ms at mean capture size (table CRC 0.156 ms), the IDAT size check retains 2 x 8.2 MB, and the CLI runs the validator twice per capture.
verifierReason: Code citations are correct: `packages/compare/src/binary.ts:14-23`, `:56`, `:66`; `png.ts:75`, `:200-201`; CLI `packages/cli/src/local-comparison.ts:44` and `:239`, before the shortcut at `:260-273`. I ran the auditor scripts again: CRC 2.26 ms of 4.94 ms at 640x845; 7.49 ms of 14.96 ms at 1248x1650; the inflate helper holds 8,238,450 bytes two times. Corrections: (1) The 82,053-byte sample is not 'corpus mean size'. It has the mean pixel count, but the recorded mean encoded size is 28,292 bytes (`packages/compare/evidence/corpus-study.json:10`). CRC cost follows encoded bytes. My script `verify/crc-share-density.mjs` gives a CRC share of 52% for the auditor sample, 33% at 34,367 bytes (near the corpus density), and 3% for a flat image. 'About half' is the upper end. (2) The recommended snippet uses `for (const byte of bytes)` and `?? 0`. As written it takes 1.64 ms for 295,311 bytes. The indexed loop that the auditor measured takes 0.49 ms. The current code takes 7.17 ms (`verify/crc-snippet-and-decode.mjs`). Use `for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length; i += 1)`. (3) The live run has 3,832 variants, not 3,582 (orchestrator measurement in live-authenticated.md). (4) In the CLI path the CRC is checked two times for each decode, because pngjs checks it by default (`pngjs/lib/parser.js:8`) and `png-comparison.ts:25` passes no option. Severity is low: the CRC saving is about 6 to 15 s of CPU for a 3,832-capture Submit on this machine. The second full decode at `local-comparison.ts:239` costs more: 12.3 ms for each capture with the auditor sample, about 47 s in total. The memory claim (16.5 MB of extra transient memory) is correct.

title: The image bounds were sized for the Worker isolate, and the largest known capture uses 98% of the pixel bound
oneLine: maxPixels is 2,100,000 (types.ts:8-14, still marked provisional) while the capture adapter accepts 32,000,000 pixels and 20 MiB, so an oversized capture fails only at trusted Submit.
verifierReason: Citations are correct: `packages/compare/src/types.ts:8-14`; `packages/compare/evidence/corpus-study.json:14-18` (maximum 2,059,200 pixels = 98.06% of 2,100,000); `hosted-resource-evidence.md:23`; adapter bounds at `packages/playwright/src/visual.ts:352` and `:356`; service use at `apps/web/src/api/local-comparison.ts:548`. rg finds no 2.1 megapixel check in `packages/playwright`. The first check of the small bound is `validateLocalImages` (`packages/cli/src/engine.ts:781`), so the failure comes at Submit and stops the complete run. Hosted evidence supports the origin of the bound: isolate memory was 101 MB of the 128 MB limit (`hosted-resource-summary.json:59`; https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/). Corrections: (1) At width 1248, 1682 rows still fit. 33 more rows exceed the bound, not 32. (2) The adapter's 32 megapixel check applies to the source screenshot. The cropped item has only the 20 MiB check (`visual.ts:387-403`). (3) The snippet needs `imageLimits` in the published adapter, but the adapter does not depend on `@visonaut/compare`. Move the constant to `@visonaut/protocol` or bundle it. (4) A larger bound needs a contract decision (`docs/current-contract.md:57`), as the report says. The size of the current largest capture was not measured by the auditor or by me, so confidence stays medium.

title: If /validate stays, its current design adds avoidable latency and reports failures incorrectly
oneLine: One codec token per isolate with no wait gave [200,503,503,503,503] for five concurrent calls; each 503 costs the CLI at least 1 s, and any comparator 5xx becomes a permanent invalid_image.
verifierReason: Citations are correct: `apps/compare/src/capacity.ts:17-20`; `packages/cli/src/engine.ts:33`; `packages/cli/src/http.ts:109`; `workflow-owned.ts:1042`, `:1075-1077`, `:1081-1087`; `packages/compare/src/image.ts:35`, `:42`. I ran `measure-concurrency.mjs` again: each of five rounds gave `[200, 503, 503, 503, 503]`. The `.buffer` hazard at `image.ts:42` is real and is safe today only because `png.ts:205` and `webp.ts:82` return arrays that own their buffer. The path has no caller today (CMP-01), so the impact is conditional, as the report says. Corrections: (1) The example 'an HTTP 500 from a CPU or memory limit' is not proved. The official service binding page does not say what the caller receives when the target fails. The mapping defect itself is proved for each non-503 error status. (2) The same page says that both Workers run 'on the same thread of the same Cloudflare server' by default. Thus uploads that reach one web isolate also reach one compare isolate. This makes the one-isolate case plausible, but it was not measured on Cloudflare. (3) The second snippet returns code `validation_busy` for a permanent failure. The CLI then retries up to 25 times (`http.ts:7`, `:196-200`). The existing code `service_unavailable` (`http.ts:212`) fits better.

title: Both consumers discard the validation error codes
oneLine: png-comparison.ts:34-39 replaces every ImageValidationError code with one generic sentence, so a failed Submit does not say whether size, profile, or CRC caused it.
verifierReason: Citations are correct. `packages/cli/src/png-comparison.ts:34-39` replaces each `ImageValidationError` with one sentence: 'An image is not a supported, bounded PNG. Capture the image again.' `workflow-owned.ts:1075-1077` does the same, but that consumer is not reachable (CMP-01), so only the CLI matters in practice. Addition: the CLI message also names no capture. `decodePng` gets no item key, and the callers at `packages/cli/src/local-comparison.ts:44`, `:239`, and `:285` add none. A run has about 3,800 captures, so the maintainer cannot find the bad one. This makes the CMP-06 failure worse. The snippet is feasible, because `ImageValidationError` is exported and the CLI bundles the package (`packages/cli/tsup.config.ts:14`). Print `capture.itemKey` and the variant key at the call sites; a digest prefix is harder to use.

title: Four documents describe a comparator that no longer exists
oneLine: README.md:5, apps/web/src/operations/README.md:3, and apps/compare/README.md still say the Worker processes legacy comparisons, consumes queue work, and has open deployment gates.
verifierReason: The quoted sentences exist: `README.md:5` and `:60`; `apps/web/src/operations/README.md:3`; `apps/compare/README.md:5`, `:12`, `:18`, `:34`; `apps/compare/wrangler.jsonc:33`. The Worker has only a fetch handler (`apps/compare/src/index.ts:4-8`), and the rollout is recorded as complete (`docs/operations/retire-server-comparison.md:5`). Corrections: (1) The evidence lists three Markdown files and one configuration comment, not four documents. (2) `apps/web/src/operations/README.md:3` says in the same paragraph: 'This runbook describes source behavior before the selected retirements.' It is stale, but it says so. (3) The report missed these stale texts: `packages/compare/README.md:3` ('Its RGBA comparator serves the retained legacy path'), `:12` ('decodeImage must also succeed before image registration', which is false for local uploads), `:25` ('before launch'); `packages/cli/README.md:21` ('the legacy Worker's 0.05% policy') and `:25` ('WebP is supported by the legacy upload protocol', but `workflow-owned.ts:182-187` refuses that protocol). `docs/current-contract.md:32` and `:188` are covered in CMP-01.

title: The Wrangler files differ in dates, preview URLs, and limits without a stated reason
oneLine: Three compatibility dates (09-21, 09-22, 09-29), preview_urls unset in wrangler.probe.jsonc, cpu_ms 30000 left from queue work, and no declared PROBE_TOKEN secret.
verifierReason: Citations are correct. Dates: `apps/compare/wrangler.jsonc:5` 2026-09-22, `wrangler.probe.jsonc:5` 2026-09-21, `wrangler.container-probe.jsonc:5` 2026-09-29, and the test `apps/compare/test/validation.native.test.ts:51` hard-codes 2026-09-22. `preview_urls` is absent only in `wrangler.probe.jsonc`. `cpu_ms` is 30000 in two files and absent in the Container probe. Platform check (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/configuration/): when `preview_urls` is omitted and no setting exists, 'its initial value depends on workers_dev'. Thus the codec probe gets preview URLs on its first deploy, because `workers_dev` is true. Addition: `cpu_ms: 30000` is equal to the paid-plan default ('default: 30 seconds', https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/), so the key has no effect today. The recommendation is feasible. The impact is small, because CI deploys neither probe.

title: The compare tests are not type-checked, and the Container type check does not run in CI
oneLine: apps/compare/tsconfig.json excludes test/, typecheck:container is not called by CI, and a scratch tsc run found 11 errors in 2 test files while Container tests still run in normal CI.
verifierReason: Citations are correct: `apps/compare/tsconfig.json:13` includes only `src`; root `package.json:9` runs only scripts named `typecheck`; no step in `.github/workflows/checks.yml` runs `typecheck:container`. I ran the scratch type check again (`tsc6 -p verify/typecheck/tsconfig.json`): 11 errors, 6 in `apps/compare/test/container-probe.test.ts` and 5 in `container.test.ts`, and none in `container/probe.ts` or `container/transport.ts`. The three errors at `container-probe.test.ts:38`, `:41`, `:42` do not depend on the stand-in types. Corrections: (1) The title is too wide. `packages/compare/tsconfig.json:14` includes `test`, so the package tests are type-checked. Only `apps/compare/test` is not. (2) With `--shard`, each test file runs in one of the three shards, not in each test job. (3) `.github/workflows/README.md:3` most probably refers to `pnpm test:container` and the image build, which need sharp and Docker. The vitest Container tests use fake transports. That disagreement is a wording problem. (4) If `test` enters the `include` list, the 11 errors must be fixed first. Node types then mix with Workers types in one program. A separate tsconfig for tests is safer.

title: Codec identity strings and the policy type are duplicated, and no check ties them to the installed versions
oneLine: rgba-visible-1 and jsquash-png-3.1.1-webp-1.5.0 exist in both packages/compare and packages/protocol, and a jSquash update would not change the recorded identity.
verifierReason: The facts are correct. `packages/compare/src/compare.ts:3-4` and `packages/protocol/src/types.ts:44-45` hold the same two strings. `ComparisonPolicy` exists at `compare.ts:6-13` and at `types.ts:47-52`. Two validators exist (`compare.ts:36`, `packages/protocol/src/validate.ts:730`). `apps/compare/container/transport.ts:6` hard-codes the sharp identity, and `:62-68` repeats the thumbnail rule. No test reads the installed versions. Correction to the recommendation: do not add a test that makes the string follow the installed jSquash version. The contract requires an 'immutable old engine/codec identity' (`docs/current-contract.md:48`), and `packages/service/src/rendering-profile-conversion.ts:5-6` uses the protocol constants to fill old tuples. With such a test, a Renovate update forces a change of a historical identity. The listed alternative is the correct action: stop Renovate for the two jSquash packages, or delete the jSquash code (CMP-04), and keep the strings frozen in `@visonaut/protocol`. The report also missed the live identity strings, which have the same problem on the production path (see the missed list).

title: Three codec stacks exist, and the PNG-only local path stores 2.4 to 3.1 times more bytes than lossless WebP
oneLine: pngjs (production), jSquash WASM (no caller), and sharp (diagnostic) coexist; measured PNG is 2.4x to 3.1x larger than lossless WebP on committed screenshots, and the WebP validator has no production consumer.
verifierReason: The facts are correct. Three stacks exist: pngjs and pixelmatch in the CLI, jSquash WASM (181,088 and 137,960 bytes, checked with ls), and sharp 0.35.4 in the Container. The CLI rejects WebP (`packages/cli/src/png-comparison.ts:11-13`, `local-comparison.ts:255-258`). I ran `measure-webp-size.mjs` again: ratios 2.42, 2.84, and 3.12 with identical pixels. The decode times also reproduce: jSquash 12.6 ms and pngjs 26.9 ms at 1248x1650. Corrections: (1) The number in the title comes from three 640x360 demo pages. The repository's own large fixture gives 10.3 times (368,370 to 35,796 bytes, `packages/compare/evidence/hosted-largest-fixture.json:4-5`). Do not use the range as a production figure. (2) The storage cost is negligible. R2 costs $0.015 for each GB-month with 10 GB free (https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/pricing/). 27,287 originals (`docs/evidence/issue-204-completion.md:27`) at the recorded mean of 28,292 bytes are about 0.77 GB. This is a calculation from two repository numbers, not a bucket measurement. (3) A move to WebP changes each image digest and the codec identity `pngjs-7.0.0`, so it changes the approval tuples; the report says this. The real argument is the maintenance of three decoders, and that part is confirmed.

title: Workspace dependency declarations do not match the imports
oneLine: apps/web imports @visonaut/compare at runtime from devDependencies, packages/compare declares no dev tools, and apps/compare depends on @visonaut/service for type-only imports in legacy files.
verifierReason: All four citations are correct. `apps/web/package.json:37` lists `@visonaut/compare` as a devDependency, but `apps/web/src/runtime.ts:2` and `apps/web/src/api/local-comparison.ts:1` import it at runtime. `packages/compare/package.json` declares only the two jSquash packages, while it uses `tsc6`, `vitest`, Node types, and `@playwright/test` (`scripts/browser-study.ts:2`); its `node_modules` holds only `@jsquash`. `apps/compare/package.json:18` lists `@visonaut/service` for type-only imports (`src/process.ts:15`, `container/transport.ts:2`). `packages/service/src/service.test.ts:17` imports `../../compare/src/compare.ts` by relative path. No correction. One caution for the fix: `packages/cli` keeps `@visonaut/compare`, `pixelmatch`, and `pngjs` in `devDependencies` on purpose, because tsup bundles them (`packages/cli/tsup.config.ts:14`). Do not change that one.

title: Better Auth checks the full database schema on each request
oneLine: createAuth is built per request and Better Auth 1.7.5 defaults validateSchema to true, so each request adds 2 D1 round trips (76 statements, 856 rows read, about 85 KB) before the session lookup; validateSchema:false cuts getSession from 4 round trips to 2 (measured).
verifierReason: Code and rerun agree. auth.ts:47-51 has no advanced.database key; to-auth-endpoints.mjs:41-42 awaits the check; schema-check.mjs:57-68 keeps the result in one adapter instance; api/index.ts:130 and server.ts:85,93 make a new instance for each request. Rerun scenario A1 starts with the sqlite_master query and 'batch of 75 x pragma_table_info'; scenario L goes from 4 round trips and 78 statements to 2 and 2 with validateSchema false. Cloudflare docs confirm batch() is one call. Corrections: (1) 'no effect on the result' is true only while the schema matches; a mismatch fails the request. (2) No test or deploy step compares migration 0003_auth.sql with the Better Auth schema, so the runtime check is the only guard today; the test must come with the change, not as an alternative. (3) The shared-instance alternative contradicts auth.ts:15 and packages/security/README.md:5 and is not tested in workerd.
secondLensReason: Hot path confirmed in the installed better-auth 1.7.5: schema-check.mjs:7-9 enables the check unless validateSchema is false; kysely-adapter index.mjs:712 registers a new check for each adapter instance; to-auth-endpoints.mjs:41-42 and api/index.mjs:169-170 await it; api/index.ts:130 and server.ts:85,93 build a new instance for each request, and no validateSchema setting exists in the repository. Measured in production (6 samples, Worker at GRU): signed-out GET /api/runs, which does only the two check round trips, has a median TTFB of 0.357 s against 0.023 s for /health, so the check costs about 0.33 s for each private request. That is about 0.67 s of the 2.6-3.7 s dashboard load (2 sequential requests), 0.33 s of a run page, and 0.67 s or more for each decision. Fix feasibility: advanced.database.validateSchema: false exists in the installed types (init-options.d.mts:390-400) and removes all three call sites; Better Auth documents it and upstream issue 11346 recommends it. Option B (check one time for each isolate with a WeakSet keyed by the D1 binding) is also feasible; authorization.ts:19 already keeps isolate state keyed by the binding, and checkSchema is a typed context field. CORRECTION to the first verifier: a CI guard exists today, implicitly. auth-d1.test.ts uses the real createAuth on Miniflare D1 with all migrations. Measured: getSession resolves null with the matching schema and rejects with 'Database schema mismatch ... Missing columns session.userAgent' after one column is dropped. A hard-coded false removes this guard, so the option must be a parameter and one test must keep it on. No rule in docs/current-contract.md is affected; the live session and account checks stay. Strongest counter-argument: the runtime check is the only guard against a missing migration in the real production database, and Worker placement near D1 would reduce its cost to a few milliseconds without removing it.

title: Session, user, account, and project checks are four more sequential round trips
oneLine: Project row, session, user, and account are read one at a time before each private handler, and the project check repeats inside /api/operations and /v1/plan; joins:true makes session+user one query (measured) and a batch can merge the rest.
verifierReason: Rerun scenario A3 shows the order: project row, schema check x2, session, user, account, then the handler. internal-adapter.mjs:343-350 uses join user; authorization.ts:40-43 reads the account after getSession; api/index.ts:123-126 runs the project check alone. Repeats confirmed at api/operations.ts:16-18 and api/pre-run.ts:50, and also at api/webhooks.ts:157 and api/workflow-materialize.ts:495 (not in the report). Scenario L gives 1 round trip with joins true. The contract (current-contract.md:186) requires live session and account checks, and the proposal keeps them. Corrections: the count is 3 on GET /api/runs and 4 on other paths; the parallel sketch changes the answer for an anonymous request on a wrong project from 503 to 401; joins true is a SQLite result, not tested in workerd.

title: A cold isolate makes three sequential GitHub requests, and nothing is persisted
oneLine: Installation token, login hint, and the 60 s grant live only in isolate memory, so the first private request per isolate does token mint, GET /user/:id, and the permission call in sequence, and two parallel cold requests do each twice; the report lists ten caching options with tradeoffs and the contract text.
verifierReason: Counts confirmed: github.ts:102, :193 and authorization.ts:19 are module memory only; pendingToken is per client (github.ts:133, 169-172, deliberate per :106). Rerun A1 shows token, user, permission in sequence; H1 shows 2+2+2. Contract quotations at current-contract.md:186 and :204 are exact, and no rule forbids persistence. Corrections: (1) 'This is the checking access wait' is too strong. Production samples in live-authenticated.md show warm /api/runs at 865-1077 ms with no GitHub request expected, one sample at 1967 ms, and run pages at 5251-5680 ms for 5-6 MB of JSON. The cold GitHub path is about 1 s in one sample; the D1 path is about 1 s on each request; the run page is dominated by model size. (2) The table says the operations poll makes '0, or 1 after 60 s' GitHub requests. Measured: 1 on each of 5 polls, because the poll period (operations-attention/index.tsx:280, 60000) equals the grant lifetime with a strict > test (authorization.ts:21, :63). (3) A persisted token table must be added to sanitizeRestoredDatabase (operations/recovery.ts:35-41).
secondLensReason: Hot path confirmed: apps/web/src/api/index.ts:191-205 builds a client and calls requireMaintainer on every private route; token, login hint, and grant live only in module memory (github.ts:102, :193, authorization.ts:19) and production has no KV or Durable Object. Magnitude: 3 sequential GitHub requests add about 0.7 to 1.0 s (I measured 215 to 302 ms for each uncached GitHub REST request from Sao Paulo, 7 samples, plus 58 to 68 ms TLS; one production sample shows +0.9 to 1.1 s on the first API request). RSA signing is about 0.5 ms and is not a factor. But this cost applies only to the first private request of a cold isolate; every warm request already waits 0.87 to 1.08 s for D1 with zero GitHub requests, so 'this is the checking access wait' is too strong. The cold-isolate rate is not known (1 of 5 samples; Cloudflare documents no idle lifetime). The client sends private requests in series on page load, so the 'each twice' case needs two tabs. Feasibility: option B (login hint) can be a LEFT JOIN in the account query with zero extra round trips and no security change; option A (token in D1) is possible but the token carries Checks write (github.ts:141 sets no permissions limit), so a stored token can set the required check to success for 1 hour, and it needs a key, an interface change in createGitHubClient, and a new entry in the restore cleanup list; option C gives nothing after idle time. Options E and F have costs that the report does not state. No contract text forbids A, B, or C (docs/current-contract.md:186, :188, :204). Severity lowered to medium because the cost is once per isolate, the evidence is one sample, and D1-01 and D1-02 remove more wait on every request without a stored credential.

title: A write deletes the cached grant and does not store the new positive result
oneLine: authorization.ts:71-82 deletes the grant before a live check and stores it only when access is not write, so POST /api/review-sessions followed by the first decision makes two live GitHub checks and each Undo forces a recheck on the next read.
verifierReason: authorization.ts:71-82 is quoted exactly: the grant is deleted before the live check and stored only when access is not 'write'. Rerun scenario C: C1 POST /api/review-sessions 1 permission request, C2 GET /api/runs 1 more, C3 0. review/client.ts:296 and :310-313 show the first decision sends a write then a review request, so two live checks in sequence; :340 shows Undo also removes the grant. No test requires a write not to store a grant: auth-d1.test.ts:253-256 and :364-367, and api.test.ts:591-634, :762-770, :1070-1143, :1750-1758 all use a denied write, which the change keeps. Contract text at :186 permits reuse of 'a positive GitHub permission result' without limiting its source. I read the tests; I did not run the suite with the change.

title: The access check and the data read run one after the other, and the entry path repeats the check
oneLine: requireMaintainer finishes before any handler query, the page navigation starts no check, and a PR check link runs /api/pulls/:n then /api/runs/:id with the full auth work twice (6 + 6 D1 round trips before handlers).
verifierReason: The proposal is a design choice. All facts are confirmed: api/index.ts:194-213 finishes requireMaintainer before the handler; server.ts:118 starts no check on the document request; routes/runs.$runId.tsx:31 has ssr false and :37-39 the loader; routes/pulls.$pullNumber.tsx:51-84 fetches then navigates; api/pre-run-checks.ts:509-512 builds the /pulls/:n?check= link. Comments: option E helps only when the grant is cold or older than 60 s; option F needs a grant that other isolates can see; on the run page the measured wait is 5.3-5.7 s for 5-6 MB of JSON, so the access check is a small part there. The entry-path change has the clearest gain: it removes one full set of 6 round trips.

title: Ingest routes build Better Auth and never use it

Limits: the money cost is small (I assume a paid plan from limits.cpu_ms 240000, not checked); how many background checks finish in production is unknown because the work is not passed to waitUntil.

title: For mutations, the origin check runs after the session and GitHub checks
oneLine: A POST with a valid cookie and a foreign Origin is refused only after 6 D1 round trips and a live GitHub permission request, and it deletes the user's cached grant; requireSameOrigin needs no I/O and can run first.
verifierReason: The order is confirmed (api/index.ts:194-208) and rerun scenario D1 shows 403 after 6 round trips and 1 permission request. But the report says no decision is needed and no alternative exists, and an existing test fails after the change. api.test.ts:575-590 expects GET /api/runs to answer 403 after a refused cross-origin POST and a permission change; that passes only because the refused write removed the read grant. So the test needs an edit and the next read after a refused write no longer asks GitHub. title: The signed session token reaches page scripts, and the raw database token works as a credential
oneLine: The bearer plugin adds set-auth-token (equal to the HttpOnly cookie value) on daily renewal and api/index.ts:220-222 forwards it to the browser; Authorization: Bearer with the plain session.token column value returns 200, so D1 read access equals maintainer access.
verifierReason: Both stated facts are confirmed: bearer() at auth.ts:53; bearer/index.mjs:34-37 signs a raw token unless requireSignature is set and :52-66 adds set-auth-token; api/index.ts:220-222 forwards all session headers; rerun F1 shows the header, G1 shows Bearer <session.token> returns 200. Corrections: (1) The exposure is wider than 'one time per day in a header'. Measured: GET /api/auth/get-session and GET /api/auth/list-sessions return the raw session token in JSON at any time, and that raw value is a full credential. (2) So forwarding only Set-Cookie does not close it; requireSignature true is the effective part. (3) requireSameOrigin compares the Origin header (http.ts:21-29), which a non-browser client can set, so a stolen token permits Approve and Reject from any client. (4) All tests in auth-d1.test.ts use raw bearer tokens (for example :53, :240, :292) and must change. (5) The bearer path is documented in packages/cli/README.md:31.

title: The access level comes from the HTTP method and a copied pattern

title: Rate limiting covers only the auth routes, uses D1, and takes the client address from X-Forwarded-For
oneLine: Each /api/auth request adds 2 D1 round trips for the limiter, requests with zero or several X-Forwarded-For values share one no-trusted-ip bucket per path (measured), and the private API has no application limit; cf-connecting-ip is not configured.
verifierReason: auth.ts:52 enables the D1 limiter with no advanced.ipAddress key; ip.mjs:190 returns null for more than one forwarded address and :196 sets the default header to x-forwarded-for. Rerun scenario M: 2 limiter round trips for one auth request and the rows '203.0.113.7|/get-session' (1) and 'no-trusted-ip|/get-session' (2). Cloudflare documents that X-Forwarded-For equals CF-Connecting-IP when the client sent none and is appended to when one exists (developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/reference/http-headers), which supports the auditor's assumption; not tested on a deployed Worker. This is not a way to avoid the limit: a client that adds the header goes to the shared bucket with the same limit.

title: Each OIDC verification gets the GitHub key set again and makes 9 to 12 sequential GitHub requests
oneLine: oidc.ts:120-124 builds a new remote JWKS per call and then awaits 9 to 12 GitHub API reads one by one for a pull request, at Plan, each shard reservation, Begin, and Submit; jose jwksCache and Promise.all would cut the sequence.
verifierReason: Confirmed: oidc.ts:120-124 builds the key set inside the function; the pull request path makes 9 to 12 sequential requests (oidc.ts:165, 190, 240, 243, 258, 295, 303, 311, 313, then 320, 324, 330 when they apply); jose 6.2.12 exports jwksCache. Wrong: 'verifies at each shard reservation' and 'rate budget is used for each shard'. workflow-owned.ts:153-165 refuses every shard key except 'combined', and pre-run.ts:55 accepts Plan only when visualRequired is false. So a visual run verifies 3 times (Begin, one Reserve, Submit) and a run with no visual work 1 time (Plan). Plan also skips the request at oidc.ts:190. The module cache helps only when one isolate serves more than one verification. Promise.all makes early rejections cost all requests and can change the first logged check name. Lower severity: CI path, 3 calls for each run.

title: GitHub OAuth user tokens are stored and never read
oneLine: Sign-in stores encrypted access, refresh, and ID tokens in account, but the only code that touches those columns sets them to NULL; permission checks use the App installation token.
verifierReason: Confirmed: no app code reads the tokens; the only statements are the NULL updates at webhooks.ts:137 and operations/recovery.ts:40. Wrong: 'never read'. server.ts:82-87 sends all of /api/auth/* to the handler, and Better Auth's built-in POST /api/auth/get-access-token (account.mjs:408-439, decrypt at :396) returns the plaintext. Measured with production options and only a session cookie: stored token is encrypted, the route answers 200 and returns_plaintext_token is true. So a script with the user's session can read it. Also wrong: 'narrow scope'. The client ID Iv23... (wrangler.jsonc:55) is a GitHub App client; GitHub says such tokens do not use scopes and have the permissions that both the user and the App have. A 6-month refresh token is stored too if expiration is enabled for the App (not verified). The databaseHooks fix is feasible; also disable the route.

title: Small gaps in the response headers

verifierReason: http.ts:31-50 sets no Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy and :39 has no includeSubDomains; api/images.ts:55 sets CORP same-origin for public images; session.mjs:33-34 sets pragma no-cache and rerun A1 shows it in the API response; server.ts:60-71 sets only Cache-Control on /health. No correction. includeSubDomains affects all hosts under visonaut.com, so it is a decision and not only a code change.

title: `pnpm dev` returns HTTP 403 for every page
oneLine: Claim verified: server.ts:73-76 compares url.origin with VISONAUT_ORIGIN (https://preview.visonaut.com) in preview mode; no committed or documented local override exists (.dev.vars* is git-ignored); Host probes give 403 with an empty body.
verifierReason: Code is as quoted: apps/web/src/server.ts:73-76 `if (url.origin !== env.VISONAUT_ORIGIN) { return securePrivateResponse(new Response(null, { status: 403 })); }`; apps/web/wrangler.jsonc:25 sets `https://preview.visonaut.com`; apps/web/package.json:7 `vite --host 127.0.0.1`; README.md:55; .gitignore:6. `rg VISONAUT_ORIGIN` finds no documented override outside evidence JSON. server.test.ts has no `preview` or `403` match. `git log -S` gives 5712036 (#155) and 0b629ce (#250), as stated. Re-measured on 127.0.0.1:4310 (override `VISONAUT_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:4310`): Host 127.0.0.1:4310 -> 200; Host localhost:4310 -> 403, content-length 0; Host 127.0.0.1:5173 -> 403, 0 bytes; http://localhost:4310/ -> 403; /health -> 200. Correction: the `Host: preview.visonaut.com` probe is not Worker evidence. Its 403 has a 158-byte body from Vite: `Blocked request. This host ("preview.visonaut.com") is not allowed ... server.allowedHosts`. So 3 of the 4 probes show the Worker check, not 4. Recommendation check: the loopback-host sketch is safe on Workers (a deployed request URL always has the routed host) and alternative 1 is feasible; this workspace proves that `.dev.vars` overrides the Wrangler var. Cloudflare docs: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/vite-plugin/reference/secrets/ and https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/vite-plugin/reference/cloudflare-environments/ ("without providing CLOUDFLARE_ENV will use the default top-level Cloudflare environment").
secondLensReason: The 403 reproduces (Host localhost:4310 and 127.0.0.1:5173 give 403 with 0 bytes; /health gives 200). It is not a production path: env.production sets VISONAUT_ENVIRONMENT=production, so server.ts:73-76 runs only in local vite dev/preview and in the public preview Worker. Cost is developer time with a one-line workaround, so I lower high to medium. The lane's preview.visonaut.com probe (403, 158 bytes) comes from Vite's allowedHosts, not from server.ts. Fix checks: the loopback rule is feasible and changes no contract (preview is public fixtures with no bindings, contract line 188) if it stays inside the preview branch. The .dev.vars alternatives are fragile: wrangler.jsonc:124 declares secrets.required [], and Cloudflare documents that only listed keys load; installed Wrangler 4.136.1 loads the override in dev only because the key is also in vars, and returns {} for the vite preview path (measured), so `vite preview` stays 403. Alternative 2 (workers_dev false) conflicts with the guard at deploy.yml:360. A committed env.local Wrangler environment is one more option that needs no private file.

title: No documented command runs the real app locally, and `db:local` prepares a database that no command reads
oneLine: `pnpm dev` is a 1-item read-only fixture; the only path with D1, R2, auth, and saves is a performance harness (review-scale/local-routes.mjs) that uses an undeclared `local` environment and exits after its samples.
verifierReason: Confirmed: apps/web/package.json:12 `db:local` applies migrations to local D1 for `--env production`; the default dev config has `"d1_databases": []` (wrangler.jsonc:31). `rg "CLOUDFLARE_ENV|db:local|persist"` finds no script or doc that starts the app on that local database (the only hits are README.md:55, a deploy note in docs/operations/adapter-service-pins.md:67, and historical runner text in docs/operations/simplification-cutover.md:63). docs/development.md:50-60 gives 5 steps and no command. The only real-backend path is apps/web/tooling/review-scale/local-routes.mjs: it sets `VISONAUT_ENVIRONMENT: "local"` (lines 73-74), uses ephemeral D1/R2, and ends with `await runtime.dispose()` (line 361); it has no keep-open option (its only env inputs are REVIEW_ROUTE_*). preview-fixtures.ts:42-65 has 1 item and 2 variants. Correction to the recommendation: the `env.local` sketch is not complete. A non-preview request calls `requireBackendBindings`, needs the five secrets (wrangler.jsonc:113-121), a COMPARATOR binding, and GitHub calls in `requireMaintainer`; local-routes.mjs solves that with a Miniflare `outboundService` stub and a signed local session. Plain `vite dev` has no such stub, so the effort is larger than the sketch shows. The statements about `vite preview` and `CLOUDFLARE_ENV=production pnpm dev` stay unverified (the auditor said so).

title: Package versions in three documents are behind the manifests, and the published CLI README names the previous version
oneLine: Manifests are visonaut 0.5.4 and @visonaut/playwright 0.5.0; README.md:35, packages/cli/README.md:3 (shipped to npm), and .github/workflows/README.md:66 say 0.5.3 and 0.4.0.

Stale text: README.md:35 (`visonaut@0.5.3` and `@visonaut/playwright@0.4.0`), packages/cli/README.md:3 (`visonaut@0.5.3`), .github/workflows/README.md:66. docs/current-contract.md:22 has the correct pair. title: Documentation volume and style: 132,000 words, a "short contract" of 5,800 words, and nine code namespaces
oneLine: 122 Markdown files, 132,356 words; current-contract.md has 47 lines above 500 characters and 199 mentions of 78 decision codes; READMEs mix dated receipts with instructions; no architecture page or glossary; 30 of the last 60 commits touch docs or evidence.
verifierReason: All numbers reproduce with the auditor's scripts. `docs-stats.mjs table`: 122 Markdown files, 132,356 words; docs/current-contract.md 5,773 words, 47 lines above 500 characters, 7 above 1,000, longest 1,661. `groups`: docs/evidence 48,449 words in 61 files; docs/simplification-audit 26,691 in 14; top-level docs 23,174 in 9; docs/operations 12,969 in 9. `codes docs/current-contract.md`: 199 mentions, 78 unique, 9 prefixes (A 7, C 6, D 20, O 14, P 6, Q 4, S 5, U 6, W 10). Contract line 177 "Keep a short current contract in the repo" and line 42 "An issue #204 D-number is separate from a revision 9 D-number" exist. `commit-scan.mjs`: 30 of 60 and 113 of 258 commits change docs, a README, or evidence. title: Error responses have at least six shapes

The path-prefix test is written three times (server.ts:106-111, api/index.ts:96-101, preview-fixtures.ts:72-77), and `/api/auth/` is handled in server.ts:82-87 before api/index.ts:131-133 can run. All JSON errors of the web Worker use one envelope, `{ error: { code, message } }`; `schemaVersion`, `reference`, and `model` are optional additions, and the review client reads them in one place (apps/web/src/review/client.ts:269-277: `record(data.error)`, `error.message`, `error.reference`).
