title: Better Auth scans the database schema on every private request
oneLine: createAuth runs per request, so Better Auth's schema check repeats each time: +2 serial D1 round trips, 76 statements, ~856 rows read before the session read; validateSchema:false measured 6 -> 4 round trips.
verifierReason: Code: packages/security/src/auth.ts:15-21,47-51 builds a new betterAuth instance per call and sets no advanced.database option. Callers: apps/web/src/api/index.ts:130, apps/web/src/server.ts:85,93. Better Auth 1.7.5: @better-auth/core/dist/db/schema-check.mjs:7-9,51-78 keeps the 'clean' flag in a closure made per adapter instance; @better-auth/kysely-adapter/dist/index.mjs:712 registers it per instance; d1-sqlite-dialect-*.mjs:88-98 reads sqlite_master and then sends one batch of pragma_table_info per table; better-auth/dist/api/to-auth-endpoints.mjs:40-42 awaits the check before each API call. The option is real: @better-auth/core/dist/types/init-options.d.mts:390-400 says 'Set false to disable runtime schema validation'. Re-run (pnpm exec vitest run --config <verify>/vitest.probe.config.mjs): default = 6 round trips / 80 statements, validateSchema:false = 4 / 4; guest GET /api/runs 401 = 2 round trips, 76 statements, 856 rows read. Same as the report. Production corroboration recorded by the live lane (audit/live/curl-prod-health.jsonl, curl-prod-api-runs.jsonl, curl-prod-guest-paths.jsonl; I did not re-run them): /health 24-41 ms server wait; guest GET /api/runs (schema scan only) 366-413 ms; guest GET /api/runs/<uuid> (project read + scan) 453-517 ms. Corrections: (1) The scope is wider than 'private request'. createAuth at index.ts:130 runs before the /v1 capability routes, and better-auth/dist/auth/base.mjs:9-19 starts the check at construction, so upload, reuse, reference and finalize requests start the scan too. The load lane measured this: audit/load/ci-routes.json shows project + sqlite_master + BATCH(75) for PUT /v1/uploads/<bad token>. (2) 'Two 75-statement batches per second' is an upper bound. The client waits 500 ms after each response (apps/web/src/review/client.ts:324-335), so the rate is one per (0.5 s + response time). (3) The report missed advanced.database.joins (init-options.d.mts:375-389). The load lane measured validateSchema:false + joins:true = 2 round trips for session, user and account (audit/load/auth-options.json). The one-line recommendation is feasible. The per-isolate instance alternative must respect the Workers rule about promises shared between requests; auth.ts:15 and github.ts:106 state that rule on purpose.
secondLensReason: Hot path proved for env.production (apps/web/wrangler.jsonc:51 sets VISONAUT_ENVIRONMENT=production, so server.ts:73 is false): api/index.ts:130 builds a new Better Auth instance for every /api/* and /v1/* request; installed 1.7.5 registers one schema check per adapter instance (kysely-adapter index.mjs:712), keeps the result in a closure (core schema-check.mjs:58-59), and getSession awaits it (to-auth-endpoints.mjs:41-42). The check reads all 75 tables (d1-sqlite-dialect 89-98). Measured by me in production from GRU (second-lens-6/prod-guest-curl.txt): /health 24-30 ms, guest /api/runs 353-375 ms; a guest request does no other D1 work, so the check costs about 330 ms per private request (about 145-165 ms per serial D1 round trip). Dashboard = 2 such requests, about 0.66 s of the 2.6-3.7 s signed-in wait measured by the orchestrator. Cost in money is negligible (856 rows per request against 25 billion included). Fix is feasible: advanced.database.validateSchema exists in the installed version (init-options.d.mts:390-400; schema-check.mjs:7-9), no contract change (current-contract.md:186 live session and account reads stay). Risks: the implicit CI check in auth-d1.test.ts is lost unless one test keeps validateSchema true; upstream docs give two different defaults, so set it explicitly. The per-isolate shared instance alternative has a real cross-request pending-promise hazard (schema-check.mjs:33, :68) and gives no extra gain. The check also starts un-awaited on every /v1 capture request, including each image PUT. Strongest counter-argument: it is a fail-closed guard and the cost is a location effect that Worker placement could shrink; but Smart Placement is not sure to activate for this traffic, and a CI test gives the same protection at deploy time.

Writers: apps/web/src/api/webhooks.ts:330-335 (also :150, :172), packages/security/src/webhooks.ts:147 and apps/web/src/operations/recovery.ts:73 set payload_json='{}' at settlement. No other title store exists (rg 'pull_request.title' finds only the two readers and one test). Commits 339926d (2026-09-28, #129) and 5712036 (2026-09-30, #155) exist as cited. Re-run: sqlite3 :memory: < title-lookup.sql prints 'Fix dialog focus' while pending, empty after the settle UPDATE, and 0 rows that still carry a title. The test fixture (apps/web/src/api/dashboard.test.ts:42-55) inserts a full payload together with processed_at, a state production code never writes. Severity lowered to medium: the feature never works, but the effect is a missing label and a title search that finds nothing (apps/web/src/routes/index.tsx:499,586,619,714). No decision or stored result is wrong. Corrections to the recommendation: (1) the CASE expression must also go into the restore-fence UPDATE (webhooks.ts:172) and recovery.ts:73. (2) docs/operations/compact-processed-webhooks.sql:6 selects payload_json != '{}', so a rerun of that backfill would erase the kept titles. (3) docs/operations/compact-processed-webhooks.md:3 states the rule 'clear it in the same write that marks them processed'; keeping three fields changes a written rule, the separate-column option does not.
secondLensReason: Hot path proved: readers run on every dashboard load (dashboard.ts:57-62 inside the batch at :68-81) and every run model (review.ts:286-290); the writer webhooks.ts:330-335 sets payload_json='{}' as the last statement of processWebhook, which runs in waitUntil with the 202 (:350-357), and the pull_request branch (:279-329) has no earlier return. Production evidence from the orchestrator's signed-in session: history rows show '#7746 · Pull request'. Effect: all pull request runs lose the title after settlement; index.tsx:499,586,714 fall back to the kind label and title search (index.tsx:619) finds nothing. No latency, data-loss, or security effect, so I rate it medium, not high (the load-lane verifier rated the same defect medium). Recommended SQL verified by me on SQLite 3.51.0 (second-lens-6/title-fix.sql and .out.txt): the kept row is 110 bytes, review.ts:288 returns the title, and the plan still uses index github_webhook_delivery_pr_title. Side effects the report omits: old settled rows cannot be repaired from stored data (needs a GitHub backfill or a new event); docs/operations/compact-processed-webhooks.sql and webhooks.test.ts:3694 use payload_json != '{}' and would erase kept titles, tests at :3452/:3463/:3611/:3629 expect '{}'; four other statements also write '{}' (webhooks.ts:150, :172, operations/recovery.ts:73, packages/security/src/webhooks.ts:147), so a restore erases titles again. The dedicated column or table alternative has no extra GitHub cost because the pull is already fetched at webhooks.ts:282, but needs a new migration. No contract rule covers titles. Counter-argument: cosmetic, number and link are shown, and compaction was a deliberate capacity choice.

title: The pull page waits forever when the Plan selected no visual capture
oneLine: review.ts:773-777 needs docs_only=1 for 'not-required', but no production code writes it; a completed no-visual check returns state 'pending' and the page polls every 15 s.
verifierReason: apps/web/src/api/review.ts:773-777 returns 'not-required' only when docsOnly is set. Every production writer sets docs_only to 0 or false: pre-run-candidates.ts:38,99,128,197; pre-run-checks.ts:568-580 (literal 0) and :643 Number(candidate.docsOnly); pre-run-attempts.ts:667 (literal 0), :753, :822. The only docs_only=1 write is the test UPDATE at apps/web/src/api/api.test.ts:752-756. The no-visual path sets plan_visual_required=0 (pre-run.ts:140-152) and state='docs_complete' (pre-run-plan.ts:190-195); the endpoint does not read plan_visual_required. Re-run: GET /api/pulls/43?check=... for a row in that exact state returns {"runId":null,"state":"pending"} (verify/errors.result.json, last entry). The page then polls every 15 s while visible (apps/web/src/routes/pulls.$pullNumber.tsx:104-118); each poll costs 8 D1 round trips (verify/roundtrips.result.txt). Corrections: (1) The assumption about GitHub keeping details_url is not needed. pre-run-checks.ts:508-514 and apps/web/src/operations/review-links.ts:65-69,281 set the /pulls/N?check= URL explicitly, and review-links.ts:96-103 already uses the rule the fix needs (state='docs_complete' and visualRequired===0 means success). (2) 'docs_complete' has two other writers with another meaning (pre-run-checks.ts:137 'Visual capture was not active', :334 'Equivalent merge check retired'). The fix must test plan_visual_required=0 as the report's snippet does, not the state alone.

title: A missing run or comparison returns 409 incomplete, not 404
oneLine: service.one() throws IncompleteError and index.ts:55-66 maps it to 409; GET /api/runs/<unknown uuid> measured 409 'incomplete'.
verifierReason: packages/service/src/service.ts:92-98 throws IncompleteError('The requested record does not exist.'); apps/web/src/api/index.ts:55-66 maps it to 409 'incomplete'; apps/web/src/api/review.ts:89-95 calls service.run first, so its own 404 is reached only for a run of another project. Re-run: GET /api/runs/<random uuid> returns 409 {"schemaVersion":"1.0","error":{"code":"incomplete","message":"The requested record does not exist."}} (verify/errors.result.json). Client effect: apps/web/src/review/client.ts:275 marks every 409 as a conflict; apps/web/src/routes/runs.$runId.tsx:76-107 shows the message with a Retry button. The CLI does not retry on this 409; it prints 'The service refused the request (HTTP 409)' (packages/cli/src/http.ts:175-229). Note for the fix: GET /v1/runs/{uuid} (CLI status, apps/web/src/api/ingest.ts:27-31) has the same mapping and is public CLI surface, and docs/current-contract.md:83 says incomplete-capture responses 'keep their current status'. A missing record is a different case, but state that in the change.

title: Each private request repeats the same serial reads
oneLine: GET /api/runs/:id makes 19 D1 round trips (about 14 in sequence): project read 3 times, run 2, comparison 2; receipt poll 23; first decision makes 2 live GitHub permission checks.
verifierReason: Re-run reproduces every count (verify/roundtrips.result.txt and .json): GET /api/runs/:id = 19 round trips / 99 statements; /state = 13; /api/operations = 9; GET /api/commands/:id/queued when complete = 23 with 4 reads of visonaut_runs; POST /api/review-sessions and the next POST .../commands each make 1 GitHub request. Code: the project is read 3 times (index.ts:125, review.ts:292, packages/service/src/run-status.ts:61), the run twice (review.ts:90, run-status.ts:27), the comparison twice (run-status.ts:45, review.ts:305). packages/security/src/authorization.ts:71-82 deletes the cached entry before a write check and stores nothing for 'write'. Platform: D1 batch is one call ('reduces latency from network round trips to D1', https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/worker-api/d1-database/), so the recommendation is feasible. Production corroboration from the live lane (not re-run by me): one more plain D1 read costs about 70-150 ms (guest /api/runs/<uuid> 453-517 ms against guest /api/runs 366-413 ms), and the signed-in waits fit the counts: /api/runs with 6 round trips = 865-1967 ms, /api/operations with 9 = 1204-1299 ms (audit/live-authenticated.md). Corrections: (1) The report's page table says /api/operations is 'sent at the same time' as /api/runs. It is not. OperationsAttention mounts only when state.status==='ready' (apps/web/src/routes/index.tsx:254-256,362-364), and the live data shows it starts about 70 ms after /api/runs ends. The two prologues add up; the dashboard is stable after 2.6-3.7 s. (2) The 19 was measured on a 3-variant run with no R2 inventory. The production run page waits 5.3-5.7 s on the server; 19 round trips do not explain that, and the rest was not measured. (3) /api/operations also runs 3 serial reads that fit one batch (apps/web/src/api/operations.ts:16-47).
secondLensReason: I compared the recorded 19-trip sequence (api/verify/roundtrips.result.json) with the code: project read 3 times (api/index.ts:125, review.ts:292, run-status.ts:61), run 2 (review.ts:90, run-status.ts:27), comparison 2 (run-status.ts:45, review.ts:305); serial depth is 14 (15 with a current promotion). Runs once per run page view, again in each completed receipt poll (review.ts:814) and each conflict (review.ts:683). First decision makes 2 live GitHub checks because a write skips the cache, deletes the entry and stores nothing (authorization.ts:63, :71, :74). Magnitude: with my measured 145-165 ms per serial D1 round trip at GRU, the smallest run page waits about 2.0-2.3 s (estimate = count x measured cost); signed-in dashboard numbers from the orchestrator agree (6 trips 865-1,967 ms, 9 trips 1,204-1,299 ms). For large archived runs (5.2-5.7 s, 5-6 MB JSON, different branch review.ts:242-248) the model size is probably the larger part; not counted. GitHub and RSA: no official latency figures, counts only; RSA signing is not on the warm path (github.ts:135, :166-173). Fix feasibility: D1 batch() is one call and one transaction (official docs) and dashboard.ts:68-90 is the in-repo precedent; minimal dedupe gives 14 to 10 serial steps, full batch plus joins about 4 (about 0.6-0.7 s at GRU). Session, user and account reads cannot be cached or served from replicas (current-contract.md:186; D1 has no South America region). Placement is the other lever (wrangler 4.136.1 accepts placement in env), but Smart Placement needs consistent traffic from multiple locations and the docs do not name D1, so its effect must be measured. Seeding the 10-second cache from a write check fits the wording of current-contract.md:204 and no test forbids it, but it changes an approved security rule and needs maintainer approval. Counter-argument: per-trip price, not trip count, is the main term, and one placement line avoids touching the 391-line security-relevant reviewModel.

title: A cold isolate asks GitHub three times, and parallel requests repeat the work
oneLine: First request per isolate: token mint + user lookup + permission (3 GitHub calls); the two parallel dashboard requests measured 6 GitHub calls and 15 D1 round trips.
verifierReason: Confirmed: the three caches are module state (packages/security/src/github.ts:102,193; authorization.ts:19) and the cold counts are right. Re-run: 3 GitHub requests on the first GET /api/session; 6 GitHub requests and 15 D1 round trips for two concurrent cold requests (verify/roundtrips.cold.json). Not confirmed: that the dashboard meets the parallel case. The dashboard does not send the two requests in parallel. OperationsAttention is rendered only after /api/runs succeeds (apps/web/src/routes/index.tsx:254-256,362-364), and the live timings show /api/operations starting after /api/runs ends. The measured 6-request case is synthetic for the dashboard; no other page sends two private requests at load. The per-client pending token (github.ts:133,169) is a stated design rule, not an oversight: github.ts:106 says 'pending I/O stays within the request's client'. Correction to the recommendation: 'load alerts after the list succeeds' is already the behavior. The option that saves time is to return the alert summary with /api/runs, which removes a second 6-round-trip prologue. Severity low: a cold isolate costs 3 serial GitHub calls once; how often that happens in production is unknown.

title: Reference selection checks ancestry with up to 100 serial GitHub requests and does not stop early
oneLine: ingest.ts:7-23 loops one compare call per eligible snapshot (LIMIT 100, no per_page, no early exit) on the first /reference page and on every materialization; lineage.ts:453-465 already exits early.
verifierReason: apps/web/src/api/ingest.ts:6-25: up to 100 distinct eligible snapshot commits, one serial compare request each, no early exit, no per_page. Callers: apps/web/src/api/local-comparison.ts:313 and workflow-materialize.ts:618. The reference path uses the list only to pick one snapshot (local-comparison.ts:315-322). The sibling functions stop early and add per_page=1 (lineage.ts:450-466, merge.ts:38-40). Eligibility lasts until 30 days after the run closes (apps/web/src/operations/snapshot-retention.ts:197-201, packages/service/src/work.ts:695). New measurement (node verify/compare-size.mjs, gh api, public ariakit/ariakit, 99 commits apart; laptop time, not Worker time): without per_page 795,761 bytes in 1,082 ms; with ?per_page=1 352,983 bytes in 592 ms. Corrections: (1) per_page=1 removes the commit list only. The first page still carries up to 300 files (338,758 bytes here), so the 'minimal' option halves the body; it does not make it small. (2) The 4 MiB failure (github.ts:89) was not reached in this sample; treat it as possible, not shown. (3) The report names two SQL readers of visonaut_ancestry. There are four: packages/service/src/local-comparison.ts:417, baseline-promotion.ts:405, run-admission.ts:553, and review-status.ts:19-21 (replacedMainRunSql, which looks up the tested SHA of another run). The last one is a reason to keep the full list in materialization, as the report's main recommendation does. (4) N in production is unknown. The database was replaced at the baseline cutover, so N can be small today and grows with accepted main runs.

title: The complete R2 inventory is read and validated again for each reference page and each review read
oneLine: Each read hashes, parses, re-serializes and validates the whole object (50 ms local for 3,582 captures / 5.05 MB); about 25 reads per Submit and 2 per review model.
verifierReason: One read = full body, SHA-256, JSON.parse, canonical re-serialization and validation (apps/web/src/capture-inventory.ts:488-518,551-553). The counts check out: first reference page 3 reads (apps/web/src/api/local-comparison.ts:334,335,432), 1 for each later page (:432), declare and finalize 1 each (workflow-owned.ts:546,1143 into local-comparison.ts:512), materialization 3 (workflow-materialize.ts:273,275,809). 18 pages give about 25 reads. Review model: 2 reads per call (review-inventory.ts:43-48, review.ts:364), also on each completed receipt (review.ts:814) and each conflict (:683). Re-run of M6: medians 15.8 ms / 49.7 ms / 150.9 ms, same as the report. Corrections: (1) M6 understates the real size. The repository's own review of PR #247 (gh api repos/ariakit/visonaut/pulls/comments/4178894713) measured 13,800,580 bytes and 317-357 ms per read locally for the 3,832-capture fixture. That was before #249 compacted the format, so today's size is between the two values and is not measured. (2) The cache recommendation has a platform limit the report does not name: 'Each isolate can consume up to 128 MB of memory' (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/). The existing cache keeps only the ID set on purpose (local-comparison.ts:54-57: 'Receipts, decoded profiles and pending I/O stay within their request', with the PR thread link). A cached parsed inventory needs a byte bound, not only an entry count. The in-request reuse (3 reads to 1) has no such risk. (3) CPU limit is not the constraint; apps/web/wrangler.jsonc:39-42 sets cpu_ms 240000. The cost is wait time and R2 transfer. Severity stays medium, but it can be higher for the run page: the production model request waits 5.3-5.7 s and nobody measured how much of that is inventory work.

title: The workflow_run webhook runs the full materialization inside waitUntil, in addition to the queue
oneLine: webhooks.ts:267-275 calls materializeWorkflowRun inline under waitUntil while the queue runs the same work; the lease does not exclude a second worker.
verifierReason: Code facts confirmed. apps/web/src/api/webhooks.ts:350-357 runs processWebhook inside waitUntil; :261-276 calls materializeWorkflowRun inline for a successful workflow_run; the queue path exists (workflow-owned.ts:1279, webhooks.ts:248, apps/web/src/runtime.ts:375-376); leaseStagedSources only extends a timestamp with MAX and excludes nobody (workflow-materialize.ts:159-164). Platform fact checked: 'ctx.waitUntil() can extend execution for up to 30 seconds after the response is sent or the client disconnects. If any Promises have not settled after 30 seconds, they are canceled.' (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/context/). Queue consumers get 15 minutes of wall time (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/). Not verified by me: 'at least 30 GitHub requests' for one materialization (a code count I did not repeat), and whether real runs exceed 30 s; the workflow_materialized log line (workflow-materialize.ts:777-799) holds that answer. Addition: the same inline call also runs from the queue. reconcileWebhooks replays pending workflow_run deliveries (webhooks.ts:376-384), and the same recovery message then runs reconcileStagedWorkflows (runtime.ts:368-374). A sealed run returns early (workflow-materialize.ts:513-586), so the duplicate cost applies only while the run is not sealed. No correctness fault is shown. The recommended one-line change is feasible.

title: Every webhook delivery costs 6 D1 round trips and 4 row writes, including events with no handler
oneLine: No-op events (check_run created, other workflows, check_suite) still do project read + INSERT + SELECT, then project read + fence + UPDATE; the receipt table has no retention.
verifierReason: Re-run: check_run created, workflow_run for another workflow file, and check_suite each cost 3 round trips before the 202 and 3 after it, with 4 rows written (verify/roundtrips.result.txt). Code: INSERT then SELECT (packages/security/src/webhooks.ts:85-102); the project check runs twice (apps/web/src/api/index.ts:125 and webhooks.ts:157); fence read (webhooks.ts:159-165); settle UPDATE (:330-335). No 'DELETE FROM github_webhook_delivery' exists in the repository, so the table has no retention. docs/operations/compact-processed-webhooks.md:5 records 30,562 receipts on 2026-09-28. Both SQL options are valid on D1; RETURNING is already in use (for example apps/web/src/api/pre-run-plan.ts:155-156). The constraint the report states is correct: upstream delivery recovery needs a receipt row for each delivery (apps/web/src/operations/github-deliveries.ts:229-238), so events with no handler must still insert a row.

title: A delivery that cannot be processed is retried every 5 minutes without a limit, and the reason is not logged
oneLine: reconcileWebhooks has no attempt cap, age limit or terminal state and both catch blocks drop the error; a merge_not_ready pull request keeps a delivery and a service alert open.
verifierReason: apps/web/src/api/webhooks.ts:362-395 has no attempt count, no age limit and a bare catch. The first pass logs only the delivery ID (:352-356). Any pending delivery records reconciliation-failed on each recovery (apps/web/src/runtime.ts:378-396). The cron is every 5 minutes (apps/web/wrangler.jsonc:110) and the step size is 25 (apps/web/src/runtime-defaults.ts:21). Example path: pre-run-candidates.ts:73-79 throws merge_not_ready when merge_commit_sha is null. The report's open assumption is now checked against GitHub: gh api repos/ariakit/ariakit/pulls/4378 returns {"state":"open","mergeable":false,"mergeable_state":"dirty","merge_commit_sha":null} for an open, conflicted, same-repository pull request against main. A delivery with action opened, reopened, synchronize or edited for such a pull request therefore throws on every retry until the head changes or the pull request closes (pre-run-candidates.ts:64-72 returns null in those cases). Each retry makes at least 2 GitHub requests (webhooks.ts:282 and pre-run-candidates.ts:58). The contract asks for 'bounded failed-delivery recovery, followed by an actionable alert' (docs/current-contract.md:186); the current alert names neither the delivery nor the error. Not verified: how many deliveries are pending in production. The live dashboard shows 1 unresolved service alert; its kind was not recorded.

title: Server-comparison branches are still in the upload path, and the comparator binding has no reachable caller
oneLine: Only local-mode capabilities can be issued, so workflow-owned.ts:549-554, 770-778 and 1066-1089 (the only COMPARATOR call) cannot run; the contract still says the Worker validates images.
verifierReason: Reservation requires the local mode (apps/web/src/api/workflow-owned.ts:175-187). Both places that issue a capability set it (workflow-owned.ts:372-384, local-comparison.ts:444-447). A token lives at most 15 minutes (packages/security/src/capabilities.ts:98,123). rg 'comparator' in apps/web/src without tests finds one call, workflow-owned.ts:1067, inside 'if (capability.comparisonMode !== LOCAL_COMPARISON_MODE)'. The non-local branches are at :549-554, :557-558, :770-778 and :1066-1089. The binding is still required (apps/web/src/runtime.ts:49) and configured (apps/web/wrangler.jsonc:85-90). On the live path an upload is checked by length and SHA-256 only (workflow-owned.ts:1042). The written rules say the opposite: docs/current-contract.md:32 'The private Worker validates PNG/WebP through fetch', :48 'Keep the Worker's image validation', and docs/operations/retire-server-comparison.md:38 'Retained images and validation still need them'. The drift is real. Removal needs an explicit contract change, not only a code change. Addition: the CLI still has retry logic for validation_busy, a code only the unreachable branch can send (packages/cli/src/http.ts:199-212, packages/cli/src/engine.ts:623; server side workflow-owned.ts:1072-1074).

title: Routes, exports, and settings with no product caller
oneLine: /api/me, /api/session, /webhooks/github alias, inner /api/auth branch, recompare tombstone plus disabled button, synchronous command branch, matchPath, ensurePreRunCheck, ApiBindings.history, maximumPlanBytes, docs_only.
verifierReason: Re-run of exports.mjs: 113 exports, 15 without another production user, matchPath with 0 references, ensurePreRunCheck with 50 test references only. /api/session appears only at apps/web/src/api/review.ts:713. /api/me has no caller in apps/web/src, and browser tests assert it is not called (apps/web/src/review/__tests__/route.browser.test.ts:103). ApiBindings.history is built at apps/web/src/runtime.ts:272-300 and has no reader. limits.maximumPlanBytes is set at runtime.ts:255 and has no reader. Recompare: every path throws (review.ts:950-987), the model always sends recompareAllowed:false (:592), and the button and its reason text still render (apps/web/src/review/review-workspace.tsx:1186-1201). The client always sends queued:true (apps/web/src/review/client.ts:317), so review.ts:879-904 has no product caller. Corrections: (1) /api/me is also the probe named in runbooks and tooling (docs/operations/retire-preview-auth-at-cutover.md:59, apps/web/tooling/review-scale/local-routes.mjs:273); a removal must update those. (2) The open question about the App webhook URL has an answer in code: apps/web/src/operations/github-deliveries.ts:165-177 reads /app/hook/config and records the alert upstream-webhook / receiver / production-receiver-mismatch unless the URL is <origin>/v1/webhooks. Read the Service page before the /webhooks/github alias is removed. (3) Two items are deliberate keeps: the recompare tombstone is a written rule (docs/operations/retire-server-comparison.md:17), and ensurePreRunCheck carries the comment 'Keep this path for checks created after a signed submit is verified' (apps/web/src/api/pre-run.ts:30). (4) docs_only also appears in packages/service/src/run-admission.ts:192.

title: Upload evidence version 2 (D1 pages) has readers and a writer function, but nothing creates it
oneLine: The only INSERT writes evidence_version 1 (workflow-owned.ts:589) since #247; about 150 lines and one table remain for rows that lived one retention day.
verifierReason: The only INSERT into ingest_staged_manifests binds the literal 1 (apps/web/src/api/workflow-owned.ts:589), and no UPDATE sets evidence_version. 'git show 6219fdf -- apps/web/src/api/workflow-owned.ts' shows that line changing back to 1. writeEvidencePages is reachable only for a stored version 2 row (workflow-owned.ts:660-669). Staged rows expire after 24 hours plus a 6 hour lease (apps/web/src/api/workflow-retention.ts:6-7). The version 2 readers and triggers remain (workflow-evidence.ts:211-235,282-348; workflow-materialize.ts:687-710; apps/web/migrations/0033_d1_upload_evidence.sql). Not verified: the production count of version 2 rows; the report's SQL check is the right first step. title: Error responses have several shapes, and the same code maps to different statuses
oneLine: Four JSON shapes plus plain text; unknown /v1 path returns 401 'Sign in with GitHub'; ProtocolError always 'invalid_manifest'; 50 GitHub responses validated as 400 invalid_body; 10 codes use two statuses.
verifierReason: Confirmed by re-run (verify/errors.result.json): the 404 fallback has no schemaVersion (apps/web/src/api/index.ts:214-219); the review conflict body is {error, model, reviewer} (review.ts:689-696); images answer text/plain (images.ts:17-21, index.ts:117-122); GET /v1/nope and GET /v1/plan answer 401 sign_in_required; ProtocolError always becomes invalid_manifest (index.ts:46-54) although the class carries other codes (packages/protocol/src/workflow-jobs.ts:17-35, INVALID_WORKFLOW_JOB_NAME). error-codes.mjs re-run: 254 constructions, 108 codes, 10 codes with two statuses. apps/web/src/server.ts:49 sends Retry-After for every status. Corrections: (1) The requireSameOrigin point is wrong as written. The comment at packages/security/src/http.ts:20 says 'before reading the request body', not 'first step', and the code does run it before any body read (index.ts:206-208; body reads start in handleReview). (2) My count of GitHub responses checked with the request-body validator is 47 call sites in 12 modules, not 51 in 14. The point stands: input.ts:19-24 answers invalid_body 400 for an upstream fault. (3) The open question has an answer: the error body is CLI contract. packages/cli/src/http.ts:185-217 branches on error.code (stale_reference, capacity_exceeded, validation_busy, service_unavailable) and on Retry-After, and :167-173 maps every 401 or 403 to 'Authentication or permission failed', so an unknown /v1 path reads as a credential fault in CI. Severity lowered to low: no current client breaks; the effects are misleading messages and harder client code.

title: The API has no route table, a few very large functions, and two ID spaces under /v1/runs/:id
oneLine: 17 route regexes in two if chains decide auth by position; reviewModel is 391 lines, workflow-owned.ts 1,289; begin/submit take the GitHub run number while sibling paths take the service UUID.
verifierReason: The facts are confirmed; the recommendation is a design opinion. wc -l matches (workflow-owned.ts 1,289; pre-run-attempts.ts 1,034; review.ts 989; workflow-materialize.ts 960; pre-run-checks.ts 724; tests 5,053 and 4,672). Function spans match (reviewModel review.ts:227-617, handleReview :699-989, materializeWorkflowRun workflow-materialize.ts:494-820, declareStaged workflow-owned.ts:476-806 start, verifyLineage lineage.ts:82-449 start). The two ID spaces under /v1/runs/:id are real: index.ts:140,186 take digits, :144-184,209 take a UUID. capture_job_prefix holds a template (workflow-owned.ts:70-71). I count 19 path expressions, not 21. One fact supports the risk claim: the repository records that this exact fault happened once, 'The canonical /v1/webhooks route reached the maintainer-session boundary and rejected a valid signed App ping with 401' (docs/simplification-implementation.md:228). It failed closed. docs/current-contract.md:53 requires 'Preserve public entry points' and forbids a 'new workflow framework or global store'; a plain route table does not conflict with that text, but the maintainer decides. Severity low: there is no runtime effect today.

title: Repeated GitHub requests inside one webhook or one materialization
oneLine: workflowAttempt is called twice in a row (workflow-reconcile.ts:234-235), the pull is fetched twice per pull_request delivery, and verifyLineage validates the target twice.
verifierReason: apps/web/src/api/workflow-reconcile.ts:234-235 calls workflowAttempt twice; for attempt 1 both build the same URL (apps/web/src/api/jobs.ts:33-43, the suffix is added only when 'historical' is true). The same URL is requested again at workflow-reconcile.ts:353 and workflow-materialize.ts:769; those are late re-checks and deliberate. webhooks.ts:282 and pre-run-candidates.ts:58 fetch the same pull for one delivery. relatedRunEvidence calls verifyLineage twice (lineage.ts:554,581) with caches local to each call (:96-97). The pull is fetched for every pull_request action (webhooks.ts:279-282). Correction: for attempt > 1 the first call at :234 is not a duplicate. It checks that the stored attempt is still the latest one. Remove it only for attempt 1, or keep one call and reuse its result. All counts come from the code; nothing here was measured.

title: Each image view costs one D1 read and one R2 read; the response is cacheable only in the browser
oneLine: images.ts sends an immutable Cache-Control header but does not use the Workers Cache API, so each new browser reads D1 and R2 again; an edge cache must respect image retention.
verifierReason: apps/web/src/api/images.ts:24-40 does one D1 read and then one R2 get (head for HEAD or a matching If-None-Match); :52 sets 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable'. Re-run: GET /images/:id = 1 D1 round trip and 1 R2 call (verify/roundtrips.result.txt). No Cache API use exists in apps/web/src (rg 'caches.default|caches.open' finds nothing). Platform fact checked: Workers run before the cache, and 'the Cache API is the only option to customize caching' when the Worker is the origin (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/reference/how-the-cache-works/). No production cf-cache-status for a real image was recorded, so the edge behavior comes from documentation, not from observation. The retention tradeoff in the report is real: the browser copy already lives one year, and docs/current-contract.md:59 accepts that 'access revocation cannot recall copied pixels'. Low: on revisit the live run page served images from the browser cache in about 1 ms (audit/live-authenticated.md).

title: better-auth checks the database schema on each private API request
oneLine: A new better-auth instance per request reruns the default schema check: 2 sequential D1 round trips, 76 statements, 856 of 941 rows read; about 310-370 ms per private request in production. Fix is `advanced.database.validateSchema: false` in packages/security/src/auth.ts.
verifierReason: NOTE FOR ALL IDS: report.md does not exist on disk, so I verified each finding by its title against code, the auditor's raw probes, and my own re-measurements; quotes, line citations and recommendation text could not be checked. Proof here: packages/security/src/auth.ts:15-21 builds betterAuth per request with no validateSchema key; apps/web/src/api/index.ts:130 and server.ts:85,93 call it per request; installed better-auth 1.7.5 enables the check unless `validateSchema === false` (@better-auth/core/dist/db/schema-check.mjs:7-9), registers it per adapter instance (kysely-adapter index.mjs:712) and awaits it before each endpoint (to-auth-endpoints.mjs:41-42). My re-run (verify/api-path-verify.json): every request, also in the same isolate, does `sqlite_master` + `batch[75] pragma_table_info` (76 statements, ~856 rows read). Correction: it also runs for signed-out requests, /api/auth/* and /api/me; production signed-out GET /api/runs is only these 2 trips and takes 332-376 ms vs 24-28 ms for /health. Fix is feasible: `advanced.database.validateSchema: false`, or validate once per isolate (env.DB identity is stable in workerd).
secondLensReason: Hot path proved: apps/web/src/api/index.ts:130 and server.ts:85,93 build a new betterAuth() for each production request; installed better-auth 1.7.5 registers a new schema check per adapter instance (kysely-adapter index.mjs:712) and each auth.api call awaits it (to-auth-endpoints.mjs:41-42). Measured by me in production from GRU: /api/runs 401 median 360 ms vs /health 31 ms, so about 330 ms per awaited check; 2 checks in sequence per dashboard load (about 0.66 s of 2.6-3.7 s), 1 per run page (6% of the 5.3-5.7 s wait), 2-3 per decision. Reproduced on native local D1: guest 2 -> 0 round trips and signed-in 5 -> 3 with validateSchema: false. The option exists in the installed types (init-options.d.mts:390-400) and the official database page confirms 'enabled by default, including in production ... per adapter instance'; 1.7.7 does not change this. Correction: the check is a real fail-closed guard. After I removed one session column, the current options returned SCHEMA_MISMATCH and validateSchema: false returned ok login=maintainer. Existing D1 tests get the check only because createAuth leaves it on, so option A needs one test with the check on (migrations run before deploy, deploy.yml:127,133). Option B (validate once per isolate via WeakSet<D1Database>) keeps the guard and matches the existing WeakMap<D1Database> pattern, but still costs 330 ms on the first request of each isolate. No contract line names the check; current-contract.md:186 session and account checks stay. Counter-argument: if REVIEW-02 moves the Worker near D1 the two trips cost tens of ms and the guard can stay.

title: The Worker runs near the user while each D1 round trip costs about 125 to 165 ms
oneLine: wrangler.jsonc has no placement; production from GRU shows 154 ms for a 1-query path vs 23-34 ms for /health, so 15 sequential round trips in GET /api/runs/:id is an estimated 1.9-2.5 s of D1 wait. Option: Smart Placement. D1 region not verified.
verifierReason: apps/web/wrangler.jsonc has no `placement`; production responses show cf-ray ...-GRU and no cf-placement header. My production timing (verify/production-timing.txt): /health 24-28 ms, 1-trip path 151-157 ms, 2-trip 332-376 ms, 3-trip 420-576 ms, so 125-154 ms per D1 trip (outliers 269 and 721 ms). Trip counts were verified locally (2 and 3). Limits: value is derived by subtraction, not traced; D1 region is unverified (remote wrangler forbidden). Platform facts to add: D1 has no South America location (wnam/enam/weur/eeur/apac/oc), so only moving the Worker or cutting trips helps; Smart Placement docs do not name D1 and can stay at INSUFFICIENT_INVOCATIONS for low multi-location traffic; explicit `placement.region` hints exist; static assets stay at the edge.
secondLensReason: apps/web/wrangler.jsonc has no placement key at top level or in env.production; my production response has cf-ray ...-GRU and no cf-placement header. Measured by me: one simple D1 trip about 145 ms (first verifier 125 ms). A count model (0.33 s schema pair + other trips x 125-145 ms) predicts the signed-in dashboard waits within about 10% (6 trips: 0.83-0.91 s vs 0.87-1.08 s measured; 9 trips: 1.21-1.35 s vs 1.20-1.30 s), so distance x count explains the dashboard. Correction: the '15 trips, 1.9-2.5 s' estimate is for an active run that needs review, which has no production sample; the measured run samples were archived runs with 10 trips in sequence (about 1.3-1.5 s of 5.3-5.7 s). Fix feasibility: the installed wrangler 4.136.1 schema accepts placement per environment ({mode:'smart'} or {region:'aws:us-east-1'}); it must go in env.production only. Official docs: Smart Placement 'requires consistent traffic ... from multiple locations', can report INSUFFICIENT_INVOCATIONS, re-analyzes for up to 15 minutes after each deployment, affects fetch handlers only, and static assets stay at the edge. D1 has no South America location and replicas are in the same six regions, so there is no other distance lever. The D1 region is still not read (served_by_region, dashboard, or wrangler d1 info); a region hint needs it. Estimated effect (assumption 5-20 ms in-region trip, about 120 ms hop): /api/runs 0.9-1.1 s -> about 0.15-0.27 s, document +0.12 s, images about equal. No security contract change. Counter-argument: the count fixes are deterministic and testable, and after them placement saves only about 0.25-0.4 s per request while adding 0.12 s to each document; for the measured run page D1 is only about a quarter of the wait.

title: The run model reads the same rows again and awaits 15 round trips in sequence
oneLine: GET /api/runs/:id makes 21 D1 round trips (project read 3 times, run 2-3 times, comparison 2 times; readRunStatus awaits 6 reads one by one; two R2 inventory reads are sequential). One batch keyed by run ID can cut the depth from 15 to about 4.
verifierReason: Confirmed: duplicate reads (run, project, comparison each 2x inside reviewModel; review.ts:89-90, 292-306; run-status.ts:27,45,61; plus project at api/index.ts:125 and run pointer at inventory-records.ts:45-49) and 15 D1 trips + 2 R2 gets for an inventory-backed run (re-measured). Correction: they are not all in sequence. review.ts:276 and :323 use Promise.all. With an injected delay I measured 11.7-13.1 sequential I/O steps for the model (expected chain 11: 9 D1 + 2 R2). For the whole HTTP request it is 21 D1 trips, 15 of them sequential (6 prelude + 9 model), plus 2 sequential R2 reads. Batching and passing already-read rows are feasible.
secondLensReason: Counts reproduced with the real reviewModel (state-depth-3582.json): active run that needs review = 15 D1 trips + 2 R2 gets in the model, 21 D1 trips for the request, 15 in sequence with the 6 prelude trips; project read 3 times, run 3 times, comparison 2 times. Correction 1: the depth depends on run state. readRunStatus returns after one read for active = 0 (run-status.ts:27-35, review-status.ts:77). I measured an archived (superseded) run: 10 D1 trips in the model, 4 in sequence, so 10 in sequence for the request. The production samples (5.3-5.7 s) were archived pull request runs, so this finding explains only about 0.5-0.6 s of them; the 9-trip case (about 1.1-1.3 s) has no production sample. Correction 2: 'one batch cuts 15 to about 4' needs three changes (REVIEW-01, a 2-trip prelude with joins and a parallel project read, and the model batch). The model batch alone leaves 7-8. Feasibility confirmed: D1 batch() is one round trip and one transaction (official docs), per-statement limits apply inside a batch, and review.ts:277 and :335 already use it; the existing measureD1 helper can hold a round-trip budget test. Risks: readRunStatus is shared with prepareStatusIntent, which publishes the GitHub check, so the status rule order must not change; the 404 project check must still run before any row is used. Severity medium, not high: the gain is 0.3-1.1 s today, it falls to about 0.01-0.16 s if REVIEW-02 lands, and REVIEW-04 holds most of the measured wait. No contract effect.

title: Each model read downloads, hashes, and validates two complete inventories from R2
oneLine: reviewModel reads both immutable inventory objects on every call (9.4 MB and 166 ms Node CPU at 3,582 captures), rehashes, re-canonicalizes, validates each capture, and round-trips each capture through JSON strings; this repeats on every receipt and Undo.
verifierReason: review.ts:364 calls readReviewInventory; review-inventory.ts:44-48 reads the run inventory then the snapshot inventory in sequence; capture-inventory.ts:492-517 reads all bytes, sha256, JSON.parse and a second canonicalJson pass; :553 validates all captures and the receipt. No cache on the review path. Re-measured for 3,582 captures: 2 R2 gets, 9.38 MB, readReviewInventory 128 ms of the 168 ms model time (Node, not Workers CPU). Corrections: the read itself is deliberate (docs/current-contract.md:26 'Review reads the full inventory to show unchanged items'); re-validation per read is not required by the contract; no production timing for this step exists; a per-isolate cache has a memory risk (16 MiB objects, 128 MiB isolate).
secondLensReason: Hot path proved: review.ts:364 reads both inventories on every reviewModel call (run page load, ready receipt at :814, Undo and direct save at :637-639, conflict at :683), also for archived runs; review-inventory.ts:44-48 reads them one after the other. Measured by me (Node 24, M4 Pro, memory store, synthetic 3,582 captures): readReviewInventory 130-190 ms of a 170-220 ms model read. Split: sha256 3%, JSON.parse 9%, canonical check 36%, expand plus validate 52%. So 'rehashes' is true but not the cost. Production share by elimination: the D1 count model explains only about 1.3-1.5 s of the 5.25-5.68 s server wait for the archived samples, so about 3.8-4.3 s (72-76%) is R2 downloads, validation, model build, and JSON output. That split is not measured; one trace (observability.traces is enabled) gives it. The local numbers are a lower bound: the fixture model is 2.15 MB for 3,582 variants and production models are 5.3-6.0 MB for 3,832. Fix feasibility: (1) start both R2 reads together, because visonaut_comparisons.reference_snapshot_id already holds the baseline ID and the service enforces equality (local-comparison.ts:477); measured chain 4 -> 1.7 I/O steps. (2) Keep the size and digest check and skip the canonical check and validation on review reads: objects are content-addressed, validated before write (capture-inventory.ts:465), and R2 returns the sha256 given at put (official R2 docs). This removes about 88% of local inventory CPU but is a trust-rule choice; contract lines 24 and 26 require validation before import and a full inventory read, not validation per read. (3) An isolate cache retains 13.4 MiB at fixture size against the 128 MB per-isolate limit; a smaller review object needs a new decision (P01, contract line 26). Counter-argument: if the trace shows R2 transfer dominates, the validation is not the problem and should stay as defense.

title: The first response contains each unchanged capture, although the page needs only the changed ones first
oneLine: The model has about 600 bytes per capture for all captures (633 KB raw at 1,058, 2.15 MB at 3,582) while unchanged items sit in a closed Accepted group; an attention-first response needs D1 only and no R2. Contract line 26 mentions full-inventory reads.
verifierReason: Confirmed: review.ts:371-374 and review-inventory.ts:105-163 add one unchanged row per inventory capture; re-measured 3,578 of 3,582 variants unchanged, 2.15 MB JSON (205 KB gzip); production 5.3-6.0 MB / ~692 KB. Corrections: this is approved decision P01 'One compact complete model' (docs/current-contract.md:148) which rejected summary-plus-detail and has an explicit reopen clause that the production numbers now meet, so the finding must cite it; 'needs only the changed ones first' is not always true (Accepted count, search, keyboard order use all items; item-list.tsx:105-107 opens Accepted when the selection is inside, as in the production samples); the server wait, not the transfer, dominates.
secondLensReason: Hot path confirmed: each run page load calls GET /api/runs/<id> (runs.$runId.tsx:37-39), and review.ts:364 and :371-374 read two R2 inventories and add one row for each unchanged capture. The same build runs again for each decision. Measured (my probe, 3,582 captures, 4 changed): full model 2,153,156 B (205,102 gzip) against 4,580 B (1,301 gzip) for the attention items only; 15 D1 round trips and 2 R2 gets. Production (orchestrator): server wait 5.25-5.68 s, download only 0.05-0.33 s, so the transfer is not the bottleneck. By count, about 2.0 s is D1 (15 sequential trips at my measured 0.133 s) and about 3.2-3.7 s is R2 reads, validation, and serialization (a subtraction, not a trace). CORRECTION: the claim that an attention-first response needs D1 only and no R2 is wrong today. local-comparison.ts:325-327 writes NULL for reference_capture_id, and review.ts:442-446 takes the reference from the R2 baseline inventory. Measured: 0 of 4 reference images are available from the D1 model queries (4 of 4 candidates are), and a lookup by digest is SCAN visonaut_images (no index). A removed row also gets its name from the inventory. So the fix needs a data change at Submit, a digest index, or one R2 read. completeReviewRows is also an integrity check that would run after Approve is shown. No security rule changes. P01 (contract line 148) is an approved decision whose reopen clause names a budget that does not exist (docs/development.md:70-72). Strongest counter-argument: P01 says to do simple query cleanup first, and a cheap projection (REVIEW-04) removes the inventory cost with no second protocol.

title: Each saved decision and each Undo builds and returns the complete model again
oneLine: The receipt endpoint (review.ts:812-832) and Undo (commandResult) rebuild the full model (23 and 30 D1 round trips measured) although the stored receipt is sufficient and applySavedReview already handles a receipt without a model.
verifierReason: Receipt: review.ts:812-832 builds reviewModel and returns `{...result, model}`. Undo: review.ts:938-939 via commandResult (637-639). Client parses it (client.ts:250). Auditor probe: receipt 3,420 B vs 3,028 B model, 23 D1 trips; undo 30 trips. Addition: the light no-model response (review.ts:881-904) is unreachable because client.ts:313-318 always sends `queued: true`; review.ts:816 can discard a built model and force another poll. The contract keeps queued receipts but does not require the full model in them.
secondLensReason: Hot path confirmed: client.ts:313-318 always sends queued: true, so each Approve and Reject reads the receipt at review.ts:812-832, which builds the complete model. Undo does the same (review.ts:637-639, :938-939). Measured (my probe, handler only): receipt as coded is 19 D1 round trips, 2 R2 gets, 2,153,615 B; a receipt without a model is 3 D1 round trips and 425 B. With the 6 prelude trips: 25 against 9. By inference each decision costs about the same 5.25-5.68 s server wait as a page load in production, plus 692 KB and 5-6 MB of JSON to parse; no production save was measured. Worse than stated: review.ts:816 discards the built model when one more decision commits during the build, so fast decisions keep earlier receipts in a rebuild loop, and several builds can run at the same time in one 128 MB isolate (one build holds about 16 MB at its end in Node). Fix feasibility for saves: measured. The stored receipt (review-queue.ts:127) has exactly the keys that applySavedReview (navigation.ts:85-142) needs, and the page result is equal to the server model, field for field, for approve, reject, and a chain of four approvals that ends in status passed. A browser test already uses a receipt with no model (route.browser.test.ts:47-58). CORRECTIONS: (1) the receipt is not sufficient for Undo; the Undo result has no restored verdict, reviewer, runRevision, or runStatus (review-commands.ts:377-383). (2) api.test.ts:1272-1289 tests that a receipt shows a later decision of another reviewer; a receipt without a model needs the current run revision in the response and one refresh on mismatch. client.ts:235-252 does not parse previousRunRevision today. No contract or security rule requires the model in the receipt. Strongest counter-argument: the model in the receipt is deliberate and makes the page correct with no merge logic; the save does not block the reviewer; if the model becomes cheap, the simple design costs little.

title: Save confirmation has a fixed 500 ms wait, a late session request, and a permission cache that write requests clear
oneLine: client.ts sleeps 500 ms before the first receipt poll, creates the review session on the first Approve, and authorization.ts deletes but does not re-store the permission after live write checks (48 GitHub permission calls for 12 cycles).
verifierReason: 500 ms: client.ts:326-328, and the auditor's raw data shows 501-502 ms between admission end and the app's receipt GET (the earlier GET is the harness, run-routes.mjs:80). Late session: client.ts:295-303,310 sends POST /api/review-sessions on first save. Cache cleared by writes: authorization.ts:63,71,74; probe shows a GitHub permission call after each write request. Limits: save timings are local with near-zero D1 latency; no production number. Contract (current-contract.md:186,204) requires live checks for writes but does not require a successful write to drop the read grant, and the tests do not assert it, so storing the fresh positive result is feasible; it is a security rule for the maintainer.

title: Each first view of an image goes through the Worker, D1, and R2 with no edge cache
oneLine: /images/:id does 1 D1 query plus 1 R2 read per request and never uses the Cache API, so `immutable` helps only one browser; the D1 lookup alone is 154 ms TTFB in production and Approve stays disabled until both images decode.
verifierReason: images.ts:24-28 (one D1 read), :39-40 (one R2 get/head), :52 (immutable, 1 year). No Cache API use in the app; /images/* always runs the Worker. Production /images/<unknown> = 151-157 ms with no cf-cache-status. Corrections: no production measurement of a real first image view exists (the live sample was a browser-cache hit); the Cache API is per data center and the app has few viewers, so an edge cache gives little for first views; the changeable cost is the per-image D1 lookup plus missing preload; an edge copy needs a purge rule for deleted bytes. Severity lowered from high.
secondLensReason: Path confirmed: index.ts:113-116 calls publicImage before any auth work; images.ts:24-28 is one D1 read, :39-40 is one R2 get, :52 sets immutable for one year; no Cache API call exists (rg returns nothing); Workers run before the cache, so the zone cache never sees the response. use-evidence.ts:76-114 and review-workspace.tsx:302-307 keep Approve disabled until both images decode. Measured in production (6 samples, Worker at GRU): /images/<unknown id> 404 has a median TTFB of 0.156 s against 0.023 s for /health, so the D1 lookup is about 0.133 s. The R2 read was not measured by any lane, and no real first view of an image was measured. Fix feasibility: the Cache API works on the custom domain (wrangler.jsonc:49), but Cloudflare says it is local to a data center and not compatible with tiered caching, so the first view by a reviewer is always a miss and a later view already comes from the browser cache. With one or two reviewers the gain is near zero. An edge copy also keeps answering 200 after bytes_present becomes 0, and cache.delete purges only the local data center; D16 (contract line 59) makes this a retention decision, not an access breach. A public R2 domain is not an option because the IMAGES bucket also holds the private inventories. The levers that change a first view are a preload of the next variant (REVIEW-09), Worker placement, or a storage layout with no D1 lookup. Strongest counter-argument: P06 selected this simple design without a cache service; the cost is one time for each image and browser. Severity medium, not high, the same as the first verifier.

title: The page does not preload the next images
oneLine: No preload exists for the next pending variant, adjacent variants, or the diff mask; nextPending already knows the target, so each Approve or arrow key waits for fresh image requests.
verifierReason: rg for preload/prefetch/new Image in apps/web/src returns nothing; screenshot-viewer.tsx:146-149 renders only the selected variant's images; router.tsx sets no defaultPreload. Not measured, as the auditor stated. CSP (`img-src 'self' data:`) permits a preload. Related approved decisions: P02 removed optional image work and U06 asks to measure arrow-to-image display, so a preload is a maintainer choice.

title: The model request can start only after all JavaScript is loaded and hydrated
oneLine: `ssr: false` plus a client loader makes HTML -> 230 KB brotli of assets -> hydration -> API -> render -> images strictly serial (API starts at 1,875 ms on the slow profile); an inline script in the shell can start the fetch in parallel.
verifierReason: Confirmed: runs.$runId.tsx:31 `ssr: false` and :37-39 client loader; the server document holds only the pending text and 9 modulepreload links; production model request starts 206-300 ms after navigation start. Corrections: 'all JavaScript' is too strong (in the auditor's slow warm sample the fetch starts at 483 ms while three chunks end at 502-517 ms); today it is ~4% of a 6.7-7.8 s wait; the client-only loader is approved decision P03 (current-contract.md:150). An inline nonce script that starts the fetch early is feasible (__root.tsx:23-26 already emits one); preload-as-fetch fits poorly with `cache: no-store`.

title: The pull-request page makes a second authenticated round trip before the run starts to load
oneLine: /pulls/:n hydrates, calls /api/pulls (8 D1 round trips, 6 of them the repeated preamble), navigates, lazy-loads 4 run chunks, then calls /api/runs; a server redirect or a combined response removes one hop (estimated 1.0-1.3 s).
verifierReason: pulls.$pullNumber.tsx:47-58 fetches /api/pulls in a useEffect, :80-82 then navigates to the run, whose loader fetches /api/runs/<id>. Probe: lookup 8 D1 trips (82 statements), then 19 for the run; ~1.1 s by count at 140 ms per trip (not measured in production). Additions: the production pull document preloads no runs._runId-* chunk (my curl: 7 modulepreload links), and the pull card stays ~1 s more after navigate (pendingMs). A server redirect for signed-in ready checks is feasible.

title: Hashed assets are revalidated on each load, and main navigation reloads the document
oneLine: Assets are served with `public, max-age=0, must-revalidate` (no public/_headers), so 10 conditional requests run per document load and the favicon revalidates per variant change; header links are plain anchors and the router has no defaultPreload.
verifierReason: Production header for /assets/index-MxeSnhFR.js: `cache-control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate` with an etag; apps/web/public has no `_headers` file; Cloudflare documents that default and the `_headers` override. Main navigation uses plain anchors (app-shell.tsx:15-19, 29, 53-58; review-workspace.tsx:580). My Chrome check: clicking 'Run history' issues a document request and loses JS state, while a router Link does not. Revalidation cost is small; the reload matters more on the dashboard lane.

title: The waits show text only, the layout moves, and a signed-out visitor waits for a 401
oneLine: The pending shell is one grey line with no workspace frame; three loading texts show at once; the viewer shifts 41 px on each image load; a visitor without a session cookie waits 515-569 ms for a 401 before the sign-in card.
verifierReason: Text-only waits: runs.$runId.tsx:66-74 and pulls.$pullNumber.tsx:179-183, visible in the auditor's screenshots. Layout movement re-measured: pane label moves 41 px (437 to 396) when images become ready, one layout-shift entry of 0.0135 (small, in the 'good' range). Signed-out wait: loader maps 401 to guest (runs.$runId.tsx:42-44); production 401 for /api/runs/<uuid> takes 436-576 ms after JS loads, and all 3 D1 trips on that path are avoidable. Whether text-only is a problem is a design opinion.

title: The sidebar thumbnail has no source in current runs
oneLine: `thumbnailImageId` is written only by the retired compare Worker; local-v1 results never set it, so every sidebar row of a new run shows a dash while test fixtures show thumbnails.
verifierReason: review.ts:505-507 sets a thumbnail only from result.thumbnailImageId. The only producer is apps/compare/src/process.ts:191,206,228, which the production entry apps/compare/src/index.ts:1-7 does not import. The current path writes localResult without a thumbnail (workflow-materialize.ts:345-353). item-list.tsx:239-243 then shows a dash tile for every item.

title: A cold isolate makes three GitHub calls in sequence before any data is read
oneLine: Installation token, login hint, and permission caches live only in isolate memory, so the first private request after a cold start does token mint, GET /user/:id, and the permission read one after the other; cold frequency and GitHub latency not measured.
verifierReason: github.ts:164-173 mints a token on first use (134-158), :251 resolves /user/<id> with no login hint, :256 checks permission; caches are module state (github.ts:102,193; authorization.ts:19). Re-measured: cold isolate makes access_tokens, /user/42, permission; same isolate makes none. Corrections: 6 D1 trips come first, so it is 'before run data', not 'before any data'; no production timing and no data on cold-isolate frequency; a warm isolate still makes 1 GitHub call after 60 s idle, which is the more frequent case. The permission call can run in parallel with data reads.

title: The CLI stops on answers that the server marks as temporary
oneLine: Server uses 503 + Retry-After: 1 for waiting states (55 throw sites, 10 codes); the CLI retries only 2 codes on GET/PUT/reuse, so no OIDC or service request of an unchanged Submit (27 of 36 requests) has a retry and network errors are never retried.
verifierReason: Facts hold: packages/cli/src/http.ts:201-214 retries only validation_busy and service_unavailable for GET, PUT, and the reuse POST; four retryUnavailable call sites; network errors are never retried (http.ts:225-233); the server adds Retry-After: 1 to each 503 (apps/web/src/api/index.ts:42,82); my rg count is also 55 sites and 10 codes; probe M1 re-run is identical (2 fetch calls, exit 4). Waiting states exist (pre-run-checks.ts:473-475, pre-run-candidates.ts:73-86, pre-run.ts:138-139). Corrections: (1) the policy is deliberate, and retry.test.ts:99 'does not retry a semantic failure disguised as a 503' contradicts the main recommendation; (2) the server uses 503 plus Retry-After for states that need a person, for example capacity_exceeded (apps/web/src/capacity.ts:109-113), so 'retry each 503' repeats permanent failures; (3) the replay proof cites packages/service reserveRun and commitShard, but POST /v1/runs calls reserveStaged (apps/web/src/api/workflow-owned.ts:327-474); the HTTP layer is still replay-safe (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, renewReservation, submitStaged returns the stored receipt at 1248-1261). The allow-list alternative is the feasible form. Failure frequency is not measured.

title: The CLI hides the cause of most failures
oneLine: Five catch blocks replace specific errors with general sentences; server error.code and error.reference are dropped, a 503 during begin returns exit 4, a wrong job-name template returns 'The verified capture submission failed.', and no message names the item or limit.
verifierReason: All five catch sites exist as quoted (http.ts:221-223, bundle-submit.ts:69-71, index.ts:37-38, files.ts:50-57, png-comparison.ts:34-39). captureJobNames throws ProtocolError, not CliError (packages/protocol/src/workflow-jobs.ts:17-20), so a wrong template gives the general message with exit 1. Probe M1 re-run is identical. Corrections: the CLI parses the error body only for HTTP 503 and 409 (http.ts:175-183), so the recommended snippet prints no code for 400, 404, 413, or 422 unless that line changes too; the general messages are a stated security rule (http.ts:179 and 229, retry.test.ts:71-79, protocol README line 34 'private diagnostic message'), so print only code and reference, not the server message; bundle-submit.ts:69 also hides the useful OIDC CliError.

title: Image and capture limits differ in six places, and the smallest limit applies last
oneLine: Adapter accepts 20 MiB and 32 MP, trusted Submit accepts 2 MiB, 2.1 MP, 8192 px; the largest documented Ariakit capture (1248x1650) is at 98.1% of the pixel limit and an oversize capture fails only in Submit with 'Capture the image again'.
verifierReason: Each cell of the limits table is correct (visual.ts:352,356,399; artifact-archive.ts:7-11; files.ts:9-11; compare/src/types.ts:9-14; validate.ts:114,348-350; runtime-defaults.ts:7-18) and probe M3 re-run is identical. Corrections: (1) the '98.1% of the pixel limit' and '33 pixels' impact use an old grouped WebP fixture (hosted-resource-evidence.md:19). The repository records the current split capture set in docs/evidence/ariakit-capture-measurement/README.md:39: maximum 1,547,520 pixels (73.7% of 2,100,000) and maximum 210,157 bytes (10.0% of 2 MiB). The report says this distribution is unknown. (2) The 'Minimal' alternative breaks visualBatch: visual.ts:352-357 is readScreenshot, which also reads the full-page source screenshot that is cropped later (visual.ts:239-247, 387-403); the item limit belongs in cropScreenshot or attachCapture. (3) packages/cli/README.md:25 documents the Submit limits.

title: Submit decodes each candidate PNG two times, also when the bytes equal the reference
oneLine: validateLocalImages and compareLocally both fully decode every capture; in an unchanged run 90-100% of compareLocally time is spent before the digest equality check (3.9-5.1 ms per real 640x360 image, 42-55 ms per synthetic large image).
verifierReason: Mechanism confirmed: decode at local-comparison.ts:44 and again at 239, before the equality branch at 260-274; decodePng inflates two times (packages/compare/src/png.ts:200, then PNG.sync.read at png-comparison.ts:25); the recommended code is correct. Impact corrected: my probe (verify/decode-entropy.out.txt) shows about 12 ms for each million pixels and about 40 ms for each MiB of encoded data (1248x1650: 24 ms at 12 KiB, 51 ms at 706 KiB). The M2 images are high-noise. With the recorded Ariakit pass (510 million pixels and 60 MiB in total, mean 142,444 pixels and 17.6 KiB) one decode pass is about 14 seconds on this machine. The 149 to 196 second range does not apply. CI runner time is not measured.

title: Service.status() makes 5 to 6 sequential round trips and reads rows that the caller already has
oneLine: readRunStatus runs run, comparison, a legacy dead-task join, counts, project, and promotion as separate awaits; review page load and each poll (7-8 sequential round trips) repeat reads of run, comparison, and project; one database.batch would make it 1 round trip.
verifierReason: packages/service/src/run-status.ts:26-80 has 5 to 6 sequential awaits; probe M5 re-run is identical (5 round trips, 6 with a promotion pointer). reviewPollState (apps/web/src/api/review.ts:104-130) is 7 to 8 sequential round trips with run and comparison read two times. D1 batch is one call and a transaction (https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/worker-api/d1-database/), and the app does not use D1 sessions, so the batch is feasible. Corrections: on page load review.ts:276-307 runs project, status, and comparison in one Promise.all, so the repeated reads add queries but not waiting time; the gain is the batch inside status(). The recommended batch has no query for the failed branch (run-status.ts:36-42 reads visonaut_audit).

title: The comparison identities accept one value, and stored manifests are validated again on each read
oneLine: validateLocalComparison accepts only 'playwright-pixelmatch-1.63.0' and 'pngjs-7.0.0', stored inventories pass through parseManifest on every read, and no test or Renovate rule binds the constants to the installed pngjs/pixelmatch versions.

Each stored run inventory keeps the manifest with the receipt (workflow-materialize.ts:377-386) and each read calls parseManifest two times (apps/web/src/capture-inventory.ts:193 and 369 via 553), which calls validateLocalComparison (validate.ts:354). The review page reads it for each run with inventory_key (review.ts:364). No test binds the constants to the installed pngjs 7.0.0 or pixelmatch 5.3.0; renovate.json has only a Playwright rule. title: Reference downloads are sequential, and three server write loops use small pages
oneLine: compareLocally downloads one reference per changed capture with no concurrency, a capability renewal re-reads all 18 reference pages, and commitShard spends 36 assertion-only round trips for 3,582 captures because the page size is 100.
verifierReason: Cited code exists: one awaited download for each changed capture (cli local-comparison.ts:219, 275-281); renewal reads all reference pages again (engine.ts:416-429); the capability lives 600 seconds; commitShard asserts all captures in pages of 100 (run-admission.ts:542-564, 36 batches for 3,582 captures); registerImages takes 50 and reads the run each time. Corrections: commitShard runs in the background materialization after submitStaged queues an ingest message (workflow-owned.ts:1279), not in the Submit request; a page of 1,000 entries is about 70 KB in one bound value, inside the D1 limits (2 MB value, 100 parameters, https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/platform/limits/); parallel comparison changes the stated rule at local-comparison.ts:208 (one decoded pair at a time).
