title: The adapter waits a fixed 100 ms and decodes two PNGs for each capture, and the reporter loads modules that it does not use
oneLine: Each visual() call sleeps at least 100 ms and decodes both screenshots (30-47 ms measured versus 0.05 ms to compare encoded bytes), the published reporter.js imports @playwright/test and pngjs for two constants, and the font list that feeds fontsDigest is sorted with ICU collation.
verifierReason: Facts hold: 100 ms wait at visual.ts:382, decode at 359, pixel comparison at 374, the published reporter.js imports @playwright/test and pngjs (lines 484-485), and environment.ts:49 sorts with localeCompare before the list goes into fontsDigest. Corrections: the recommended line does not remove a decode, because readScreenshot decodes before it returns (visual.ts:359); visualBatch needs the decoded source pixels for cropScreenshot (visual.ts:239-247); the wait is one time for each stable screenshot, so one batch waits one time for all items and '358 seconds' is an upper limit; the wait is documented behavior (playwright README line 3); the ICU risk is bounded by the exact Node 24.18.0 engines pin, and a profile change with zero changed pixels needs no review (current-contract.md:124).

title: Each API request runs a full database schema check inside better-auth
oneLine: createAuth builds a new better-auth 1.7.5 instance per request; each one sends 1 sqlite_master query + 1 batch of 75 pragma_table_info statements before any auth call. Guest /api/me 344-351 ms and /api/runs 366-413 ms vs 28 ms without auth. advanced.database.validateSchema:false gives 0 statements locally.
verifierReason:
All quoted code exists and does what the finding says.

Proof (code): `packages/security/src/auth.ts:15-21` builds `betterAuth(...)` in each call and sets no `advanced.database` option (`rg validateSchema` in the repository: no match). Callers: `apps/web/src/api/index.ts:130`, `apps/web/src/server.ts:85`, `:93`. better-auth is 1.7.5 in the committed lockfile and in `packages/security/package.json:16`. `better-auth/dist/auth/base.mjs:15` starts `ctx.checkSchema?.()` when the instance is built. `better-auth/dist/api/to-auth-endpoints.mjs:40-42` awaits it before each `auth.api.*` call, before a cookie is read. `@better-auth/core/dist/db/schema-check.mjs:51-77` keeps `clean` in a closure of one adapter, so a new instance checks again. `@better-auth/kysely-adapter/dist/d1-sqlite-dialect-D4qp4-wW.mjs:88-98` sends 1 `sqlite_master` query and 1 `batch` of `pragma_table_info`. The built Worker contains this code (`rg -c 'pendingSchemaCheck|pragma_table_info' apps/web/dist/server`: index.js 13).

Proof (local re-run of `auth-guest-cost.mjs`, output in `verify/rerun-*.txt`): guest 76 statements and 2 round trips; `--no-validate` 0; `--shared` 76 then 0; construct-only 76; session 78 and 4; session `--no-validate` 2 and 2. My row count (`verify/schema-rows.mjs`): `sqlite_master` 230 + columns 625 = 855. better-auth needs only 5 tables with 38 columns.

Proof (live re-run, 20:09 UTC, GRU, guest): `/health` 28, 28 ms (first 43). `/api/me` 389, 318, 428 ms. `/api/runs` 338, 317, 322, 358 ms. Added time: 290 to 400 ms (report: 320 to 350 ms). Nothing else in the guest path does I/O: `createGitHubClient` only hashes the key (`packages/security/src/github.ts:107-126`).

No contract rule asks for a runtime schema check. The recommendation is correct: the option is `advanced.database.validateSchema` (`@better-auth/core/dist/types/init-options.d.mts:390-400`) and deploy applies migrations first (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml:125-133`).

Additions:
1. `packages/security/test/auth-d1.test.ts:35` builds `createAuth` on the real migrations, so the default check is also the CI schema test. A hard-coded `false` removes it. Make it a parameter of `createAuth`, or keep one test with the check on.
2. A safer per-isolate option than a shared instance (no promise crosses requests): `const checked = new WeakSet<D1Database>();` then `database: { validateSchema: !checked.has(db) }`, and `checked.add(db)` after the first call that succeeds.
3. Missing option: `createAuth` at `api/index.ts:130` runs before the `/v1/*` capture routes (`:134-189`). The `/api/auth/` branch at `:131-133` cannot run, because `server.ts:82-87` answers first. Build the instance after line 189. Capture requests then never start the check.
4. The production proof is indirect. Workers traces are on (`apps/web/wrangler.jsonc:15-20`) and Cloudflare records `d1_all` and `d1_batch` spans with `rows_read` (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/observability/traces/spans-and-attributes/). The dashboard can confirm the two schema calls on a real request.
5. Limit: the experiment runs in Node, not in workerd.
secondLensReason: Hot path proved: apps/web/src/api/index.ts:130 and apps/web/src/server.ts:85,93 build a new better-auth 1.7.5 instance for each /api/* and /v1/* request in production. better-auth/dist/auth/base.mjs:15 starts the check, to-auth-endpoints.mjs:41-42 awaits it, and the clean flag lives in one adapter instance (@better-auth/core/dist/db/schema-check.mjs:58-67), so a per-request instance never has a cached result. The D1 dialect sends 1 sqlite_master query plus one batch of pragma_table_info for every table (d1-sqlite-dialect-D4qp4-wW.mjs:89-98); I counted 74 tables + 1 view in the local schema copy. Magnitude: my 16 anonymous production GETs give guest /api/runs 374 ms median against /health 29 ms, so about 345 ms for the check at GRU (other lanes: 332 to 356 ms). That is 31 to 39% of the signed-in /api/runs wait (865 to 1,077 ms, orchestrator measurement) and 26 to 28% of /api/operations; a dashboard load pays it two times in series. It also runs, not awaited, on each CI /v1 request including one per uploaded image, on a database that Cloudflare documents as single-threaded. Fix is feasible: advanced.database.validateSchema exists in the installed version (init-options.d.mts:390-400) and the better-auth documentation names it as the way to disable the check; upstream issue 11346 describes this per-request factory case. No change to the security contract (docs/current-contract.md:186 session and account checks stay). Risks: a schema mismatch then shows as a failed query (still fails closed with 503), and no repository test compares the better-auth schema with the migrations. The shared-instance alternative has a real cross-request I/O risk and should not be used. Strongest counter-argument: the check is the only automatic guard between hand-written migrations and the library schema, and near the database it would cost two short round trips.

title: One D1 round trip costs about 90 ms from GRU, and a signed-in API request makes 6 to 9 in series
oneLine: Measured: 1 extra point query adds 85-135 ms (/api/runs/<id> 453-517 ms vs /api/runs 366-384 ms). Counted from code, not measured: /api/runs 6 and /api/operations 9 serial D1 round trips when signed in. No placement setting; operationsStatus reads the project a second time.
verifierReason:
The code facts and the round-trip counts hold. Two numbers and four recommendations need a correction.

Confirmed: `apps/web/src/api/dashboard.ts:68` is one `batch`; `apps/web/src/api/operations.ts:16,30,45` are 3 serial reads; `apps/web/src/api/context.ts:128-141` with `packages/service/src/service.ts:104-106` is 1 point query that `GET /api/runs` skips (`api/index.ts:123-126`); `packages/security/src/authorization.ts:40-43` is 1 account query; the local experiment (re-run) gives 4 round trips for a signed-in `getSession`. `apps/web/wrangler.jsonc` has no `placement` key. So 6 (`/api/runs`) and 9 (`/api/operations`) serial round trips are correct when the GitHub cache is warm.

Corrections:
1. The 90 ms figure is not stable. My 4 paired guest samples: `/api/runs` 338, 317, 322, 358 ms against `/api/runs/<id>` 466, 451, 482, 501 ms. Difference: 128 to 160 ms (median 144). The report's warm samples give 69 to 90 ms. Write '70 to 160 ms for one point query from GRU'. With about 140 ms the count model gives about 0.9 s for `/api/runs` and about 1.3 s for `/api/operations`. That agrees with the signed-in measurement in `audit/live-authenticated.md` (865 to 1077 ms and 1204 to 1299 ms). The report's 0.5 s and 0.8 s are too low.
2. The option is `advanced.database.joins`, not `experimental.joins` (`init-options.d.mts:351-389`; read at `@better-auth/core/dist/db/adapter/factory.mjs:192`; `experimental` at `:1549-1561` has only `instrumentation`). I tested it locally: with `joins: true` and no schema check a signed-in `getSession` sends 1 statement (`verify/rerun-session-joins.txt`).
3. `operationsStatus` does not repeat the same check. `operations.ts:16-18` reads `ORDER BY id LIMIT 2` to require exactly one project. Removing it changes behavior. The `batch` option keeps it.
4. The alternative 'cache from session token to account ID' breaks a contract rule: `docs/current-contract.md:186` 'Live session and linked-account checks still run for every request' (also `authorization.ts:62`).
5. Smart Placement: the key `"placement": { "mode": "smart" }` is correct. But Cloudflare says 'Smart Placement requires consistent traffic to the Worker from multiple locations to make a placement decision' (status `INSUFFICIENT_INVOCATIONS`), and the page does not name D1 (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/placement/). A tool with a few users can stay on default placement. The same page gives a fixed option: `"placement": { "region": "aws:<region>" }` near the D1 primary. The primary region is the span attribute `cloudflare.d1.response.served_by_region` in the Workers traces that are already enabled.
6. D1 read replication is not a drop-in for the auth path. The Kysely adapter accepts a D1 object only when it has `batch`, `exec`, and `prepare` (`@better-auth/kysely-adapter/dist/index.mjs:102`); `D1DatabaseSession` has no `exec` (`@cloudflare/workers-types` `index.d.ts:14596-14604`). A replica can also lag, which conflicts with the 'live session' rule unless the session starts with `first-primary` (https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/best-practices/read-replication/).
secondLensReason: Hot path proved from code: GET /api/operations makes 9 serial D1 round trips (project 1, schema check 2, session and user 2, account 1, operationsStatus 3 at apps/web/src/api/operations.ts:16,30,45) and GET /api/runs makes 6; the load lane counted the same with a D1 wrapper and a signed cookie. apps/web/wrangler.jsonc (125 lines, read in full) has no placement key. Magnitude: one extra point query costs 107 ms in my samples (/api/operations 481 ms minus /api/runs 374 ms), 140 to 142 ms in the load lane, 87 to 133 ms for the auditor, so about 90 ms is the low end; use 105 to 145 ms. The count model (335 ms + 7 x 105 to 145 ms = 1.07 to 1.35 s) agrees with the signed-in measurement of /api/operations (1.20 to 1.30 s), so confidence is now high. Platform reason: D1 has no South America region, so each round trip from GRU is intercontinental. Three corrections to the options: (1) experimental.joins does not exist in better-auth 1.7.5; the option is advanced.database.joins (init-options.d.mts:375-389, factory.mjs:192,562). (2) placement mode smart can stay in INSUFFICIENT_INVOCATIONS because the documentation requires consistent traffic from multiple locations; the documented choice for one database is a region hint, which wrangler 4.136.1 accepts (config-schema.json:261-333), but the D1 region must be read first and the gain is not measured. (3) Read replicas give nothing here (no replica in South America, Sessions API required, replica lag touches the live-session rule). The in-isolate session-to-account cache alternative conflicts with docs/current-contract.md:186. Joins, the operationsStatus batch, and placement do not change the contract. Round trips after the small fixes: /api/runs 6 to 3, /api/operations 9 to 4. Strongest counter-argument: the cost is a fact of one location, the contract fixes a floor of 2 to 3 round trips, and placement adds an opaque decision that also makes each document one hop slower.

title: The first data request starts only after all JavaScript has loaded and run
oneLine: SSR always sends 'Checking access'; index.tsx fetches in useEffect and the run route has ssr:false. Production guest: loading line on screen 406 ms cold, 454 ms warm, 940 ms with 4x CPU + slow 4G, 535 ms on the run page; the API wait is 92% of it.
verifierReason:
The facts hold. One alternative is not valid and the main recommendation needs a limit.

Confirmed: `apps/web/src/routes/index.tsx:161` starts with `{ status: "loading" }`, `:176-210` fetches in `useEffect`, `:275-279` renders the line. `apps/web/src/routes/runs.$runId.tsx:31` has `ssr: false` and the loader at `:37-47` runs in the browser. The captured production document has only this visible text: 'visonaut. Review queue Run history Service status Checking access and loading runs…' (83 characters by my count, `verify/doc-facts.out.txt`). The four table rows equal the raw summaries (`summary-prod-home-guest.txt`, `summary-prod-home-guest-throttled.txt`, `summary-prod-run-guest.txt`). Each row is 1 sample.

Corrections:
1. Size of the effect. On the measured fast link the script chain is 231 − 94 = 137 ms of the 406 ms wait. The API wait is the other 92%. This finding alone is worth about 0.14 s on a fast link and about 2.0 s on slow 4G. That is why my severity is medium. LIVE-01 and LIVE-02 are the larger part of the 'checking access' wait.
2. A blocking server loader moves the wait; it does not remove it. Signed in, `/api/runs` needs 0.9 to 2.0 s, and the run model needs 5.3 to 5.7 s and is 5.3 to 6.0 MB of JSON (`audit/live-authenticated.md`). If the document waits for that, the first paint waits too, and the run model is sent inside the HTML. For the run page use streamed (deferred) loader data or the early-fetch option. For guests the cookie test on the server is cheap and correct (documents are `no-store, private`, `packages/security/src/http.ts:33`).
3. The alternative 'remove `ssr: false` from the run route' is not valid as written. With `ssr: false` the server already renders the shell and the pending component (the captured run document has the header and the loading line). Without it the loader runs in the Worker, where `fetch("/api/runs/<id>")` has no origin and no cookie (`apps/web/src/review/client.ts:254-262`).
4. The early inline fetch is feasible: the CSP allows inline scripts that carry the nonce (`http.ts:40-43`), and `apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:23-26` already has one.
secondLensReason: Facts confirmed: apps/web/src/routes/index.tsx:161,176-210 fetch only in useEffect, the route has no loader, apps/web/src/routes/runs.$runId.tsx:31 has ssr:false, and the saved production documents contain the loading text. It runs on each document load, and header links and the run page Queue button are plain anchors, so each click reloads the document. Severity lowered: what this finding owns is the gap between the document first byte and the API start. That is 107 to 138 ms for a guest on a fast link and 199 to 303 ms for the signed-in maintainer (5 orchestrator samples), against a /api/runs end at 1.2 to 2.3 s, so about 10 to 20% of the wait; the report itself says the API is 92%. It is about 2 s only with 4x CPU and slow 4G. Fix feasibility: createServerFn, createIsomorphicFn, getRequest, ssr data-only and getSessionCookie all exist in the installed versions, but the main recommendation has three problems the report does not state. (a) Server-function responses skip securePrivateResponse: apps/web/src/server.ts:23-28 wraps only the router callback (createStartHandler.js:386), and server functions take another branch (createStartHandler.js:337-348), so a private server function would answer without no-store and the other security headers. (b) An awaited loader moves the 0.9 to 2.0 s access check into the document first byte (createStartHandler.js:372). (c) The run page cannot use it: the model is 5.3 to 6.0 MB and decision P03 keeps that route client-only. Low-risk parts: render the sign-in view in SSR when no session cookie is present, and the early fetch from a nonce inline script (the CSP and apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:23-26 already allow it). title: /api/operations starts only after /api/runs ends, and repeats the auth work

title: Hashed assets are served with max-age=0, must-revalidate
oneLine: No _headers file. A warm load of the production home page sent 10 conditional requests, all 304, 46-98 ms wait each; scripts were usable only after them.
verifierReason:
Confirmed by a new measurement and by the platform documentation.

Proof: my re-run `GET https://visonaut.com/assets/index-CXm4JU5N.css` gave `cache-control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate`, `etag: W/"9e4cfd6955347432dd08ee4c96daa415"`, `cf-cache-status: HIT`. The raw warm load (`summary-prod-home-guest.txt`) has 10 responses with wire status 304, 452 to 470 bytes, 46 to 98 ms wait. `apps/web/public` has only `favicon.svg`. `apps/web/dist/server/wrangler.json` has `"assets":{"directory":"../client"}` and no header rule. All 14 files in `apps/web/dist/client/assets` have a content hash in the name.

Platform: Cloudflare states the default `Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate` for static assets, and that `_headers` rules 'are not applied to responses generated by your Worker code' (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/headers/). So the 404 HTML for a missing asset stays `no-store`. `_headers` in the Vite `public` directory works 'at build, preview and deploy time' (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/vite-plugin/reference/static-assets/).

Small corrections:
1. Check the rule with `vite preview` or after a deploy. It does not apply in `pnpm dev`, and this project does not use `wrangler dev`.
2. The impact is larger than stated. The header links and the 'Queue' button cause full page loads (see LIVE-14), so each view switch repeats the 10 conditional requests, not only a repeat visit.
3. The same file can add the security headers that static assets do not have now (see Missed).

title: A cold Worker adds about 300 to 450 ms to the document
oneLine: Document wait 354-511 ms with cfEdge 199-267 ms on cold hits vs 56-131 ms with cfEdge 9-21 ms warm (preview cold on 3 of 3 new connections, production on 1 of 3). Server build is 4.1 MB of unminified JS (888 KB gzip); the link to startup time is an assumption.
verifierReason:
The measurement holds. The cause is not proved, production has one sample, and a cheaper number exists.

Confirmed (raw files): production `/` first curl request 406 ms with `cfEdge;dur=267, cfWorker;dur=112`, next four 91 to 131 ms. Preview 370 ms (`266`, `75`), then 56 to 97 ms. Preview browser loads 511 ms (`265`, `79`) and 354 ms (`199`, `49`). The server build numbers are exact (my count): 33 files, 4,104,202 bytes, 888,351 bytes gzip, `index.js` 46,193 lines, so not minified, and `"no_bundle": true` in `apps/web/dist/server/wrangler.json`. The same new-connection test on `/health` gave 41 and 43 ms, so the extra time is not connection setup.

Corrections:
1. Production has 1 cold sample (406 ms). The other 3 are preview.
2. The cause is an assumption, as the report says. The evidence does not define `cfEdge`.
3. A cheaper number exists. Cloudflare: 'To measure startup time, run `npx wrangler@latest deploy` … Wrangler reports `startup_time_ms` in the output' and 'Larger Worker bundles can impact startup time' (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/). The log of each production deploy already has the startup time. Read it before any change. `wrangler check startup` is real and gives the profile.
4. Minify must be set in the Vite SSR build. Wrangler does not change the files when `no_bundle` is true.
5. Size: at most 0.45 s, one time for a new edge machine or an idle period, against 2.6 to 7.8 s for the signed-in pages. That is why my severity is low.

title: No recovery when a lazy chunk is missing after a deploy
oneLine: Not reproduced. Missing assets return 404 HTML, there is no vite:preloadError handler, the run route is a separate chunk, and production deploys on each push to main.
verifierReason:
Refuted. The router already reloads the page one time when a route chunk is missing.

Proof (code): `apps/web/node_modules/@tanstack/react-router/dist/esm/lazyRouteComponent.js:35-46`:
`if (isModuleNotFoundError(error) && …) { const storageKey = \`tanstack_router_reload:${error.message}\`; if (!sessionStorage.getItem(storageKey)) { sessionStorage.setItem(storageKey, "1"); window.location.reload(); throw new Promise(() => {}); } }`
`isModuleNotFoundError` matches 'Failed to fetch dynamically imported module', 'error loading dynamically imported module', and 'Importing a module script failed' (`@tanstack/router-core/dist/esm/utils.js:147-150`).

Proof (shipped build): `apps/web/dist/client/assets/preload-helper-B-8p3_4s.js` contains `tanstack_router_reload`, and `index-MxeSnhFR.js` loads the run route as `component: pe(() => _e(() => import("./runs._runId-QUJlDVZ1.js"), …), "component")`, where `pe` is that function.

Proof (measurement, local dev server, `verify/nav-probe.mjs` step 2.1, output in `verify/nav-probe.out.txt`): I answered the first request for the split run component with status 404 and an HTML body, then clicked 'Review changes'. The page sent a new document request for `/runs/<id>`, `sessionStorage` got the key `tanstack_router_reload:Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: …`, and the run page then rendered.

The evidence lines of the finding are true (no `vite:preloadError` handler in `apps/web/src`; a missing asset returns 404 HTML). The conclusion is not. The proposed listener would add a second reload path that has no loop guard.

Limits of my proof: dev server and Chrome only; I did not test a real deploy. What remains: the guard allows one reload for each error message. The app has no other dynamic import (`rg 'import\(|lazy\(' apps/web/src` outside tests: no match), and the loader is not a separate chunk.

title: Error bodies and headers differ between routes
oneLine: /api/runs 401 has schemaVersion and no Retry-After; /api/me 401 has no schemaVersion, sends Retry-After: 1, and is logged as an operation failure; /health and /images 404 lack the security header set.

Proof: `body-prod-api-runs.bin` is `{"schemaVersion":"1.0","error":{"code":"sign_in_required",…}}` and `body-prod-api-me.bin` is `{"error":{"code":"sign_in_required",…}}`. 2. Two more shapes exist. The 404 fallback at `api/index.ts:214-219` has no `schemaVersion`. `server.ts:75, 84, 90-92` send 403 and 405 with an empty body.
3. The web app never calls `/api/me`. The browser tests assert that (`apps/web/src/review/__tests__/route.browser.test.ts:103`), and the only caller is `apps/web/tooling/review-scale/local-routes.mjs:273`. So the effect on users is small. Low is correct.

title: API responses have no application Server-Timing
oneLine: All 29 API and health responses sampled with curl lack server-timing; only documents carry Cloudflare's cfEdge/cfWorker. Auth, GitHub, and D1 time cannot be attributed from the browser.
verifierReason:
The fact holds. The stated impact is too strong.

Confirmed: no `/health` or `/api/*` response has a `server-timing` header (the auditor's raw captures and my 14 new samples). `rg -i server-timing apps packages` gives no match. `apps/web/src/server.ts:57` records `startedAt`.

Correction: 'A maintainer cannot see … why one request is slow' is true for browser DevTools only. Workers traces are on (`apps/web/wrangler.jsonc:15-20`, default sampling rate 1). Cloudflare records a span for each D1 call (`d1_all`, `d1_batch`, `d1_first`, `d1_run`) with `db.query.text`, `cloudflare.d1.response.rows_read`, `cloudflare.d1.response.sql_duration_ms`, and `cloudflare.d1.response.served_by_region`, and a span for each `fetch` (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/observability/traces/ and https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/observability/traces/spans-and-attributes/). The dashboard can already show why a request is slow. It also answers three open questions of the report: the D1 region, the cost of the two schema calls, and the background check on `/v1/*`. I could not open the dashboard, so I did not confirm that the spans are there.

Server-Timing still has value in DevTools and in the Resource Timing API of real sessions. The sketch is workable: it sets the header on success responses only, and `Date.now()` moves forward across awaited I/O in Workers.

title: Each return to the queue loads the run list again and shows the loading line again
oneLine: Index starts in 'loading' and fetches on every mount with no cache (index.tsx:161,176-210); the run route uses gcTime: 0. From code only; needs a session to measure.
verifierReason:
Part of the mechanism is wrong. The cost is larger than stated, and the recommendation is not sufficient.

Confirmed: `apps/web/src/routes/index.tsx:161` and `:176-210` (each mount starts in `loading` and fetches), no loader and no cache on `/`; `apps/web/src/routes/runs.$runId.tsx:35-36` (`gcTime: 0`, `staleTime: Infinity`).

Correction 1. The visible ways back to the queue are plain anchors, not router links: the 'Queue' button at `apps/web/src/review/review-workspace.tsx:580` (`render={<a href="/" />}`), the logo at `apps/web/src/components/app-shell.tsx:29`, and the three header links at `app-shell.tsx:15-19, 52-63` (`<NavLink href={href}>`). Each click is a full document load. Local measurement (`verify/nav-probe.mjs`, dev server, output in `verify/nav-probe.out.txt`): the click on 'Queue' and the click on 'Run history' each sent a new document request, a marker on `window` was lost, and `/api/runs` was fetched again. So each return, and each switch between Review queue, Run history, and Service status, pays the document, 10 conditional asset requests (LIVE-05), hydration, `/api/runs`, and `/api/operations`. Signed in this is 1.2 to 2.3 s to the list and 2.6 to 3.7 s to a stable page (`audit/live-authenticated.md`). The three views read the same `/api/runs` response (`index.tsx:363-374`).

Correction 2. The report's mechanism (client navigation, `Index` mounts again) is right only for the browser Back button after a router-link navigation, and for the link at `apps/web/src/routes/pulls.$pullNumber.tsx:155`. Measured locally (`verify/back-probe.mjs` 2 runs and `verify/back-probe-2.mjs` 1 run): Back kept the same document, showed the loading line, and fetched `/api/runs` again. Note: step 1.5 of `nav-probe.mjs` shows no request, because that script pressed Back before the run page had rendered.

Correction 3. A router cache or a module-level variable does not survive a document load. The anchors must become router links first, or the data must come with the document. The workspace also renders without a router in the test fixture (`review-workspace.tsx:743`), so the link element must be passed in. A loader on `/` also runs in the Worker during SSR, where the relative `fetch` has no origin and no cookie; it needs a server function or a client-only loader.

My severity is high: this is the core review loop, and the full reload is measured. The dev server sends `/api/runs` two times for each mount (React StrictMode); production sends it one time.
secondLensReason: The headline is correct and has local measurements from the first verifiers: browser Back shows loading=true at 11 ms and sends /api/runs again (live/verify/back-probe.out.txt, load/verify/nav-reload.rerun.txt). The cause is in the installed router: only routes with a loader are cached (router-core load-client.js:783) and the index route has none. Each return costs the same as a dashboard load: 6 + 9 serial D1 round trips, measured for a fresh load at 0.87 to 1.97 s then 1.20 to 1.30 s; the exact return sequence was not measured in production. Material corrections: (1) the usual return path is not a client navigation. The Queue button (apps/web/src/review/review-workspace.tsx:580) and the header links (apps/web/src/components/app-shell.tsx:29,55) are plain anchors, and the probe shows a new document for that click, so a router cache or a module variable is empty again. The fix needs router links first. (2) staleTime 30_000 in the sketch is a correctness risk: for 30 s after a decision the queue would show the old list with no request. The installed defaults already give the wanted behavior (staleTime 0, gcTime 5 minutes, background reload at load-client.js:330,346). (3) gcTime 0 on the run route is part of the selected P03 design for a 5 to 6 MB model and is not evidence for this finding. A loader with a relative fetch also cannot run in SSR, so it needs ssr:false or an isomorphic function. No server-side contract change; the browser would keep a private list in memory for at most 5 minutes, and sign-out and 401 or 403 on the background reload must clear it. Strongest counter-argument: after LIVE-01 and LIVE-02 the read on return is 3 round trips, and a list that is wrong for a moment after an approval can be worse than a short loading line.

I recovered the full report from the auditor's transcript into /Users/diegohaz/.claude/jobs/f65a6229/tmp/audit/load/verify/recovered-report.md and verified that text. Code: packages/security/src/auth.ts:15-16,47-51 (no advanced.database key); createAuth per request at apps/web/src/api/index.ts:130 and apps/web/src/server.ts:85,93. Better Auth 1.7.5: @better-auth/core/dist/db/schema-check.mjs:7-9 and 51-78 (verdict lives in one closure per adapter instance), @better-auth/kysely-adapter/dist/index.mjs:712, d1-sqlite-dialect-D4qp4-wW.mjs:89-98 (one sqlite_master query, then a batch with one pragma_table_info for each table and view in the whole database), better-auth/dist/auth/base.mjs:15, api/to-auth-endpoints.mjs:41-42. All quotes are exact. Local re-run with a signed session cookie instead of the auditor's Bearer header (verify/cookie.json): guest GET /api/runs = 2 round trips (sqlite_master + BATCH(75)); validateSchema:false gives requireMaintainer 'ok login=maintainer' with 3 round trips; plus joins:true gives 2. Production re-run (verify/prod-probe.rerun.txt): guest /api/runs median 365 ms, /health median 33 ms, difference 332 ms, and a guest does no other D1 work. No repository text or contract line requires the runtime check (rg for validateSchema|SchemaMismatch|getMigrations has no result outside node_modules). Additions: on /v1/* routes the check is started but not awaited (base.mjs:15-18), so CI requests do not wait for it but D1 still receives the 76 statements; PUT /v1/uploads/:token is one request per image (api/workflow-owned.ts:1005-1017), so it repeats per uploaded image on a single-threaded database (https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/platform/limits/). The recommendation is feasible: the option is documented in init-options.d.mts:390-400. No current test validates the auth schema, so the proposed test is new work.
secondLensReason: Hot path proved: apps/web/src/api/index.ts:130 builds a new Better Auth instance for each /api/* and /v1/* request, the kysely adapter registers one check per instance (kysely-adapter/dist/index.mjs:712, verdict in a closure at core/dist/db/schema-check.mjs:58-59), and to-auth-endpoints.mjs:41-42 awaits it before getSession. It runs 2 times per dashboard load, 1 time per run read, and also 1 time per Approve/Reject POST (not in the report). My own production probe (6 rounds, GRU): /health 40 ms, guest /api/runs 353 ms, so the check costs 313 ms; three independent runs give 313-333 ms, which is 29-38% of the measured signed-in /api/runs wait. Upstream docs confirm the cause: 'Validation is enabled by default, including in production, and caches a clean result or mismatch per adapter instance.' The fix exists in installed 1.7.5 (init-options.d.mts:390-400, schema-check.mjs:7-9) and is the documented way to disable it. No contract line requires the run-time check; session, account, and permission checks do not change. Risk: schema drift is then found by SQL errors (still fail-closed, 503) unless a CI test validates apps/web/migrations/0003_auth.sql. Counter-argument: it is the library default guard, and placement (LOAD-03) alone would decrease its cost to about 25-40 ms (estimate).

title: The server sends the loading text, and the data request starts only after hydration
oneLine: The `/` route has no loader, so the server HTML always contains "Checking access and loading runs…" and `/api/runs` starts only after 602 KB of JS loads and hydrates (166-367 ms guest, 240-595 ms signed in); a server loader or streamed loader removes the JS gate and one browser round trip without changing the access check.
verifierReason: Confirmed: apps/web/src/routes/index.tsx:39-44 has no loader; :161 and :176-184 as quoted; the saved production document contains role="status">Checking access and loading runs…; 1 CSS + 8 JS preloads; sizes re-measured exactly (JS 602,062 raw / 191,660 gzip; CSS 464,666 / 60,125); /api/runs starts at 367, 266, 166, 182 ms in prod-guest-waterfall.json. Corrections: (1) Size of the problem. The delay before the data request is 0.17-0.37 s for a guest and 0.24-0.60 s signed-in (orchestrator file audit/live-authenticated.md: 322, 359, 240, 277, 595 ms), while the measured signed-in server wait of /api/runs is 0.87-1.97 s. A loader removes about 0.2-0.6 s, which is 14-27% of the wait in four of five samples (41% in one). LOAD-01/03/04 remove more, so I rate it medium. (2) The P03 evidence does not apply. P03 in docs/simplification-audit/audit-data.json:2228-2330 is about the run page review model only, and its migration note says 'Keep this browser-oriented route client-only initially; server loading would need a separately scoped authenticated server read.' So ssr:false on the run route is deliberate and the dashboard was not part of the selection; this is not contract drift. (3) The first recommendation (a loader that awaits the read) moves the whole access check before the first byte: the document would arrive after about 0.9-2.0 s instead of 50-100 ms unless the streaming variant or a cookie pre-check is used. The report does not state this cost. Feasibility checked against installed types (createIsomorphicFn in router.tsx:5, getRequest in start-server-core request-response.d.ts:8, RequestOptions.context in request-handler.d.ts:56-66). Not built.
secondLensReason: The sequence is correct (routes/index.tsx:39-44 has no loader; fetch is in a useEffect at :176-184). The size is overstated: the gain of a server read is the gap between document first byte and /api/runs start, which is 199-303 ms in the 5 signed-in samples (10-21% of the 1.2-2.3 s to the queue), not 240-595 ms. The APIs exist in the installed versions (getRequest, RequestOptions.context, Await, defaultStreamHandler, ssr 'data-only'). The fix has hazards that the report does not list: (1) a streamed read cannot send the daily session Set-Cookie (api/index.ts:220-222; better-auth session.mjs:198-214 updates the row then sets the cookie), so it needs query.disableRefresh, which requireMaintainer does not accept today; (2) server-rendered rows give a hydration mismatch because runDate uses toLocaleString(undefined) (routes/index.tsx:153-157); (3) the document path has no origin check while production has workers_dev: true; (4) preview has no bindings; (5) an awaited loader delays the first byte by 0.9-2.0 s today. The P03 decision covers the run page only and says server loading 'would need a separately scoped authenticated server read'. Counter-argument: the other three findings remove more with smaller changes. Note: after those fixes the gap becomes about half of the wait that remains.

title: Each D1 round trip costs about 105-125 ms from the São Paulo edge, and the Worker has no placement setting
oneLine: Production probes at GRU show 32 ms with no D1, 157 ms with one D1 round trip, and +106 ms per further round trip; private reads make 6-9 serial round trips and wrangler.jsonc has no `placement`, so smart or targeted placement near D1 is the main latency lever (database region not verified).
verifierReason: apps/web/wrangler.jsonc:1-125 has no placement key; rg for withSession and "placement" in apps/ and packages/ has no result; wrangler config-schema.json:261-330 accepts the four listed forms. Production re-run (8 samples, colo GRU, cf-placement null): /health 33 ms, /images/<unknown> 175 ms (1 D1 round trip, api/images.ts:24-35), guest /api/runs 365 ms, guest /api/operations 505 ms. Per round trip: 142 ms and 140 ms (auditor: 125 and 106). Use 'about 105-145 ms'. The signed-in measurement fits the model: /api/operations has 9 round trips = 332 ms + 7 x 105-145 ms = 1.07-1.35 s; measured 1.20-1.30 s. Platform facts: 'D1 location hints are not currently supported for South America ... D1 databases do not run in these locations' (https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/configuration/data-location/), so every D1 round trip from GRU is intercontinental; read replicas exist only in ENAM, WNAM, WEUR, EEUR, APAC, OC and need the Sessions API (https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/best-practices/read-replication/), so the replica alternative gives no gain in Brazil if the primary is ENAM. Placement syntax {mode:'smart'} and {region:'aws:us-east-1'} is as documented; 'Smart Placement requires consistent traffic to the Worker from multiple locations', hints are recommended when 'Your Worker connects to a single database', placement 'only affects the execution of fetch event handlers', and static assets stay at the edge (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/placement/). Smart Placement considers D1 (https://blog.cloudflare.com/sqlite-in-durable-objects/). Corrections: the region hint uses cloud-provider region names, so the D1 region must be read first; it is still not verified. The stated tradeoff (one long hop per Worker request) is correct.
secondLensReason: env.production in apps/web/wrangler.jsonc:46-123 has no placement key; all my production responses had colo GRU and no cf-placement header. Per round trip cost is 106-142 ms in three independent runs, and the model matches the signed-in /api/operations wait (1.09-1.39 s computed, 1.20-1.30 s measured). New evidence from the repository: a diagnostic Worker already used "placement": {"region": "aws:us-east-1"} (apps/web/tooling/backup-v2-recorded/wrangler.example.json:60-62), the recorded result is cf-placement remote-IAD for a request that entered at CWB (docs/evidence/backup-restore-v2.json:493-497), and 316 recorded D1 queries served by primary colo EWR show a median wall-minus-SQL time of 16.5 ms (12-18 ms per file). So a near round trip is about 8 times cheaper. Estimate with placement: /api/runs 0.24-0.28 s (measured today 0.87-1.08 s), /api/operations 0.28-0.32 s (1.20-1.30 s), document +0.12 s. Feasible: Wrangler 4.136.1 schema accepts all four forms, the Vite plugin keeps the key, and Cloudflare docs recommend hints for a Worker with a single database. Risks: smart mode can stay at INSUFFICIENT_INVOCATIONS on low traffic; the production database colo is not read (meta.served_by_colo gives it); D1 has no South America region, so read replicas do not help. No contract change. Counter-argument: with 3 round trips per read after LOAD-01 and LOAD-04, placement saves about 0.24 s per private read and costs 0.12 s on each request with no D1 work.

title: The access check and the operations read send their D1 statements one at a time
oneLine: Session and user are two statements because Better Auth joins are off, the account lookup is a third, `/api/operations` checks the project twice and runs 3 independent statements serially; `joins: true` plus one batch brings `/api/runs` from 6 to 3 and `/api/operations` from 9 to 3 round trips (with LOAD-01).
verifierReason: packages/security/src/authorization.ts:32-43 (getSession then the account statement); @better-auth/core/dist/db/adapter/factory.mjs:562 exact; advanced.database.joins is a normal option in 1.7.5 (init-options.d.mts:375-389), not experimental; apps/web/src/api/operations.ts:16-18, 30-36, 45-47 are three awaited statements with no dependency; the project is read twice for /api/operations (api/index.ts:123-126 and operations.ts:16-29). Re-run with a signed cookie (verify/cookie.json): current = 5 round trips (sqlite_master, BATCH(75), session, user, account); validateSchema:false = 3; plus joins:true = 2 (one session statement with join_user columns, then account). All variants return the same identity. At the measured 105-145 ms per round trip, joins saves about 0.1 s per private read and the operations batch about 0.3-0.4 s. The statement that the session cookie cache needs a contract change is correct (docs/current-contract.md:186).

title: Each header navigation click reloads the whole document
oneLine: `AppHeader` uses plain `href` anchors, so Review queue, Run history, and Service status each cause a full document load, 9 asset revalidations, hydration, and a new access check, while the in-page router `Link` to the same view causes zero requests.
verifierReason: apps/web/src/components/app-shell.tsx:15-19, :29, :53-58 use plain href values; nav.ariakit.react.tsx:577-606 renders ak.Role.a. Re-run of nav-reload.mjs on the preview fixture: each header click gives documentLoads 1 plus the loading text; the in-page router Link gives documentLoads 0 and apiRunsRequests 0. I found no stated reason for the full reload in docs or history. Each click therefore costs one complete load, measured at 2.6-3.7 s for the signed-in maintainer (audit/live-authenticated.md). The recommendation is feasible: render={<Link … />} is already used at routes/index.tsx:510 and :549. NavLink computes aria-current from rest.href (nav.ariakit.react.tsx:590), which is empty with Link, but AppHeader passes aria-current explicitly. Not built.
secondLensReason: Confirmed: app-shell.tsx:15-19, :29, :53-58 use plain href anchors, NavLink renders ak.Role.a, and AppHeader is on all four page shells, so each main-navigation click costs one complete load (1.2-2.3 s to the queue, 2.6-3.7 s to a stable page for the signed-in maintainer), while queue and history use the same /api/runs data. The NavLink + render={<Link/>} pattern is already used (review-workspace.tsx:733-760, item-list.tsx:197-214). The recommended code is wrong as written. I ran it with the installed packages: on /?view=history both the queue link and the history link get aria-current="page", because Link matches an empty search partially (react-router link.js:34-43) and writes aria-current after the caller's props (link.js:221-224). activeOptions={{ exact: true }} gives the correct result (measured). The first verifier wrote that aria-current is not a problem; it is. Two more effects: a router link removes the beforeunload prompt for unsent decisions on the run page (use-review-session.ts:175-184; contract line 196 'Unsent decisions still require the browser'), so it needs useBlocker or reloadDocument there; and the reload is the only implicit refresh of the dashboard today. No security contract change. Counter-argument: the reload is simple, always shows new data, and keeps the unsaved-decision prompt without router code.

title: The dashboard data lives only in component state
oneLine: Browser Back from a run and the `Refresh runs` button both reset the page to the loading text; during a refresh the queue, the alert bell, and the account menu are removed and the bell refetches when it returns.

Re-run of refresh-blank (verify/refresh-blank.txt): during Refresh runs the result is queueHeading false, loadingText true, accountMenu false, cards 0. Re-run of nav-reload: browser Back from a run sends /api/runs again and shows the loading text. No correction. title: The service view and the alert bell wait for /api/runs before they request /api/operations
oneLine: `OperationsAttention` mounts only after `/api/runs` succeeds, so the service view runs two full access checks in sequence (15 serial D1 round trips; alerts visible at about 2.7 s signed in) although it needs only `preview` and `repository` from the first read.
verifierReason: apps/web/src/routes/index.tsx:254-256 and :356-365 mount OperationsAttention only when state is ready. Re-run of service-chain (1,000 ms added per read): /api/runs 299 -> 1,312 ms, then /api/operations 1,337 -> 2,344 ms, data at 2,641 ms. Signed-in production (orchestrator): /api/operations starts 66-250 ms after /api/runs ends and takes 1.20-1.30 s more. Corrections: the estimate 'about 1.9 s' is low; measured is 2.6-3.7 s to a stable page. The option 'start both reads together' has an unstated cost: packages/security/src/authorization.ts:71-82 has no shared pending check, so two parallel reads with a permission older than 60 s can each call GitHub (my local run with an instant GitHub stub made 1 call; real latency can give 2). The option that adds the alert count to the dashboard batch does not have this cost.

title: The alert poll period equals the permission cache lifetime, so each poll calls GitHub
oneLine: The bell polls 60 s after each response and the read permission cache lasts 60 s from the start of the check, so every poll misses the cache: 1 GitHub call, 9 D1 round trips, and 83 statements per minute per open tab, also when the tab is hidden.
verifierReason: operations-attention/index.tsx:280 schedules setTimeout(load, 60000) in finally, after each response; authorization.ts:21, :63, :72 use a 60,000 ms lifetime from a checkedAt taken before the GitHub call, so the next poll is always after expiry. Re-run of M1 (verify/roundtrips.json): each 60 s poll records GET /repos/ariakit/ariakit/collaborators/maintainer/permission, 9 D1 round trips, 83 statements. The effect at index.tsx:228-289 has no visibilitychange handler; pulls.$pullNumber.tsx:105-119 has one. Notes: 1,440 calls per day is the upper limit (a tab open 24 hours on a device that does not sleep). Two UI strings state the period (operations-attention/index.tsx:330-338) and must change with it. The sub-claim that the 5-minute cron records 'most' alerts was not verified.

title: The permission, token, and login caches live in one isolate only
oneLine: The first signed-in read in each new isolate makes 3 serial GitHub calls (token, user by ID, permission); a D1-stored grant with `checked_at`, read in the same batch as the account lookup, keeps the 60 s and 10 s limits and removes the calls across isolates.
verifierReason: Confirmed: authorization.ts:19, github.ts:102 and :193 are module-level maps; apps/web/src/runtime.ts:117-136 and :259-260 pass env.DB directly and set no custom fetch; env-identity re-run gives sameDatabaseBinding true and weakMapHit true; the first signed-in request makes 3 serial GitHub calls (verify/cookie.json). Corrections: (1) M13 does not show that new isolates occur. A new connection is not a new isolate; in my run 0 of 10 new connections had a slow first /health (77-366 ms with TLS setup) and the one slow request (1,012 ms) was the third /api/runs on a warm connection. The frequency is unknown. (2) The gain of the recommended D1 table is overstated. The contract limits the stored result to 60 s, so a maintainer who returns after more than 60 s needs a live permission call in every design, and the installation token cannot be stored. In the usual case the table saves only GET /user/:id (if the login is stored). It saves all calls only when a new isolate serves a request less than 60 s after the last check. (3) The table adds one D1 write per live check. The 'store only the login hint' alternative gives almost the same gain with less code, and placement (LOAD-03) also shortens the GitHub calls.

title: A cold Worker adds 0.6-1.3 s to the first request
oneLine: 2 of 8 new production connections needed 702 ms and 1,402 ms for the first `/health` (others 83-232 ms); the Worker is 33 modules, 4.1 MB raw, with an unminified 2.1 MB entry; the startup time itself is not known.
verifierReason: The slow requests are real, but the cause in the title is not shown and the open question is answered against it. Sizes re-measured exactly (33 modules, 4,104,202 bytes raw, 888,351 gzip; index.js 2,098,892 bytes, 46,193 lines, not minified). The Worker startup time is known: the production deploy log /Users/diegohaz/.claude/jobs/f65a6229/tmp/audit/infra/deploy-37357689984.log:6971-6972 says 'Total Upload: 4007.84 KiB / gzip: 856.53 KiB' and 'Worker Startup Time: 47 ms'. The platform limit is 1 second for the global scope (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/). 47 ms cannot explain 700-1,400 ms. Re-run of fresh-connections (10 new connections): first /health 366, 79, 121, 158, 80, 88, 179, 83, 77, 107 ms, no slow first request; first /api/runs 341-397 ms; one 1,012 ms outlier on the third request of a warm connection. Re-run of the probe series: first guest /api/runs 436 ms, not about 1,050 ms. So the 'first request after a new connection' pattern did not repeat. Corrections: retitle to 'some requests take 0.7-1.4 s more; cause not known'. The recommended work (minify the server build, lazy-load the render path and Better Auth) has no evidence behind it. The traces enabled at apps/web/wrangler.jsonc:15-20 are the place to find the cause.

title: Content-hashed assets are revalidated on every document load
oneLine: Production serves `/assets/*` with `public, max-age=0, must-revalidate`, so each document load sends 9 conditional requests before hydration; a `public/_headers` rule with `immutable` removes them.
verifierReason: Re-run: curl on /assets/index-MxeSnhFR.js and /assets/index-CXm4JU5N.css returns cache-control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate with an etag. prod-guest-waterfall.json shows 9 asset entries with transfer 300 on each of 3 reloads, ending 37-106 ms after start; the CSS is one of them and first paint follows it (reload 1: CSS 104 -> 210 ms, first paint 244 ms). apps/web/public holds only favicon.svg; dist/server/wrangler.json has assets.directory ../client; wrangler-dist/cli.js:156046 is HEADERS_FILENAME = "_headers". Platform: the default is 'Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate' and the docs recommend 'public, max-age=31556952, immutable' for fingerprinted assets (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/headers/); the Vite plugin supports _headers in the public directory at build, preview, and deploy time (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/vite-plugin/reference/static-assets/); _headers rules are not applied to Worker-generated responses, so private responses are not affected. No correction. Not built.

title: Opening a run from the queue shows no change for 1 second, and nothing is preloaded
oneLine: The router default `pendingMs` of 1,000 ms keeps the queue on screen with no feedback for 1 s after `Review changes`, then shows a text-only pending page; no link sets `preload`, so the run chunk and model start only after the click.
verifierReason: apps/web/src/router.tsx:8 sets no defaultPendingMs or defaultPreload; routes/runs.$runId.tsx:31-36 has ssr false, pendingMinMs 0, gcTime 0, staleTime Infinity, and no pendingMs; @tanstack/router-core 1.171.32 dist/esm/router.js:625-627 has defaultPendingMs: 1e3. Re-run of pending-states (2,500 ms added): urlChangedMs 21, loadingTextMs 1000, queueGoneMs 1000. No Link sets preload. Caveat for the recommendation: preload="intent" starts the most expensive read of the service on hover. The orchestrator measured /api/runs/<id> for a 626-item run at 5.3-5.7 s server wait and 5.3-6.0 MB of JSON. A preload for a run that is not opened keeps the single-threaded D1 database busy for that time, and a client abort does not stop server work. pendingMs: 0 and feedback on the clicked control have no such cost. The interaction with gcTime 0 is still not tested.

title: Pull request titles are erased before the dashboard reads them
oneLine: `processWebhook` sets `payload_json = '{}'` after each delivery, but the dashboard and run page read the PR title from that payload, so titles disappear after processing; reproduced locally and visible in production (`#7746 · Pull request`).
verifierReason: apps/web/src/api/dashboard.ts:57-62 and api/review.ts:288 read json_extract(payload_json,'$.pull_request.title') from github_webhook_delivery. apps/web/src/api/webhooks.ts:279-335: the pull_request branch has no early return, so the final statement always runs: UPDATE github_webhook_delivery SET processed_at = ?, payload_json = '{}' …. dashboard.test.ts:42-56 inserts processed rows that still have the full payload, a state the processor never leaves. Re-run of the local test: title 'Add the tooltip arrow' before the update, no title after it. History confirmed (339926d on 2026-09-28, 5712036 on 2026-09-30). Production is also confirmed, which the auditor could not do: the orchestrator's signed-in notes say 'History rows show #7746 · Pull request because no pull request title is available'. Additions: the compaction is deliberate and has a runbook (docs/operations/compact-processed-webhooks.md), and a one-time backfill cleared old rows, so the fix must store the title elsewhere; the 'keep three fields in the payload' alternative works against that runbook. After compaction every key of the partial index in migrations/0028_pr_title_index.sql is NULL, so the index is dead but still maintained.

title: /api/me and /api/session are not used by the app, and their error shape differs
oneLine: Two identity endpoints exist with duplicate auth wiring, the UI calls neither and the user menu shows no login; `/api/me` errors have `Retry-After: 1` and no `schemaVersion`, unlike `/api/runs`; a doc line still says routes call `/api/me` first.
verifierReason: apps/web/src/server.ts:88-105 and api/review.ts:713-721 as described. Re-run on production: /api/me returns 401 with retry-after: 1 and {"error":{…}}; /api/runs returns 401 with no retry-after and {"schemaVersion":"1.0","error":{…}}. Source: server.ts:47-50 always sets Retry-After; api/index.ts:38-44 sets it for 503 only; index.ts:131-133 is not reachable through server.ts:82-87; index.ts:216-218 is a third shape. routes/index.tsx:258-263 passes no login and user-menu.tsx:24 shows 'Account'. docs/review-evidence-plan.md:62 is stale. Corrections: /api/me has a documented operator use that the report does not list (docs/operations/retire-preview-auth-at-cutover.md:59 names it as a probe target, and review/__tests__/preview-fixtures.test.ts:25 covers it), so removal must change that runbook. /api/session has no caller and no test anywhere in the repository (rg finds only review.ts:713).

title: The dashboard leaves 401 and 403 response bodies unread
oneLine: On 401 or 403 the client returns without reading or cancelling the body, so Chrome never finishes the request and the guest page never reaches network idle (Playwright `networkidle` timed out on production).
verifierReason: routes/index.tsx:185-195, operations-attention/index.tsx:239-242, and pulls.$pullNumber.tsx:59-69 return without reading the body; review/client.ts:268-269 reads the body first, so the run page is not affected. The auditor's M18 used a response that Playwright replaced, so I tested a real 401 from a local HTTP server with the production headers in Chrome (verify/unread-body-local.mjs): body not read = events request, response; network idle never reached in 14 s; 0 Resource Timing entries. body.cancel() = request, response, requestfailed; idle reached; 1 entry. response.json() = request, response, requestfinished; idle reached; 1 entry. Correction to the recommendation: await response.body?.cancel() works, but Chrome then reports the request as failed. Reading the 92-byte body (await response.arrayBuffer()) gives a clean finish. Real impact is limited to test tooling and Resource Timing data.

title: A failed GitHub read marks a check "ambiguous" forever
oneLine: deliverStatus sets request_started before the sender runs and treats every sender error as ambiguous (packages/service/src/work.ts:491-548); a failed GET before the PATCH locks the check until a manual D1 repair, and no repair procedure or tool exists.
verifierReason: Code and re-run agree. packages/service/src/work.ts:491-499 sets request_started=1 before the sender; work.ts:538-548 makes every sender error ambiguous; packages/security/src/checks.ts:173 reads before the PATCH at :191. Only settleStatus (work.ts:598) clears the flag and no path reaches it for an ambiguous sender. Re-run: failedReads 1, patches stay 1, sender ambiguous 1 after five healthy passes. Worse than reported: one failed installation-token request made 5 of 5 ready checks ambiguous in one pass (verify/results-token-mint.json; lazy client at apps/web/src/runtime.ts:163-171; production bound 25 per pass), and an ambiguous sender blocks a rerun of the same commit (api/pre-run-attempts.ts:636-643). Corrections: the lock is per check/commit, a new commit gets a new check (not tested end to end). The send contract already has a "not-sent" result (work.ts:467, 528-536), so no new error class is needed. The fix needs a retry delay: settleStatus sets available_at=now (work.ts:581) and a deferred outcome triggers a 1-second continuation, so 5 attempts would be used in seconds and the row becomes dead. The "minimal" alternative is not small because isStatusCurrent requires request_started=1 (work.ts:479).
secondLensReason: Every check delivery takes this path: work.ts:491-498 sets request_started = 1, checks.ts:173 reads the check, and work.ts:538-548 turns every error into ambiguous = 1. github.ts:73-94 maps every non-2xx answer, every network error, and the 15 s timeout to one error, so a 5xx, a 403 or 429 rate-limit answer, a failed token request, or an identity mismatch on the read all lock the check before any PATCH. I measured it across runs: a failed read of check 1 during a pass caused by run B left sender 1 with ambiguous 1, request_started 1, leased 1, and no PATCH. Only settleStatus clears the flag (work.ts:598) and no caller reaches it for this state; apps/web/tooling has no repair tool. The trigger is realistic: GitHub's availability report records about 9 % failed API requests for 80 minutes on 2026-06-10 and 56 % failed or slow front-door requests at the peak on 2026-08-17; with 6 reads in a pass and 9 % failures the chance to lock at least one check is about 43 % (estimate). A lock keeps the required check on its old state, makes reruns of the same commit return 503 check_pending (pre-run-attempts.ts:83-102, 636-643), and starts OPS-02. Fix feasibility: the sender contract already has 'not-sent' (work.ts:467, 528-536) and no new platform API is necessary. Measured with the real claimStatus and deliverStatus: five 'not-sent' results one second apart end as dead (attempts 5 of 5), the dead intent stays dead while GitHub is healthy, and it comes back only on the next project revision. So the fix needs a retry delay in available_at and must not count deferred items as more work; it must wrap only the read, never the PATCH. It does not cover an invocation that stops between request_started = 1 and the PATCH. The saved requirement says 'reconcile ambiguous failures' (contract-issue-1.md:328), and status delivery has no reconcile step. Counter-argument: the lock is fail-closed on purpose; it does not hold because a failed GET in the same invocation proves that no write exists.

title: An ambiguous check with a newer status starts an endless status loop, and each cron tick adds one more loop
oneLine: operations/checks.ts:347-349 counts an "attention" outcome as more work, so runtime.ts:446-454 re-sends status every second and every recovery pass starts another chain (queue depth 1..6 over six ticks, 33 D1 round trips per loop pass).
verifierReason: work.ts:673-691 returns an ambiguous check joined to its newest (pending) intent; operations/checks.ts:258-266 returns "attention" and changes nothing; checks.ts:347-349 counts it as more work; runtime.ts:446-454 re-sends status from every recovery and status pass. Re-run: six status passes all hasMore true; queue depth 1..6 over six ticks, 234 passes, 33 round trips each. The precondition existed in production (docs/evidence/diagnostic-check-rename-repair.md:7: ambiguous at revision 47 while runs wanted revision 243). The loop survives run closure because obsoleteCheckDeliverySql needs ambiguous=0. Correction: the proposed hop bound does not work as written, because operationsMessage() rebuilds the object and drops unknown fields (packages/service/src/work.ts:8-28), so hop is always undefined unless the decoder copies it. The hasMore change itself is correct.
secondLensReason: The loop is real and its trigger is wider than the title says: any project revision change of any run starts it, not only a newer status of the same run. Measured: check 1 of run A was locked, then only run B got a status touch, and four status passes all returned checksHasMore true, attention ['1'], passHasMore true, with no GitHub request from pass 2; outbox of check 1 ended with revision 4 sending and revision 5 pending with 0 attempts. The path is checks.ts:258-266 (attention changes nothing), checks.ts:347-349 (attention counts as more work), runtime.ts:454 (resend after 1 s), and runtime.ts:446-453 (each 5-minute recovery pass adds one more status message). Production had the precondition for about 8.6 hours (docs/evidence/diagnostic-check-rename-repair.md:7). Magnitude (arithmetic on measured counts, not a measurement): with one serial consumer and 0.5 to 5 s for each pass that is 17,000 to 173,000 passes each day, 0.6 to 5.7 million D1 round trips each day, and up to about $6 each month in queue operations; rows read stay inside the included 25 billion on an almost empty database but would pass it in 1 to 12 days at 126,000 rows for each pass. The main effect is delay: loop messages grow by 288 each day, so ingest and check updates wait about 2 to 24 minutes after one day and longer each day. Fix feasibility: the one-line hasMore change is correct and has no contract effect; a deferred item cannot loop because the fifth attempt ends as dead (measured); the cron pass still visits attention checks every 5 minutes. The hop bound needs the decoder change, and both deploy directions are safe because operationsMessage drops unknown fields (work.ts:8-28). A 'completed' outcome still asks for one extra idle pass (measured hasMore true after a pass that only delivered). Counter-argument: it needs a locked check; it does not hold because a real unanswered PATCH still makes a correct lock and no tool clears it.

title: Two statements in each status pass read (accepted runs x snapshots) rows
oneLine: statusRunEligibleSql (packages/service/src/review-status.ts:25-27) scans visonaut_snapshots for each accepted run: 999,999 full-scan steps at 1,000 runs; a rewritten predicate needs 999.
verifierReason: The predicate, the missing index, the plan, and the scan steps reproduce (Fullscan Steps 999999 for 1,000 x 1,000; alternatives 999 / 0 / 999). The growth model is wrong. Only promoted main runs get state='accepted' (baseline-promotion.ts:465), and retireSnapshot moves old accepted runs to 'superseded' (packages/service/src/retention.ts:98-104) through the source-retention step after 30 days (operations/snapshot-retention.ts:194-215). Measured with 100 accepted and 900 superseded runs: 100,899 scan steps, so cost is (recent accepted runs) x (all snapshots), linear not quadratic. Planner statistics alone remove it: after ANALYZE the same statement needs 999 scan steps; the repository never runs ANALYZE or PRAGMA optimize, and production statistics are unknown. Production had about 27 baseline revisions on 2026-10-02 (docs/current-contract.md:236). The 23.6 billion rows/day projection is not supported. The rewritten predicate is still a correct, cheap fix.

title: The review-links step pages through every pull request on every cron tick
oneLine: publishReviewLinks has no state or time filter and reports hasMore for full pages of rows it skips; one tick causes floor(P/25) extra status passes (41 passes, 1,363 round trips at 1,000 pull requests).
verifierReason: operations/review-links.ts:46-61 has no state or time filter, :173-174 skips current head checks only after paging them, :406 sets hasMore for any full page, and runtime.ts:446-454 sends a status continuation. title: Webhook delivery recovery runs 3 D1 statements for each listed delivery, including successful ones
oneLine: operations/github-deliveries.ts:229-246 does a SELECT and two UPDATEs per delivery: 303 of the 383 round trips of an idle pass; the cursor walk also delays detection of new failed deliveries.
verifierReason: operations/github-deliveries.ts:229-246 runs a receipt SELECT, an UPDATE, and resolveEvents for each received or 2xx delivery; :165-179 reads /app/hook/config each pass; :186-210 walks one page per pass and returns to the newest page only after the last. title: Two alerts are resolved by an operation that did not fix them
oneLine: The runtime reconciler kind "checks" collides with the step "checks" (runtime.ts:371, operations/index.ts:49,80), and the runtime scheduler alert is resolved by any successful pass of any kind (runtime.ts:455).

title: Several alerts never clear, and one alert fires for normal retries

title: A stopped scheduler, a dead-lettered message, or a killed pass raises no signal

title: Failure isolation is not the same for all parts of a pass
oneLine: The ten steps are isolated, but the pre-steps (operations/index.ts:32-46), expireExports (index.ts:96-110) and the prepareStatusIntent loop are not; one error aborts the pass, drops continuations, and causes full-pass retries.

The code sketch does not type-check because expireExports returns a number (operations/exports.ts:40).

title: One queue with one consumer puts check updates and ingest behind maintenance, and the wait is not measured
oneLine: max_concurrency 1 serializes status and ingest behind long recovery work; repository evidence records 21 to 33 s from approval to success intent and 65 s for one conversion, but no log holds queue wait.
verifierReason: Facts confirmed: max_batch_size 1 and max_concurrency 1 (wrangler.jsonc:101-103), all kinds in one handler, the review command runs inline but the check update goes to the queue (api/review.ts:641-667), the recorded intervals and the 'do not identify the exact queue occupancy' limit (docs/evidence/checks-7710/README.md:43, 65), and no log of queue wait. The choice between inline delivery, two queues, or higher concurrency is a design judgment; 'one queue' is a selected contract decision (docs/current-contract.md:141). Raising max_concurrency before fixing OPS-02 and OPS-04 would multiply those loops.
