title: Each request that uses auth runs a full schema check against D1 first
oneLine: Better Auth 1.7.5 validates the schema for each new auth instance (sqlite_master select plus a 75-statement batch); createAuth runs for each request, so /api/me with no cookie takes 0.442 s median against 0.131 s for a path that exits before createAuth. validateSchema: false removes both calls (verified locally).
verifierReason: All cited code exists and does what the finding says. packages/security/src/auth.ts:15-16 creates a new Better Auth instance for each request; call sites are apps/web/src/server.ts:85, :93 and apps/web/src/api/index.ts:130. Library: @better-auth/core 1.7.5 dist/db/schema-check.mjs:7-9 (`validateSchema !== false`), :58 (`let clean = false` in a closure for each adapter instance); kysely-adapter dist/index.mjs:712 registers the check for each instance; better-auth dist/api/to-auth-endpoints.mjs:41-42 and dist/api/index.mjs:169-170 await it; dist/auth/base.mjs:15 also starts it when the instance is created. The option is typed and documented: init-options.d.mts:390-400 `validateSchema?: boolean` ("Set `false` to disable runtime schema validation"). I ran the probe again in my scratch directory (verify/authprobe/result.json): no session gives `select ... from sqlite_master` plus `BATCH(75)` and nothing else; an instance that is never used gives the same 2 calls; a reused instance gives 0 calls on the second call; `validateSchema: false` gives 0 calls with no session and 2 calls (session, user) with a session. Two other lanes got the same result with their own probes. Production, my samples (verify/ttfb-rerun.txt, new TLS connection each time): GET /api/me with no cookie returns 401 with min 0.368 to 0.409 s and median 0.43 to 0.51 s in 3 sets (36 samples); GET /health has min 0.068 to 0.083 s and median 0.10 to 0.14 s. The difference is 0.30 to 0.40 s, so the report's 0.29 s is correct or a little low. No contract text requires the runtime check: docs/current-contract.md does not mention it, and packages/security/README.md:5 only requires that the instance is made inside each request, which the main recommendation keeps. Corrections: (1) the report says 76 tables and views but the batch has 75 statements; the difference of 1 is not explained and is not important. (2) The first alternative (one instance for each isolate in a WeakMap) is against packages/security/README.md:5 and auth.ts:15, and a shared instance shares its init promise between requests; Cloudflare documents the failure class at https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/observability/errors/ ("Cannot perform I/O on behalf of a different request"). The auditor says that it needs a test; I agree, and I rate it the riskier option. (3) The `/api/auth/` branch at api/index.ts:131 is not reached in production because server.ts:82-87 handles that path first. (4) Webhooks (api/index.ts:127) and /images return before createAuth, so only the other /v1 routes pay the background check.
secondLensReason: Hot path proved from code: createAuth runs for each request at apps/web/src/server.ts:85, :93 and apps/web/src/api/index.ts:130; packages/security/src/auth.ts:47-51 does not set advanced.database.validateSchema; installed @better-auth/core@1.7.5 dist/db/schema-check.mjs:7-9 enables the check unless the option is false, and better-auth dist/auth/base.mjs:15 plus dist/api/to-auth-endpoints.mjs:41-42 run and await it for each new instance. My own measurement on one reused connection from GRU (10 samples each): /health 35.4 ms median, /images miss (1 D1 query) 161.4 ms, /api/me with no cookie 344.3 ms. So the schema check costs 309 ms for each auth request. Against the orchestrator's signed-in data this is 31% of the /api/runs server wait (median 992 ms), 25% of /api/operations (1,249 ms), and about 0.62 s of the 2.72 s until the dashboard is stable. Each Approve or Reject request pays it too. Fix feasibility: validateSchema is a documented option in the installed version (dist/types/init-options.d.mts:390-400, 'Set false to disable runtime schema validation') and in the Better Auth database docs. It does not change the security contract (docs/current-contract.md:186: live session and linked-account checks stay). Risks: schema drift then fails only at query time (still HTTP 503), and packages/security/test/auth-d1.test.ts loses its implicit schema proof unless one test keeps the check on. Deploy applies migrations before code (.github/workflows/deploy.yml:125-133). Counter-argument: the check is a safety net for a Better Auth upgrade, and it becomes cheap if the Worker moves near D1.

title: The Worker has no placement setting, so each D1 query and GitHub call is a long round trip
oneLine: No placement key and no cf-placement header; the Worker runs at the visitor edge (GRU) and D1 has no South America region, so the 3 or more sequential D1 calls and 2 to 3 GitHub calls of the access check each cost about 0.1 s. An explicit placement.region hint near D1 is the option; the D1 region is not verified.
verifierReason: Facts hold. apps/web/wrangler.jsonc has no `placement` key (rg returns no match in all four configs). The production response for / has no `cf-placement` header (re-measured; cf-ray ends in GRU). The sequence before the first data query is in the code: getSession (authorization.ts:32-36), account select (:40-43), requireRepositoryWrite (:73), token mint (github.ts authorize, about :135-143), 60 s cache (:21). The installed Wrangler schema accepts the recommended form: node_modules/wrangler/config-schema.json has `placement` with `region`, `host`, or `hostname`. Cloudflare confirms the syntax and that "Placement only affects the execution of fetch event handlers" and that static assets stay at the nearest location (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/placement/). D1 regions are wnam, enam, weur, eeur, apac, oc (https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/configuration/data-location/). New measurement that the report did not have: GET https://visonaut.com/images/00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000 makes exactly 1 D1 query and no auth instance (apps/web/src/api/images.ts:24-36, reached at api/index.ts:113-116). 26 samples: min 0.198 s, medians 0.240 s and 0.239 s. /health in the same sets: min 0.068 s, medians 0.100 s and 0.102 s. So one D1 round trip from this location costs about 0.13 to 0.14 s. This is a direct measurement and it agrees with the report's indirect estimate of 0.10 to 0.15 s. Corrections and limits: (1) the benefit of placement is still not measured, and the D1 primary region is still not read; 0.13 s is compatible with ENAM but does not prove it, so `aws:us-east-1` is an example value only. (2) The shell route / makes no D1 call today (median TTFB 0.10 to 0.15 s). With placement its HTML will be slower by one visitor-to-region round trip for a visitor in South America. The finding states this only in the decision question; it must be a visible cost. (3) Placement does not change queue or cron handlers. (4) The contract (docs/current-contract.md:186) requires live session and linked-account checks on each request, so a cookie or isolate cache can cover only the GitHub permission (at most 60 s). (5) Not tested option that the auditor did not list: better-auth 1.7.5 has `advanced.database.joins` (init-options.d.mts, just above `validateSchema`), which may read session and user in one query.
secondLensReason: Confirmed part: apps/web/wrangler.jsonc:1-125 has no placement key; all 41 of my production responses have cf-ray ...-GRU and no cf-placement header; one D1 round trip costs 126 ms from GRU (161.4 ms for a 1-query path minus 35.4 ms for /health). Signed-in GET /api/runs makes 6 sequential D1 round trips (schema check 2, session, user, account, dashboard batch), GET /api/operations 6 or more, GET /api/runs/<id> 9 or more. A model from these counts gives 0.85 s for /api/runs, which agrees with the measured 0.87 to 1.08 s. Not supported: 'each GitHub call is a long round trip'. A local unauthenticated GitHub REST call from São Paulo takes about 25 ms on a warm connection (328 ms with connection setup); this is not from the Worker. Not verified: the D1 region (126 ms agrees with ENAM; that is an inference) and the size of the gain (estimate: about 0.55 to 0.65 s on /api/runs today, 0.30 to 0.36 s after INFRA-01, with an assumed 5 to 20 ms for a near D1 call). Fix feasibility: wrangler 4.136.1 config-schema.json:261-333 accepts mode smart and region/host/hostname; the key is inheritable and the Vite plugin copies it into dist/server/wrangler.json (code read, no build run). Cloudflare docs: placement affects only fetch handlers, static assets stay at the edge, region hints take cloud provider regions only (no hint for 'near D1'), Smart Placement needs traffic from several locations. Cost of the fix: the HTML shell and /health also move, about 0.11 to 0.13 s more TTFB for a visitor in Brazil (inferred). No change to the security contract; the 'permission cookie' alternative would break docs/current-contract.md:186 if it replaced the session check. Counter-argument: code changes (INFRA-01, joins, fewer queries) remove most round trips of /api/runs without a platform change.

title: The browser revalidates all hashed static files on each page load
oneLine: Production assets return cache-control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate; the home page references 10 static files and apps/web/public has no _headers file. An /assets/* immutable rule removes the revalidation round trips.
verifierReason: Re-measured. https://visonaut.com/assets/index-CXm4JU5N.css, /assets/index-MxeSnhFR.js and /favicon.svg all return `cache-control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate` with an ETag. A request with `If-None-Match` returns 304 (0.173 s on a new connection in my sample; the auditor had 0.094 s). The production HTML references 10 static files: 1 stylesheet, 8 `modulepreload` scripts, 1 icon. apps/web/public contains only favicon.svg and there is no `_headers` file. Cloudflare states the default header and that `_headers` in the public directory is supported at build, preview and deploy time (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/headers/ and https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/vite-plugin/reference/static-assets/). The same page states that `_headers` rules "are not applied to responses generated by your Worker code", so the HTML 404 for a missing asset (INFRA-04) will not get the long lifetime. The recommendation is correct and safe for hashed names. Severity correction: I rate this low, not medium. The 10 conditional requests go in parallel on one HTTP/2 connection after the HTML arrives, so the cost on a repeat visit is about one round trip to the nearest edge (the measured 0.09 to 0.17 s includes a new TLS handshake of about 0.05 s). The fix is one small file. Addition: static assets also have no `X-Content-Type-Options` header (full headers of index-MxeSnhFR.js checked), because the Worker's securePrivateResponse does not see them; the same `_headers` file can add it.

title: A missing asset URL runs the full server render, and production deploys about 16 times each day
oneLine: An unknown /assets/*.js path returns an SSR HTML 404 (2,414 bytes, up to 1.45 s); with 67 production deploys in 4 days, open tabs can request chunks that no longer exist.
verifierReason: Confirmed parts: GET https://visonaut.com/assets/runs._runId-OLDHASH1.js returns 404 with `content-type: text/html; charset=utf-8`, `cache-control: no-store, private`, 2,414 bytes. The generated config has `assets: { directory: "../client" }` with no `not_found_handling`, and server.ts:106-118 sends all other paths to `render(request)`. The lazy chunk exists (dist/client/assets/runs._runId-QUJlDVZ1.js, 137,841 bytes). docs/development.md:57 says that a reload clears the local Undo stack. The Cloudflare quote about "a 404 error and a broken page" is on the cited page. Corrections: (1) The deploy rate is not consistent in the report: the title and INFRA-09 say 13 each day, the index says 16. From gh data (verify/runs-stats.mjs): 67 successful push deploys between 2026-10-01 20:49 and 2026-10-05 18:47 UTC, which is 16.6 each day as a mean. The rate is not steady: 11, 33, 25, 2, 4 for the five UTC days. (2) The 1.448 s time to first byte was one outlier. My two samples were 0.109 s and 0.162 s, so the render cost of such a request is small. (3) The skew after a normal deploy is an inference from how Workers keeps one asset list for each version. The test used an invented file name, not a real file of an older build, and the Cloudflare page does not say when old files stop. (4) The code example puts the check before `requireBackendBindings(env)` at server.ts:81, which is after the preview branch returns at :73-80. To cover preview too, the check must be directly after the /health branch.

title: D1 read replication is not in use, and it gives little for the current users
oneLine: No withSession call exists, so all queries use the primary; replicas need the Sessions API and there is no South America region, so the gain for the current maintainer is small.
verifierReason: `rg withSession|first-unconstrained|first-primary apps packages` returns no match. The Cloudflare page confirms the quotes: the Sessions API is required, replica regions are ENAM, WNAM, WEUR, EEUR, APAC, OC, a replica "may be arbitrarily out of date", and there is no extra cost (https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/best-practices/read-replication/). Whether read replication is enabled on the database is not read (remote commands are not permitted), which the report states. Addition that strengthens the 'no change' position: docs/current-contract.md:186 requires a live session and linked-account check on each request. A replica that is out of date could accept a session after sign-out, so the access-check queries must stay on the primary (`first-primary`), and those are the queries that cost the most today. The statement that the nearest replica for São Paulo is probably in the primary region is an assumption; my measurement of about 0.13 s for each D1 query is compatible with it.

title: Deploy runs the full check suite again; 87% of deploy time is this second run, and superseded runs end as failures
oneLine: Deploy run 37357689984 took 433 s: 376 s for the repeated checks and 50 s for the deploy job; 9 of 78 push deploys failed at the 'current main commit' step because a newer commit superseded them.
verifierReason: Numbers re-computed from fresh gh data and they match. Run 37357689984: wall 433 s; verify / Test 2/3 366 s; Gate 10 s; deploy job 50 s (build 9 s, validator 7 s, web 8 s). Verify takes 380 of 433 s, 88%. Push deploys since 2026-10-01 18:00 UTC: 78 runs, 67 success, 9 failure, 2 cancelled; success median 257 s, p90 352 s, max 451 s. For commit f83fef6 the pull request head 1fcf31c and the merge commit have the same tree (aa62458c) and the same parent (e277a91), so the same tree did pass CI 5 minutes before (run 37357042248, 284 s). Corrections: (1) Not all 9 failures are superseded runs. I read the failed step of all 9 (verify/failures.sh): 7 failed in "Require the current main commit and production build" (one log read: "A newer main commit supersedes this deployment"); 2 (36926645388 and 36923498834, 2026-10-01) failed in "Deploy production comparator" with the Wrangler error "Unable to fetch bindings, routes, or services metadata from the dashboard". Those 2 are real failures. So 7 of 78 runs are red by design, not 9. (2) Missing context: the branch rule for main has `strict_required_status_checks_policy: false` (gh api repos/ariakit/visonaut/rules/branches/main). A pull request can merge with CI that ran on an older base. For such a merge the run on main is the only test of the exact merged tree, so the second run is not always a repeat. .github/workflows/README.md:3 also states the intent: "deploy.yml owns normal main verification". The tree-compare alternative and the merge queue both handle this; a plain removal of `verify` does not. (3) A merge queue is available here (public repository in an organization), but on a day with 33 deploys each pull request would wait for a queue run of about 5 minutes. This cost is not stated. (4) The min success time of 46 s shows that some runs did not run the full verify (2 runs under 120 s); '4.5 to 7.5 minutes' is the median-to-max range, not all runs.

title: Each push redeploys both Workers, and each change with a changeset causes a second CI and deploy cycle
oneLine: 43 of the last 120 main commits changed no deployable runtime file but each redeployed both Workers; private-package versioning adds a Version packages pull request (33 of 200 CI runs) and a second production deploy.
verifierReason: Facts confirmed. deploy.yml:3-5 has no path filter and :130-133 deploys both Workers each time. My own classifier on the last 120 commits of origin/main (verify/commit-scope.mjs) gives the same counts: 7 docs only, 12 version files only, 43 with no web or validator runtime file, 8 that touch the validator. No runtime source reads a package version (rg in apps/web/src, apps/compare/src, packages/*/src returns nothing), so a 'Version packages' deploy ships the same code. 33 of the last 200 CI runs are on changeset-release/main; 3 of the last 11 push deploys are 'Version packages' (#243, #246, #248); pull request #253 is open. Corrections: (1) The recommended `paths:` filter is not safe with the current guard. deploy-source.mjs:17-21 requires that the run commit is the tip of main. Example: commit A (code) starts a run; commit B (docs only) lands 2 minutes later and starts no run because of the filter; run A then fails with "A newer main commit supersedes this deployment"; A is not deployed until the next deployable push. The same problem applies to the `[skip deploy]` alternative. The guard must change together with the filter (for example: accept when no deployable path changed between the run commit and the tip). (2) '36% of production deploys' is a count of commits, not of deploys. (3) Private package versions are a recorded decision, not an accident: .github/workflows/README.md:46 describes `privatePackages: { version: true, tag: false }` and .github/workflows/scripts/changesets.test.mjs tests it. The decision question is still valid. (4) The repository is public, so standard runner minutes cost no money; the cost is time, noise, and a new Worker version (dropped warm isolates) for each no-op deploy. No user-visible effect was measured, so I rate this low.

title: CI wall time went from about 210 s to about 294 s in 3 days; shards are unbalanced and old runs are not cancelled
oneLine: Vitest shard steps take 72 s to 292 s for the same commit, each shard pulls the Playwright image (26 s to 40 s) for 2 browser-dependent files, and checks.yml has no concurrency cancel for pull requests.
verifierReason: Confirmed: CI success medians are 210 s for 84 runs on 2026-10-01 and 10-02 and 294 s (249 to 316) for 11 runs since 10-04. Run 37357042248: Test 218/268/140 s, Browser 222 s, Gate 10 s; vitest steps 155/201/80 s; on the merge commit 149/292/72 s. 'Initialize containers' takes 26 to 40 s in each shard. checks.yml:1-13 has no `concurrency` key. Only packages/playwright/test/clients.test.ts:16,110 and comparison.test.ts:12,87 start the Playwright CLI; packages/cli/test/local-comparison.test.ts:572-578 only loads Playwright's core bundle. The sum of job time in the run is 16.3 minutes. Corrections: (1) The increase is in one shard only. Vitest step time from 16 sampled runs (verify/shards.sh): shard 2/3 was 92 to 107 s in 8 runs on 10-02, 151 s on 10-03 15:35, and 201 to 243 s in 9 runs since the first run of branch `baseline-delta-storage` (pull request #247, merged 10-04, +7,997 lines with large new test files such as apps/web/src/operations/sparse-storage.test.ts and apps/web/tooling/baseline-reset/reset.test.ts). Shard 1 stayed at 119 to 167 s and shard 3 at 70 to 118 s. So the work is to find the slow files in shard 2, not general growth. Note that vitest.config.ts:5 (`apps/**/*.test.ts`) also runs the tests under apps/web/tooling. (2) The Browser claim is not supported. The report compares 75 to 101 s with 118 to 153 s from 2 runs. In my 8 runs since 10-04 the Browser test step is 74 to 153 s (median about 108 s); in 8 runs on 10-02 it is 70 to 108 s (median about 103 s). That is noise, not a regression. (3) The trend is not a steady rise: daily medians were 245, 268 and 272 s on 09-28 to 09-30 before they fell to about 210 s. (4) The same tree gave 201 s and 292 s for shard 2 in two runs 5 minutes apart, so that shard also has large run-to-run variance. The `concurrency` example is valid: the group for a called workflow differs from the caller group `production-deploy`, so there is no deadlock.

title: The normal deploy has no check after deploy, no version identity, and a weaker config guard than the manual path
oneLine: The push path ends at wrangler deploy; /health exposes no commit or version; deploy-source.mjs checks 3 config values while the manual path checks 19. Options: --tag, version_metadata binding, health check, wrangler rollback.
verifierReason: deploy.yml:125-133 ends with the two `wrangler deploy` steps; there is no later step. GET https://visonaut.com/health returns `{"service":"visonaut","status":"ready","launchEnabled":true,"environment":"production","fixtureMode":false}` with no commit or version (server.ts:60-71). deploy-source.mjs:22-27 checks 3 values on the push path; the manual path at deploy.yml:306-370 has 19 assertions. `pnpm exec wrangler deploy --help` (4.136.1) lists `--tag`, `--message` and `--strict`. The `version_metadata` binding gives `id`, `tag`, `timestamp` (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/bindings/version-metadata/). .github/workflows/README.md:7 has the rollback sentence. Extra evidence that the report did not use: runs 36923498834 and 36926645388 (2026-10-01) failed at "Deploy production comparator", which is after "Apply production schema migrations" and before the web deploy. So the three steps are not atomic and a partial deploy has occurred. Corrections and context: (1) 'about 13 deploys each day' should be about 16.6 as a mean (see INFRA-04). (2) The manual guard asserts `queues.consumers` is empty after a patch (deploy.yml:355), because it is for a consumer-free cutover deploy. It cannot run on the push path without a parameter. (3) A check directly after deploy must retry, because the new version does not serve all locations at once; an automatic `wrangler rollback` reverts only the Worker version, not migrations, queue consumers, cron, or the validator. (4) Maintainer decision D12 (docs/current-contract.md:56, docs/development.md:52) keeps a manual built-app check and says not to add a second automated smoke project. An HTTP health request is smaller than that, but the maintainer must see the relation. O03 (current-contract.md:166) selects standard Wrangler deployment, which the gradual-deployment alternative is not.

title: Each deploy depends on two retired queues and runs one-time cutover gates
oneLine: deploy-comparison-retirement.mjs reads two fixed legacy queue IDs and asserts response.ok on each production deploy; if the unused queues are deleted, all deploys fail. The container gate is now a no-op.
verifierReason: Confirmed: deploy-comparison-retirement.mjs:5-10 holds two fixed queue IDs and :32 asserts `response.ok`; deploy-infrastructure.mjs:7-8 returns when there is no `CODEC_CONTAINER` binding; deploy.yml:117-124 runs both in each production deploy (3 Cloudflare API reads). The deploy log of run 37357689984 lists only OPERATIONS, DB and IMAGES for the validator, so the Container gate returns early. The contract records the cutover as complete (docs/current-contract.md:32 W08 and :188 'the former production and preview Container resources are retired'). If a queue is deleted, the read returns a non-OK status and the deploy fails at that step; this follows from the code. docs/operations/retire-server-comparison.md:68 says that physical queue deletion is outside the retirement patch, so the queues are expected to exist for now. Corrections: (1) The claim that the deploy token needs queue and Worker-settings read access 'only for these gates' is not supported. Standard `wrangler deploy` registers the queue producer and consumer and reads Worker metadata for the web Worker, and .github/workflows/README.md:32 states that the credential needs those permissions. (2) Severity: a deleted queue blocks deploys with a clear message; it does not affect the running service. The gates cost about 1 s. I rate this low. (3) .github/workflows/README.md:32 says 'Once the live binding is gone, the gate needs no retirement receipt', so the Container gate was left in place on purpose as a guard; removal is a maintainer decision, as the finding says.

title: The production validator Worker has D1, R2, and queue bindings that its code does not use
oneLine: visonaut-compare binds the production DB, IMAGES, and OPERATIONS (deploy log), but apps/compare/src/index.ts reads no env; the Worker that decodes untrusted images has more access than it needs.
verifierReason: apps/compare/wrangler.jsonc:38-59 binds DB (production database ID), IMAGES and OPERATIONS in `env.production`. apps/compare/src/index.ts:4-8 is `fetch(request) { return validateRequest(request, await codecsReady) }`; it has no `env` parameter. `rg env apps/compare/src` matches only probe.ts, and there is no `cloudflare:workers` import. The deploy log shows the three bindings on `visonaut-compare`. apps/compare/README.md:18 says that the production environment 'retains the provisioned D1, R2, and OPERATIONS bindings' and gives no reason. No test asserts these bindings (rg in apps/compare/test and .github/workflows/scripts). Removal is feasible: a removed binding does not delete the resource, and deploy-infrastructure.mjs only looks for `CODEC_CONTAINER`. Severity correction: low, not medium. The handler cannot reach the bindings without a code change, and the untrusted bytes are decoded in WebAssembly, which can call only its imports. This is a least-privilege clean-up with no known path to misuse.

title: Production also answers on visonaut.ariakit.workers.dev
oneLine: workers_dev is true in env.production; the workers.dev host returns /health 200 and the full SSR shell 200, outside zone rules; the API returns 403 wrong_origin.
verifierReason: apps/web/wrangler.jsonc:48 has `"workers_dev": true` in `env.production`; deploy.yml:360 asserts it. Re-measured: https://visonaut.ariakit.workers.dev/health returns 200 with the production JSON; / returns 200 with 28,538 bytes; /api/runs returns 403 `wrong_origin`; https://visonaut-compare.ariakit.workers.dev/ returns 404 `error code: 1042`. The deploy log lists both `https://visonaut.ariakit.workers.dev` and `visonaut.com (custom domain)`. Commit bc78b85 added the explicit key in the same change that closed the diagnostics routes. `rg workers.dev` finds no document that uses the production address. server.ts has an origin check for /api/auth (:83), /api/me (:89) and handleApi (api/index.ts:110-112), but not before `render(request)` at :118 or for /health. Both the recommendation and the alternative are feasible; the change also needs deploy.yml:360 and the fixture in deploy-web-target.test.mjs. Whether zone rules exist on visonaut.com is not known, so the 'rules do not cover it' impact is a general platform fact, not an observed gap.

title: The raised CPU and subrequest limits apply to all handlers and to the preview Worker
oneLine: cpu_ms 240000 (8 times the default) and subrequests 250000 (25 times the default) are top-level, inherited by production, and present in the preview build; they date from the first commit and have no recorded reason.
verifierReason: Confirmed: apps/web/wrangler.jsonc:39-42 sets `cpu_ms: 240000` and `subrequests: 250000` at the top level; the generated preview config (apps/web/dist/server/wrangler.json) has the same `limits`; both values are in the first commit 43552ce. Cloudflare confirms the defaults: CPU '5 min (default: 30 seconds)' for HTTP, 30 s for cron with an interval under 1 hour, subrequests '10,000/request (up to 10M)' (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/). server.ts:133 has the cron comment. Refuted part: 'No document gives a reason for the numbers' is false for the CPU value. docs/evidence/runtime-bounds/README.md:3-7 states that real queue measurements of 2026-09-22 'support these selected limits in each web Worker environment' with 'Queue CPU 240 seconds'; :21 gives the estimate (120.61 s at the 2 GiB ceiling); :25 says 'The original 30-second CPU configuration failed on this fixture'. So 240 s was a measured choice for the queue consumer. I found no reason for 250,000 subrequests (the nearest is 150,000 in apps/web/tooling/backup-v2-recorded/wrangler.example.json:11). Useful follow-up that the finding should have asked: the measured workload was a SQL backup export and rehash in the queue. Product export was later retired (docs/current-contract.md:34, D06), and the current queue steps in apps/web/src/runtime.ts are budgeted reconcile, history, retention and status steps. So the documented reason may be out of date. That needs the Workers metrics, as the finding recommends. The statements that the limits apply to all handlers and to preview are correct.

title: The environment model (top level is preview, env.production is production) has specific risks
oneLine: Commands without an environment hit preview (safe), but production needs CLOUDFLARE_ENV at build and --env elsewhere, there is no local environment with bindings, 5 vars are duplicated, and every binding is optional in the generated Env type.
verifierReason: Confirmed: names at apps/web/wrangler.jsonc:3 and :112; scripts at apps/web/package.json:11-13; the auditor's `wrangler types` output (infra/web/worker-configuration.d.ts) has `DB?: D1Database` on the base interface and a `Cloudflare.ProductionEnv` interface with all bindings required; runtime.ts:40-54 repeats this by hand; apps/compare/wrangler.jsonc:3 uses `visonaut-compare-local` as its top level; the five variables are written twice (:23-29 and :52-65); there are 33 migration files; the deploy log shows that the migration step works with a build redirect present. Corrections: (1) Item 3 is too strong. A local `.dev.vars` file can override `vars`: the running dev server uses one line (`VISONAUT_ORIGIN=...`) and then answers 200 on 127.0.0.1:4310. So full local work does not have to use the origin https://visonaut.com. packages/security/src/http.ts:5-8 also has a `local` environment for http loopback origins. What is true is that no committed or documented local environment with bindings exists. (2) The finding missed the concrete break that this model causes: with the committed config, `pnpm dev` answers 403 for each page, because server.ts:73-76 compares the request origin with `VISONAUT_ORIGIN` = https://preview.visonaut.com (wrangler.jsonc:25). Measured on the dev server: Host 127.0.0.1:4310 gives 200 only because of the uncommitted override; Host localhost:4310 gives 403 with 0 bytes. README.md:55 says that `pnpm dev` starts the fixture demo. The hygiene lane has this finding. (3) `export type BackendEnv = Cloudflare.ProductionEnv` was not type-checked. ProductionEnv has literal types (for example `VISONAUT_ORIGIN: "https://visonaut.com"`), and tests use `runtime.getBindings<BackendEnv>()` and override values (apps/web/src/runtime-config.test.ts:64, runtime.test.ts:346). It may need `wrangler types --strict-vars false` or test changes. (4) Extra risk in the same area: apps/web `deploy` is `pnpm build && wrangler deploy`. With `CLOUDFLARE_ENV=production` in the shell it would build and deploy production from a laptop with none of the workflow guards (from the scripts; not run).

title: The public preview deploys only by manual dispatch and is behind main
oneLine: preview.visonaut.com serves older asset names (review-D6dKKXbW.css, index-CaJ_2b8I.css) while production serves the f83fef6 build (index-CXm4JU5N.css); preview deploys only through the preview-web dispatch.
verifierReason: Re-measured. https://preview.visonaut.com/ references /assets/review-D6dKKXbW.css and /assets/index-CaJ_2b8I.css and has `<html lang="en">`. https://visonaut.com/ references /assets/index-CXm4JU5N.css and has `<html lang="en" class="[font-synthesis:none]">`. The local build of f83fef6 has index-CXm4JU5N.css. deploy.yml:263-270 deploys preview only for a manual dispatch with `action == 'preview-web'`. The last manual dispatch of the Deploy workflow was run 37076012733 on 2026-10-02 23:07 UTC at commit ea88996, so the preview is at least 3 days and 4 merged interface or preview changes behind (#247 to #252). Context that the finding should state: the manual path is documented and selected (.github/workflows/README.md:38 'use manual preview-web with target preview'; contract O11 and current-contract.md:188 keep the public fixture preview). So 'behind main' is the result of a chosen process, and the alternative 'remove the hosted preview' is against the current contract. Feasibility notes: a preview deploy in the push job needs a second build with `CLOUDFLARE_ENV` unset after the production deploy, because both builds write apps/web/dist. A preview for each pull request needs deploy credentials in pull request runs; the Infisical OIDC binding is for `refs/heads/main` only (.github/workflows/README.md:22-30), so that alternative is larger than the text suggests.

title: Renovate is configured but has opened no pull request; pins are behind, and 8 release-age exclusions are stale
oneLine: 0 of 233 pull requests are from Renovate and there is no dashboard issue; wrangler is 4.136.1 against 4.147.0; all 8 minimumReleaseAgeExclude versions are about 14 days old against a 1-day default.
verifierReason: renovate.json:1-9 exists since the first commit (2026-09-22). `gh api repos/ariakit/visonaut/pulls?state=all` gives 233 pull requests: 222 by diegohaz and 11 by ariakito[bot]; none by Renovate. The search for a Dependency Dashboard issue returns `[]`. The remote has only the branches `main` and `changeset-release/main`. Re-ran release-age.mjs: all 8 versions in pnpm-workspace.yaml:13-21 were published 13.8 to 14.3 days ago; latest versions are wrangler 4.147.0 (pinned 4.136.1), @cloudflare/vite-plugin 1.62.5 (1.57.1), miniflare 5.20261001.0-alpha, @cloudflare/workers-types 5.20261005.1, @tanstack/react-start 1.168.60. pnpm documents `minimumReleaseAge` default '1440 (since v11)' and exact-version exclusions (https://pnpm.io/settings/dependency-resolution); the repository does not set `minimumReleaseAge`, and there is no .npmrc. That the Renovate app is not installed is an inference, which the report states; it is a strong one because `config:recommended` opens an onboarding pull request or a dashboard issue. Severity correction: low. The repository is 13 days old and the pins are at most 14 days behind; nothing is broken. A maintainer-level pnpm setting with a longer release age could still make the 8 exclusions necessary on that machine; I cannot see that.

title: Version constants and resource identifiers are repeated by hand, and the compatibility date has 3 values
oneLine: Node 24.18.0 appears in 14 workflow lines, pnpm 12.5.1 in 13, the setup block 13 times; compatibility dates are 2026-09-21, -22, and -29, and the pinned workerd rejects 2026-09-29; the account ID is both a variable and a literal.
verifierReason: Counts re-done. `node-version: 24.18.0` appears 14 times (checks 7, deploy 3, release 4); `version: 12.5.1` appears 13 times (6, 3, 4). Account ID literal: deploy.yml:151, :184, :279, deploy-comparison-retirement.mjs:19, wrangler.container-probe.jsonc:12, and the variable at deploy.yml:60 (the log shows the same value). D1 ID: apps/web/wrangler.jsonc:71, apps/compare/wrangler.jsonc:42, deploy.yml:202, :346. Compatibility dates: 2026-09-22 (web and validator), 2026-09-21 (wrangler.probe.jsonc:5), 2026-09-29 (wrangler.container-probe.jsonc:5); 18 test files hold a date literal. Re-ran compat.mjs: workerd 1.20260921.1 accepts 2026-09-21 and 2026-09-22 and fails for 2026-09-29 with 'the newest date supported by this server binary is "2026-09-28"'. renovate.json:7 groups only the two npm names. The setup recommendation is feasible: pnpm/action-setup reads `packageManager` when `version` is absent and setup-node accepts `node-version-file: package.json`; a composite action does not change `workflow_ref`, which the Infisical claims use (.github/workflows/README.md:22-30). Limits: the 2026-09-29 failure affects only the on-demand container probe with direct Miniflare; `wrangler dev` was not tested (stated by the auditor), and production deploys are not affected. The release-guard tests read deploy.yml as text, so a setup refactor must update them.

title: 20 TypeScript files are in no checked project, and the tsconfig files differ
oneLine: apps/web/tooling, apps/compare/test and container, packages/protocol/test, and root tooling are outside every include; typecheck:container is not run; two tsconfig files are unused; 5 of 8 projects do not extend the root file.
verifierReason: The structure claims are correct: package.json:8 runs `typecheck` in each workspace and the root has no project; 5 of 8 package projects do not extend the root file; targets are ES2022 (security), ES2023 (root, protocol), ES2024 (cli, compare, compare worker); `verbatimModuleSyntax` is only in the root file and packages/cli; apps/web/src/api/tsconfig.json (38 files) and apps/web/tooling/baseline-reset/tsconfig.json are used by no script; `typecheck:container` is used by no workflow; packages/service/src is loaded by 3 projects. The count is wrong. I ran `tsc6 --listFilesOnly` for the 8 typecheck projects and compared the result with `git ls-files` (verify/unchecked-ts.mjs): 315 tracked TypeScript files, 290 in at least one project, 25 in no project. Differences from the report's 20: (1) 3 of its files are fully checked because checked files import them: tooling/test-migrations.ts, tooling/legacy-comparison-fixture.ts, and apps/web/tooling/baseline-reset/reset.ts (all three are in the apps/web project list). TypeScript checks a whole imported file, not 'the imported part'. (2) vitest.config.ts is unchecked (the report names it but does not count it). (3) 7 files under docs/simplification-audit (4 in source/, 3 in evidence/) are unchecked and not in the report; .oxlintrc.json also ignores that folder. The 25 files are: 7 in apps/compare (test and container), 6 in apps/web/tooling, 2 in packages/protocol/test, 2 in tooling/evidence, vitest.config.ts, and the 7 docs files. The minimal alternative ('add test and tooling to the include lists') is feasible for protocol and compare; apps/web/tooling files need Node and workers types that the web project does not load.

title: No version drift between workspaces, but some workspaces use dependencies that only the root declares
oneLine: 0 of 17 shared dependencies have two versions; apps/web, packages/service, packages/compare, and packages/cli use vitest, tsc6, @types/node, or @playwright/test from the root; the adapter pins engines to exactly 24.18.0.
verifierReason: Re-ran deps.mjs and undeclared.mjs: 44 distinct dependencies, 17 shared, drift count 0; all ranges are exact, `workspace:*`, or an exact npm alias. apps/web declares neither `vitest` (50 importing files by the script, 49 by my rg) nor `@playwright/test` (6 to 7 files); it also imports `@jsquash/png` and `@jsquash/webp` in src/api/api.test.ts without a declaration. packages/service/package.json and packages/compare/package.json have no `devDependencies` and use `vitest` and `tsc6`. packages/cli uses `@playwright/test` (test/local-comparison.test.ts:575) and `@visonaut/playwright` (test/binary.test.ts) without a declaration. Engines: packages/playwright/package.json:58 is exactly `24.18.0`; packages/cli/package.json:47 is `>=24.18.0 <25`. The quoted rule is in the ariakit-general-workflow skill (Dependencies section). Small corrections: lock.mjs now prints 494 resolved packages, not 496; and most of the 49 names with two versions are the esbuild platform packages (0.27.7 and 0.28.1), so that number describes about 4 real duplicates (esbuild, lightningcss, pngjs, @better-auth/utils).

title: Deploy guards are inline JavaScript in YAML, and tests cut them out with a regular expression
oneLine: Four node heredoc blocks in deploy.yml hold guard logic; release-guard tests extract them by regex and compile them; the largest guard repeats wrangler.jsonc values and runs only on manual actions.
verifierReason: deploy.yml has four inline `node --input-type=module <<'JS'` blocks at :179-191, :193-204, :252-258 and :309-370. .github/workflows/scripts/deploy-web-target.test.mjs:17-34 reads deploy.yml, cuts the block with the quoted regular expression, removes the `import` lines and compiles it with `compileFunction`. deploy-migrations.test.mjs:39-42 does the same with `new Function`. The guard at deploy.yml:324-366 repeats the production values of apps/web/wrangler.jsonc. apps/web/src/cutover-fence.ts:1 says 'Temporary entrypoint for the existing web Worker during data conversion'. One correction to the recommendation: 'Run the same config guard in the push path' cannot be done as written. That guard asserts `configuration.queues.consumers` is `[]` after a patch (deploy.yml:336, :355), because the manual path deploys without a consumer. The push path must keep the consumer, so the shared function needs a parameter for the expected consumers. The step names in deploy.yml are also Infisical-independent, so a move to .mjs files does not affect the OIDC claims.

title: Logs and traces use defaults only; there is no export and no alert from outside the service
oneLine: Workers Logs keep 7 days; there is no Logpush, Tail Worker, or uptime check; alerts live in the app's own D1 table and /health is static, so a dead Worker or D1 outage alerts nobody.
verifierReason: apps/web/wrangler.jsonc:15-20 has only `observability.enabled` and `traces.enabled`; `rg head_sampling_rate|logpush|tail_consumers` over the four configs returns nothing. Cloudflare confirms 7 days retention on the paid plan, 20 million events included, $0.60 for each additional million, the three export options, and a default sampling rate of 100% (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/observability/logs/workers-logs/). apps/web/src/runtime.ts:467-479 (`reportSchedulerFailure`) writes to `operations_events` and falls back to one `console.error`. The dead-letter queue at wrangler.jsonc:105 has no consumer in the config (a consumer attached outside the config cannot be excluded). /health is static (server.ts:60-71), so a workflow that only requests /health detects a Worker that does not start, not a D1 failure; the recommendation should say this. In-app alerts are the selected design (docs/current-contract.md:186 'followed by an actionable alert'; .github/workflows/README.md:40), so the gap is a judgment about whether one outside signal is wanted. The facts are correct.

title: Several names no longer match what the thing does
oneLine: The 'compare' Worker, COMPARATOR binding, and README now only validate images; queues keep '-production-' while storage names lost it; routes differ in form; a legacy webhook path is still routed.
verifierReason: This is a naming opinion; the facts under it are correct. apps/compare/src/index.ts only validates images, and the names say 'compare' (directory, package `@visonaut/compare-worker`, Worker `visonaut-compare`, binding `COMPARATOR` at apps/web/wrangler.jsonc:87, README title 'Comparison Worker'). Storage names lost the environment part in #251 (e277a91) and the queues kept it (wrangler.jsonc:95-105). The npm package `visonaut` is the CLI (packages/cli/package.json:2) and the Worker `visonaut` is the web service. Preview routes have `zone_name` (:9-13) and production does not (:49). Both webhook paths are routed; the line is apps/web/src/api/index.ts:127, not :126, and .github/workflows/README.md:38 names only /v1/webhooks. Context: contract D03 and D17 (docs/current-contract.md:48, :60) keep the Worker and the package boundaries; a rename is not a merge, so it is permitted, but a Worker or queue rename is a resource migration, as the finding says. The binding rename `COMPARATOR` to `VALIDATOR` is not free either: the deploy guard (deploy.yml:352-354), tests and `runtime.ts` name it.

(2) apps/compare/container/Dockerfile:1 has a digest with no tag (I did not repeat the Docker Hub lookup). (3) .infisical.json:2-3 points to workspace fb5ba4be with `dev`; deploy-scope.mjs:10 uses project 2e3bd11a; .github/workflows/README.md:11 says 'Do not use the workspace's development project' but does not say what it is for. (11) Now verified from source, not an assumption: Vitest 5.0.1 `findConfigFile(root)` (node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/index.DzobfTyw.js:14194-14202) looks only in the root or current directory, so `vitest run` in a package folder does not load the root config. Not defects: (5) `pnpm check` without release guards and package checks is a recorded decision. docs/development.md:7-15 has a check-scope table that lists them as separate commands, and decision Q02 of the simplification audit selected 'Keep a local check and name the extra CI checks'. Only VISONAUT_WORKFLOW_OWNED (wrangler.jsonc:61) is an open choice, and its reader expects a string today.

title: Better Auth validates the whole database schema on every request
oneLine: createAuth builds a new Better Auth instance per request (auth.ts:15-21, api/index.ts:130) and validateSchema defaults to true, so each request adds 2 D1 round trips, 76 statements (sqlite_master + 75 pragma_table_info) and ~856 rows read; ingest requests pay it too.
verifierReason: Code and dependency code agree (packages/security/src/auth.ts:15-21; apps/web/src/api/index.ts:130; @better-auth/core/dist/db/schema-check.mjs:51-78; better-auth/dist/api/to-auth-endpoints.mjs:41-42). My own test on native local D1: each new instance makes 4 calls (sqlite_master read=231, batch x75 pragma_table_info read=625, session, user); the same instance makes 2; validateSchema:false makes 2 with the session found; validateSchema:false + joins:true makes 1. Corrections: the cited parity test (test-migrations.test.ts:22-41) compares migrations with fixtures, not with the Better Auth schema, so keep one test with the check on; the module-level instance cache alternative shares a promise across requests (Workers cross-request I/O risk); for ingest requests the check is not awaited, so it adds D1 load (76 statements, about 856 rows per upload), not latency.
secondLensReason: Hot path confirmed for production: Better Auth 1.7.5 has no environment switch for the check (schema-check.mjs:4-9, 'Enabled in every environment unless explicitly disabled'), base.mjs:9-19 starts it at construction, to-auth-endpoints.mjs:40-42 awaits it, and apps/web/src/api/index.ts:130 and server.ts:85, :93 build one instance per request. Magnitude is measured in production by two other lanes and recalculated here: guest /api/runs minus /health is 332 to 334 ms at the GRU edge (two sets of 8 samples). That is about 34% of a warm /api/runs, about 0.67 s of each dashboard load (2 serial requests), and 0.67 to 1.0 s of each decision. Rows read (856 per request) have no billing effect. Fix feasibility: advanced.database.validateSchema exists in the installed version (init-options.d.mts:390-400) and changes no contract text; the deploy applies migrations before the Worker (deploy.yml:127, :133). Correction to both first verifications: a schema guard does exist in tests today, because packages/security/test/auth-d1.test.ts:28-54 applies the real migrations to native D1 and then calls createAuth and getSession, which runs the runtime check. Turning the check off inside createAuth removes that guard without a test failure, so one test must keep it on. Strongest counter-argument (fail-closed runtime guard; small gain after placement) is weak against a one-line change.

title: Every private request waits for 6 sequential D1 calls before its handler starts, and the review model needs 20
oneLine: Measured through handleApi: GET /api/runs 6 calls, /api/operations 9, /api/runs/:id 20 (sequential depth 15), /state poll 14, queued receipt 24; project, run and comparison rows are each read 3 times and readRunStatus is 6 awaits in a row.
verifierReason: Call counts and depths are reproduced at a different data scale with the auditor harness (6/6/9/20 depth 15/14/24 depth 19/26 depth 21), and my hand count of review.ts:232-365 plus run-status.ts:26-80 gives 20 calls and depth 15. Corrections: (1) the dashboard requests are not parallel: OperationsAttention mounts only when state.status === 'ready' (apps/web/src/routes/index.tsx:254-256), so /api/operations starts after /api/runs returns (6 round trips for the list, then 9 more); (2) /api/runs skips the project read, so its preamble is 5; (3) the cookie-cache alternative conflicts with docs/current-contract.md:186 ('Live session and linked-account checks still run for every request'); (4) a hand-written session join replaces Better Auth cookie verification, while advanced.database.joins:true (measured: getSession = 1 call) plus Promise.all for the project read reaches a 2-round-trip preamble with Better Auth kept. Latency is still not measured.
secondLensReason: The call counts and the sequential order are correct (index.ts:123-130, authorization.ts:32-43, run-status.ts:27-68, review.ts:232-365, operations.ts:16-47). Real cost: one small D1 call costs 105 to 145 ms from the GRU edge (measured by the live and load lanes, recalculated here), because D1 has no region in South America. The model 30 ms + 333 ms + (depth - 2) x 105 to 145 ms agrees with signed-in production samples: /api/runs 0.78 to 0.94 s predicted vs 0.87 to 1.08 s measured, /api/operations 1.10 to 1.38 s vs 1.20 to 1.30 s. Predicted and not measured: active review model 1.7 to 2.2 s, queued receipt 2.1 to 2.8 s. For an archived run page the D1 chain is only 25 to 30% of the measured 5.3 to 5.7 s. Wrong in the report (first verification found both): the dashboard requests are serial, not parallel, and /api/runs skips the project read. Feasibility: advanced.database.joins exists in 1.7.5 and gives 1 call for session and user, but it changes every joined Better Auth query including the OAuth callback, so a deployed sign-in check is necessary; batch() is one call and one transaction, so a batched readRunStatus is feasible with subqueries; an explicit placement region is accepted by Wrangler 4.136.1 and needs the D1 region first; read replicas give no gain in Brazil; the cookie cache is against docs/current-contract.md:186; the report's main recommendation (hand-written join) replaces Better Auth cookie checks and is not necessary. Strongest counter-argument: one placement key can remove most of the wait without code changes in contract-heavy code.

title: Pull request titles are read from webhook payloads that the service has already erased
oneLine: webhooks.ts:330-335 sets payload_json='{}' after processing, but dashboard.ts:57-62 and review.ts:286-290 read $.pull_request.title from it; measured title 'Audit title' before processing and NULL after; index 0028 only holds NULL keys.
verifierReason: All write paths set payload_json='{}' (apps/web/src/api/webhooks.ts:150, :172, :332; packages/security/src/webhooks.ts:147; operations/recovery.ts:73). Both readers exist (dashboard.ts:57-62, review.ts:288). Git history matches (339926d on 2026-09-28, 5712036 on 2026-09-30). The test fixture state (dashboard.test.ts:42-54) cannot occur in production. The UI uses the field (routes/index.tsx:499, :586, :619, :714). My measurement: title before scrub {"title":"Verify title"}, after scrub null. The recommended WITHOUT ROWID table works on local D1.

title: One status wakeup becomes a chain of queue messages that grows with the number of pull requests
oneLine: publishReviewLinks pages all PRs 25 per step and reports hasMore, and runtime.ts:454 re-sends the message; with 750 PRs an idle wakeup took 31 queue messages, 3,949 D1 calls and 7,597,795 rows read with zero work.
verifierReason: Mechanism confirmed in code (review-links.ts:168-171, :405-412; operations/index.ts:95; runtime.ts:454; review.ts:659-662) and at three scales: 31 messages for 750 pull requests, 21 for 500 (my rerun), 6 for 130 with zero work and zero GitHub requests (my own test). Corrections: the production D1 binding changed three times on 2026-10-04 and 2026-10-05 and the cutover copies no old rows, so the chain does not occur until 25 pull requests exist; an exact filter exists (append 'AND checkHeadSha IS NOT sourceSha' to the page query, the same rule as the loop skip at review-links.ts:174; measured page 25 rows -> 3 rows, hasMore false); the recommended updated_at time filter can skip an old legacy pull request that gets a new verdict; in a fresh database no legacy row can exist (pre-run-checks.ts:629-631), so the whole step has no work.
secondLensReason: Mechanism confirmed: review-links.ts:405-412 sets hasMore when a page has 25 rows, runtime.ts:454 sends the same message again, and review.ts:661 sends one status message for each decision; pre_run_checks rows are never deleted. In the current database the step has no useful work, because new rows get check_head_sha = source_sha (pre-run-checks.ts:629-646) and the loop skips them (review-links.ts:174). The chain starts at 25 pull requests. I measured the velocity: 17 pull requests since the 2026-10-04 cutover and about 8 to 9 each day (256 in 31 days), so the limit is 1 to 3 days away, about 250 after one month and 750 after three months. Chains do not merge: K wakeups cost K x (floor(P/25)+1) passes. Corrections: the 7.6 million rows and 3,949 calls are for a synthetic 3,001-run database and mostly come from scans in other steps (results.txt:139-140); at production size the cost is near zero for months (about 41 USD each month only at the synthetic size). 'Real check updates wait behind it' is too strong, because each pass runs review-decisions and checks first (operations/index.ts:47-51). Fix feasibility: the exact filter from the first verification is correct and keeps contract line 212; the report's updated_at filter can skip a legacy pull request; the report's minimal alternative (hasMore only when work was done) has a bug, because line 411 saves the cursor only when hasMore is true, so the sweep restarts at 0 and never reaches later pages. Severity is medium today with no user-visible slowness, and it rises with time with no code change.

title: One review decision sends a new GitHub check update for every active run
oneLine: project.revision is one global counter (status-touch.ts:9-13) and checks.ts:200-209 treats every run with an older source_revision as stale; one decision caused 31 GET + 31 PATCH check-run requests and 740 extra D1 calls for 30 active runs.
verifierReason: Code confirmed (status-touch.ts:10-12; operations/checks.ts:206; run-status.ts:92-141 about 10 calls; security/checks.ts:173 GET and :191-202 PATCH with no comparison; 0002_work.sql:48-53 trigger). Reproduced at a second scale: idle sweep 0 GitHub requests, after one decision 31 GET + 31 PATCH, same after a second decision. The newer review-link path already skips unchanged verdicts (review-links.ts:191-204) and the run-check path does not. Additions: pull request status does not read the baseline revision (review-status.ts:84), any fix must keep the send-time fence at run-status.ts:148, and GitHub documents 500 content-generating requests per hour as a secondary limit (not verified that check PATCH counts).
secondLensReason: The path runs in production for every project event, not only for decisions: review-commands.ts:301/451, run-admission.ts:340/728/794, local-comparison.ts:362/545/668, baseline-promotion.ts:252/504, run-retirement.ts:63/145, history.ts:215, retention.ts:117 all add 1 to the project revision, and checks.ts:206 then selects every eligible run. I measured it again at the real scale: ariakit/ariakit has 5 open pull requests (gh api, 2026-10-05), and with 5 active runs plus the baseline one decision costs 6 GET + 6 PATCH and +140 D1 calls (+66 rows written); the cost is linear and agrees with the report's 31 + 31 and +740 at 30 runs. A status touch of run B alone re-sent the unchanged check of run A (results-ops.json). At N = 6 this is 36 GitHub points for each pass against a limit of 900 each minute, so rate limits are not a real risk today; at N = 31 it is 186 points and a fast review session can reach the limit. The decided run is sent last (measured order: PATCH run1..run4, then PATCH run5) after about N x 10 sequential D1 calls. Severity is medium, not high, at today's scale, but it multiplies the OPS-01 exposure by N and is the trigger of OPS-02. Fix feasibility: the recommended source_revision update needs a migration because of trigger work_status_identity (0002_work.sql:48-53) and changes the meaning of an immutable intent; the 'same as last intent' alternative trusts D1 while 6 other code sites PATCH the same check IDs. A safer option exists with no schema or contract change: compare the GET response that sendGitHubCheck already holds (name, status, conclusion, details_url, output.title, output.summary are in the documented response) and skip the PATCH when equal; pre-run-checks.ts:322-331 already uses this pattern. None of these options removes the D1 fan-out; that needs a narrower fence than project.revision in run-status.ts:148, which is a contract decision. Counter-argument: at N = 6 the cost is small, and the repeated PATCH makes GitHub agree with D1 again and revives dead intents.

title: The dashboard history query reads every comparison row in the database
oneLine: dashboard.ts:35-44 plan is SCAN row USING INDEX visonaut_rows_comparison plus a temp sort of all runs; 126,608 rows read for 100 runs shown, 18,214 with CROSS JOIN order, 12,312 with a (project_id, created_at) index; SELECT * also copies plan_json.
verifierReason: Same plan on native D1 (SCAN row USING INDEX visonaut_rows_comparison). My scaling test with 100 runs shown: 3,000 rows -> 8,189 read; 15,000 -> 34,589; 30,000 -> 67,589; the CROSS JOIN rewrite reads 3,199 / 5,599 / 8,599 and returns the same result. Correction: the 'PRAGMA optimize' alternative does not work here (67,589 rows before and after ANALYZE, plan still scans). Severity lowered: growth is linear, the fix is small, the production database is new, and the auditor's own run shows 68 ms SQL time at 50,240 rows.
secondLensReason: The facts are correct, but the real impact is low today. GET /api/runs runs dashboard() once for each dashboard mount or Refresh (routes/index.tsx:176-210, no polling) as one D1 batch, so it is one round trip. I ran the real SQL text of dashboard() on native local D1 with 12 changed rows for each run: history statement rows read 16,177 / 55,177 / 107,177 at 6,000 / 24,000 / 48,000 comparison rows, but only 5 / 14 / 27 ms of local SQL time. Production /api/runs already waits 865 to 1,967 ms on a 5.5 MiB database (orchestrator's live record), so this query is not the cause of the slow dashboard. Growth is bounded by a contract fact the report did not use: D1 keeps only changed comparison rows (docs/current-contract.md:26, local-comparison.ts:325-327), and ci.yml had 296 runs in 7 days, so 4,000 runs need 3 months or more. Fix feasibility is verified: the minimal CROSS JOIN change returned byte-identical JSON for both batch statements at three sizes (rows read 5,489 / 8,489 / 12,489; 4 / 9 / 19 ms), SQLite documents that CROSS JOIN is never reordered, and local D1 accepts AS MATERIALIZED. The 'actionable' statement does not change with CROSS JOIN and still reads all runs of the project. I did not measure the full recommended rewrite (AS MATERIALIZED plus column list). No security contract effect. Counter-argument: it is an optimization of an almost empty table; the only reason to act is that the change is one join keyword.

title: Recurring queue and cron statements scan whole tables; three of them are quadratic
oneLine: Closed-summary candidates (632,837 rows), staged-alert resolution (1,218,583) and statusRunEligibleSql (91,539 + 100,699) scan operations_events or snapshots per run; idle recovery step 921,542 rows read dropped to 91,798 with trial indexes and a rewritten predicate plan.
verifierReason: Independently measured without statistics: eligible-runs filter 41,403 rows (rewrite 2,396); closed-summary candidates 597,980 = 1,980 old runs x 300 events with 0 candidates; resolve staged alerts 606,000; resolveEvents SCAN. The scan also runs for runs that already have a summary (9,000 / 306,000 / 1,206,000 rows for 0 / 100 / 400 events). The proposed indexes work (3,980 / 6,000 / 0). Addition the report missed: ANALYZE alone, with no index and no code change, gives 2,396 / 6,260 / 8,300. Also the partial lineage index from D1-08 cuts the active run count from 2,000 to 20 rows. Costs are near zero today on the new database.

title: Lookups on request paths have no supporting index
oneLine: EXPLAIN shows SCAN for visonaut_checks by (project_id, external_run_id) on every decision (3,007 rows), visonaut_promotions by comparison_id, visonaut_audit by run_id, visonaut_status_outbox by run_id, and all project runs read per pull_request webhook.
verifierReason: Plans and rows confirmed: SCAN visonaut_checks 2,001 -> 3 with the index; SCAN visonaut_status_outbox 5,000 -> 0; pull request lineage lookup reads all 2,000 runs -> 0; SCAN visonaut_promotions, visonaut_audit, snapshots, commands. Correction: the suggested fix 'put the primary key first' does not change the plan (measured 801 rows before and after reordering); a unary plus does ('WHERE +comparison_id = ? AND id IN (...)' reads 3 rows). Severity lowered: a few thousand rows per item at the synthetic size, on a new database.

title: The review-queue index from migration 0030 is not used; the queue poll reads every review task
oneLine: review-queue.ts:83-94 plans as SEARCH work_tasks_publication (kind=?) + temp sort, never work_tasks_review_queue; 1,501 rows read per poll with 1,500 completed tasks; adding state IN ('queued','leased') gives (kind=? AND state=?).
verifierReason: My test: poll reads 2,001 rows with 2,000 completed review tasks, plan uses work_tasks_publication (kind=?) plus a temp B-tree; with state IN ('queued','leased') it reads 3 rows; INDEXED BY work_tasks_review_queue gives a full index scan. Correction: the 0030 index is partial (WHERE kind='review'), so it is updated only for review tasks, which is every row now because enqueueWorkStatement has one runtime caller (review-queue.ts:58). Severity lowered: one row per stored review task per status step.

title: Many tables only grow, and admission stops new runs at 2 GiB
oneLine: No DELETE path for github_webhook_delivery (215 B/row measured), visonaut_status_outbox (149), pre_run_checks (667), work_checks, operations_events, ingest_staged_runs, ingest_review_sessions and others; capacity.ts rejects new runs above databaseAdmissionBytes = 2 GiB.
verifierReason: The admission stop (runtime-defaults.ts:15-16, capacity.ts:107-113) and the missing deletes for the bookkeeping tables are confirmed by my own DELETE search. Corrections: the 680,124,416 bytes belong to database 15fcd402 which is no longer bound (git log -L on wrangler.jsonc shows three binding changes on 2026-10-04/05), so the distance to 2 GiB is unknown and probably large; rateLimit is pruned by Better Auth (better-auth/dist/api/rate-limiter/index.mjs:171-181); expired sessions are deleted when presented (api/routes/session.mjs:153-162); the main effect of these tables is scan cost, not bytes.

title: Each decision rebuilds and returns the complete review model
oneLine: The queued receipt (review.ts:812-833) calls reviewModel again: one decision on an 800-row comparison cost 49 D1 calls, 33,646 rows read and an 844 KB response although the command result already lists the changed revisions.
verifierReason: review.ts:812-833 always builds the model for a completed queued receipt; the UI always sends queued:true (review/client.ts:313-317), so the model-free branch at review.ts:900-904 is unused by the UI. Reproduced: 24 D1 calls, 26,582 rows, 844,488 bytes. The client already accepts a receipt without a model (client.ts:254). docs/simplification-implementation.md:203 records the same problem as a moderate performance gap for the direct path. Corrections: the queued path has no expectedRunRevision fence like review.ts:881-887, so the recommended code needs one; the contract (current-contract.md:196) requires newer route-model handling to stay; 844 KB is the size before compression.

title: Image requests always reach the Worker, D1, and R2
oneLine: images.ts:24-40 does one D1 primary read and one R2 read per first view; the response is immutable but the Worker does not use the Cache API, so the edge never stores it.
verifierReason: images.ts:24-40 and :52 are as quoted; no Cache API use and no cache key in wrangler.jsonc. Correction: a configuration-only option exists. Cloudflare Workers Cache (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/cache/) is accepted by the installed Wrangler 4.136.1 schema (CacheOptions.enabled). Private responses already send 'no-store, private' (security/http.ts:33) and image 404s send no-store, so only successful image responses can be stored. The contract allows public image bytes (current-contract.md:59).

title: Read replication cannot help yet: no Sessions API, and code depends on the raw binding object
oneLine: No withSession call exists and wrangler.jsonc has no placement key; the permission cache is a WeakMap keyed by the D1Database object (authorization.ts:19) and several flows read right after a write, so sessions need a bookmark plan.
verifierReason: No withSession, no placement key, permission cache keyed by the binding (authorization.ts:19). The open item is now verified: Better Auth needs exec (kysely-adapter/dist/index.mjs:22, :102) and a D1 session has only prepare, batch, getBookmark (Cloudflare D1 Worker API docs), so auth must keep the raw binding. Corrections to options: Smart Placement needs enough traffic from several locations and may not decide for this low-traffic Worker, while an explicit placement region is documented and accepted by Wrangler 4.136.1; replicas exist only in ENAM, WNAM, WEUR, EEUR, APAC, OC, so they do not shorten the path for a user in South America (commit time zone -0300 is an assumption about location). Latency is not measured; meta.served_by_region in a trace shows the real region.

title: Migration numbering has a duplicate and two gaps, and nothing checks it
oneLine: Two 0030_* files from PRs #190 and #198 (documented as kept), numbers 0017 and 0025 missing, and no test or CI script rejects a duplicate or out-of-order migration number.
verifierReason: Directory listing shows both 0030 files and no 0017 or 0025; git log gives 7893072 (#198) and 8ebf821 (#190) on 2026-10-02; operations/README.md:3 and current-contract.md:126 say both files must stay; deploy.yml:125-127 runs wrangler d1 migrations apply, which records migrations by name. The recommended test finds a new duplicate number but not a lower number added later.

title: Unused schema objects remain: 11 tables, 1 view, and 2 indexes
oneLine: Eight operations_backup_* tables, operations_promotions, transfer_key_redemptions, visonaut_baseline_restorations and view operations_ready_history_archives have no runtime reference in 169 source files; indexes work_tasks_review_queue and github_webhook_delivery_pr_title give no benefit.
verifierReason: My whole-worktree search finds the 11 tables and the view only in migrations, tests, recorded tooling, evidence, and docs; the trigger at 0024_core_simplification.sql:53-58 reads visonaut_baseline_restorations.
