title: Independent statements are sent one by one where one batch or one statement is enough
oneLine: An idle recovery step makes 385 D1 calls (60 are resolveEvents scans); persistWebhook is INSERT then SELECT, claimWork is two UPDATEs, operationsStatus is three independent reads, and review links run 4 statements per candidate (104 calls per page).
verifierReason: The serial statements exist at the cited lines and the call counts are reproduced (persistWebhook 2 calls, recovery step 385, status steps 79 to 179). Corrections: 'Use RETURNING for persistWebhook' does not work with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, because a duplicate delivery returns no row (measured: 1 row on first insert, 0 on duplicate); a batch of the two statements or a no-op DO UPDATE ... RETURNING works (measured). createChecks has 7 statements before the loop (checks.ts:46-85), not 6.

title: Wide rows and API bounds that can meet D1 limits
oneLine: Service.run uses SELECT * including plan_json (up to 1.5 MB) and is called up to 4 times per request; a command may carry up to 40,000 targets with 4 batch statements each and per-target JSON in one visonaut_commands row, which can pass the 2 MB value limit.
verifierReason: Confirmed by reading only, as the report states: service.ts:108-110 SELECT *; run-admission.ts:79-82 allows 1,500,000 bytes and :644 shrinks the plan for inventory runs; review.ts:842 and :847-850 allow up to 40,000 targets inside a 1 MB body; review-commands.ts:227-271 adds 4 statements per target. D1 limits (2,000,000 bytes per value, 100 bound parameters) match the Cloudflare limits page. Only a signed-in maintainer can send such a command and the batch is atomic. I did not re-check the claim that no statement builds a placeholder list.

title: The dashboard requests its data only after JavaScript loads and hydrates
oneLine: SSR sends only 'Checking access and loading runs…'; /api/runs starts in useEffect after 602 kB of JS (564 ms at 150 ms/9 Mbps; production sign-in panel at 1,068 ms vs first paint 504 ms).
verifierReason: Code confirmed. apps/web/src/routes/index.tsx:39-44 has no loader; :161 is `useState<DashboardState>({ status: "loading" })`; :176-210 requests `/api/runs` in `useEffect`; :275-279 renders the loading text. The built HTML for `/` (28,538 bytes) contains only the header and `Checking access and loading runs…`. Re-measured on the build (150 ms latency, 9 Mbps, 5 runs): first contentful paint 476 ms, loading text 470 ms, `/api/runs` 566 to 720 ms, queue 753 ms (auditor: 476 / 471 / 564 to 717 / 752). Re-measured in production (anonymous, 2 loads): first contentful paint 412 ms, loading text 413 ms, sign-in panel 1,123 ms (805 to 1,123). curl on one connection: `/api/runs` 401 with time to first byte 330 to 420 ms; document 45 ms. I found no cache, guard, or contract rule that makes this deliberate. The P03 research names an authenticated server function as the path for server data (docs/simplification-audit/evidence/feedback-performance.md:30). CORRECTIONS. (1) Size of the gain: in my production load the HTML arrives at 195 ms, the scripts finish at 308 ms, and hydration ends near 410 ms. An earlier request saves about 0.2 s of about 1.1 s. The API time (0.33 to 0.7 s) is the larger part and belongs to other lanes. (2) The sketch sets `staleTime: 30_000`. That stops the refresh for 30 s after a return from a run, so a finished run can still show as pending. The router default (`staleTime: 0`, stale-while-revalidate, https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/framework/react/guide/data-loading) already shows the cached list at once and refreshes it in the background. (3) A blocking server loader moves 0.33 s or more into the document response (45 ms today), so the first paint becomes later unless the loader streams a deferred promise. (4) The server function must forward `identity.sessionHeaders` (Set-Cookie, apps/web/src/api/index.ts:220-222) and needs the bindings. `render(request)` in src/server.ts:118 passes no `env`, so use `import { env } from "cloudflare:workers"` (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/bindings/). `createServerFn` and `getRequest` exist in the installed 1.168.57. The inline early-fetch alternative is allowed by the CSP (`script-src 'self' 'nonce-…'; connect-src 'self'`, packages/security/src/http.ts:39-42).
secondLensReason: Mechanism confirmed for production: GET / reaches render(request) at apps/web/src/server.ts:118, the route has no loader (apps/web/src/routes/index.tsx:39-44), state starts as loading (:161), and fetch('/api/runs') runs in useEffect (:176-184). The captured production HTML has only the loading text. Real impact is smaller than the finding implies: in the orchestrator's signed-in samples the request starts 199 to 303 ms after the first HTML byte (median 232 ms) and the server then takes 865 to 1,967 ms, so the JavaScript wait is about 17% of the time to the queue (232 of 1,353 ms). The other 83% is server time (INFRA-01, INFRA-02). The finding's numbers come from a 3 ms fixture API and an anonymous visit. Fix feasibility: createServerFn, getRequest and request context exist in the installed TanStack Start (start-client-core 1.170.32, start-server-core 1.169.37 request-handler.d.ts), but Start awaits loaders before it renders (createStartHandler.js:372-390), so a blocking server loader moves the document TTFB from 41-119 ms to about 0.9-2.0 s today unless the data is deferred. It also adds a second private data path that must repeat the origin check, requireMaintainer, the session Set-Cookie headers, the preview fixture source, and the HTTP 503 error.reference contract (docs/current-contract.md:81). runDate uses toLocaleString(undefined) (index.tsx:153-157), which causes a hydration mismatch for server-rendered dates. The minimal alternative (an inline nonce script in the head, same pattern as sidebarPreferenceScript in __root.tsx:23-26) is allowed by the CSP in packages/security/src/http.ts:40-44 and changes nothing in the security contract. Severity rises after the server fixes, because the same 0.2 to 0.3 s then becomes about half of the remaining wait.

title: The run page requests the review model only after the entry JavaScript runs
oneLine: ssr: false plus a client loader makes HTML, scripts, model, render, and images sequential (model request 520 to 679 ms, first screenshot 814 ms at 150 ms/9 Mbps).
verifierReason: Code confirmed. apps/web/src/routes/runs.$runId.tsx:31 `ssr: false`; :37-47 client loader; :66-74 pending text. Built HTML: `s:"pending",ssr:!1` and `Checking access and loading this run…`. Re-measured (150 ms, 9 Mbps, 3 runs): entry script ends at 493 ms, `/api/runs/<id>` 512 to 667 ms, one long task of 105 ms, workspace 781 ms, first image 808 ms (auditor: 520 to 679 / 792 / 814). Not refuted, but the current behavior is deliberate and the report does not say so: the P03 research records `ssr: false` as "the smallest safe migration" and server data as "a separate increase in scope" (docs/simplification-audit/evidence/feedback-performance.md:30), and src/review/client.ts:364 says "Router loaders own reads". CORRECTIONS. (1) Severity medium, not high. The loader already starts before hydration. An early request saves only the gap between the HTML and the entry script: 354 ms in the throttled profile, about 110 ms in my production load (HTML at 195 ms, scripts done at 308 ms), and less after FE-05. The model time, the 105 ms render, and the image time stay. (2) The sketch calls `parseReviewModel(await early.promise)` and skips the checks in `request()` (src/review/client.ts:254-283: content type, `!response.ok`, and the `ReviewCommandError` with status 401 that gives the guest page). Pass the early `Response` through the same function. (3) An inline request takes the read out of the loader (no `abortController.signal`). P03 selected loader ownership, so this is a contract question for the maintainer. `ssr: "data-only"` exists in router-core 1.171.32.
secondLensReason: Mechanism confirmed for production: ssr: false at apps/web/src/routes/runs.$runId.tsx:31 and a client loader at :37-39 that requests /api/runs/<id> (apps/web/src/review/client.ts:365-373). The captured production run document has ssr:!1, s:"pending" and the loading text. This design is selected decision P03 (docs/current-contract.md:150; docs/simplification-audit/evidence/feedback-performance.md:30). Real impact is small: the finding measured the preview fixture (1 item, 2 variants, 3 ms API). For real runs (626 items, 3,832 variants) the orchestrator recorded a request start at 206 to 300 ms, a server wait of 5,251 to 5,680 ms, a 5.3 to 6.0 MB body, and content visible at 6,676 to 7,756 ms. An earlier request can save about 0.1 to 0.25 s, at most about 4% of the wait. The model request is the cost, and this finding does not reduce it. Fix feasibility: the recommended head script plus loader fallback is feasible (CSP allows it, the fallback keeps the route browser tests working) and does not touch the security contract or P03; it copies the URL rule into an inline string and does not use the loader abort signal. The alternative ssr: 'data-only' exists in the installed router (router-core 1.171.32 router.d.ts:42) but would put 5 to 6 MB of model data in the HTML and make the first byte wait for the model build, so it is not practical with the present model size. Severity becomes medium only after the model request is fast.

title: The header links and the Queue button are plain anchors, so each click reloads the document
oneLine: app-shell.tsx and review-workspace.tsx:580 use <a href>; each tab click is 1 document plus 11 more requests and a repeated access check, while the router Link to the same view needs 0.
verifierReason: The finding is confirmed. apps/web/src/components/app-shell.tsx:15-19, :29, :53-58, src/review/review-workspace.tsx:580, and nav.ariakit.react.tsx:590-609 (`<ak.Role.a … {...rest} />`) are as quoted. No router code intercepts plain anchors, and no test depends on them. Re-measured with a 1,500 ms API delay: header `Run history` = 1 document request, 12 requests, loading text from 102 to 1,631 ms; router Link `View history` = 0 document requests, done in 54 ms; `Queue` button = 1 document request, 12 requests. CORRECTION to the recommendation: an unconditional `<Link>` breaks the fixtures. `ReviewWorkspace` renders `AppHeader` (review-workspace.tsx:535) and the `Queue` button without a router in src/review/__tests__/fixture.tsx (used by review.browser.test.ts and scale.browser.test.ts) and in tooling/review-scale/fixture.jsx. I ran `renderToString(<Link to="/">)` without a `RouterProvider`. Result: `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'protocolAllowlist')`. The workspace already guards this case (review-workspace.tsx:748-759): `render={route ? <Link … /> : undefined}`. Do the same for the header links and the Queue button, or mount a memory router in both fixtures. Also not in the finding: the two comparison links at review-workspace.tsx:474-478 are plain anchors too.
secondLensReason: Problem and numbers hold. Production path: server.ts:118 renders the document with no access check, then /api/runs repeats the check (6 D1 round trips per the auth lane). Orchestrator's signed-in samples: content at 1,220 to 2,290 ms per header click; a router link between views of `/` needs 0 requests (41 ms on the build). The gain for the Queue button and the run-page header is smaller (240 to 595 ms of the wait), so that part is medium. The recommended snippet is not safe as written; I measured three defects. (1) A client navigation skips the beforeunload guard (use-review-session.ts:175-184) and the unmount cleanup aborts the unsent command: the anchor gave a beforeunload dialog, router.navigate gave no dialog and POST .../commands net::ERR_ABORTED. Contract line 196 says unsent decisions still require the browser. useBlocker exists in 1.170.38 but must live in the route file. (2) Default active matching marks Queue and History both aria-current=page on /?view=history (link.js:38-40, 221-224); activeOptions {exact:true} corrects it. (3) Link throws without a RouterProvider (TypeError ... 'protocolAllowlist'); 71 browser tests and the review-scale fixture mount ReviewWorkspace without one. Safe scope: router links only on the dashboard route. No server or security-contract change.

title: Dashboard data lives in component state, so each mount and each refresh shows the loading text again
oneLine: No loader or cache for /api/runs; Back from a run and 'Refresh runs' blank the page to the loading text for the full API time.
verifierReason: Code confirmed. apps/web/src/routes/index.tsx:161-162 and :176-210 keep the run list in `useState` plus an effect keyed on `reload`; :242-245 `refresh` sets `{ status: "loading" }` first. Re-measured with a 1,500 ms API delay, Run to browser Back: 0 document requests, 1 `/api/runs` request, loading text from 102 to 1,526 ms. Notes. With a route loader, the router default (`staleTime: 0`, stale-while-revalidate, https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/framework/react/guide/data-loading) shows the cached list and refreshes it in the background, so the question "how old can the list be" needs no `staleTime` value and no module cache. D08/D09 ("No new workflow framework or global store", docs/current-contract.md:53) is about the review workspace refactor. It does not forbid loader data.

title: Hashed static assets are served with max-age=0, must-revalidate
oneLine: Production and local both return 'public, max-age=0, must-revalidate' for /assets/*; there is no public/_headers, so each document load sends 9 to 10 conditional requests.
verifierReason: Confirmed in production. `curl -sI https://visonaut.com/assets/index-CXm4JU5N.css` returns `cache-control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate` and `cf-cache-status: HIT`. With `If-None-Match` it returns 304 in 39 ms. On a reload of the build, 9 assets return 304. apps/web/public has only favicon.svg. wrangler.jsonc has no `assets` block (the plugin writes `"assets":{"directory":"../client"}`), so the Worker does not run for asset paths and cannot set the header itself. The value is the documented default, and `_headers` is the documented fix (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/headers/). With the Vite plugin the file goes in `public/` (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/vite-plugin/reference/static-assets/). I re-ran the scratch check: `/assets/*` returns `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`; `/favicon.svg` and the document keep their headers; `/_headers` returns 404. CORRECTION: severity low, not medium. The measured cost is one parallel round trip of about 40 ms for each document load from this location. It grows with network latency and with FE-03.

title: A click on a run gives no feedback for 1 second, and nothing is preloaded
oneLine: Default pendingMs of 1000 keeps the old page on screen until 1,123 ms after the click; no defaultPreload, and the 138 kB run chunk loads only after the click.
verifierReason: Confirmed. apps/web/src/router.tsx:8 sets no `defaultPendingMs` and no `defaultPreload`. router-core@1.171.32/dist/esm/router.js:626-627 has `defaultPendingMs: 1e3` and `defaultPendingMinMs: 500` (the docs say the same: https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/framework/react/guide/data-loading). src/routes/runs.$runId.tsx:33 has `pendingMinMs: 0`. Re-measured with a 1,500 ms API delay: the URL changes at 102 ms, the queue stays on screen until 1,118 ms, the pending text stays until 1,626 ms, and the evidence is ready at 1,745 ms. The `runs._runId` chunk is requested 31 ms after the click. NOTE: `defaultPreload: "intent"` preloads the model on hover. The P03 research says "Do not add global infinite freshness or automatic model preloads" (docs/simplification-audit/evidence/feedback-performance.md). Keep to `defaultPendingMs` plus the code-only warm-up.

title: Each review action re-renders the whole workspace several times
oneLine: ArrowDown: 7 commits and 3,442 component renders of 1,121 mounted; approve: 10 to 12 commits, 64 to 80 ms keydown at 1x CPU and 256 to 264 ms at 4x; no memo or compiler.
verifierReason: Measurements reproduced on the build (1,000 items x 6 variants, 1x CPU): 1,121 mounted components. ArrowDown: 7 commits, 3,442 component renders, keydown 32 ms, task time 68 ms. Approve: 10 commits, 6,106 renders, keydown 64 ms, task time 133 ms, longest task 87 ms. Search key: 3 commits, 1,523 renders. Causes confirmed in the code: all state is in `ReviewSession` (review-workspace.tsx:196-213, :253-260, :296-301); use-evidence.ts:54-62 sets state for each decoded image; item-list.tsx:91-104 with `onOrderChange={setOrder}` (review-workspace.tsx:453) gives one more full render for each model change; navigation.ts:64-73 gives each item a new identity; runs.$runId.tsx:133-138 builds a new `route` object for each render. `rg` finds no `memo(`, `startTransition`, or compiler option. The render counter is valid: it reads the PerformedWork flag, which React DevTools also uses. The two sketched fixes do not change behavior: `applyPendingReviews` is pure, and use-review-session.ts:461 compares `savedModel`, not the derived model. `react({ compiler: true })` is in the installed plugin README, marked experimental. CORRECTION: severity medium, not high. At 1x CPU the input handling is 32 ms and 64 ms. That is below the 100 ms perception limit and the 200 ms INP limit. The 256 ms value needs 4x CPU throttling. The gain of the fixes is not measured.
secondLensReason: Counts are correct and were reproduced by the first verifier (ArrowDown 7 commits and 3,442 renders; approve 10 to 12 commits). The impact claim is overstated: input handling is 32 ms and 64 to 80 ms at 1x on an M4 Pro, far below the 200 ms INP 'good' limit (web.dev); only the 4x throttle case (256 to 264 ms) reaches 'needs improvement'. The image wait in the same loop is larger (FE-08). Fix checks: use-review-session.ts:133-136 already memoizes the model, so the applyPendingReviews fix helps approve only; applySavedReview (navigation.ts:116-130) has the same full rebuild and is not in the report; memo needs stable props in 4 places and rows are an inline function (item-list.tsx:178-278). The history.replaceState alternative does not work: @tanstack/history 1.162.4 index.js:338-340 patches replaceState and notifies the router. React Compiler packages are not installed; my probe with babel-plugin-react-compiler 1.0.0 compiles ReviewSession, ItemList, ScreenshotViewer and 18 more, but not useReviewSession, useEvidence and 5 others (??= and try/finally limits). Gains are not measured. Client-only; no contract effect, but D08/D09 behavior is in the same files.

title: The next screenshot is not preloaded
oneLine: Full images are requested only 26 to 29 ms after the key press; with 300 ms image latency each step waits 355 to 393 ms against 63 to 126 ms without it.
verifierReason: The finding is confirmed. screenshot-viewer.tsx:146-150 is the only place that requests a full image. `rg` finds no `new Image(`, `preload`, or `fetchpriority` in src. navigation.ts:144-163 and api/images.ts:24-40, :52 are as quoted: each image is one D1 read and one R2 read, and no Cache API is used, so the edge does not cache it. Re-measured: 2 full-image requests start 26 ms after each ArrowDown, and none start before it. New production lower bound: `GET https://visonaut.com/images/<unknown uuid>` (D1 read only, 404) has a time to first byte of 146 to 149 ms on a warm connection; `/health` has 31 to 55 ms. A real image adds the R2 read and the transfer. CORRECTIONS. (1) Two alternatives ("also preload … the current diff image" and "preload only the diff image … when the two main images are ready") are the option that contract P02 rejected ("Load diff after required evidence"). P02 selected "Load diff when selected" (docs/current-contract.md:149). They reopen a contract decision. The main recommendation (reference and candidate of the next pending target) does not. (2) In the sketch, the effect cleanup runs when `evidence.status` changes at the moment of the move, and `element.src = ""` can cancel the preload that is now needed. Do not clear the source when the target becomes the selection. (3) U06 records the risk of extra image loads during rapid arrow keys, so keep the preload to one target.
secondLensReason: Hot path holds: each first view is one Worker request, 1 D1 read and 1 R2 get (api/images.ts:24-40), not edge-cached (Workers run before the cache), and approve/reject is blocked until both images decode (review-workspace.tsx:302-307, 385-386). I measured the gain the lane left unmeasured, on the production build with 300 ms image latency, real HTTP cache and the production CSP: approve 389 ms to 122 ms, ArrowDown 370 ms to 57 ms; with 100 ms think time 227 ms (joins the in-flight request); every image requested once. Production image latency itself is not measured (lower bound about 150 ms from the review-load lane's D1-only 404 path), so confidence in the production size is medium. No contract change: images are public (D16, contract line 59), the evidence gate stays, and reference plus candidate preload agrees with P02; the 'preload diff' alternative reverses P02 in part. Cost is negligible (requests only move earlier; at most 2 wasted per wrong prediction). Two sketch defects: useMemo on `selection` does not memoize (new object each render, review-workspace.tsx:286-290) and the cleanup restarts preloads on every model identity change; key the effect on the two URL strings.

title: Tailwind compiles the stylesheet twice
oneLine: styles.css imports review.css and two TSX files import review.css again; 254 duplicate rules (128,286 bytes, 28%) stay in the 464,666-byte build file and dev injects two 371 kB style tags.
verifierReason: The finding is confirmed. src/styles.css:1, src/review.css:1-2, and the three script imports (__root.tsx:2, runs.$runId.tsx:21, review-workspace.tsx:66) are as quoted. My own scan of the built file gives the same counts: 1,796 utility rules, 1,542 unique, 254 duplicates, 128,286 bytes (`@container` 186, `@supports` 29, `@media` 23). The dev page has two `<style>` elements of 371,158 bytes each. I compiled a single entry with the plugin's own steps (`@tailwindcss/node` compile, oxide Scanner, optimize): 332,367 bytes raw, 45,688 gzip-9, 31,901 brotli-11 (auditor's simulation: 336,380 / 46,448 / 32,271). At brotli quality 4, which matches production (43,560 computed, 43,803 served), the single compile is 41,119 bytes: a saving of 2.4 kB. CORRECTIONS. (1) Severity low: about 2 kB on the wire and about 2 ms of parse time. (2) The recommendation says to delete review.css and names two fixtures. More references exist: src/components/operations-attention/__tests__/fixture.tsx:4 imports `../../../review.css`; tooling/review-scale/run.mjs:63 lists `review.css`; docs/simplification-implementation.md:87 links to it. tooling/review-scale/fixture.jsx:2 already imports styles.css. The smallest fix is one line in src/routes/__root.tsx:2: `import "../review.css";`. All three script imports then name one CSS module, and Tailwind compiles it once.

title: A large part of the stylesheet is for classes that the app never applies
oneLine: Up to 41.6% of unique utility bytes (123,735 of 297,711) belong to classes never seen in a broad session; unused vendored tabs and kbd recipes are scanned.
verifierReason: Facts confirmed: 464,666 bytes; 644 `:has(`, 592 `@container`, 245 `@property`, 85 `@supports`. Re-run of measure-unused-css.mjs: 825 classes seen, 729 of 1,542 unique rules never seen, 123,735 bytes (41.6%). tabs.ariakit.react.tsx and kbd.ariakit.react.tsx have no importer; each other vendored component has one. CORRECTION: the recommendation recovers much less than 41.6%. I measured it with a real compile. `@source not` for tabs and kbd changes the single-entry stylesheet from 332,367 to 294,717 bytes raw (minus 37,650, 11%), gzip-9 from 45,688 to 40,949, brotli-11 from 31,901 to 28,706 (tabs minus 34,365; kbd minus 3,285). The line `@source not "./**/__tests__"` changes 0 bytes. The 78 scanned files outside src (migrations, tooling, CHANGELOG) add 0 bytes: `@import "tailwindcss" source(".")` gives the same output. This answers the auditor's open question. `ui-bevel-button` (2,641 bytes) stays, because button.ariakit.react.tsx:167 names it. The other never-seen rules belong to variants of components that the app imports, so `@source not` cannot remove them. The `@source not` syntax is documented (https://tailwindcss.com/docs/detecting-classes-in-source-files). Severity low: about 3 kB on the wire, cached after FE-05. D10 (docs/current-contract.md:54, "No pruning or replacement is selected") is not touched by a scan exclusion, but that is the maintainer's call.

title: Class attributes dominate the markup
oneLine: 73% of the 28.5 kB loading-shell HTML is class attributes; a 100-run history table is 1.0 MB of markup with 874 kB of classes (1,683 bytes for each td).
verifierReason: Sizes confirmed with my own scripts. Built HTML for `/`: 28,538 bytes, of which 20,987 bytes are `class` attributes (73.5%). Run page: 436 elements, 180,122 bytes of markup, 119,448 class bytes, 14,792 style bytes. History with 100 runs: 1,690 elements, 1,007,659 bytes of markup, 874,148 class bytes; 200 `td` elements with 1,683 class bytes each; the table is 953,651 bytes of markup for 12,873 bytes of text. Long task on the run page load: 105 ms. CORRECTION: no measurement isolates the class strings as the cause of the long tasks. The auditor's own trace shows small style work for each action (ArrowDown: 9 style recalculations, 4.5 ms in total, 1 to 3 elements each). Treat the link from class bytes to render time as an assumption, not a measured fact. title: The service writes completed_at again on each re-send, so GitHub shows a wrong and growing duration and public data cannot show when a check first passed
oneLine: packages/security/src/checks.ts:197-200 sets completed_at to now on every delivery and every project event re-sends all eligible runs; one main check was read with completed_at 19:26:20Z, 21:20:31Z, then 21:37:03Z and the same conclusion; main median 'Submit end to completed_at' is 2 h 27 min 59 s (n=17), and 22 of 25 late writes follow another run's event.

Live read at 2026-10-06T00:23Z: check 111879629441 has completed_at 21:37:03Z; the auditor's data from 21:05Z has 19:26:20Z; same conclusion. The report's open assumption is now measured: the public page github.com/ariakit/ariakit/runs/111879629441 shows 'succeeded Oct 5, 2026 in 4h 41m 40s', which equals completed_at minus started_at. My recount: 25 of 50 successful Submit executions have a late last write and 22 of the 25 follow another run's event within 150 s (chance level about 4 %); main median 2 h 27 min 59 s (n=17). Corrections: the 'minimal' alternative must send existing.completed_at, not omit the field (GitHub docs do not define the omitted case); the 'same' test must also compare existing.name because the PATCH renames legacy checks (checks.ts:194); the skip removes only the PATCH, the GET stays.
secondLensReason: Reach: each status pass sends one GET and one PATCH with a new completed_at for each eligible run (packages/security/src/checks.ts:173, :191-202; apps/web/src/operations/checks.ts:200-209); any other run, a decision, or maintenance starts it. Live read 2026-10-06T00:48Z: check 111879629441 still has completed_at 21:37:03Z and the public page shows 'in 4h 41m 40s'. Local probe with the real sendGitHubCheck: 3 deliveries of one unchanged success intent give 3 PATCH bodies with 3 different completed_at. Magnitude (my recount, completed_at minus started_at): 15 of 15 passed main checks show more than 30 min (median 2 h 30 min 57 s, max 11 h 56 min 6 s); pull request checks have median 4 min 6 s, 4 of 32 above 30 min. It changes no conclusion and blocks no merge; no consumer workflow listens to check_run. The request cost is the D1-05 cost and is not counted again here (estimate: at least 64 to 106 redundant PATCH each day, far below 5,000 requests each hour). Fix feasibility: I ran the proposed 'same' test against 50 real checks; it is true for 48 (GitHub returns details_url, title, summary equal to the code text), false only for the 2 green 'running' checks of PIPE-09. No migration, CLI release, pin change, or contract change is necessary. Caveats: compare existing.name; a pending check gets no refresh (GitHub's 14-day stale rule, PATCH effect not documented); omitting completed_at is not documented. Not verified: check_run webhook for each re-PATCH; merge box display. Counter-argument: display value only; any D1-05 fix repairs it. Severity low for the wrong time alone (report and first check: medium).

title: A capacity pause refused Submit after the complete capture: 5 failed Submit steps in one afternoon, and two main commits keep a red check

secondLensReason: Reach: POST /v1/runs -> reserveVerifiedStagedRun -> checkRunAdmission (apps/web/src/api/workflow-owned.ts:398-431; apps/web/src/capacity.ts:25-30, :107-113); production uses the defaults 2 GiB and 5 runs (wrangler.jsonc:64, runtime-defaults.ts:15-17). title: Six of eleven failed Submit steps print only 'The signed Submit check could not be started.'; three of them came 4 s to 3 min after the target branch moved
oneLine: Full table of the 11 failed Submit steps with log text, exit code, and cause; begin refuses for wrong pins, a superseded commit, or a merge ref that is not ready with the same sentence and exit 4; for a superseded main commit the server answers 503 with Retry-After for a permanent state (pre-run-attempts.ts:782-787), which matters for the PKG-01 option 'retry each 503'.
verifierReason: Confirmed: 11 of 61 started Submit steps failed at the listed times with the listed texts and exit codes; bundle-submit.ts:57-71 hides each begin error; api/index.ts:42 adds Retry-After to each 503. Corrections: (1) for the main case the push webhook stores a main candidate (webhooks.ts:186-191), so ensureSignedAttemptCheck skips pre-run-attempts.ts:772-788 and the refusal most probably comes from pre-run-candidates.ts:247-250 ('The main branch changed.', 503); the sketch changes only the less probable site; (2) that second site is shared with settlePreRunWorkflow, whose catch needs error.code 'workflow_candidate' (pre-run-attempts.ts:950-962), so a new code there breaks the retirement path; (3) the main case failed in a job that GitHub cancelled, so 10 Submit jobs have the conclusion failure; (4) step time separates the classes: 0 to 1 s for the three pin cases, 4 to 5 s for the three others; (5) 'main moved' does not make a pull request run untrusted by design (oidc.ts:318-335, contract:210-214); the server code of the two pull request cases stays unknown; (6) a new server status has no effect for the consumer without the CLI change, which needs a release and a cutover.
secondLensReason: Reach: beginSubmission replaces each error with one sentence and exit code 4 (packages/cli/src/bundle-submit.ts:57-71); begin is sent one time and Retry-After is not used (http.ts:119, :201-220). Probe with the real CLI: 8 different server refusals (503 merge_not_ready, workflow_candidate, check_pending, service_unavailable, capacity_exceeded; 403; 409; 401) give the same sentence with 1 request each. Magnitude: 6 of 61 Submit steps (9.8 %): 3 pin cutover, 1 replaced main commit in a job that GitHub cancelled, 2 pull requests. New evidence for the 2 pull request cases: the head did not change before the failure (timelines of #7739 and #7732); main moved 116 s and 186 s before; of 35 first-attempt pull request Submit steps without pin or capacity failure, main moved during 4 and 2 of those failed, 0 of 31 others (chance about 1 %); the new main commits changed the same files (6 files for #7732 vs #7731, 3 for #7739 vs #7740); a conflict repair followed each time (merge of main; Renovate force push 30 s later). GitHub returns merge_commit_sha null for a pull request with a conflict (measured on #4378: mergeable false, dirty, null; also null while mergeable is null). The real verifyGitHubOidc turns that null into 503 invalid_metadata 'Trusted metadata is unavailable.' after 6 GitHub reads (oidc.ts:302, errors.ts:19-24), which fits the 4 to 5 s step time. So the most probable cause is a conflict with the moved main, not proved; the Worker log (api_rejected, 7 days retention) decides until 2026-10-11. Consequence: 0 of the 6 jobs could be saved by a better message or a retry; the cost is diagnosis time, and the server calls a state that needs the author 'temporary'. Fix feasibility: the CLI message needs a release plus new pins B and C (one cutover with a measured 34 to 41 min failure window); a server status change has no effect for the consumer with CLI 0.5.4; the report's sketch at pre-run-attempts.ts:782 is the wrong site (the conflict site is oidc.ts:302; the main site is pre-run-candidates.ts:251-254, and settlePreRunWorkflow needs the code workflow_candidate there). Severity low (report and first check: medium): no avoidable job loss was measured and the fix is cheap only with the next planned CLI release.

The webhook alternative is the only option with no cutover; it reverses #145 and must not create a check for the 'edited' action (contract line 212). The create-before-verify alternative is not safe as written. Not verified: the pull request page in a browser, and the true report after a change of line 55 (code reading and history only).

title: On main, 7 of 22 commits do not end with a passed check, and two checks are green with the title 'Visual review is running'
oneLine: Final main states: 15 passed, 2 red from the capacity pause, 1 red 'has not passed', 3 with no check (run cancelled by a newer push), 1 completed/success titled 'Visual review is running'; inferred cause: a pending intent after a success does not reopen a completed check on GitHub (not verified, needs a test write); no pull request path to that state was found.
verifierReason: Facts confirmed: my recount of the 22 main commits gives 15 passed, 2 capacity failures, 1 'has not passed', 1 green 'running', 3 with no check; checks 111369835207 and 111219809935 read live are completed/success with the title 'Visual review is running'. The cause is not proved but is stronger than inferred: only sendGitHubCheck writes that title on an existing check and it always sends status in_progress with it, and none of the other seven PATCH sites sends success without its own title, so GitHub took the output and kept completed/success; the old baseline's check has its last write in the same second (05:27:49Z). GitHub documentation does not state this behavior. Corrections: (1) the code sketch turns each pending intent on a complete check into neutral, and GitHub counts neutral as passed for required checks, so it must be limited to main runs or replaced by a new check generation; (2) baseline-promotion.ts:489 excludes only kind pull_request, so merge_group runs can go from passed to pending; no merge queue rule is active on Ariakit main, so there is no exposure today; (3) one of the two checks is a superseded first attempt.

With the current ci.yml, app=false runs 'visonaut submit --no-visual' (ci.yml:66-70) and the service refuses a base that is not main at oidc.ts:299 (from pre-run.ts:73-98), so the Plan job fails and each job that needs Plan is skipped. title: In WebKit, Shift+Tab does not move focus after a mouse click on the label or the icon of a button

title: When only Firefox or Safari variants changed, the selected chip is off screen at load, and no other text names the browser

title: A direct link to an item far down the list does not bring its row into view

title: A decision fails with 409 when any other write of the project commits at the same time
oneLine: Approve, Reject, and Undo assert the project revision and the run revision (review-commands.ts:213-216), so a commit on another row, run, or pull request gives 409 "State changed"; 17 of 40 concurrent decisions were lost locally, one overlap discards the queued chain, and the same guard makes the status `checks` step fail with a step-failed alert.
verifierReason: Code and all measurements are confirmed (re-run of a-concurrency and status probes gave the same results; review-commands.ts:213-216, :107, :368-370; status-touch.ts:11; review-queue.ts:106-116,134-146; checks.ts:210-218). Correction: the '17 of 40' result is for two requests that start in the same instant (Promise.all). The report says the conflict 'needs no special timing'; my probe v-stagger shows 8/16 conflicts at 0 ms offset, 6/16 at 40 ms, and 0/16 at 80 ms and 160 ms (local read-to-write window: median 116 ms, inflated by the harness). So a decision is lost only when another commit lands inside one read-to-write window. A lone reviewer on a pull request has no self-conflict (prepareStatusIntent does not change the project revision; consumer max_concurrency is 1). No wrong state is saved; the cost is repeated work, a generic message, and step-failed alerts that clear at the next pass. Options are feasible; the 'narrow guards' option must also compute the stored runRevision in SQL (review-commands.ts:224-225 computes it before the write).
secondLensReason: The mechanism is confirmed, but the real effect on decisions is small. Reach: one project for all runs (apps/web/wrangler.jsonc:60), decisions run in the HTTP Worker, the consumer is serial (wrangler.jsonc:98-107). Measured window: 1 D1 call from the revision read to the guarded write for a queued decision (call 15 to call 16), 2 to 3 for Undo (probe s01-window). One reviewer lost 0 of 60 chained queued decisions in two local sessions with the consumer's status passes at the same time (s01-lone). The real team is small: 2 persons started all 134 user runs of the newest 300 pull request CI runs. Estimates (rate times window, round trip 5 to 140 ms, not measured in production): CI as second writer at most 1 lost decision in 2,450; a second reviewer who saves each 2 s loses 0.25 to 7 % (Undo 0.75 to 21 %). No wrong state is saved. The frequent effect is a different one: a decision commit at 45 of the 170 D1 call positions of one status pass (6 eligible runs) makes the complete checks step fail (sweep, 87 positions tested), and 13 of 30 passes failed in a one-reviewer session with a 150 ms gap. Each failure records checks/scheduler/step-failed and the next pass repairs it (0 unresolved at the end, check success). Fix feasibility: a second call of service.review with the same input after a conflict saves exactly 1 command with the correct runRevision in 3 more D1 calls, and gives the precise 'A target changed' error with the row when the row is really stale (s01-retry); D1 batches roll back as a transaction (official docs). Correction to the option 'catch per run and set hasMore': hasMore re-sends after 1 s (runtime.ts:454), so a permanent conflict would loop like OPS-02; use one inline retry and then skip. Narrow guards also need previousRunRevision, baselineRevision, and promotionId from SQL. Severity rises to medium only if two or more persons review at the same time as normal work.

title: A Reject of a carried approval is dropped at the next push
oneLine: The reuse query (local-comparison.ts:24-36, :591) ignores a later rejection of the same tuple: approve in run 1, copy in run 2, Reject in run 2 by another reviewer, then run 3 with the same pixels is `approved/human(copied)` by the first reviewer and the check is `success`; this contradicts contract-issue-1.md:209.
verifierReason: The defect is confirmed and reproduced (rules-reuse.json identical: run 3 'approved/human(copied)@1', check 'success'; g3 the same for an automatic approval). Production links every earlier run of the same pull request (apps/web/src/api/lineage.ts:362-365, :568-580), so the fixture is representative. It is wider than stated: my probe v-rerun shows that a workflow re-run with no push also restores the approval, and that the main run after a merge copies the old approval and is 'passed' with check 'success'. Corrections: (1) the index the recommendation names does not exist; migration 0009_retention_history.sql:43 drops it, and the recommended SQL as written gives 'SCAN later' (full scan of visonaut_decisions); with the two json_extract digest predicates it uses visonaut_decisions_pixels. The SQL is valid and gives the intended result (v-reuse-fix.json). (2) The contract citation (contract-issue-1.md:209) needs the C02 context: the maintainer selected 'copy' with 'removes later cross-run revocation' (audit-data.json C02, handoff-draft.md:22); C02 names only the other direction, so this direction is undecided, not clearly a contract breach. The code is not consistent with itself (g4 keeps a Reject, g2/g3 drop it). (3) The option 'revoke the source decision' writes to closed history (D05, current-contract.md:50).
secondLensReason: The defect and its impact are fully confirmed and reach farther than measured before; the corrections of the first verification stay valid. Reach: every earlier run of a pull request is a verified source (apps/web/src/api/lineage.ts:358-365, :568-580), each push is a new workflow run (live ci.yml lines 3-7), main always starts a visual run after a merge (ci.yml lines 60-61) with links from the merged pull request (lineage.ts:370-386), and the Visonaut check is a required check on main (ruleset read with gh api). 27 of 55 recent pull requests had 3 or more head commits, 13 had a workflow re-run, 166 of 300 runs were started by bots, 0 came from forks. Measured end to end with the real operations pass and with each old run retired at the push (s02-end-to-end): run 1 approves a new item with no person and user 42 approves a changed item; run 2 copies both; user 43 rejects both (check failure); run 3 with the same pixels is passed with check success; the main run after the merge is passed; one status pass promotes it (baseline revision 1 -> 2); a later run sees the rejected pixels as unchanged. For the new item the baseline changed with 0 human approvals and 1 human Reject. The reviewer has no action that keeps the Reject, because the source is in a closed run (D05, docs/current-contract.md:50). Fix feasibility (s02-fix-cost, 300 changed rows, 4 earlier runs, 1,505 decisions): current rule 10,205 rows read; the condition as the report wrote it 1,816,205 rows read (178 times, plan 'SCAN later'); with the two digest predicates 10,205 rows read and the index visonaut_decisions_pixels. Both forms block exactly the 10 rejected rows. The condition runs only at finalize, survives history cleanup, and keeps the binding C02 sentence (current-contract.md:184) because it revokes no copy. New evidence for intent: the code before C02 had this guard (migrations/0024_core_simplification.sql:9-22; C02 evidence: 'a new decision cannot accidentally revive a revoked approval'). Contract status stays a maintainer decision: contract-issue-1.md:209 against the C02 'copy' text. Mitigation outside the service: the ruleset needs one code owner approval after the last push, but that person sees a green check titled 'Visual review passed'.

title: A check that is locked after "success" keeps "success" after Reject or Undo
oneLine: After one failed GitHub read locks a check (OPS-01), a later Reject changes the service status to `rejected` but three healthy status passes send nothing, so the required check stays `success`; the lock blocks the fail-closed direction too.
verifierReason: Confirmed by code and re-run (work.ts:538-548 sets ambiguous on each error and keeps the lease; claimStatus needs lease_token IS NULL at work.ts:441-447; checks.ts:258-266 sends nothing). Re-run identical: after Reject the service is 'rejected', the stub check stays 'success', 3 healthy passes send no request. Head checks use this sender only (review-links.ts:174 skips them). My probe v-status-reads confirms that each event of another pull request gives one new GET for each check. Severity medium, not high: it needs a failed GitHub read on a check that already shows success and then a Reject or Undo on the same head; no user can cause the first event; an alert is open; the cause is OPS-01, already high. Correction to the option: the two-line sketch does not work alone (the delivery object has no lease time or conclusion; deliverStatus and isStatusCurrent need ambiguous = 0; the old outbox row is 'sending'). Platform facts are correct (GitHub 10 s timeout per official docs; client 15 s at github.ts:78; lease 12 minutes).
secondLensReason: Confirmed on the only production publisher of the required head check (run-admission.ts:202-206 binds the pre-created check; work.ts:491-498 sets request_started before the sender; security/checks.ts:173 reads first; work.ts:538-548 locks on each error; checks.ts:258-266 sends nothing). Correction 1, wider: no earlier lock is necessary. Measured (s03-order): the check is healthy, the reviewer rejects, only the read of that delivery fails one time; the service is rejected and the GitHub check stays success through 2 healthy passes, a recovery pass, and a pass with the clock 24 hours later (github: [] each time). The same pass also locked the baseline run's check (fan-out). Correction 2, narrower: the baseline stays protected. Merged at the stale head, the main run is needs-review with check failure and baseline revision 1 -> 1, because a Reject is not carried; the second gate fails only together with STATE-02. A new head commit gets a new, correct check (s03-new-head); a workflow re-run on the same commit is blocked with 503 check_pending (pre-run-attempts.ts:637-643). Magnitude: one failed GitHub request is sufficient; about 9 % of API requests failed for 80 minutes on June 10, 2026 (GitHub availability report); no published rate outside incidents; a read above 15 s also locks (github.ts:78). Fix feasibility: the OPS-01 change removes the measured case (needs a retry delay, per second-lens-5). A fail-closed write after the lease end is possible on the platform (GitHub permits a new update of a completed check run; the normal Reject path already moves success to failure), but the two-line sketch is not sufficient (work.ts:479, :494 need ambiguous = 0; old outbox row is 'sending'), the new write needs a delay or it loops like OPS-02, and settling the lock after it is an accepted-risk decision (GitHub's 10 s limit is not a guarantee). Medium and not high: no user can cause the first event, the exposure is one head commit, the baseline is protected, and the ruleset still needs a person. Not low: a required check is wrong in the passing direction with no end and no repair tool.

title: A queued decision that fails 5 times is dead for its command ID, the 5 attempts take seconds, and a stopped consumer holds a decision for 12 minutes
oneLine: failWork retries with no delay (review-queue.ts:148-154), so a short storage fault makes the task `dead`; the receipt is 409 code `conflict`, the same ID again answers 202 and then 409 forever, no operations event is recorded, and the consumer's 12-minute lease delayed a decision to 721 s when the worker stopped.
verifierReason: Code and probe are confirmed (review-queue.ts:148-154, :62, :28-32; review.ts:817-830; runtime.ts:454; re-run of e-dead-task identical: dead after 5 attempts, receipt 409 'conflict', no operations event, same ID again 202 then 409). Corrections: (1) 'a storage fault of some seconds makes the task dead' holds only for a partial fault; the auditor's probe fails only the review write batch (e-dead-task.probe.ts:48-52). In a complete outage the claim fails and attempts stay 0: my probe v-outage shows 6 failing passes with attempts 0, then completion. A repeating error (for example a too-large command) is the realistic cause. (2) The reviewer is not blocked: a 409 receipt clears the client queue and a new command ID works (use-review-session.ts:275, :378). (3) After a stopped inline worker no status message is sent (review.ts:643-665), so the repair delay is up to the 5-minute cron, not 30 s. The 12-minute consumer lease is correct from the code. Options are feasible.

title: The queued path and the direct path give different answers for the same refusal, and the queued path never names the reviewer
oneLine: The task result keeps only the error message (review-queue.ts:140-145), so the receipt has no `reviewer`, `incomplete` becomes `conflict`, a closed or promoted run answers the generic "State changed", and a missing predecessor answers 503 service_unavailable; review-guide.md:55 promises the reviewer name.
verifierReason: Confirmed: the queued receipt never has 'reviewer', 'incomplete' becomes 'conflict', the admission guard gives the generic 'State changed', and a missing predecessor answers 503 (review.ts:682-697, :817-830; review-queue.ts:36-38, :140-145; re-run of errors and c-undo-replay identical). contract-issue-1.md:225 still asks for the reviewer in the private UI. Corrections: (1) 'offers a retry that cannot succeed' is wrong for the web client: POSTs are serialized (client.ts:306-323), the client reports the first failure, keeps all commands, and Retry sends them again in order (use-review-session.ts:286-305, :373-379), so the predecessor arrives first and the 503 is discarded. (2) 'cannot see who changed a row' is too strong: the receipt has the current model and the details line prints the row's reviewer (review-workspace.tsx:463-466). The value is the numeric GitHub user ID (review.ts:500, :857), already reported by the ui-copy lane. No wrong state; only codes and sentences differ.

title: Two runs of one pull request can be open for review, and approvals on the older run are not carried
oneLine: reserveRun closes only attempts of the same workflow run (run-admission.ts:120-124); a new push leaves the older run open until the pull_request webhook retires it, and an approval saved there after the newer run is ready answers 200 but is not copied to the newer run.
verifierReason: Mechanics confirmed (run-admission.ts:120-124; webhooks.ts:283-323; local-comparison.ts:612-624; re-run of case b2: approval on the older run 200, newer run still 'no decision'). Correction: the assumption 'nothing retires the run when the merge commit is not ready' is incomplete. In that state the same webhook fails with 503 merge_not_ready (webhooks.ts:299-307; pre-run-candidates.ts:73-87; merge.ts:16-23), the delivery stays unprocessed (webhooks.ts:330-335), and reconcileWebhooks runs it again in each 5-minute recovery pass (runtime.ts:369-371; wrangler.jsonc:61, :110). So the older run is retired by the first attempt after GitHub has the merge commit, normally before the new run is ready. Two open runs need a lost delivery or a recovery that fails for the full CI time. Real timing is not observed. Option note: a guard on the lineage link alone is too wide; it must also compare lineage_key.

title: "Equivalent merge check retired" makes the newest Visonaut check neutral also when the tested result failed
oneLine: pre-run-checks.ts:255-260 accepts a source check with conclusion `failure` and then writes `neutral` to the alias check on the same pull request head; GitHub counts `neutral` as passing, but which of two same-name check runs GitHub uses is not verified, and the path needs an unbound check row (old data or a stopped begin request).
verifierReason: Code facts confirmed (pre-run-checks.ts:255-260 accepts 'failure'; :350-363 writes 'neutral'; re-run of i-equivalent identical). The GitHub quote is correct ('Successful check statuses are success, skipped, and neutral'). The impact is not verifiable: the documentation has no rule for two same-name check runs, and a read of 25 recent ariakit pull request heads found 0 heads with two Visonaut check runs. Reach is small, as stated (webhooks store a candidate with no check, pre-run-checks.ts:590-604). Correction: the main recommendation (write 'failure' for a failed source) can block a pull request for good, because the alias is processed only while queued or in_progress (:323-331) and is not selected again after lease_until is NULL (:203-204, :373-377); it stays 'failure' when the source later passes. The 'minimal' alternative (accept only 'success' at line 257) is correct under both possible GitHub rules.

title: A carried approval looks like a first-hand approval
oneLine: A copied decision keeps the kind and the actor of its source, and the review model returns only verdict, source `human`, and the first reviewer; no field says that the approval came from an earlier run, and the review guide has no sentence about carried approvals.
verifierReason: Confirmed by code and re-run: the copy takes the kind and actor of its source (local-comparison.ts:614-615) and the model returns only verdict, source, and reviewer (review.ts:497-500; measured variant keys have no origin field). The review guide has no sentence about carried approvals. Addition: the reviewer value is the numeric GitHub user ID. The 'carriedFrom' option is feasible; a copy of a copy points to its direct source, so 'decided at' needs a rule for chains.

title: One command can have about 6,000 targets, and each target adds 4 statements and 2.4 KB to one batch
oneLine: 1,000 targets are 4,010 statements and 2.44 MB in one batch (114.5 ms locally), 5,000 targets are 20,010 statements and 12.2 MB (509.8 ms), both accepted by local D1; the 40,000 target limit cannot be reached because the 1 MiB body holds about 6,190 targets; the UI sends one item for each command today, so this matters for an "approve all" design.
verifierReason: Confirmed by code and re-run (4 statements for each target, review-commands.ts:227-271; re-run: 1,000 targets 4,010 statements and 2,442,021 bytes; 5,000 targets 20,010 statements and 12,202,022 bytes, error null). Additions from the official D1 limits page: row and string limit 2,000,000 bytes, statement 100 KB, 100 bound parameters, 30 s query time, 1,000 queries for each Worker invocation, no stated batch statement limit. My probe v-command-row measured 542 bytes for each target in the stored command row, so the row passes 2,000,000 bytes at about 3,690 targets, below the about 6,190 that the body limit accepts. Local D1 does not enforce this. Not verified on production. The UI sends one item for each command, so impact today is none.

title: Three "expected" fields of a decision command have no guard effect
oneLine: applyReviewCommand does not read expectedBaselineRevision or expectedPromotionId, and the route uses them and expectedRunRevision only to select the answer shape of the direct path; they are still part of the command identity for replay.
verifierReason: Confirmed by code: applyReviewCommand reads neither expectedBaselineRevision nor expectedPromotionId (review-commands.ts:126-317; types.ts:158-159), and the route uses the three body fields only for the answer shape of the direct path (review.ts:881-887). Small correction: only two of the three fields are part of the command identity; expectedRunRevision is not passed to the service or to the task payload (review.ts:855-871). Note: current-contract.md:53 says to preserve 'expected revisions' and 'exact command IDs', and a removal changes the stored request text for replay, so a removal needs a maintainer decision (the report says none is needed).

title: After a new sign-in, an open review tab cannot save again, and "Refresh current state" cannot repair it
oneLine: client.ts keeps one review-session promise; a new auth session makes every command answer 409 review_session_expired, shown as "Conflict. Start a new review session after signing in." until a browser reload (1 session request, same reviewSessionId on each retry).
verifierReason: client.ts:293-303 keeps one sessionPromise; runs.$runId.tsx:161 memoizes the commands object; refresh() does not renew it. Real handler probe: review_session_expired 409. Browser re-run: 1 review-session request, session-1 on 4 commands, same alert after 3 refresh cycles. Medium, not high: needs an existing review session in the tab plus a new auth session made outside the tab; a browser reload repairs it. Option correction: the renewal works for save() (same commandId admitted with a new session, measured) but not for undo() (review-commands.ts:340-347) and not across a previousCommandId chain (review-queue.ts:41-47); the Undo stack must be cleared.

title: An expired session during a review shows "Not saved. Sign in with GitHub." with no way to sign in, and "Refresh current state" then drops the decision
oneLine: The 401 text is plain server text, the workspace has no sign-in control, refresh() clears the held queue before the read, and a 401 on the receipt poll shows "Could not confirm…" instead of the cause.
verifierReason: Measured again: 'Not saved. Sign in with GitHub.'; after 'Refresh current state' the held decision is gone, review controls are disabled, no sign-in control, focus on body (use-review-session.ts:484-488, :502). Correction: 'no way to sign in' is too strong; a browser reload shows 'Sign in to review this run' with a callback to the same item and variant, and the header keeps 'Review queue'. The loss is the held decision. Option correction: a popup cannot post back through window.opener because each response has Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin (security/http.ts:37); use BroadcastChannel.

title: The page says "You can close this window", but a queued decision that fails later is never shown, and a reload forgets each receipt
oneLine: Command IDs live only in React state and no endpoint lists a user's receipts, so after a close or reload pending decisions look undecided and failed ones leave no trace; this conflicts with docs/current-contract.md:196.
verifierReason: Facts confirmed: 'You can close this window.' (review-workspace.tsx:1113), command IDs only in React state, the only receipt read needs the command ID and actor (api/review.ts:799-836). Probe on real code: a second decision after a reload ends with receipt 409 also for the same verdict. Corrections: 'conflicts with the contract' is a reading; the server keeps receipts until the run is archived, the gap is that no screen can find them. The reload scenario used a queue that never completes; real processing starts in the admission request (api/review.ts:641-667, :876), so the exposure is a short window or a consumer fault. A list endpoint has no index today.

title: A queued decision that never completes shows the same line without end, and each queued decision polls 2 times each second with no bound
oneLine: Same text after 30 s (60 polls) and after 5 min (600 polls); one 500 ms loop per queued command, no backoff, no visibility pause, no elapsed time or link to Service status.
verifierReason: client.ts:326-336 polls each 500 ms with no bound; measured 19 polls in 10 s and the same bar text. Corrections: 'also when hidden' was measured only with a simulated visibilityState; real hidden tabs are throttled by the browser (Chrome: one check each second, then each minute). 'Never completes' needs a stopped operations consumer; the scheduled operations also drain the review queue (operations/index.ts:48). The load argument is weak for a few maintainers; the missing 'stuck' state is correct.

title: A newer push replaces the run under an open tab: the page finds out only when a save fails, uses four sentences for one cause, and has no link to the newer run
oneLine: No read between load and save; after the failed save four different texts say the run is over, ReviewModel has no successor field, and "Refresh current state" answers "Check the evidence before saving a new command." on a read-only run.

(review-queue.ts:49-57, database.ts:65; measured on the real handler). 'Only the active complete comparison can be reviewed.' shows only if the run closes between admission and processing. 'Wasted review time on each push' is too strong: each decision is a save. A successor lookup by lineage_key has no index.

title: Decisions of another reviewer or another tab appear only after a failed save, and the conflict names the person by a numeric ID

title: A ready run page never reads again and has no refresh control; the queue never updates; no surface shows the age of its data
oneLine: staleTime Infinity with no refresh control outside error states; a dashboard hidden 10 minutes sends 10 alerts requests and 0 run-list requests, reads nothing on return, and shows no age text.

title: The client ignores error.code: each 409 is "Conflict", each 403 is "write access", each other error is "Not saved" or "temporarily unavailable"
oneLine: Three call sites map the HTTP status differently and none reads the code; 29 of 103 realistic matrix cells name the wrong cause and 33 have no way forward.

title: The three "no access" screens differ, and two are dead ends
oneLine: Dashboard has Retry and Use another account, pull page only Use another account, run page only Retry and no account menu; on a wrong origin Use another account fails with "Sign-out failed."
verifierReason: The three control sets are as stated (index.tsx:340-352, pulls.$pullNumber.tsx:216-233, runs.$runId.tsx:55-63 and :76-111); sign-out on a wrong origin answers 403 (server.ts:82-84).
