title: When a background poll gets a 401, the dashboard silently becomes the public landing page
oneLine: The queue or history is replaced by "Every change. A clear decision." with no session-ended text, no live-region entry, lost search state, and focus on body.
verifierReason: operations-attention/index.tsx:239-242 calls onAccessDenied(401); index.tsx:165-174 sets guest; the guest view has no reason text and no live region. Low: an open dashboard renews its session with each poll, so the realistic cause is a sign-out in another tab, and the landing page is then the correct state. Missing sentence, lost search text, and lost focus are small.

title: Offline: no automatic retry for saves or images, the browser's raw error text, and no connection state
oneLine: "Not saved. Failed to fetch"; 0 requests in 5 s after the connection returns; no online listener; blocked A/X keys give only a screen-reader-only line.
verifierReason: Re-run with real offline and online window events: 'Not saved. Failed to fetch', 0 requests in 5 s after the online event, key A gives only the screen-reader line. No online listener exists. Method note: the auditor simulated the loss with route.abort, so navigator.onLine never changed; the result still holds. Addition: 'Refresh current state' pressed while offline drops the held decision (measured).

title: A click on a run while offline replaces the app with the browser's offline page
oneLine: The router treats any failed chunk import as deploy skew and reloads the document, so an offline click on a not-yet-loaded route ends on chrome-error with ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED.
verifierReason: Dev re-run reproduces the browser offline page; lazyRouteComponent.tsx:52-71 confirmed. Production is derived (assets are max-age=0, must-revalidate, so the HTTP cache does not help). Corrections: this is designed router behavior and a run cannot open offline in any case; Chrome opens the run after reconnection. The Start plugin refuses autoCodeSplitting (start-plugin-core/src/schema.ts:6-8); use codeSplittingOptions. router.preloadRoute also runs the loader; the chunk-only call is router.loadRouteChunk.

title: A chunk that stays missing after the automatic reload ends in the router's bare "Something went wrong!" screen
oneLine: A single missing chunk is fixed by a silent reload, but a second failure shows TanStack's default error with the module URL and no shell; the run route's own error component is a lazy chunk too, and there is no defaultErrorComponent.
verifierReason: Dev result reproduced; the production build splits the run errorComponent; no defaultErrorComponent. Corrections: in production the default error screen hides the details (CatchBoundary.tsx:59; bundle has useState(!1)), so users see 'Something went wrong!' and 'Show Error', not the module URL. A normal 'wrangler deploy' does not reach this state; the second failure needs an asset fault. 'Keep old assets' is not a Workers setting (Cloudflare documents only version affinity for gradual rollouts).

title: A tab cannot detect a deploy, and an API format change gives messages that hide the cause and a button that cannot help
oneLine: No build ID on responses or /health; a newer model format shows "Could not confirm…" then "Not saved. This review format has changed. Refresh before reviewing." although the server saved the decision, and only "Refresh current state" is offered.
verifierReason: client.ts:157-159 format check; /health has no build field (server.ts:60-71); the measured message sequence follows from use-review-session.ts:380-388 and :502. A build ID is feasible with the Workers version metadata binding and a Vite define.

title: A 5xx answer that is not JSON tells the user to check the connection; the maintenance text and its Retry-After: 60 are dropped
oneLine: The cutover-fence 503 text answer shows "The service did not return review data. Check your connection and refresh." on the run page and on saves.
verifierReason: client.ts:263-267 maps each non-JSON answer to 'Check your connection'; cutover-fence.ts:4-8 answers 503 plain text with Retry-After: 60. The fence is deployed only during a cutover (deploy.yml:376-402).

title: 503 handling differs on each surface: the reference is dropped on five of ten, Retry-After is never read, and the retry policy is one of four
oneLine: Queue, history, service page, bell, and pull page drop the server message and reference; retries are none, fixed 2 s, fixed 60 s, or stop; no client code reads Retry-After: 1.
verifierReason: The per-surface table matches the code. Corrections: 'no client reads Retry-After' is true only for the web client; the CLI reads it (packages/cli/src/http.ts:195). Alternative (c), remove the header, is not open: docs/current-contract.md:81 requires Retry-After: 1. The missing reference on the dashboard is not a contract fault (contract line 83 names the review client only). Automatic retry is safe for commands and Undo; POST /api/review-sessions is not idempotent.

title: The Service status page cannot open while /api/runs fails
oneLine: The status view renders only after the run list is ready, so a run-list 503 shows "The review queue could not be loaded" under the Service status tab with 0 requests to /api/operations.
verifierReason: index.tsx:356-364 renders the status view only in the ready state. Re-run: /?view=service with a 503 from /api/runs shows 'The review queue could not be loaded', 0 requests to /api/operations. Note: both endpoints share the auth and GitHub checks, so the fix helps only for faults of the run list read alone.

title: Permanent states offer "Retry", and evidence errors offer nothing
oneLine: An unknown run (409 incomplete) and a missing check offer only Retry; an image 404 says "Check your connection"; a dimension mismatch has no control because recompareAllowed is always false.
verifierReason: Real handler probe: unknown run gives 409 incomplete 'The requested record does not exist.'; a bad comparison value gives 400 invalid_id (was 'derived'). Image texts and recompareAllowed: false confirmed. Correction: the cards have no exit link, but the header keeps 'Review queue', so these are not dead ends. The evidence-error part (no control, no next step named) is fully correct.

title: A sign-in that fails at GitHub leaves the app: the user gets Better Auth's default error page, or the landing page with no message, and the deep link is lost
oneLine: Sign-in passes no errorCallbackURL and auth.ts sets no onAPIError; a cancel, an expired state (10 min), or a failed code exchange redirects to /api/auth/error, which renders a foreign page with an "Ask AI" link or redirects to /?error= that the landing page ignores (branch depends on NODE_ENV; not verified on production).
verifierReason: Auth probe re-run reproduces each result (better-auth 1.7.5; callback.mjs:37, :79-86; error.mjs:380-384). The production branch is still not verified; the built chunk reads NODE_ENV at run time, wrangler.jsonc has no such variable, and Cloudflare states that NODE_ENV is not a runtime value, so the built-in HTML page is likely. Option correction (measured): errorCallbackURL covers access_denied but state_mismatch and state_not_found still go to /api/auth/error, so onAPIError.errorURL is required. Low: needs a cancel, a wait of more than 10 minutes, or a GitHub fault.

title: The auth rate limit answers 429 after three sign-in starts in 10 seconds; the page says "could not start, try again" and enables the button at once
oneLine: Better Auth's built-in /sign-in rule is 3 per 10 s with X-Retry-After: 10; the three sign-in surfaces and sign-out show a generic failure, ignore the wait, and the pull page swaps to "Review unavailable".
verifierReason: Re-run: 200, 200, 200, 429 x-retry-after=10, 429; rate-limiter/index.mjs:302-308; the three sign-in surfaces show a generic text and enable the button at once (index.tsx:220-226, pulls.$pullNumber.tsx:128-131). The production client address handling is not verified here (default header x-forwarded-for; AUTH-14 owns it).

title: A historical comparison is marked by one unstyled sentence; counts and badges still say "need review", and the decision keys do nothing with no feedback
oneLine: Only a plain line and 10 px header text mark the read-only view; "9 of 11 need review" and a filled Approve button remain; key A gives no request, text, or announcement; the current comparison has no visible mark in Details.
verifierReason: A taste claim about the marking of a read-only view. Each factual part is correct: the sentence (api/review.ts:581), the silent return at !ready (review-workspace.tsx:385-387), plain anchors with aria-current only (:473-488), and the screenshot shows '9 of 11 need review' with a filled Approve button. Traffic of this view in production is not known.

title: Recovery moves focus to body, alerts read their button labels as text, and one blocking message exists only for screen readers
oneLine: Focus is on body after Retry, after Refresh current state, and after a session end; the bar's live text is "Not saved. Failed to fetchRetry same commandRefresh current state"; the 'resolve first' message is sr-only.
verifierReason: Focus is on body after 'Refresh current state' in three re-run cases; the bar is one element that changes role and contains the buttons (review-workspace.tsx:1104-1134); the 'resolve first' line is sr-only (:1202-1204). Correction: 'alerts read their button labels as text' was not measured with a screen reader; the recorded string is the element's textContent.

title: After a sign-out in another tab, an open run page keeps its content and all its controls
oneLine: No cross-tab signal; the run stays on screen with 0 requests until a navigation or a save fails; Back to the queue and Forward to the run then show the sign-in screens.
verifierReason: No cross-tab signal exists; the run page keeps its content until a request fails. Real exposure is small: a person at the same browser profile sees what was already on screen, no request works after sign-out, nothing can be changed, and images are public by URL by design (docs/review-guide.md:3). Kind 'security' is generous.

title: The real run inventory uses 69.5% of its 16 MiB write limit; at about 5,500 captures each Submit fails
oneLine: The inventory for the real 3,832-capture set is 11.66 MB (3,043 bytes for each capture, 60% is the embedded manifest); writeCaptureInventory throws at 16 MiB, which is about 5,500 captures, below the 10,580 that the contract plans for.
verifierReason: Core finding confirmed. I ran the size probe again: unchanged run inventory 11,662,476 bytes, 69.5% of the limit, 3,043 bytes for each capture (verify/results/inventory-size.json). apps/web/src/capture-inventory.ts:56 and :468-470 throw at 16 MiB; workflow-materialize.ts:377-386 and :403 embed the manifest and write it; reconcileStagedWorkflows (:894-949) only retries and records retry-delayed. Corrections: (1) Two limits in the published CLI follow immediately: the combined manifest file is 67.2% and the linux shard manifest 66.6% of 8 MiB (packages/cli/src/files.ts:9, artifact-archive.ts:10). Growth factors to the limits are 1.439 (inventory), 1.487, 1.502. So the option 'raise the constant' gains about 3% and then needs a CLI release and a new pin in Ariakit. (2) The first recommendation (clip out of the profile) gives about 9.5 MB and about 6,760 captures; with zero profile bytes the bound is 7,130. 10,580 captures need 1,585 bytes for each capture. (3) '60% is a second copy' is not exact: after compaction the manifest is the only copy of profiles; it is 60.2% of the object. (4) 81 distinct profiles without clip in the combined set, not 54 (54 is the linux shard). The 10,580 number is a binding planning number (current-contract.md:7), but D54 does not assert numeric limits at cutover.
secondLensReason: Core finding confirmed and made stronger; two numbers corrected. Reach: every trusted Submit writes one inventory (workflow-materialize.ts:403); live Ariakit ci.yml and app.yml have the pinned blobs 4d34ca17 and 202fd63a (gh api), each main push sets app=true (ci.yml:59-64), CLI visonaut@0.5.4; about 25 Submit steps and 9 main commits each day (consumer lane). The limit was ALREADY passed in production on 2026-10-04: PR #249 body says the first submission after #247 was 18.8 MB, above 16 MiB, and materialization retried; main run 37202597656 ended 21:33:46Z, fix merged 22:45:55Z, so at least 72 minutes blocked. Corrections: (1) the production object is 12,222,666 bytes (PR #249), 72.9% of the limit, not 11,662,476 (69.5%). My probe with import-shaped images (64-character ID, 157-character key, reset.ts:411-421) and the real writer gives 12,222,098 bytes, 568 bytes from production. The stop is at about 5,260 captures, growth factor 1.373, headroom 1,427 captures (about 233 example cards, or one more Chromium-size browser project reaches 97.9%). (2) 'Raise the constant' gains about 8% (to the CLI 8 MiB limit at about 5,700), not 3%. (3) Clip out of the profile gives about 6,390 captures, 60% of the 10,580 planning number; no single option reaches 10,580 (needs 1,585 bytes per capture, production has 3,190). Damage by code reading (not run): plain Error, hourly retries for 24 h, no terminal check state because the run row exists (pre-run-attempts.ts:984-990), alert on the dashboard only. Growth: 3,582 -> 3,646 -> 3,832 captures in 13 days, about 20 a day, 3 weeks to 7 months to the stop; not a forecast. Counter-argument: closed failure, no data loss, fixed in 72 minutes last time, D54 says measure first; but the cheap compaction lever is now used and the next limit is in the pinned CLI. Raw: second-lens-1/results/import-shape.json, hotpath.json.

title: One Submit reads and validates the complete reference inventory at least 27 times
oneLine: Each of the 20 reference pages, three validations, and two input reads downloads and validates the same immutable 11.5 MB object again (about 310 MB for each run); the count for each call is measured, the total is computed, and the production time share is not measured.
verifierReason: The count is confirmed by reading and by the probe: local-comparison.ts:334, :335, :432 (first page 3 reads, each later page 1), validateLocalSubmission at workflow-owned.ts:546, :1143 and workflow-materialize.ts:273, referenceCaptureInputs at :275 and :809; inventory-records.ts has no cache. 20 pages for 3,832 captures gives 27. Corrections: (1) 27 is a minimum. Each CLI credential renewal calls readReference again (packages/cli/src/engine.ts:416-431): 20 more reads, plus one more declare when the renewal is inside the upload loop. (2) The alternative 'complete list in one response, about 1.2 MB' is wrong: I measured 2,395,231 bytes (625 bytes for each entry), above the CLI response limit of 2 MiB (packages/cli/src/http.ts:3). It works only up to about 3,300 captures without a CLI release. (3) Production bound added: six unchanged Submit jobs took 157 to 227 s in the step 'Submit captures' with 0 originals staged; about 141 s pass before the upload phase in run 37332053157. The share of the inventory reads is still not measured. The isolate cache is feasible (same pattern as local-comparison.ts:57) but applies to one isolate only.
secondLensReason: The count of 27 is correct (first page 3, pages 2-20 one each, declare 1, finalize 1, materialization 3) and the path runs on every Submit, about 21 successful each day. Measured cost on the real capture set (second-lens-1/results/hotpath.json, Node on M4 Pro, memory store): 425 ms median per read, 9.5 s CPU for the 22 reads of the page loop, 11.5 s for all 27, 315 MB read (330 MB with the production object). With a list cache the page loop is 0.55 s (94% less). Real impact is small: at least 6% of the median 147 s Submit step; estimate 10 to 30 s (assumptions stated, not measured), which is 1 to 2.5% of the 20-minute push-to-pass time; R2 and CPU cost are cents (R2 Class B $0.36/million with 10 million free; Workers $0.02 per million CPU ms with 30 million included). The local CLI work is larger: 29 s here, two full decodes of 3,832 PNG files. Corrections to the first verification: (1) the alternative 'larger page or complete list' is not possible at ANY size without a CLI release: published CLI 0.5.4 rejects a page with more than 200 captures (packages/cli/src/local-comparison.ts:105), in addition to the 2 MiB response limit. (2) The renewal multiplier did not occur in the six sampled runs (157-227 s against a 555 s threshold); it applies to long uploads. Fix feasibility: the isolate cache works in local workerd (binding object identical across requests, WeakMap hit from request 2: binding-identity.mjs) and has no trust cost, because the CLI and the server both check inventoryDigest; no guarantee of an isolate hit in production (Cloudflare docs). The repository's own review of PR #247 rated the same defect on the image route as medium, where the multiplier grows with changed images; here it is fixed at 22. Cost grows almost with the square of the capture count (1.7 times at the STORE-01 stop). Counter-argument: users do not see the gain and the repeated validation is a contract defense.

title: inherited-by pins form a chain, so replaced baseline images and the imported baseline do not expire after 30 days
oneLine: An inherited-by pin is released only when the borrowing run's bytes are deleted, so each retained main run holds all owners that its inventory named; in the probe the imported image stayed stored and public after three later baselines had replaced it.
verifierReason: Confirmed by code and by a second run of the probe. run-admission.ts:634-641 creates inherited-by pins; the only release is retention.ts:206-210 at the byte deletion of the borrowing run. Final probe state: import <- inherited-by:run-b, run-b <- inherited-by:run-c, run-c <- inherited-by:run-d, imported image still 200. I found no document that makes this deliberate. I lower the severity: the saved requirement is about unpinned runs (contract-issue-1.md:336), these runs are pinned, the images are public by design, and only small replaced main images are kept. Correction: an owner is free only when each run that named it has had its own bytes deleted, which is stricter than the text. I emulated the recommended release in two scenarios (verify/results/v03a and v03b): needed images stay 200, replaced images become 404, a new pull request and the CLI reference download work, an open pull request against an older snapshot keeps its images. Not tested: old-form runs, shard-inheriting reruns (run-admission.ts:331-335), and runs that already have references_released_at set.

title: After a D1 restore, objects written after the restore point have no row, no check finds them, and no step deletes them
oneLine: In a modeled 24-hour rewind, inspectRecoveryImages found the three rows that point to deleted objects and the ordinary passes repaired them, but four objects of runs created in the window stayed with no row forever; the recovery code has no list call, does not read QUARANTINE, and does not check masks.
verifierReason: Confirmed. operations/recovery.ts has get calls only (:98, :200, :220), no list, no quarantine read, and role='original' at :91. My second run of the restore probe gives the same result: 3 rows that point to deleted objects are reported, 4 objects with no row are not reported and remain after 31 days. R2 list supports delimiter and delimitedPrefixes (Cloudflare R2 Workers API reference; installed workers-types 5.20260922.1, index.d.ts:2482 and :2623), so the recommendation is feasible. I lower the severity: the objects are private, the amount is one restore window, and current-contract.md:244 says hosted restore is UNVERIFIED and not a required drill. Correction: sanitizeRestoredDatabase does change work_retained_runs.closed_at (recovery.ts:62-65); it does not change byte_state. The saved requirement 'Reconcile orphaned objects' (contract-issue-1.md:336) supports the finding. The 420 MB number is an estimate that I did not check.

title: The QUARANTINE bucket no longer holds images; facts and options for the two-bucket rule (S01, D16)
oneLine: Uploads go directly to IMAGES with only a size and SHA-256 check, QUARANTINE gets only the staged manifest and plan evidence, nothing moves between the buckets, and private inventories live in IMAGES; five options are listed and none is selected.
verifierReason: All facts confirmed. quarantine.put exists only at workflow-evidence.ts:203 and workflow-materialize.ts:707. Uploads and reuse copies write to context.images (workflow-owned.ts:1103, :969). quarantineKey (workflow-evidence.ts:87) is a ticket identity only. local-v1 is the only admitted mode (workflow-owned.ts:182-187) and skips the comparator (:1066-1106). The public route needs a visonaut_images row with validated=1 (api/images.ts:24-27). Direct upload to IMAGES exists since 2026-09-24 (commit 494718f); I found no recorded decision that accepts it. The five options are a judgment. I lower the severity because nothing is exposed today: the exposure needs an operator to make the IMAGES bucket public, which contract-issue-1.md:334 forbids. Live bucket settings are unknown. Note for the options: a life-cycle rule for the complete QUARANTINE bucket also deletes old-form manifests/<run>/ objects that hasReferencedManifest protects; use a prefix rule.

title: The full operations pass and most retention steps have no test on runs with an inventory
oneLine: By script census, runOperations has 0 of 6 tests with an inventory run, expireRunImages 3 of 12, expireComparisonReferences 0 of 2, and sanitizeRestoredDatabase 0 of 21; the sparse fixture uses an old-form baseline except in one test, and production first runs these paths about 30 days after the cutover.
verifierReason: Confirmed. I ran the census again from a copy: runOperations 0 of 6, expireRunImages 3 of 12, expireComparisonReferences 0 of 2, sanitizeRestoredDatabase 0 of 21, promoteBaselines 8 of 23. I checked for indirect coverage: runOperations( appears only in core-storage, main-retirement, and operations tests, with no inventory fixture; no API test calls expireRunImages or runOperations. sparse-storage.test.ts sets referenceInventory: true once (:644). The import writes closed_at = now (tooling/baseline-reset/reset.ts:298-311), so no row can be 30 days old before 30 days after the import. Limits: the census counts direct calls in a test body only, and the date 2026-11-03 comes from commit dates; the real import time in production is not verified.
secondLensReason: Confirmed. Reach: production cron */5 (wrangler.jsonc:109-111) -> server.ts:129-139 -> queue -> runScheduledOperations -> runOperations (runtime.ts:431), 288 passes each day with no user action. Five steps (history, reference-retention, source-retention, snapshot-retention, retention; operations/index.ts:52-56) select only rows closed 30 days ago (retention.ts:53-56, closed-summary.ts:392-398). The inventory form was merged 2026-10-04T21:06:31Z (#247), so the first real action is no earlier than 2026-11-03; the production import time is not verified. Addition: NO environment runs these steps before production (preview has no cron, queue, bucket, or database, and both handlers return first: server.ts:130, runtime.ts:311-312). Search confirms runOperations( is only in three test files with no inventory. Magnitude (my probe, results/retention.json): the normal S1 scenario is correct (X returns 200, no events). Negative control with the four pins of the owner run removed (emulated defect, not a present bug): one pass deletes the owner images, X returns 404 on the public route and the CLI route, the baseline review says imagesExpired false, a new run fails with ConflictError at commitShard, and operations_events is empty. So a pin defect is silent, not reversible (R2 has no versioning; the buckets have no lock), stops every new Submit, and needs a new baseline import. Fix feasibility: high; the complete S1 scenario with the existing test doubles runs in 87 ms (both scenarios 148 ms); risk is a hand-built inventory fixture that drifts from materializeBundle; no contract change. Counter-argument: the audit probes passed, the delete code is shared with the tested old form, pins have service tests, and the known deviation keeps images too long. Severity stays medium because the form is one day old, the first execution is in about four weeks in production only, and the damage of a regression is permanent.

title: No code deletes run inventories: 11.7 MB for each run, about 5 to 8 GB each month, and the key layout prevents a prefix rule
oneLine: Each service run (estimate 450 to 680 each month from four days of CI data) leaves one 11.66 MB inventory forever; the price is about 1.27 USD each month after one year, gzip makes the object 8 times smaller, and inventories share the runs/<run>/ prefix with deletable images.
verifierReason: Facts confirmed: operations/retention.ts:22 and :46 keep the inventory on purpose, no delete names an inventory key, size measured again, rate computed again from the raw GitHub data (86.4 runs in 3.82 days, 678 each month, 7.9 GB each month), prices equal to the Cloudflare pricing page, life-cycle rules select by prefix only. Correction: the recommended code does not work on R2. In local workerd, put with the readable side of a CompressionStream throws 'Provided readable stream must have a known length', the current sha256 option fails with a gzip body ('The SHA-256 checksum you specified did not match'), and get returns gzip bytes with the compressed size (verify/results/r2-gzip-put.json). The bytes must be buffered first, the sha256 option and the size check at capture-inventory.ts:492 and :547 must change, and the reader needs DecompressionStream. The Infrequent Access alternative saves about 0.43 USD each month at 95 GB and adds a retrieval price.

title: 25 candidates that cannot be deleted stop all later image deletions
oneLine: expireRunImages has no cursor and skips an unsafe-prefix candidate without a state change, so 25 such rows fill each page; in the probe a normal run behind them was never deleted over six cron ticks and the step reported hasMore false.
verifierReason: Confirmed by code and by a second run of the probe. operations/retention.ts:50-57 has no cursor; :65-75 records an alert and continues with no state change; hasMore is set only at :61 and :109. claimExpiredRun (packages/service/src/work.ts:783-802) has the same conditions as the query. Probe: each call returns completed [] with 25 attention and hasMore false, and the normal run stays live. The trigger needs a manual data change or a future prefix form, so low is correct. Corrections: a row whose delete fails does not stop the queue, because it is outside the candidates for its 12-minute lease. The first recommendation (skip rows with an open unsafe-prefix alert) adds a stuck state: no code or operator action resolves that alert except a complete deletion (retention.ts:134), so a corrected row stays skipped. The alternative with the prefix rule in SQL or a cursor does not have this effect.

title: Plan evidence in QUARANTINE has no reader and no deleter, and ingest_manifests.object_key points to an object that is deleted after one day
oneLine: Each run writes plans/workflow/<digest>.json (545 bytes) that only test-reachable code reads and no prefix delete covers, and the staged manifest key stored in ingest_manifests is deleted with the stage after about 24 hours.
verifierReason: Confirmed. workflow-materialize.ts:687-710 writes plans/workflow/<digest>.json for storage version 1, and new declarations are version 1 (workflow-owned.ts:589). The only reader of plan_object_key is operations/history.ts:503, and archiveClosedRuns and archiveHistoricalComparisons have no call site. ingest_manifests.object_key gets the staged key (workflow-materialize.ts:445-451) and workflow-retention.ts:201 deletes that prefix; hasReferencedManifest matches only manifests/<run>/%. The raw cost output shows one 545-byte quarantine put with no matching delete. Corrections: the keep-list effect is harmless, because a list that names absent objects cannot cause a wrong deletion. The recommendation is feasible, because verified_json holds the same fields (:742-752). History: #241 moved evidence to D1 and #247 returned new declarations to version 1 one day later.

title: On the sparse path the reuse endpoint handles only changed images; an unchanged run costs no image operation
oneLine: Unchanged captures are not staged, so an unchanged full run has 0 image puts, gets, and reuse copies; reuse now copies only changed images uploaded in the last day by another run, and the copy is necessary only because a changed capture must be owned by its run.
verifierReason: Facts confirmed: packages/protocol/src/validate.ts:477 leaves unchanged captures out of the upload set, workflow-owned.ts:546-548 stages only that set, the reuse path is get then put (:935-969), run-admission.ts:553 accepts another owner only for unchanged captures, promotions.ts:51-55 verifies only the run's own images. Production data added: six of six sampled Submit jobs printed 'Visonaut staged 0 originals (0 reused, 0 uploaded)' (verify/results/submit-logs.json). Correction to the recommendation: no new logging is necessary, because the CLI already prints both counts in each Submit job (packages/cli/src/engine.ts:653-655) and returns them in JSON mode. The keep-or-remove question is a judgment. One more fact: when a challenge is offered, the CLI sends a reuse request for each upload page before any upload, also when no source exists.

title: A closed summary hides images that still exist, and the expired flag looks only at the run's own bytes
oneLine: 30 days after close, also for the current baseline, the page shows a text box while all image URLs in the model return 200; imagesExpired stays false when reference images of other owners return 404, and a proposed UI text says the images are deleted.
verifierReason: Facts confirmed: api/review.ts:242 and :589-591 set evidenceState 'summary' and imagesExpired from the run's own byte_state; review-workspace.tsx:298 and :805-813 show a text box with no image; review-inventory.ts:39 sets bytes_present to 1 with no check; :364 still reads the inventories for a summary. My probe runs repeat both cases: current baseline with imagesExpired false and all images 200, and a baseline with imagesExpired false whose reference images return 404. The copy proposal at ui-copy/report.md:1051 is false for imagesExpired false. Not stated in the finding: the summary with no images is documented as deliberate (operations/README.md:28 'At expiry, the read path serves a terminal summary … A baseline can retain originals after its detailed review has closed'; current-contract.md:184). So the defects are the meaning of the flag and the proposed text. To show images in a summary is a product judgment.

title: All Better Auth routes are served, and a session of any GitHub account is sufficient for them
oneLine: server.ts passes all of /api/auth/* to Better Auth; with a session cookie, refresh-token and get-access-token return GitHub user tokens in plain text, account-info proxies GitHub, update-user writes the profile, and each sign-in of any GitHub account stores user, account, session, and audit rows.
verifierReason: Confirmed by code and rerun: apps/web/src/server.ts:82-87 has no path filter, packages/security/src/auth.ts:21-79 has no disabledPaths, 31 endpoints (30 HTTP), and with a session cookie only POST /get-access-token returns the plain text GitHub token. disabledPaths exists in Better Auth 1.7.5 (dist/api/index.mjs:166-168). Corrections: (1) 'any GitHub account' is wrong. The sign-in client Iv23lihLxwLZeW7tlh5u belongs to App visonaut-ci, which is private (anonymous API 404; page text 'Visonaut CI is a private GitHub App'). GitHub docs: 'Only members of the organization that owns it can authorize it.' The ariakit org has 10 members, 5 without push. Not tested with an outside account. (2) Impact is higher than stated: GitHub docs list POST and PATCH check-runs for GitHub App user access tokens, and the App has checks: write, so a maintainer sign-in token can by the docs set the required Visonaut check (not tested). (3) /refresh-token works only if GitHub sends a refresh token; my probe gives 400 REFRESH_TOKEN_NOT_FOUND without one, while /get-access-token still gives 200. (4) Part E of the auditor probe sent a wrong body; my probe confirms the new-user path with {accountId}. (5) disabledPaths is an exact match; GET /reset-password/:token stays live (measured 302). New option: a separate sign-in App with no repository permission.
secondLensReason: Confirmed: apps/web/src/server.ts:82-87 sends all of /api/auth/* to auth.handler with no path test, packages/security/src/auth.ts:21-79 has no disabledPaths, and wrangler.jsonc env.production uses client ID Iv23lihLxwLZeW7tlh5u, which is the client of App 5028451 (gh api apps/visonaut-ci). So the sign-in App is the check App, and a session cookie alone returns the plain text GitHub token (measured again). Too wide: 'any GitHub account'. The App is private (anonymous GET gives 404) and GitHub says 'Only members of the organization that owns it can authorize it'. Measured: 10 organization members, 5 with push. Reach: the client sends only POST /sign-in/social and POST /sign-out (measured with the installed client), so the 25 other routes have zero requests in normal use. This is unused surface, not a hot path. Magnitude: a session gets a new GitHub token at any time, also after the stored one expires, because the service refreshes with its own client secret (measured). A copied refresh token alone has no use (GitHub needs the client secret) and a copied access token lives 8 hours if expiry is on (GitHub default, setting not read). GitHub docs data lists POST and PATCH check-runs for App user tokens, so the token can, by documentation, set the required Visonaut check; not tested. It cannot push, approve, merge, or change the baseline. An outside party needs a script injection (production CSP has a nonce and connect-src 'self', measured) or a database copy with a live session first. A maintainer already may approve the own pull request (D09), so the insider loss is the audit record. Fix feasibility: disabledPaths exists in 1.7.5 and 21 path spellings gave no bypass (measured), but it is an exact list, fails open on new routes, and had a bypass advisory before 1.4.5. An exact allow-list keeps sign-in, callback, error, and sign-out and answers 30 other cases with 404 and 0 D1 round trips (measured). Trap: apps/web/src/api/index.ts:130-133 is a second handler; handleApi returned the token with 200 (measured), so a gate in server.ts must return and not fall through. A database hook that stores no tokens keeps sign-in working on create and update (measured); old rows need a one-time update. No option changes contract text except 'Encrypt stored GitHub tokens', which then has no object. Severity is low because no outside path exists without a second failure and the gain is limited. It rises if the App becomes public, if device flow is on, if token expiry is off, or if the private repository is in the installation.

title: A signed-in account without repository access causes 2 GitHub App requests on each private request
oneLine: A refused user costs 5 D1 round trips and 2 installation-token requests on each request, with no negative cache and no rate limit, so one outside account can use up the App rate budget that the required Visonaut check depends on.
verifierReason: Counts confirmed by rerun: a refused session causes GET /user/999 and GET .../collaborators/newcomer/permission on each request (github.ts:226-228, :236, :260; authorization.ts:71-82). GitHub docs confirm the 5,000 requests per hour minimum for an installation. Correction 1: the actor is not any GitHub account. The private App limits sign-in to ariakit org members by the GitHub docs (about 5 members have no write permission), or a person who lost access and kept a session. This is identifiable insider misuse with no gain, so severity is low. Correction 2: the sketch keys the refusal by a key that contains the session ID (authorization.ts:49-54); about 42 sessions polled each minute still use the budget. Key by GitHub user ID and add a size limit. The login-hint option (2 requests to 1) is correct. The Workers rate limit binding is feasible (ratelimits, period 10 or 60 s, Wrangler 4.36.0+) but is per Cloudflare location and not exact.

title: Pull request code selects the comparison settings, and the loosest settings make each change unchanged
oneLine: The capture manifest carries threshold, maxDiffPixels, and maxDiffPixelRatio with no service-side limit; threshold 1 made an all-black image unchanged against an all-white one, and unchanged captures create no review row, so the check passes with no review.
verifierReason: Facts confirmed: validate.ts:44-64 accepts threshold 1 and any maxDiffPixels; png-comparison.ts:68-83 and api/local-comparison.ts:529, :550-561 use the capture's own settings; no service limit exists; rerun gives 'unchanged' for white versus black with threshold 1. The reach statement is correct (workflow-materialize.ts:302-306 keeps the reference image). Server acceptance is from code reading only. Corrections: ariakit/ariakit has pull_request_creation_policy collaborators_only and fork PRs get no check, so a human author has write permission, and decision D09 (contract-issue-1.md:417) says one maintainer 'including the PR author' can approve. The bypass gives no new right; it removes the decision record. PR code also controls the image bytes, so a settings limit closes one of several ways. The 'looser setting is a review event' option needs a protocol field, a CLI release, and new workflow pins, not only a service change. What remains is a visibility gap, not a privilege problem.

title: On main, new and removed identities reach the baseline with no human decision and no upper bound
oneLine: Automatic acceptance of introductions and removals is a contract rule and the only path from capture output to the baseline without a person; a main run that captures too few tests removes the rest of the baseline with a passed check.
verifierReason: Facts confirmed: packages/service/src/local-comparison.ts:592-593 and :627 create automatic approvals for introductions and removals; workflow-materialize.ts:656-657 sends empty test and capture lists. The behavior is a contract rule (contract-issue-1.md:203, :207), and the contract also rejects 'human approval of every new item/variant/removal' (:473), so the rule itself is deliberate. An upper limit is a new idea and a contract change. Small correction: only a key with no identity history in the lineage or on main is accepted automatically; a returning key needs review. The actor is merged code or a wrong test selection, so this is a reliability risk.

title: The ingest capability renews itself without OIDC, also after Submit
oneLine: Each answer of POST /v1/runs/:id/reference contains a new 600-second capability and the route does not check submitted_at; a chain of 17 calls stayed valid for 154 minutes and kept read access to the baseline inventory.
verifierReason: Rerun reproduces 17 reference calls with status 200 and a new 600 s capability, 16 after Submit, to minute 154. Code: api/local-comparison.ts:444-448 reissues with a new lifetime; workflow-owned.ts:250-280 has no submitted_at check; the CLI renews with a new OIDC reservation (engine.ts:416-430). The chain ends when the staged run leaves 'live' after 24 hours (workflow-retention.ts:6, :114-153). Corrections to the fix: verifyIngestCapability must return exp; the JSON field expiresAt (local-comparison.ts:448) must carry the same expiry because CLI 0.5.4 reads it to decide renewal; issueToken throws a plain Error below 1 second; the reissue must stay because it carries the reference binding. A leak needs a failure of the fixed Submit job first, and the gain is baseline metadata of a public project.

title: An OIDC token is accepted again inside its 10 minutes, and one audience serves three endpoints
oneLine: jti is required but never stored, Begin, Reserve, and Submit share the audience <origin>/submit, and environment and runner_environment are not checked; a replay of Reserve returns a new capability.
verifierReason: Confirmed: oidc.ts:129-130 requires jti and nothing stores it; Begin, Reserve, and Submit share the /submit audience (workflow-owned.ts:315, :342, :1224); rerun accepts one token 3 times and accepts runner_environment self-hosted. Correction: the 9-minute acceptance was measured with a 15-minute test token. jwtVerify also enforces exp, and the example token in the GitHub documentation has exp minus iat of 300 seconds, so the real replay window is probably 5 minutes and maxTokenAge 10m never decides (not measured with a real token). Separate audiences need a CLI release, new blobs B and C, and a service pin update with a dual-accept period, for a small gain. The runner_environment check is the cheapest option and needs no client change.

title: The Submit job installs the CLI by version only, the saved consumer patch shows a digest check that is not live, and the pinned blobs use action tags
oneLine: The live app.yml runs pnpm add visonaut@0.5.4 with no archive digest check while docs/operations/ariakit-consumer.patch shows curl plus sha256sum, and the blob pin does not fix the code behind actions/*@v7 tags.
verifierReason: Live app.yml and ci.yml blobs equal the pins in apps/web/wrangler.jsonc:61 (gh api and git hash-object). Live app.yml:249-253 installs visonaut@0.5.4 by version; the saved patch (ariakit-consumer.patch:753-758) has a sha256sum check; four actions use tags. No recorded decision removes the archive check. Additions: the docs call the patch 'prepared', but the current cutover guide (simplification-cutover.md:48) still tells the operator to apply it with a package digest. Measured: npm audit signatures works in a pnpm-installed directory and reports one verified signature and one verified attestation, but it does not compare the source repository; the job must read the attestation (repository ariakit/visonaut, release.yml, refs/heads/main) to get the stated guarantee. Commit pins for actions change blobs B and C on each update, which needs a service pin deploy each time.

title: A fork pull request never gets the required Visonaut check, and no document says so
oneLine: pre-run-candidates.ts and oidc.ts refuse a head repository other than ariakit/ariakit, so a fork pull request cannot satisfy the branch rule; 0 of the last 400 consumer pull requests came from a fork.
verifierReason: Service facts confirmed: pre-run-candidates.ts:64-72 and :360-369 and oidc.ts:300 refuse a fork head; rerun gives 403 untrusted_run with check pull.head_repository_id. GitHub docs support that a fork run cannot get id-token: write. 'No document says so' is wrong: the binding saved contract says 'External-fork capture and Ariakit merge-queue runs are out of scope at launch' (contract-issue-1.md:53) and records decision D10 'Maintainer branches first' (:418). The auditor did not search docs/simplification-audit. Also measured: ariakit/ariakit has pull_request_creation_policy collaborators_only, which explains 0 cross-repository pull requests. The remaining case is a collaborator without push permission (5 of 10). README.md and the review guide do not state the rule; one sentence is sufficient.

title: A signed webhook body is accepted again under a new delivery ID
oneLine: The delivery ID and event name are unsigned headers, so a captured revocation body with a new GUID signed the user out a second time; the alias URL /webhooks/github is still live.
verifierReason: Behavior confirmed by code (packages/security/src/webhooks.ts:27-29, :55, :84-150) and rerun: the same signed body with a new delivery ID gives 202 and deletes the user's sessions again. The main recommendation is not safe: the github_app_authorization body has only action and sender, with no time or ID, and no code deletes github_webhook_delivery rows, so a digest rule would refuse a second real revocation by the same user and leave that user's sessions and tokens in place. The query also has no index. An outside party has no known way to get a signed body: the table stores parsed JSON, clears it after processing, and never stores the signature. 'No change' is a reasonable option; retiring the alias and verifying the signature before the project read are correct and small.

title: Ingest routes do database work, and one outbound request, before they check the credential
oneLine: Anonymous POST /v1/runs/:n/submit answers 401 or 404 by staged-run existence after 3 to 5 round trips, a forged bearer starts a JWKS fetch, and a bad percent sequence in a shard path gives 503 plus an operation-failed log line.
verifierReason: Rerun repeats all five lines with the same status and round-trip counts. Code: workflow-owned.ts:1177-1196 reads staged rows before verifyWorkflowJob at :1209; api/index.ts:170 decodes the shard key before the capability check and a URIError becomes a 503 with an operation-failed log; oidc.ts:120-124 makes a new key set for each call. Corrections: the valid-escape input %E0%A4 also throws, so the finding does not depend on edge handling of a broken escape; reading the bearer first does not remove the 401 or 404 signal for a caller that sends any bearer string, and Submit needs the staged row before the OIDC check; no code reads operation-failed lines, so the effect is log noise only; use jose jwksCache with a per-request key set function instead of a module-level function that holds a pending fetch.

title: There is no procedure to rotate a secret outside database recovery
oneLine: The five runtime secrets each have one accepted value and rotation is described only as a step of database recovery, so the effects of a change during an incident are not written down.
verifierReason: A search for 'rotat' in current Markdown files finds only the recovery step (apps/web/src/operations/README.md:82), drill tooling, and dated restore evidence. apps/web/wrangler.jsonc:113-121 lists five secrets, and each verifier takes one key (capabilities.ts:117, webhooks.ts:45-51, auth.ts:25). Addition: Better Auth 1.7.5 has a versioned 'secrets' option (dist/context/create-context.mjs:70, secret-utils.mjs) that keeps stored OAuth tokens readable across a change of the auth secret. I did not test whether signed session cookies stay valid. The new operations section can name this option.

title: Each model read validates two 12 MB inventories again; this is 84 to 95% of the request time on a local machine
oneLine: readCaptureInventoryDocument repeats the canonical check, two manifest parses, 21,678 profile digests, and the receipt check on each read; keeping only the digest check cuts the request from 696 ms to 158 ms in workerd (870 to 129 ms in Node) with the same response bytes.
verifierReason: All cited lines exist and do what the finding says (capture-inventory.ts:514, :552-553, :402-410, :369, :193). I rebuilt the fixture with the real code (same bytes: 12,154,546 and 12,153,016) and ran the probes again. Node state (b): 829.6 ms, of which 780.7 ms is the inventory read and validation (auditor: 870.1 ms). workerd handleApi: 598.0 ms, readReviewInventory 512.2 ms (auditor: 696.4 and 585.8). Digest-only lever: 158.4 ms in workerd and 124.6 ms in Node, with a byte-identical response (5,332,792 bytes). 21,678 digests and four parseManifest calls are correct. Corrections: the confirmed saving is 0.44 to 0.54 s of a 5.25 to 5.68 s production wait at M4 Pro speed, and the Workers CPU factor is not measured. The validation on read is deliberate and tested (capture-inventory.test.ts:677-720), so the new reader needs its own tests and a maintainer decision. The snapshot already has a durable inventory_verified mark that is set at promotion and required on read (baseline-promotion.ts:342, inventory-records.ts:87), and the read validates again; this supports the recommendation. The production baseline shape is still an assumption. The per-isolate Set alternative depends on how long an isolate lives (see WAIT-08).
secondLensReason: Reach: each run page load, each finished decision receipt, each Undo and each conflict of a signed-in user with repository write permission (index.ts:194-213, review.ts:638, :683, :789, :814; runs.$runId.tsx:34-36 loads the model again on each navigation). No anonymous reach (401/403 before reviewModel). The same validating reader also runs about 22 times for each CI Submit (local-comparison.ts:45, :334, :335, :432; lane api, API-08). Magnitude: local saving of the digest-only read is 440 to 538 ms; I measured 456 ms on the first request of a new workerd process (680 ms becomes 225 ms, same 5,332,792 bytes) and 473 ms warm. New measurement: Cloudflare's cfWorker for the guest document is 45 to 60 ms in production against 18.1 to 20.5 ms in local workerd from the same build, a factor of 2.2 to 3.3 (another workload, so an estimate). With it the production saving is about 1.0 to 1.8 s of 5.25 to 5.68 s (17 to 34%); the floor is 0.44 s (8%) if a Workers core equals an M4 Pro core. Three reads at the same time take 3.1 times one read locally (lane raw data), so overlapping receipts queue on the CPU. No correctness, security, or money damage. Feasibility: a digest-only reader works and parseManifest returns its input (validate.ts:387-390), but it changes a tested trust rule (capture-inventory.test.ts:677-720) and does not help Submit. A bounded set of validated digests inside the reader needs no contract change, keeps validation by each code version, has a precedent (local-comparison.ts:54-77, PR #247 review comment), and serves review reads and Submit pages; it does not help the first read in a new isolate. Counter-argument: the validation is deliberate, the production CPU time is not measured, and one trace (cloudflare.cpu_time_ms) decides it.

title: About 3.0 to 3.7 s of the production wait is not split yet: 24.3 MB from R2 in two sequential reads, and the speed of a Workers core
oneLine: Bytes, sequence, and local CPU are measured; the production split is not. One invocation log or trace (CPU time, R2 spans) decides between compressing the inventory (12.15 MB becomes 1.5 MB gzip) and the CPU fix of WAIT-01.
verifierReason: The measured facts are correct: 2 sequential R2 reads of 24,307,562 bytes in all states (review-inventory.ts:44-48), plain JSON (capture-inventory.ts:481-484), gzip 1,506,911 bytes, and the arithmetic of 3.0 to 3.7 s. Two corrections. (1) The remainder has three possible parts, not two: the GitHub permission and token caches are in isolate memory (authorization.ts:19-21, github.ts:102), so 0 to 1.0 s of GitHub calls can be in each production sample. The report's claim that this cannot be in three samples is an assumption, and it conflicts with WAIT-08's own inference of frequent new instances. (2) The compression sketch fails on R2 as written. Measured in local workerd: put of a CompressionStream output throws 'Provided readable stream must have a known length', and put with the sha256 of the canonical JSON throws a checksum error. A real change must buffer the compressed bytes, pass the digest of the stored bytes, change the size check at capture-inventory.ts:547, widen the InventoryStore.put type, and read both old and new objects. My local CPU is 0.60 s against the auditor's 0.66 to 0.70 s. The recommendation to read one production trace first is correct; observability with traces is on and inherited by env.production.
secondLensReason: The measured facts hold: 2 sequential R2 reads (review-inventory.ts:44-48), 24,307,562 bytes, plain JSON, direct R2 binding (runtime.ts:175, :261). The size of the part that is not split is probably wrong: the lane used a CPU factor of 1. With the measured factor of 2.2 to 3.3 (guest document render, production cfWorker against local workerd) the CPU is about 1.3 to 2.3 s, and the rest for R2 transfer, GitHub calls and all other is about 1.5 to 3.1 s, not 3.0 to 3.7 s (estimate; 1.0 to 2.0 s at a factor of 4, 2.7 to 3.5 s at 1.5). No official number exists for R2 read time; R2 has no region in South America. Feasibility: the trace reading needs no code change; observability and traces are set and inherited by env.production; the field names are cloudflare.cpu_time_ms, cloudflare.wall_time_ms, r2_get, d1_* with served_by_region, and fetch; retention is 7 days, so the three requests measured on 2026-10-05 are readable until about 2026-10-12; tracing is early beta and the page does not say if an r2_get span includes the body read. Compression is possible but needs more than the sketch: buffered bytes, the digest of the stored bytes, a new key form in four places (capture-inventory.ts:479, :532, :536-538, :556), a size rule, gzip only through CompressionStream, and old objects stay plain. Parallel reads hold 12 to 24 MB more for a short time (code reading). Smart Placement needs consistent traffic from multiple locations, which this service probably does not have. Counter-argument: it is a missing measurement, not a defect, and each code option can be the wrong one before the trace.

title: The first response carries 3,828 unchanged variants to show 4 changed ones: 5.33 MB against 7.5 KB
oneLine: With only the rows that D1 stores, the response is 7,483 bytes with 0 R2 reads and 8 D1 calls, but the changed rows have no reference image because that link is only in the baseline inventory; contract line 26 and decision P01 require the complete model today.
verifierReason: Reproduced exactly: D1 rows only give 7,483 bytes (gzip 2,150), 0 R2 reads, 8 D1 round trips, 4 variants with a candidate image and 0 with a reference image, against 5,332,792 bytes (gzip 681,328), 2 R2 reads, and 10 D1 round trips. review.ts:442-446, local-comparison.ts:325-327 (reference_capture_id NULL), and the missing index on visonaut_images.digest are correct. Contract :26 and decision P01 require the complete model today; P01 itself says that a new protocol needs a measured reason, and this lane gives one. Corrections: '4 changed' is invented fixture data (the production samples had all 626 items accepted). By code reading, a D1-only response also has no name, no labels, and no image for a removed capture (review.ts:437-449), so the stored row needs more than the reference image identity. Cheaper steps that need no new endpoint are not in the report: images[].url repeats images[].id (299,719 bytes), and referenceProfile equals candidateProfile in all 3,613 metadata entries.
secondLensReason: Reach: each model read; the client uses the unchanged items for the Accepted group (item-list.tsx:72) and for direct links. Magnitude: rows of D1 only give 7,483 bytes, 0 R2 reads and almost no CPU (measured by the lane and the first verifier). By the D1 count model the server wait would be about 1.2 to 1.4 s in place of 5.25 to 5.68 s, a saving of about 3.9 to 4.5 s for each first load and each receipt (estimate), plus most of the 1.1 to 1.8 s client parse. This is the largest saving of the lane. The ratio 4 of 3,832 is fixture data; the cost depends on the capture count, not on the ratio. New measurement: the lane's minimal options save little on the wire (no label and short id: 12,242 gzip bytes, 1.8%; with images[].url removed: 33,939 bytes, 5.0%) and do not change the server wait. Feasibility: effort L. It needs a new column on visonaut_comparison_rows (the reference image cannot go into tuple_json because approval reuse compares the complete tuple, service local-comparison.ts:27), name and labels for removed captures, a fallback path for old runs and closed summaries, a decision on receipts, client changes (sidebar, arrows, direct links, model merge), and a contract change (current-contract.md:26, P01 at :148, with D08/D09 at :53 as a limit). Counter-argument: P01 is a selected decision and the present design has one request and one state; other parts of the wait cost less to remove, and a second protocol can cost more than it gives for a few users.

title: Almost each capture has its own profile, because the clip rectangle is part of the profile
oneLine: The real run has 3,613 profiles for 3,832 captures (81 without the clip); profiles are 47% of the manifest, 22% of each inventory, 1.3 MB of the model, and the source of the 21,678 digests for each model read.
verifierReason: My own count on the two real manifests gives the same numbers: 3,832 captures, 3,613 profiles, 81 distinct profiles without the clip; all 3,613 profiles have a clip. visual.ts:173 and hash.ts:97-103 are as cited. manifest.profiles is 2,645,645 bytes (21.8% of the inventory) and the model metadata table is 1,322,359 bytes. Correction: the recommendation changes a written contract rule that the report does not cite. Contract :107 puts 'screenshot settings' in the rendering identity, and :124 with packages/cli/src/png-comparison.ts:82 makes a profile change with nonzero changed pixels need review. With the present consumer settings (maxDiffPixels 0 for all 3,832 captures) that rule cannot change a result, so the practical effect is on approval reuse (:184). The maintainers already treat the clip as a special case (hash.ts:97, types.ts:201), so the present state is a partial deliberate choice. The 128 to 186 ms digest times are CPU profile shares that I did not run again; my wall time for the 21,678 digests alone in Node is 374.6 ms.
secondLensReason: Reach: each visual CI run of the live consumer (app.yml on main uses VISONAUT_SERVER https://visonaut.com and the pinned executor digest; about 20 visual runs each day as a lower bound from 40 pull requests in 79 hours) and each model read. The clip is not written by a test author: the consumer's one helper computes it from boundingBox() plus scroll in document coordinates (app/src/test-utils/visual.ts on main), and the adapter writes it into each item profile (packages/playwright/src/visual.ts:231-235). Magnitude: 3,613 profiles for 3,832 captures; 21.8% of each inventory; 164,512 of 681,308 gzip bytes of the model (24.1%, measured); 128 ms of digest CPU locally for each model read (about 0.28 to 0.42 s in production, estimate, and inside WAIT-01); the 16 MiB limit moves from about 5,270 to about 6,600 captures without it (computed); money is about $0.02 each month. One more effect by code reading: the rendering digest contains the clip (hash.ts:85-95) and approval reuse needs an equal tuple (service local-comparison.ts:27, :209-210), so a layout change above an element stops the reuse of an approval for the same two images. Feasibility: moving the clip is a protocol change with a rollout in three places (adapter and CLI release, production pins at wrangler.jsonc:61-62, one consumer pull request); the environment digest already excludes the clip, and the zero-pixel rule (current-contract.md:124) absorbs the digest change, but open approvals are lost one time and two profile forms exist together; it changes current-contract.md:107 and :184. The service-only option (no profile digests in the shared table, compact-model.ts:74) gives the 24% wire saving with no contract change; one digest when equal gives 2.5%. Counter-argument: the rule is written and deliberate, the cost is modest, and WAIT-05 options do more for capacity.

title: A run with more than about 5,270 captures cannot be stored (1.38 times today), and the limits do not agree
oneLine: writeCaptureInventory throws at 5,326 captures (16 MiB) while the CLI accepts about 5,700 and maximumCaptures is 40,000; by code reading the error is an hourly retry with a generic alert, not a named failure (that path was not run).
verifierReason: Reproduced with the real code: 5,250 captures are stored at 16,705,886 bytes (99.6%), and 5,326 captures throw 'Capture inventory exceeds its size limit.' (capture-inventory.ts:468-470). Each row of the limits table has the cited value at the cited line. The failure path (hourly retry with a retry-delayed event, no failRun, for up to 24 hours) agrees with my reading of workflow-materialize.ts:900-934 and :871; neither the auditor nor I ran it. Additions: the bad window is about 5,270 to 5,700 captures, because the CLI stops first above that. One more browser project of the present size (1,316 captures) gives about 97% of the limit, and one more theme or viewport for all items is over it. By code reading, a run that fails this way stays active and 'uploading' and is counted by capacity.ts:41, so five such runs pause all new runs. The ratio 1.73 is not constant: with run-owned image identities the same inventory is 4.0% smaller. It is a capacity limit with a bad failure mode, not a defect that occurs today.
secondLensReason: Reach: production uses the defaults (VISONAUT_API_LIMITS is {}), each CI run with visual jobs goes through this path (about 25 Submit steps each day), and the Visonaut check is required on main (live ruleset). No run fails today (72.4%). I ran the failure path with repository code (the first two passes only read it): plain Error, run stays uploading and active, check intent stays pending, 5 fast attempts then one each hour, event retry-delayed with no reason, 0 log lines with the error text, 2 stuck runs with a limit of 2 give 503 capacity_exceeded. Correction: the slot is held 24 to 30 hours, not without end; expireStagedAttempts then fails the run, and the service refuses to publish a failure for it. New facts: the binding contract plans about 10,580 captures (2.0 times the limit), and the count grew from 1,058 to 3,832 in about 10 days. Fix: a terminal failRun with a named class is small and frees the slot at once; an early 413 in declareStaged is feasible, but the pinned CLI 0.5.4 prints only the HTTP status for it. Raising the limit is blocked by memory (WAIT-06). Counter-argument: one consumer, the first breach blocks only the pull request that adds the captures, and the small fix can be made on that day.

title: Three model reads at the same time need 105 to 109 MB of live JavaScript heap at today's size; the isolate limit is 128 MB
oneLine: V8 heap caps in Node: one read completes at 56 MiB, two at 88, three at 112; receipts can overlap by design (client.ts:306), and sha256() copies each 12 MB buffer; hosted accounting is not measured.
verifierReason: The Node heap-cap table agrees with its raw file (one read completes at 56 MiB, two at 88, three at 112; live heap 44 to 51, 71 to 80, 105 to 109 MB), and the cited client and server lines are correct. Overlapping model builds are a normal case of fast review (use-review-session.ts:286-305). But the numbers do not transfer to workerd as written. workerd uses compressed pointers and Node 24 does not. Measured: a small object takes 23.9 bytes in local workerd and 48 bytes in Node; the two real parsed inventories take 20.1 MiB against 25.3 MiB (0.79), and 30.0 against 35.3 MiB with one JSON string for each capture (0.85). So the table is an upper bound for the workerd JavaScript heap; three reads are about 83 to 93 MB by this ratio (an estimate, not a measurement of a complete read). Hosted memory accounting and buffers stay unmeasured. The sha256 sketch does not pass the repository type check (TS2345 with TypeScript 6.0.2); the parameter must be Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>, as in packages/compare/src/binary.ts:35, so the fix is small but not free. A heap snapshot call gives a live-heap number in local workerd, which the report said was not possible.
secondLensReason: Reach is real: each ready receipt builds the complete model, the client runs one poll loop for each decision, and a build is repeated when another decision commits; maintainers only. The title numbers do not apply to workerd. Measured in local workerd with the real reviewModel (heap after a full collection): one read holds 45.0 MiB at its largest point (canonical check of the second inventory) and 31.1 MiB after both inventories; three reads all held after both inventories hold 86.7 to 87.5 MiB (Node table: 105 to 109 MB). That state cannot occur in workerd: awaited WebCrypto digests do not let another request run (measured), so only one request is in a CPU phase. A request that waits for its second R2 object adds 9.1 MiB. By a sum of measured parts, three overlapping reads are about 63 MiB of heap. But each read also has one 11.6 MiB buffer for each download and a second one at the digest moment, which the report does not count; with them the sum reaches 128 MiB at 4 reads today and at 3 reads at the 16 MiB limit (estimate; hosted accounting not known). Documented result above the limit is mild (requests in flight complete, new isolate, possible Error 1102), and no decision is lost. Fix notes: the hash-without-copy change is small in effect and needs a type change; a per-isolate lock can stay locked when its holder is cancelled; starting the two reads together doubles the buffer memory of a request. The count of Exceeded Memory in the dashboard decides between low and medium.

title: A run with a closed summary still reads both inventories from R2, and its response is the largest
oneLine: For detail_archived = 1 the request still makes 2 R2 reads of 24.3 MB (14 D1 calls, 12 in sequence) and returns 6.35 MB, because one 106-character reason is repeated two times for each variant; the comment at closed-summary.ts:20 says the API reads only D1.
verifierReason: The measurements are correct: for a closed summary the request makes 2 R2 reads of 24,307,562 bytes, 8 D1 round trips in the model (5.9 in sequence against 4.1), and returns 6,347,544 bytes; the repeated reason is 265 bytes x 3,832 = 1,015,480 bytes. The 'inconsistency' is a wrong reading. The comment at closed-summary.ts:20 is about the old R2 history archive that only the converter reads (closed-summary.ts:80-87), and readClosedSummary does read only D1. The inventory of a closed run is kept on purpose for review (retention.ts:46 'Keep sparse review inventories after their original images expire', snapshot-retention.ts:85, contract :33). Measured: without the inventory, the changed rows of a closed summary have no candidate, no reference, and no diff image (the summary captures have image_id ""), so the alternative 'summary rows only' removes all images from closed history. The extra 1.0 MB is 7,861 bytes more after gzip. Sending the reason one time is a correct small step. Low because closed runs are opened rarely and the cost is the same as WAIT-01 to WAIT-03.

title: After 10 s or more with no request, the first Worker request on a new connection waits about 0.2 s more in 70% of the samples; Cloudflare reports the time before the Worker code runs
oneLine: 45 samples: cold /health is over 100 ms slower in 1 of 8 at 1 s, 4 of 9 at 10 s, 7 of 9 at 60 s, 6 of 9 at 300 s, 7 of 8 at 900 s (median 185 ms, p90 268 ms when slow), all as cfEdge with cfWorker 0 to 1 ms; the asset and D1 are not the cause, and no sample was within 10 minutes of a deploy.
verifierReason: My recount of the 45 recorded samples (270 requests) gives the same table: slow /health in 1 of 8, 4 of 9, 7 of 9, 6 of 9, and 7 of 8 samples; 27 slow samples with cfEdge 135 to 363 ms and cfWorker at most 1 ms. '26 of 37' includes two samples with no controlled gap (24 of 35 without them). My own 12 anonymous GET requests (4 new connections, edge CWB, 04:57Z to 05:01Z) show the same signature one time (cfEdge 133 ms, cfWorker 0) but 0 of 3 slow /health after 60 s, and the wait on the static asset in 2 of 4 samples (cfEdge 142 ms on a cache HIT, 392 ms on a MISS). So the 70% rate is a fact of one edge location and one evening, and 'the asset is not slow' does not hold in general. The cause is an inference; Cloudflare does not document where an instance start is counted. The recommendation is overstated: nothing starts the Worker during the JavaScript download, so a static shell moves the wait to the first API request. The sketch also needs an index.html that the build does not make (dist/client has only assets and favicon.svg; the TanStack Start shell default is /_shell), no 'directory' key in the source config, and a CSP with no nonce. It is about 0.2 s, not a defect of the application code.
